Stress test beyond the committed suite: wrote /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-lyonwj-github-neo4j-labs-agent-memory/66a2977c-9670-4b56-8270-fc84ea0f1100/scratchpad/review/stress_create_message.py, which starts its own Neo4j 5.26-community testcontainer, then for 5 rounds: adds 1 message to establish the conversation (matching the documented pattern in test_concurrent_message_additions, since `_ensure_conversation`'s own read-then-create race for brand-new sessions is explicitly called out in that test's docstring as a separate, out-of-scope data-model issue, not something CREATE_MESSAGE/GET_LAST_MESSAGE fix), then fires 24 more `add_message` calls concurrently via `asyncio.gather` (25 total), then verifies via Cypher: exactly one `FIRST_MESSAGE`, exactly one tail (no outgoing NEXT_MESSAGE), an unbroken NEXT_MESSAGE chain from FIRST_MESSAGE to the tail covering every HAS_MESSAGE node exactly once, and no constraint errors from `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)`. All 5 rounds passed cleanly with zero problems reported — no forked chains, no orphaned messages, no duplicate/missing chain coverage, no exceptions. areas.title: Python library, dependencies and their tests
areas.coverage:
I fully checked every changed file in scope: pyproject.toml, uv.lock, src/neo4j_agent_memory/__init__.py, core/_unsupported.py, graph/queries.py, nams/_unsupported.py, nams/ontology.py, tests/integration/nams/test_ontology.py, tests/integration/test_short_term_memory.py, tests/unit/nams/test_ontology.py, tests/unit/nams/test_unsupported.py and tests/unit/test_bolt_optional_dependencies.py.

Verified by running things:

- **CREATE_MESSAGE fix.** Against neo4j:5.26 in a testcontainer, the old CREATE_MESSAGE forked or hit ConstraintError in 10 of 10 concurrent 1+5 trials; the new one forked in 0 of 10. The SET-before-read lock works for single appends.
- **Edge cases.** An empty conversation still yields one row with last=null, so FIRST_MESSAGE is created. Properties, metadata, embedding and timestamp are still written. updated_at is still set, now before the create. Callers in short_term.py (single add ignores the result; batch reads results[0]["m"]["id"]) see the same shape.
- **Integration tests.** RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 on tests/integration/test_short_term_memory.py: 26 passed. The new deterministic forked-chain test fails on the old query, because the constraint error comes from the fan-out.
- **Unit tests.** tests/unit/nams plus test_bolt_optional_dependencies: 474 passed. The bolt import-boundary test fails when pointed at the ec9fc65 source ("Blocked optional backend import: neo4j_agent_memory.nams"), so it guards the real invariant.
- **Sentinel move.** Class identity is preserved through nams._unsupported, there is no import cycle (core/_unsupported imports only core.exceptions), and no public name is removed from __init__.
- **Static checks and lock.** mypy src is clean. ty reports only an environment-specific gliner unresolved-import. ruff lint and format are clean. `uv lock --check --offline` is consistent; the lock removes only the mkdocs tree, and nothing imports those packages.
- **get_active parity.** Pydantic document equality ignores explicit-vs-default fields, so the conflict check matches TypeScript's normalizedDocument.

Not findings, but worth knowing:

- **Tail lookup cost.** In CREATE_MESSAGE the tail lookup still expands every HAS_MESSAGE relationship; that was already O(n) before the branch.
- **Timestamp ties.** Among forked tails with equal timestamps (the same statement's datetime(), for example batch rows), the chosen tail is arbitrary because there is no secondary sort key. This only matters once a chain is already forked.
- **Legacy response shape (pre-existing).** Python get_active falls back to treating a bare document payload as the ontology; TypeScript raises NotSupportedError for the same payload.
- **Leftover clones.** The ontology integration fixture no longer deletes leftover "conservation-clone" ontologies from earlier failed runs. That is deliberate (it deletes only IDs it owns), but a crashed run may block later clone() calls until someone cleans up by hand.

Needs a human decision:

- Whether the hosted /ontologies/active now returns a populated `version`. The previous code and its unit test say it returned version: null, and I cannot observe the service. If it still does, the Python and TypeScript get_active rewrite silently drops validation_mode, revision and version_id.

Not done: the live NAMS ontology tests, which need a MEMORY_API_KEY and an isolated workspace.

Small differences: TS throws plain Error where Python raises ValueError, and TS also requires a safe integer.

Headers are a plain object, so the namespace check can fail.

At ec9fc65, the source comment said the response \"carries no version metadata\", and the old unit mock returned `version: null`. If the hosted service still sends null, TS (and Python) getActive now return no validationMode/revision/versionId, where 0.5.0 filled them in. I cannot observe NAMS from here.

Programs run:
- Against a neo4j:5.26 testcontainer with the local MiniLM embedder: hello-memory/main.py (bolt), eval-harness/main.py, eval-harness/ci_gate.py, audit-trail/main.py, buffered-writes/main.py. Every output matches its README expected block (buffered timings vary, as the README says).

areas.title: Mechanically link-check every changed Markdown file, including fragments and docs-site deep links
areas.coverage:
Method: I built the Antora site fresh from HEAD (npx antora antora-playbook.yml --to-dir <scratchpad>/review/site; the build had no warnings and wrote 289 pages to agent-memory/*.html, with the version segment dropped). I then ran a Python link checker (<scratchpad>/review/linkcheck.py) over all 55 .md files in `git diff --name-only ec9fc65..HEAD` (excluding docs/audit-evidence). For each file it:
- parses inline links, reference definitions, href/src attributes, autolinks and bare neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory URLs, skipping fenced code and inline code;
- resolves relative targets on disk and confirms each target is tracked in git at HEAD;
- resolves #fragments against GitHub-style heading slugs (including duplicate suffixes and explicit <a id>/name), or against ids in the rendered HTML for .adoc and docs-site targets;
- maps every https://neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory/... URL to <path>.html or <path>/index.html in the fresh build and checks the fragment ids;
- flags any link that leaves the repository.

I also spot-checked the tricky anchors by hand (README.md#option-c-self-hosted-neo4j-bolt resolves through the explicit `<a id>` at line 149; the examples/README.md index anchors; typescript/examples/README.md#copying-an-example; the vercel-ai-provider README in-page anchors; aws-strands#_session_manager_push_based and #_memory_store; first-agent-memory.html#_step_2_set_up_neo4j; authentication.adoc#_key_lifecycle). As an extra pass, I checked the repository paths in inline code on added lines, and cross-referenced renamed or deleted files (the diagram move) against Markdown references in the repo.

Files fully checked (all 55): .claude/skills/docs-diataxis/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/docs-excalidraw/SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README-pypi.md, README.md, deploy/cloudrun/README.md, deploy/mcpb/README.md, docs/MAINTAINING.md, docs/assets/images/diagrams/diagram-descriptions.md, examples/AURA_SETUP.md, examples/README.md, and every changed README.md / GETTING_STARTED.md / frontend/README.md under examples/ (audit-trail, buffered-writes, claude-code-team-memory, domain-schemas, eval-harness, existing-graph, financial-services-advisor and its aws/gcp subtrees, full-stack-chat-agent (+frontend), google_adk_demo, google_cloud_integration, hello-memory, lennys-memory (+frontend), microsoft_agent_retail_assistant (+frontend), nams-fastapi, nams-langchain, nams-quickstart, no_llm, ontology-lifecycle, strands-memory-store, strands-session-manager), typescript/README.md, typescript/examples/README.md, and the READMEs of all ten typescript/examples/*, typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/README.md and its examples/README.md.

Results: every relative link and every in-file or cross-file fragment resolves. Every docs-site URL maps to a built page with a valid fragment, except the one pre-existing case below. The only links that leave the repository are the already-reported typescript/examples/README.md:41 and :82 (ts-ex-b#1). The DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md footers in 28 example READMEs are the already-reported py-examples#0 and were not re-reported; microsoft_agent_retail_assistant/README.md:369 is a separate body link and is reported.

Pre-existing broken links on lines this branch did not touch (left out of the findings under the untouched-lines rule; a human should decide whether to fix them in this PR):
- typescript/README.md:111 https://neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory/how-to/typescript: no how-to/typescript.html or how-to/typescript/index.html exists in the build, and none existed on main.
- typescript/README.md:160 https://github.com/neo4j-labs/agent-memory/blob/main/SECURITY.md: no SECURITY.md exists anywhere in HEAD (git ls-tree | grep -i security finds nothing), so the security-reporting pointer is dead.
- examples/financial-services-advisor/google-cloud-financial-advisor/GETTING_STARTED.md:257 ../COMPARISON.md: missing, and no COMPARISON.md appears anywhere in the git history.
- typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/README.md links to ./examples and examples/*.ts, which are not in the package's npm "files", so on npm they depend on npm's link rewriting. These lines are unchanged.

For a human decision (neither form is called broken): the changed Markdown contains 25 .html-form docs URLs, 84 extensionless, and 20 root/directory URLs. The .html form appears at README.md:37,103,153,222,251; README-pypi.md:80; examples/audit-trail, buffered-writes, eval-harness, existing-graph, google_cloud_integration, microsoft_agent_retail_assistant READMEs line 15; examples/claude-code-team-memory/README.md:55; examples/financial-services-advisor/README.md:30,139,203; aws-financial-services-advisor/GETTING_STARTED.md:168; examples/full-stack-chat-agent/README.md:47,166; examples/google_adk_demo/README.md:21,239,246; examples/google_cloud_integration/README.md:248; examples/lennys-memory/README.md:163; examples/microsoft_agent_retail_assistant/README.md:405. The two forms are mixed within README.md, README-pypi.md and examples/buffered-writes/README.md (html at :15, extensionless at :39). findings.title: ruff format --check fails on 3 branch-touched test files, breaking CI's format-check step
findings.detail: `make format-check` (== `uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples`, the exact command ci-python.yml's 'Run ruff format check' step runs) reports 'Would reformat' for three files this branch added/modified: tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py, tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py, and tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py. All three were committed un-formatted (long lines that ruff format wraps, e.g. multi-argument function signatures and long assert messages left on one line). This will fail the ci-python.yml format-check job on this branch's PR.
findings.evidence: Command: `make format-check` → 'Would reformat: tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py' / 'Would reformat: tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py' / 'Would reformat: tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py' / '3 files would be reformatted, 562 files already formatted' / 'make: *** [format-check] Error 1'. Confirmed all three are branch-touched via `git log --oneline ec9fc65..HEAD -- tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py` (non-empty). CI step: .github/workflows/ci-python.yml:80 `run: uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples`.
findings.fix: Run `uv run ruff format tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py` and commit the reformatted files.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced. `uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples` prints 'Would reformat' for tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py, tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py and tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py, then '3 files would be reformatted, 562 files already formatted' and exits non-zero. This is the same command as the 'Run ruff format check' step at .github/workflows/ci-python.yml:80. Running `git log ec9fc65..HEAD` on the three files shows branch commits (c90d191, d3db0ff, 4de6a1e, d41e4bd, 8fc3ead), and none of them has uncommitted changes. So the CI format-check job will fail on this branch.
findings.v2reason: The finding holds up. Three files fail the exact command that CI runs, and this branch added all three: tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py, tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py and tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py. None of them exists at ec9fc65, so main cannot be the cause. The local ruff is 0.14.14, the same version pinned in uv.lock, and CI installs from that lock with `uv sync --group dev`, so a version difference can't explain it either. Changes under tests/** trigger ci-python.yml on both push and pull_request (lines 8 and 27). The lint job has no `if:` condition that would skip it. Its 'Run ruff format check' step (line 80) runs `uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples`, which exits 1. The lint job will therefore fail on this branch's PR. Blocker is the right severity because this breaks a CI job. The fix is to run `uv run ruff format` on the three files.
findings.reproduction:
From the repo root:
1. `uv run ruff --version` printed `ruff 0.14.14`. uv.lock pins `name = "ruff" version = "0.14.14"`.
2. `uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples` printed 'Would reformat: tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py', 'Would reformat: tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py', 'Would reformat: tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py' and '3 files would be reformatted, 562 files already formatted', then exited with EXIT=1.
3. `git cat-file -e ec9fc65:tests/docs/<f>.py` failed for all three files, so they are absent on main and new on this branch.
4. `uv run ruff format --diff tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py` shows that PRODUCT_ALLOWLIST at line 23 would be reflowed from packed multi-item lines to one item per line. That is a real formatting difference, not a trivial one.
5. `git status --short tests/docs` shows no uncommitted changes, so what I checked is the committed HEAD content.
6. In .github/workflows/ci-python.yml, `tests/**` appears in both the push and pull_request `paths` filters. The lint job has no `if:` condition, and line 80 is `run: uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples`.

findings.title: New pytest.mark.rendered used but not registered in pyproject.toml, causing a warning on every run
findings.detail: tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py (added by this branch) sets `pytestmark = pytest.mark.rendered` at module scope, but pyproject.toml's `[tool.pytest.ini_options] markers` list (which the project maintains explicitly, per the docs/integration/syntax/slow/aws markers already registered there) has no `rendered` entry. Every run of this module — including via `make test-docs-build`, which targets exactly this file — emits `PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.rendered`, a warning newly introduced by this branch.
findings.evidence: tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py:21 `pytestmark = pytest.mark.rendered`. pyproject.toml:303-311 `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` `markers = [...]` has no `rendered` entry. Command: `SKIP_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 uv run pytest tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py -q -rs` → `tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py:21: PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.rendered - is this a typo? ... 7 passed, 1 warning`.
findings.fix: Add `"rendered: marks tests as requiring a rendered Antora build (see scripts/render_docs.mjs)"` to the `markers` list in pyproject.toml's `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced. tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py:21 has `pytestmark = pytest.mark.rendered`. The `markers` list at pyproject.toml:303-311 has no 'rendered' entry, and the conftest `pytest_configure` at tests/conftest.py:30-32 registers only integration, docker and slow. Running `SKIP_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 uv run pytest tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py -q -rs` ends with '7 passed, 1 warning' and reports PytestUnknownMarkWarning for line 21. The project does not use --strict-markers (filterwarnings only ignores DeprecationWarning, and `strict = true` belongs to mypy), so this is a warning, not a failure. Severity is minor or lower.

findings.title: New test file uses unregistered pytest marker `rendered`
findings.detail: tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py is a new file on this branch (added in the diff vs ec9fc65) and sets `pytestmark = pytest.mark.rendered` at module level, but `rendered` is not in pyproject.toml's `[tool.pytest.ini_options] markers` list, unlike every other custom marker used in the suite (`integration`, `benchmark`, `docs`, `syntax`, `imports`, `slow`, `aws`). Running the suite emits `PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.rendered - is this a typo?` for every collected test in the file.
findings.evidence: Command: `uv run pytest tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py ... -q -rs` → output: `tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py:21: PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.rendered - is this a typo?  You can register custom marks to avoid this warning`. Source: tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py:21 `pytestmark = pytest.mark.rendered`. Marker registry at pyproject.toml:303-311 (`markers = [...]`) has no `rendered:` entry.
findings.fix: Add `"rendered: marks tests that check the rendered docs site (requires Playwright + a build)"` to the `markers` list in `pyproject.toml`.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced. tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py is new on the branch (git diff ec9fc65..HEAD shows +169 lines) and line 21 is `pytestmark = pytest.mark.rendered`. The marker is not registered anywhere: the pyproject.toml:303-311 `markers` list has integration/benchmark/docs/syntax/imports/slow/aws only, and the conftest `addinivalue_line` calls (tests/conftest.py:30-32, tests/examples/conftest.py:30-32) register integration/docker/slow/requires_neo4j/requires_api_key but not `rendered`. Running `uv run pytest tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py -q -rs` gave `7 passed, 1 warning` with `tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py:21: PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.rendered - is this a typo?`. One correction to the finding: the warning comes once per module at import, not once per collected test. The project does not use --strict-markers, so this is only a warning and nothing fails. That makes it minor (an inconsistency with an easy fix), not a CI break.

findings.title: Only live check of the rewritten get_active() is now skipped in every CI run
findings.detail: The branch rewrites NamsOntology.get_active() so that validation_mode, revision and version_id come only from a `version` object in the GET /ontologies/active response. The second lookup through list()/get() is gone. At the same time the branch gates the whole live ontology module behind RUN_ISOLATED_ONTOLOGY_TESTS=1. Nothing in the repo sets that variable, so nams-integration.yml's consolidated `pytest tests/integration/nams/` run now skips these tests every night. The code being replaced says the service did NOT send version metadata: its comment reads 'GET /ontologies/active returns the schema body but no version metadata', and its unit test mocked the endpoint as {"ontology": DOC, "version": None}. If the service still answers that way, every Python caller now gets validation_mode, revision and version_id as None, and no test anywhere would catch it. I cannot observe the hosted service, so this is lost verification, not a proven regression.
findings.evidence: tests/integration/nams/test_ontology.py:25-31: `pytest.mark.skipif(os.environ.get("RUN_ISOLATED_ONTOLOGY_TESTS") != "1", ...)`. `grep -rn RUN_ISOLATED_ONTOLOGY_TESTS` matches only this file and typescript/test/e2e/ontology.test.ts; no .github/workflows file sets it. .github/workflows/nams-integration.yml:209 runs `uv run pytest tests/integration/nams/`. Old contract, `git show ec9fc65:src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py`: '``GET /ontologies/active`` returns the schema body but no version metadata, so we resolve the active ontology id ... and read its current version'. The old unit test mocked `respond(200, json={"ontology": DOC, "version": None})`. New code, src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py:409-411: `raw_version = payload.get("version"); if raw_version is None: return ActiveOntology(document=document)`.
findings.fix: Before releasing, confirm against the live service that /ontologies/active returns a populated `version`. Then either give the nightly workflow an isolated workspace and set RUN_ISOLATED_ONTOLOGY_TESTS=1 there, or add a non-mutating live check (call get_active() and assert version_id/validation_mode are populated) that is not gated.
findings.v1reason: tests/integration/nams/test_ontology.py:25-31 now adds a skipif on RUN_ISOLATED_ONTOLOGY_TESTS. The old header (git show ec9fc65) had plain `pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration`. The variable appears only in this file and typescript/test/e2e/ontology.test.ts; no workflow sets it. .github/workflows/nams-integration.yml still runs `uv run pytest tests/integration/nams/`, so the nightly live check now skips. The branch also rewrote get_active() (src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py:409-411) to read metadata only from payload['version'], and dropped the list()/get() lookup. The old docstring said the active response 'returns the schema body but no version metadata', and the old unit test mocked `{"ontology": DOC, "version": None}`. No other test calls get_active() live: tests/docs/test_ontology_tutorial.py is mocked. The TS getActive received the same rewrite and its e2e test is gated the same way. So no CI run checks the new contract against the service. Whether the service actually returns `version` could not be observed.
findings.v2reason:
I ran the tests and traced the code, and both support the finding. Commit d41e4bd on this branch did two things together. It rewrote NamsOntology.get_active() (src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py:409-411) so validation_mode, revision, ontology_id and version_id come only from payload["version"]. It also gated the only live get_active() test module behind RUN_ISOLATED_ONTOLOGY_TESTS=1 (tests/integration/nams/test_ontology.py:25-31).

Running that module with a key set skips all 5 tests. A repo-wide grep finds the variable only in that file and in typescript/test/e2e/ontology.test.ts. No .github/workflows file sets it, so the nightly `uv run pytest tests/integration/nams/` in nams-integration.yml:209 skips the module. Before this branch the module had only `pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration` and ran nightly.

Every other get_active caller in tests is mocked with respx: tests/unit/nams, tests/docs/test_ontology_tutorial.py, tests/examples/test_ontology_lifecycle_example.py and test_nams_quickstart_example.py. The earlier contract said the service sent no version metadata. The old Python docstring said "returns the schema body but no version metadata". The old TypeScript getActive said "the active response carries no version metadata". The old unit mock was `{"ontology": DOC, "version": None}`.

The branch's own unit test, test_legacy_document_has_no_inferred_binding (tests/unit/nams/test_ontology.py:142-152), fixes that exact old payload as returning version_id, ontology_id and revision of None. So if the service still answers the old way, every caller silently loses the metadata and no CI job would notice. That includes examples/ontology-lifecycle/main.py:271-281 and :333-336, which print active.revision, validation_mode and version_id.

The d41e4bd commit message says "Keep incomplete live checks ... explicit", which suggests the new contract was never checked live. I cannot see the hosted service, so this is lost verification, not a proven regression. Major severity is right.

findings.title: Forked-chain test builds a fork races never produce; migrate 'repair' leaves the fork edge
findings.detail: _fork() builds its sibling with no incoming NEXT_MESSAGE, and the comment calls this 'the exact state two un-serialized appends used to leave behind'. That is not what a race leaves. Both racing appends read the same tail and both run CREATE (last)-[:NEXT_MESSAGE]->(m), so the predecessor ends up with two outgoing NEXT_MESSAGE edges. On that real shape, MIGRATE_MESSAGE_LINKS only MERGEs the timestamp-ordered links and never deletes the stale branch. The tail count drops to 1, but the predecessor still has two NEXT_MESSAGE edges, so the chain is still branched. test_forked_chain_is_repairable_and_then_appendable checks only the tail count, so it passes either way. The CREATE_MESSAGE comment 'MIGRATE_MESSAGE_LINKS rebuilds a chain that is already forked' (src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:81) claims too much.
findings.evidence: tests/integration/test_short_term_memory.py:433-434: `# A second HAS_MESSAGE with no NEXT_MESSAGE into it: the exact state two un-serialized appends used to leave behind.` The old CREATE_MESSAGE (ec9fc65) runs `CREATE (last)-[:NEXT_MESSAGE]->(m)` for every append. I ran a scratch script against neo4j:5.26 (scratchpad/review/fork_check.py): A->B plus A->C, then MIGRATE_MESSAGE_LINKS. Output: `real fork before migrate: {'heads': 1, 'tails': 2, 'max_out': 2}` and `real fork after migrate: {'heads': 1, 'tails': 1, 'max_out': 2}`. The test only asserts tails: line 491 `assert shape[0]["tails"] == 1`.
findings.fix: Build the fork the way a race does, with two messages each receiving NEXT_MESSAGE from the same predecessor. Also assert that no message has more than one outgoing NEXT_MESSAGE after migrate. Either make MIGRATE_MESSAGE_LINKS delete out-of-order NEXT_MESSAGE edges before merging, or soften the queries.py:81 comment to 'restores a single tail'.
findings.v1reason: I reran the reviewer's fork_check.py against a throwaway neo4j:5.26 container. A real race shape (A->B plus A->C) followed by MIGRATE_MESSAGE_LINKS gave `before: tails 2, max_out 2` and `after: tails 1, max_out 2`. The migrate query (queries.py:15-29) only MERGEs and never deletes the stale edge, so the chain stays branched. The queries.py:81 comment 'MIGRATE_MESSAGE_LINKS rebuilds a chain that is already forked' overclaims. tests/integration/test_short_term_memory.py:433-434 calls an unlinked sibling 'the exact state two un-serialized appends used to leave behind', which is not the race shape. Line 491 asserts only tails == 1, so the repair test would pass even when the chain is still branched. The append-safety purpose of the test is still valid.

findings.title: The 'appends serialize' claim does not cover add_messages_batch, which can still fork the chain
findings.detail: The new comment says the SET lock makes 'concurrent appends to one conversation serialize'. That holds only for single add_message calls. add_messages_batch reads the tail with GET_LAST_MESSAGE in its own read transaction. It then creates the unlinked messages (CREATE_MESSAGES_BATCH) and links them (CREATE_MESSAGE_LINKS) in two more transactions, and none of the three takes the conversation lock before reading the tail. An add_message that runs between the batch insert and the link step sees the batch messages as tails. It links one of them, and the link step then forks the chain. This race existed before the branch, but the new comment and the test docstring now present appends as serialized.
findings.evidence: src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:71-73: `// Write to the conversation before reading the tail. SET takes a write lock on c that is held to commit, so concurrent appends to one conversation serialize`. In src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:422, `existing_last_id = await self._get_last_message_id(conv_id)` runs in a separate read transaction; lines 474-488 run the insert and the link as two separate execute_write calls. Scratch reproduction (fork_check.py, neo4j:5.26) interleaving batch insert -> CREATE_MESSAGE -> CREATE_MESSAGE_LINKS gave `batch interleave: {'heads': 1, 'tails': 2, 'max_out': 2}`.
findings.fix: Either limit the comment to single-message appends and note the batch gap, as the commit message does for _ensure_conversation, or take the conversation lock (SET c.updated_at) and read the tail inside the same transaction as the batch insert and linking.
findings.v1reason: add_messages_batch (short_term.py:422, 474-488) reads the tail in one transaction, then inserts and links in two further execute_write calls, and none of them takes the conversation lock. The reviewer's interleaving reproduced in my run: `batch interleave: {'heads': 1, 'tails': 2, 'max_out': 2}`. The race predates the branch and add_messages_batch is unchanged. The defect is only that the new CREATE_MESSAGE comment (queries.py:71-73), 'concurrent appends to one conversation serialize', does not cover the batch path. That is an inaccurate code comment, so nit rather than minor.

findings.title: ORDER BY on GET_LAST_MESSAGE makes the tail lookup scan every message in the conversation
findings.detail: Before this branch, GET_LAST_MESSAGE could stop at LIMIT 1 as soon as it found a tail. Neo4j walks the newest relationships first, so on a linear chain that was effectively constant work. Adding ORDER BY m.timestamp DESC forces a full expansion and sort of every HAS_MESSAGE relationship before the LIMIT. add_messages_batch runs this lookup on every call. The ordering only matters when the chain is already forked. CREATE_MESSAGE was already O(n) and is unchanged.
findings.evidence: I ran PROFILE on a 3000-message conversation in neo4j:5.26 (scratchpad/review/perf_check.py). Output: `old GET_LAST dbHits 16`, `new GET_LAST dbHits 6013`, `old CREATE dbHits 9022`, `new CREATE dbHits 9031`. The query at src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:7-13 now ends `RETURN m ORDER BY m.timestamp DESC LIMIT 1`.
findings.fix: Accept the cost and document it, or track the tail explicitly (for example a LAST_MESSAGE relationship or a c.last_message_id property updated under the conversation lock) so neither query needs to scan the conversation.
findings.v1reason: I reran the reviewer's perf_check.py (3000-message conversation, neo4j:5.26) and got: old GET_LAST dbHits 16, new GET_LAST dbHits 6013, old CREATE 9022, new CREATE 9031. The ORDER BY m.timestamp DESC added at queries.py:11 forces a full expansion and sort. The only caller is _get_last_message_id, once per add_messages_batch call, and CREATE_MESSAGE was already O(n). So this is a bounded efficiency regression.

findings.title: Branch changes shipped behaviour in src but leaves CHANGELOG [Unreleased] empty
findings.detail: The branch changes user-visible library behaviour. get_active() now sends one request instead of three, leaves metadata as None when the response has no `version`, and can raise ValueError on malformed or conflicting metadata. It also adds schema_hash to ActiveOntology. CREATE_MESSAGE no longer throws ConstraintError on forked conversations. Bolt connect no longer imports the nams package or httpx. The `docs` dependency group is emptied. The package version stays 0.6.0 and CHANGELOG.md is not touched. The docs page reference/ontology-api.adoc (#python-0-6-active-binding) still describes the released 0.6.0 get_active() as reporting the latest revision, and no changelog entry records that current source behaves differently.
findings.evidence: `git diff --stat ec9fc65..HEAD -- CHANGELOG.md` prints nothing. CHANGELOG.md:8-10 has `## [Unreleased]` followed directly by `## [0.6.0] - 2026-09-14`. The behaviour change is in src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py:391-422, and pyproject.toml:3 still reads `version = "0.6.0"`.
findings.fix: Add [Unreleased] entries for the get_active() contract change (including the new ValueError and schema_hash), the forked-chain fix in CREATE_MESSAGE and GET_LAST_MESSAGE, the Bolt/httpx import boundary, and the removal of the mkdocs docs group.

The branch does change runtime behaviour: get_active() now makes one request, can raise ValueError and adds schema_hash (ontology.py diff); CREATE_MESSAGE and GET_LAST_MESSAGE changed; the pyproject `docs` group was emptied; the TS getActive changed the same way. CONTRIBUTING.md:303 and :322 expect CHANGELOG entries, and :322 asks to 'distinguish released behavior from source-only work'. reference/ontology-api.adoc:74-81 documents the 0.6.0 limitation, but no changelog entry records the source-only fix.

findings.title: Python accepts a non-string version.schema_json; TypeScript rejects it
findings.detail: _parse_active_version passes schema_json to _parse_document, which accepts a dict as well as a JSON string. The TypeScript toActiveVersion, which the branch presents as its twin, throws when schema_json is not a string. The two SDKs therefore disagree on a malformed binding. TypeScript also checks the types of schema_hash, created_at and message explicitly, which Python leaves to Pydantic (that part behaves the same).
findings.evidence: Command: `uv run python -c "from neo4j_agent_memory.nams.ontology import _parse_active_version; print(_parse_active_version({'id':'ov_1','ontology_id':'ont_1','revision':1,'validation_mode':'strict','schema_json':{'domain':{'id':'d','name':'D'}}}).document)"`. Output: `domain=DomainInfo(id='d', name='D', ...)`, so a dict is accepted. typescript/src/ontology/index.ts:308-309: `if (value.schema_json != null && typeof value.schema_json !== "string") { throw new Error("Invalid active ontology version metadata: schema_json must be a string."); }`
findings.fix: In _parse_active_version, raise ValueError when schema_json is not None and not a str, matching TypeScript, and add that case to the test_rejects_invalid_supplied_binding parametrization.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced: `_parse_active_version({... 'schema_json': {'domain': {...}}})` returns a parsed document, because _parse_document (ontology.py:251-261) accepts a dict. typescript/src/ontology/index.ts:308-309 throws when schema_json is not a string. This is a small parity gap on malformed input only.

findings.title: E2E cleanup expects NotFoundError, but the REST transport throws TransportError(404)
findings.detail: After deleting each clone, afterAll asserts that `ontology.get(id)` rejects with `NotFoundError`. The REST transport never builds a NotFoundError. It maps every non-OK, non-auth response to `TransportError` with `statusCode`. So after a successful delete, this assertion always fails and the whole isolated ontology e2e run goes red. The mistake looks like a port of the Python integration test (`tests/integration/nams/test_ontology.py:71` uses `pytest.raises(NotFoundError)`), where Python does map 404 to NotFoundError. The branch's own docs say the TypeScript SDK does not: handle-errors.adoc:19 and typescript-api.adoc:486. So does its own contract test, which expects HTTP 404 to produce `TransportError`.
findings.evidence:
typescript/test/e2e/ontology.test.ts:55 `await expect(client!.ontology.get(id)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(NotFoundError);`
Source: typescript/src/transport/rest.ts:626-632 `const err = new TransportError(`${method} failed: ${errMsg}`, response.status, errorBody, { requestId });`. `grep -rn "new NotFoundError" typescript/src` returns no matches.
Repro (scratchpad nf.mts, fetch stubbed to return 404, then `client.ontology.get("ont_x")`): output `name= TransportError NotFoundError? false TransportError? true status 404`.
docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/typescript/handle-errors.adoc:19 "`NotFoundError` exists for compatibility but is not the normal REST 404 mapping."
findings.fix: Assert the real mapping: `await expect(client!.ontology.get(id)).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: "TransportError", statusCode: 404 })`, or use `toBeInstanceOf(TransportError)` plus a statusCode check. Drop the NotFoundError import.
findings.v1reason: The branch added typescript/test/e2e/ontology.test.ts:12 `import { NotFoundError }` and :55 `rejects.toBeInstanceOf(NotFoundError)`. The only non-auth error path in typescript/src/transport/rest.ts (around lines 626-632) throws `new TransportError(..., response.status, ...)`. `grep -rn NotFoundError typescript/src` finds only the class definition (errors.ts:44) and its re-export (index.ts:132); nothing throws it. OntologyClient.get (ontology/index.ts:443) passes transport errors straight through. docs how-to/typescript/handle-errors.adoc:18 says the same: "NotFoundError exists for compatibility but is not the normal REST 404 mapping." So after a successful delete the assertion can never pass, and the afterAll hook fails. The suite only runs when RUN_ISOLATED_ONTOLOGY_TESTS=1 and a key are set (`npm run test:e2e`), not in CI. That makes it major rather than blocker.
findings.v2reason: The finding holds. This branch added the NotFoundError import (typescript/test/e2e/ontology.test.ts:12) and the assertion `await expect(client!.ontology.get(id)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(NotFoundError)` (line 55). The old version at ec9fc65 only called `ontology.delete` and never checked the error type. Nothing in the SDK can produce that error. `OntologyClient.get` (typescript/src/ontology/index.ts:443) sends the call straight to the transport. In typescript/src/transport/rest.ts, 401 and 403 become AuthenticationError and every other non-OK status becomes `new TransportError(..., response.status, ...)`. Searching typescript/src for NotFoundError finds only the class definition (errors.ts:44) and its re-export (index.ts:132); nothing throws it. When I ran the call with a stubbed 404 response, it threw TransportError with statusCode 404, not NotFoundError. So once a delete succeeds, the check in afterAll always fails and the opt-in isolated ontology e2e suite goes red. Major is the right severity: the suite only runs when both MEMORY_API_KEY and RUN_ISOLATED_ONTOLOGY_TESTS=1 are set, so it does not break CI, but the test can never pass as written. Fix: assert `rejects.toMatchObject({ name: "TransportError", statusCode: 404 })`, or `toBeInstanceOf(TransportError)` plus a statusCode check, and remove the NotFoundError import.
findings.reproduction:
1) `git show ec9fc65:typescript/test/e2e/ontology.test.ts | grep -n NotFound` returns nothing, so the branch introduced both the import and the assertion.
2) `grep -rn NotFoundError typescript/src` returns only errors.ts:44, errors.ts:47 (this.name) and index.ts:132 (re-export). None of them throws the error.
3) I wrote scratchpad/review/nf2.mts. It replaces globalThis.fetch with a function that returns 404 and the body {"error":"ontology not found"}, builds `new MemoryClient({endpoint:"https://memory.neo4jlabs.com/v1", apiKey:"nams_test", maxRetries:0})`, and calls `c.ontology.get("ont_x")`. I ran it with `cd typescript && npx tsx <scratch>/nf2.mts`. Output:
  req GET https://memory.neo4jlabs.com/v1/ontologies/ont_x
  name= TransportError NotFound? false Transport? true status 404
So `rejects.toBeInstanceOf(NotFoundError)` fails for the real 404 path.

findings.title: Unreleased getActive() change and new ActiveOntology.schemaHash are not in the CHANGELOG
findings.detail:
This branch rewrites `OntologyClient.getActive()`: 
- It no longer composes metadata through `list()` and `get()`.
- Legacy or `version: null` responses now return no `validationMode`, `revision`, `versionId` or `ontologyId` (0.5.0 did fill them in).
- It throws a plain `Error` on malformed or conflicting metadata.
- It adds `ActiveOntology.schemaHash`.
The published typescript-v0.5.0 tag does not contain this commit, but package.json and VERSION still say 0.5.0 and `## [Unreleased]` is empty. The regenerated TypeDoc under docs attachments, titled "agent-memory - v0.5.0", now lists `schemaHash` on ActiveOntology, which is unreleased behaviour presented as 0.5.0. Meanwhile reference/typescript-api.adoc:440 still describes the old "composed" metadata, which contradicts ontology-api.adoc:88-92.
findings.evidence:
`git merge-base --is-ancestor d41e4bd typescript-v0.5.0` prints `typescript-v0.5.0 lacks d41e4bd`, and `git show typescript-v0.5.0:typescript/src/ontology/index.ts` line 410 is `// Compose version metadata via a second lookup`.
HEAD typescript/src/ontology/index.ts:472 `if (raw.version == null) return { document };` and :103 `schemaHash?: string;`
typescript/CHANGELOG.md:10-12: `## [Unreleased]` followed directly by `## 0.5.0 — 2026-09-22`.
typescript/package.json:3 `"version": "0.5.0"`; typescript/src/version.ts:6 `VERSION = "0.5.0"`.
docs/modules/ROOT/attachments/api/typescript/interfaces/index.ActiveOntology.html has 2 `schemaHash` matches at HEAD and 0 at ec9fc65; its index.html title is `agent-memory - v0.5.0`.
docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/typescript-api.adoc:440 "Active version's parsed document + composed `validationMode` / `revision` / `versionId`."
findings.fix: Add an `[Unreleased]` entry under Changed/Added. Cover the getActive() binding source, legacy responses leaving metadata undefined (a behaviour change from 0.5.0), the plain Error throws, and the new `schemaHash`. Either stop publishing the regenerated TypeDoc as v0.5.0 until the release, or label it as unreleased. Update typescript-api.adoc:440 to match.
findings.v1reason: The branch commit d41e4bd rewrote getActive(). The list()/get() composition and currentVersion() are gone. It now returns `{ document }` when `raw.version == null`, throws plain `Error` on bad or conflicting metadata, and adds `schemaHash?: string` (ontology/index.ts:103). `git merge-base --is-ancestor d41e4bd typescript-v0.5.0` shows the commit is not in the release tag. typescript/CHANGELOG.md:10-12 has an empty `## [Unreleased]` and is untouched by the branch. The regenerated TypeDoc ActiveOntology page has 2 schemaHash matches (0 at ec9fc65), and its index.html title is `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory - v0.5.0`. That labels an unreleased member as 0.5.0. One nuance: typescript-api.adoc:440 ("composed validationMode/revision/versionId") is unchanged since 2026-05 and is accurate for the released 0.5.0. It only contradicts HEAD source and ontology-api.adoc:88-92, which itself flags that this is not an npm release. Still, the missing changelog entry and the mislabeled TypeDoc hold.
findings.v2reason:
I ran the finding and it holds. Branch commit d41e4bd rewrites OntologyClient.getActive() in typescript/src/ontology/index.ts:462-485. The old list()/get() composition and currentVersion() are gone. The method now returns `{ document }` when `raw.version == null`, throws a plain Error on partial or conflicting metadata, and adds `schemaHash?: string` (line 103).

I ran the 0.5.0-tag version and the HEAD version of getActive() against the same fake transport:
- Legacy responses: 0.5.0 filled in ontologyId, validationMode, revision and versionId. HEAD returns none of them. This is a real behaviour regression for legacy responses.
- Partial metadata: 0.5.0 accepted it. HEAD throws a plain Error.

d41e4bd is not in typescript-v0.5.0. The branch does not touch typescript/CHANGELOG.md, package.json or version.ts, and `## [Unreleased]` is empty.

The branch also regenerated the TypeDoc (commit e2bcb93), which is published verbatim as a docs attachment. It is titled "@neo4j-labs/agent-memory - v0.5.0". Its ActiveOntology page now lists `schemaHash` (2 matches, 0 at ec9fc65) and the new "Legacy document-only responses leave the binding metadata absent" doc comment. That describes behaviour and an API member the npm 0.5.0 package does not have.

Nuance: typescript-api.adoc:441 ("composed validationMode / revision / versionId") is accurate for the released 0.5.0, which the docs are meant to describe. It conflicts only with HEAD source and with ontology-api.adoc:91-96. That page explicitly scopes itself to "current TypeScript source" and says it is not an npm release. So the typescript-api.adoc part of the finding is weak, and at most a minor inconsistency.

Major severity is justified by the mislabelled published TypeDoc, a wrong API claim for 0.5.0, together with an undocumented behaviour change in the SDK. The missing CHANGELOG entry alone would be minor.

findings.title: README tutorial links now point to raw .adoc source whose Antora includes don't resolve
findings.detail: The same diff turned every `./examples` link into an absolute GitHub URL, because the README ships in the npm package. It also replaced the published-site tutorial URL with two relative `../docs/modules/ROOT/pages/...adoc` links. From the npm package page, `../` escapes the package (package.json `files` is dist, README.md, LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md). On GitHub the link opens AsciiDoc source, whose `include::partial$...` Antora resource ids GitHub cannot resolve. The "Start here" tutorial therefore renders without its project setup, API and lifecycle sections.

The old README (ec9fc65) line 100 used `https://neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory/tutorials/first-agent-memory-typescript`.

findings.v1reason: typescript/README.md:109-110 link to `../docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/*.adoc`. The base README (ec9fc65) used https://neo4j.com/labs/agent-memory/tutorials/first-agent-memory-typescript. package.json `files` is [dist, README.md, LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md], so on npm the relative `../` link points outside the package. On GitHub the link opens raw AsciiDoc, whose `include::partial$typescript-tutorial-project.adoc[]` (:21), `...-api.adoc[]` (:58) and `...-lifecycle.adoc[]` (:130) are Antora resource ids that GitHub cannot resolve. The branch converted the neighbouring example links to absolute GitHub URLs for exactly this reason, which makes these two inconsistent.
findings.v2reason: The branch replaced the published-site tutorial link in typescript/README.md with two relative links to raw AsciiDoc source (lines 109-110). Both pages build fine on the Antora site (docs/build/site/agent-memory/tutorials/hosted-quickstart-typescript.html and first-agent-memory-typescript.html exist), so working published URLs were available. The branch also added the `include::partial$typescript-tutorial-*.adoc[]` directives to these tutorials. In ec9fc65, first-agent-memory-typescript.adoc had 0 includes; at HEAD, both pages have 3 each. GitHub's AsciiDoc renderer cannot resolve Antora `partial$` resource ids, so a reader who clicks through on GitHub gets the tutorial without its project-setup, API and lifecycle sections, which is 118 lines of partial content. One part of the finding is weaker than stated: package.json sets `repository.directory: "typescript"`, so npmjs.com probably rewrites the relative link to a GitHub blob URL instead of leaving it broken inside the package. That rewritten link still lands on the incomplete raw AsciiDoc, though. findings.title: Extraction wait treats only per-message status "done" as finished, so "completed" times out every cleanup
findings.detail: waitForTerminalExtraction returns only when every message status is exactly "done". It fails on "error"/"failed" and otherwise keeps polling until the deadline. The Python SDK documents the per-message statuses as pending / completed / failed. The Python hosted tutorial helper on this same branch accepts done, completed and skipped as terminal. If NAMS returns "completed" (or "skipped"), cleanupTutorial ends with "Extraction deadline expired; no records were deleted." and never deletes anything. That covers every TypeScript lesson (hosted-quickstart, first-agent, conversation, knowledge-graph, mcp), and the knowledge-graph seed/observe phases fail the same way. A "cancelled" status is also not treated as a failure; it waits for the full timeout. The offline stub returns "done", and tutorial-state-cleanup.test.ts:116 never tests "completed", so CI cannot see this.
findings.evidence: typescript/examples/shared/tutorial-cleanup.ts:37-38: `if (value.messages.some(m => ["error", "failed"].includes(m.status!))) throw ...; if (value.messages.every(m => m.status === "done")) return;`. Source of truth: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:240-241 ("``summary`` maps each per-message extraction status (``pending`` / ``completed`` / ``failed`` / …)"). The same branch's Python helper, docs/modules/ROOT/examples/hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py:56-58, accepts `terminal = {"done", "completed", "skipped"}` and treats `("failed", "error", "cancelled")` as failure. Repro: a scratch vitest that sets `stub.behavior.extraction = "completed"` (and "skipped") in docs-hosted-stub, seeds a run, then calls `cleanupTutorial(run, {timeoutMs:1500})`. Both cases rejected with "deadline expired" and the conversation stayed in the stub (2/2 passed).
findings.fix: Accept the same vocabulary as the Python helper: terminal = done|completed|skipped, failure = failed|error|cancelled, pending = pending|processing|running|in_progress|queued, and throw on any unknown status. Add "completed" and "skipped" cases to the stub-driven tests.
findings.v1reason: typescript/examples/shared/tutorial-cleanup.ts:37-38 fails only on 'error'/'failed' and returns only when every per-message status === 'done'. Any other status, including 'completed', 'skipped' and 'cancelled', keeps it polling until the deadline, and then it throws 'Extraction deadline expired; no records were deleted.' (:42). The Python SDK is the source of truth here, and it names 'completed' as a per-message status: nams/short_term.py:240-241 ('pending / completed / failed'), and _NONTERMINAL_EXTRACTION_STATUSES at :126-127 lists only pending/processing/running/in_progress/queued. Its NAMS fixtures also all use 'completed': tests/unit/nams/test_short_term.py:361-362, test_long_term.py:78/91, tests/examples/test_nams_quickstart_example.py:130, test_claude_code_team_memory_example.py:165. The branch's own Python helper, docs/modules/ROOT/examples/hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py:54-57, accepts {done, completed, skipped} as terminal and fails on cancelled. Only the TS stub emits 'done' (vercel-ai/test/docs-hosted-stub.ts:14). I cannot see what live NAMS returns, but the TS helper disagrees with the SDK's documented contract, and cleanup silently never runs if 'completed' comes back.
findings.v2reason:
I ran the helper and it behaves as the finding says. typescript/examples/shared/tutorial-cleanup.ts is new on this branch (it does not exist at ec9fc65). It was added in d41e4bd and f1a4786. Line 38 returns only when every per-message status === "done". Line 37 fails only on "error" or "failed". Any other status keeps it polling until the deadline, and then line 42 throws "Extraction deadline expired; no records were deleted."

The branch disagrees with itself on the status vocabulary:
- The Python SDK names "completed" as a per-message status: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:240-241 ("pending / completed / failed / …").
- `ExtractionStatus.is_complete` (short_term.py:126-127) treats every status outside {pending, processing, running, in_progress, queued} as terminal.
- The branch's own Python helper, docs/modules/ROOT/examples/hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py:56-58, accepts {done, completed, skipped} as terminal and treats cancelled as a failure.
- The branch's own Python test, tests/docs/test_hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py:173, runs with both terminal_status "completed" and "done". So the author expected "completed" as a real terminal status in Python but left it out of the TypeScript helper.

The only thing that emits "done" is the TS stub (typescript/examples/vercel-ai/test/docs-hosted-stub.ts:14), so the TS tests cannot catch this.

Consumers affected: shared/tutorial-mcp.ts, vercel-ai/src/tutorials/knowledge-graph.ts, and the tutorial CLI cleanup path (tutorial-cleanup.ts:177).

What I could not observe is which status the live NAMS actually returns. If it returns "done", the helper works. But it contradicts the SDK's documented contract and the branch's own Python helper and test. The failure is safe: nothing gets deleted. Still, every TS tutorial cleanup would fail with a misleading "deadline expired" error, so major is about right.

findings.title: Hooks-mode test passes even when the deny hook and the retry hook are disabled
findings.detail: The test is titled "runs all eight lifecycle events", but it never checks that any hook fired except the redaction check. The deny and retry assertions only check text that the mock model returns unconditionally once any tool result is in the prompt. A denied call, an executed delete_account and an unretried tool error all produce a tool message, so the mock gives the same answer each time. The comments "delete_account was denied, never executed" and "survived the flaky_lookup retry" describe checks the test does not make.
findings.evidence: docs-pages.test.ts:218-222 has the mock return `textResult("Graph databases are well documented.")` / `"I can't do that -- account deletion is disabled in this demo."` whenever steps>0, and :232-233 assert `answers[1]).toContain("documented")` and `answers[2]).toContain("disabled")`. Mutation run: copied src/hooks-mode.ts to the scratchpad, changed `permissionDecision: 'deny'` to `'allow'` and `attempt === 1` to `attempt === 99`, and ran the unmodified test (`npx vitest run -t "hooks mode"`). Result: `Tests 1 passed | 7 skipped`.
findings.fix: Assert on observable effects. Count delete_account executions (for example with a spy) and check that the tool result in the step-1 prompt is the `{ blocked: true, ... }` object. Assert that flaky_lookup ran twice and that the step-1 prompt holds a successful tool result. Record which hook events fired (Stop/SessionEnd log lines, or a spy per event) so the "eight events" title is actually tested.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced. I mirrored the example tree in the scratchpad (symlinked node_modules, copied shared/, vercel-ai/test and tsconfig.base.json). In the copied src/hooks-mode.ts I changed permissionDecision 'deny' to 'allow' (line 46) and 'attempt === 1' to 'attempt === 99' (line 54), then ran the unmodified test with `npx vitest run -t "hooks mode"`. Result: 'Tests 1 passed | 7 skipped'. The mock model's answers depend only on toolResultCount (docs-pages.test.ts:83-84, :218-222), so the 'denied' and 'retry' assertions at :232-233 cannot fail when either hook is disabled.
findings.v2reason: The finding holds. The mock model in the hooks-mode test (typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/test/docs-pages.test.ts:212-225) picks its reply from only two things: the current user text and whether any tool message is in the prompt (toolResultCount, :83-84). A denied delete_account, a delete_account that actually ran, a flaky_lookup that was retried and one that was not all put a tool message in the step-1 prompt. The mock therefore gives the same "documented" / "disabled" text every time, and the assertions at :232-233 cannot fail. The only hook effects the test observes are the two redaction hooks (UserPromptSubmit and PreMemoryWrite, :239-240). I checked this by running the test against mutated copies of src/hooks-mode.ts, using a different method from the first reviewer's. First, a probe inside delete_account's execute shows the deny hook works in the real code: nothing is printed when the hook is kept, and "DELETE_EXECUTED" is printed when the hook is flipped to 'allow'. The test passes in both cases. Second, deleting the SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop and SessionEnd hooks all at once still passes. So the "runs all eight lifecycle events" title and the "denied, never executed" and "survived the retry" comments claim checks the test does not make. The branch adds this test, and it passes without catching a regression it says it guards against, so major is right.
findings.reproduction:
I mirrored the example tree under scratchpad/review/mut2/typescript/examples/: copied nams-ai-provider/{src,test,package.json,tsconfig.json}, vercel-ai/test, shared/ and tsconfig.base.json, and symlinked nams-ai-provider/node_modules. Each mutation below replaces src/hooks-mode.ts with a fresh copy, edits it, and runs `npx vitest run -t "hooks mode"` against the unmodified test.
- Baseline, no change: `Tests 1 passed | 7 skipped (8)`.
- M1, `permissionDecision: 'deny'` changed to `'allow'` (line 46): `Tests 1 passed | 7 skipped (8)`.
- M2, `attempt === 1 ?` changed to `attempt === 99 ?` (line 54), so the retry never happens: `Tests 1 passed | 7 skipped (8)`.
- M3, removed SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop and SessionEnd, keeping only UserPromptSubmit and PreMemoryWrite: `Tests 1 passed | 7 skipped (8)`.
- M4, M1 plus a probe in delete_account's execute (`process.stderr.write('DELETE_EXECUTED\n')`): the output shows `DELETE_EXECUTED` and `Tests 1 passed | 7 skipped (8)`. The tool actually ran and the test still passed.
- Control, the same probe with the deny hook kept: no `DELETE_EXECUTED` in the output and `Tests 1 passed`. The hook works, but the test cannot tell whether it did.
Afterwards `git status --short typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider` shows only the package-lock.json change that was already there, so the repo is untouched.

findings.title: Entry-point check `file://${argv[1]}` silently does nothing when the path has spaces or other encoded characters
findings.detail: All four mode programs start only when `import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}``. import.meta.url is percent-encoded and argv[1] is not, so from a checkout path with a space or a non-ASCII character (and on Windows) the comparison is false. `npm run <mode>` then exits 0 with no output and no error. The pages embed these programs verbatim. The vercel-ai tutorials in this branch avoid the problem with isTutorialEntryPoint (pathToFileURL(realpathSync(argv[1]))).
findings.evidence: hooks-mode.ts:121, middleware-mode.ts:76, provider-mode.ts:85 and tools-mode.ts:106 all use `if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`)`. Repro: ran `npx tsx ".../scratchpad/review/dir with space/m.ts"` with the same check; output: `url file:///.../dir%20with%20space/m.ts` then `ENTRY NOT MATCHED`. Correct pattern: typescript/examples/shared/tutorial-state.ts:246-247 `moduleUrl === pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href`.
findings.fix: Compare against `pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href` (or reuse isTutorialEntryPoint), then re-embed the programs on the four how-to pages.
findings.v1reason: All four programs use `import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`` (hooks-mode.ts:121, middleware-mode.ts:76, tools-mode.ts:106, provider-mode.ts:85), and the four how-to pages embed the same guard. I reproduced the failure: `npx tsx '<scratch>/dir with space/m.mts'` printed import.meta.url with 'dir%20with%20space' and then 'NOT MATCHED', so the program silently does nothing. shared/tutorial-state.ts:246-247 already has the correct pathToFileURL(realpathSync(...)) pattern.

findings.title: Hooks-mode README and header comment get the turn count and hook firing wrong
findings.detail: The README says hooks mode prints one [hook] line per event across three turns (allowed, denied, redacted). The program runs four turns, including the flaky-retry turn, and only the Stop and SessionEnd handlers print [hook] lines. The program's header comment says "Each event fires once across the four turns below", but UserPromptSubmit, PreMemoryWrite and Stop run on every turn.
findings.evidence: README.md:112-113: "Hooks mode prints one `[hook]` line per event that fires, across three turns (an allowed tool call, a denied one, and a redacted one)". hooks-mode.ts:112-117 defines four turns; only :57 and :58 call console.log with `[hook]`. hooks-mode.ts:4-5: "Each event fires once across the four turns below". vercel-ai-provider-hooks.ts:304 (UserPromptSubmit), :436 (PreMemoryWrite) and :459 (Stop) run on each prepare/onFinish, not once per session. Only SessionStart is guarded by `startedSessions` (:293).
findings.fix: README: four turns; [hook] lines come from Stop (once per turn) and SessionEnd. Comment: say which events fire on every turn and which fire once.
findings.v1reason: README.md:111-113 says hooks mode prints one [hook] line per event 'across three turns (an allowed tool call, a denied one, and a redacted one)'. The program actually runs four turns, including the flaky-retry turn (hooks-mode.ts:112-117). Only Stop (:57) and SessionEnd (:58) print [hook] lines, so the output is four Stop lines plus one SessionEnd line. The header comment at :4-5 says 'Each event fires once across the four turns', but UserPromptSubmit (provider hooks :304), PreMemoryWrite (:436) and Stop (:459) have no once-per-session guard and run on every prepare/onFinish. Only SessionStart is guarded (:293).

findings.title: CI builds vercel-ai-provider only for nams-ai-provider, but nextjs-memory-chat now depends on it too
findings.detail: This branch adds `@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider: file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider` to nextjs-memory-chat and imports `createNamsProvider` from it in lib/handlers.ts. The provider's dist/ is gitignored and nothing builds it on a fresh checkout. The step that runs `npm ci && npm run build` in typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider only runs when `matrix.example == 'nams-ai-provider'`. In the `Example (nextjs-memory-chat, Node 24)` leg, the package therefore has no dist/index.d.ts, no dist/index.js and no node_modules. `tsc --noEmit` then cannot resolve the module, and `npm test` and `npm run build` fail. `make ts-test-examples` (Makefile:835-848) also never builds the provider, so the local mirror fails the same way.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci-typescript.yml:127-128: `- name: 'Build vercel-ai-provider package (populates dist for nams-ai-provider example)'` / `if: matrix.example == 'nams-ai-provider'`. The matrix at :95 includes `- nextjs-memory-chat`. typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/package.json:24: `"@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider": "file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider"`. typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/lib/handlers.ts:12: `import { createNamsProvider } from "@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider";`. typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/.gitignore:5 `dist/`, and `git ls-files typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/dist` returns nothing. The provider package.json has `"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"`. Makefile:836 builds only `$(TS_DIR)`.
findings.fix: Change the condition to `if: matrix.example == 'nams-ai-provider' || matrix.example == 'nextjs-memory-chat'`, or derive it from whether the example's package.json references packages/vercel-ai-provider. Add the same provider build to `make ts-test-examples`.
findings.v1reason: Confirmed. The branch adds `"@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider": "file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider"` to nextjs-memory-chat/package.json (git diff ec9fc65..HEAD), and lib/handlers.ts:12 imports createNamsProvider from it. The provider build step at ci-typescript.yml:127-128 runs only when `if: matrix.example == 'nams-ai-provider'`. The provider's dist/ is gitignored (.gitignore:5), and `git ls-files` shows no dist. Its package.json has `main`/`types`/`exports` pointing at ./dist, and its scripts have no `prepare` (only build/dev/typecheck/test/prepublishOnly), so installing the example never builds it. The nextjs-memory-chat leg therefore has no dist, and tsc/test/build fail. Makefile ts-test-examples (lines 835-848) builds only $(TS_DIR), so the local mirror fails the same way.
findings.v2reason:
I ran it and the finding holds. This branch adds `"@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider": "file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider"` to typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/package.json (shown by git diff ec9fc65..HEAD). typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/lib/handlers.ts:12 and lib/memory.ts:15 import from that package.

In .github/workflows/ci-typescript.yml, the step at lines 127-128 is the only one that builds the provider, and it runs only when `matrix.example == 'nams-ai-provider'`. The provider's main, types and exports all point at ./dist, which is gitignored. So after npm installs the example, node_modules/@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider is a symlink to a package that has no dist/.

To test this, I copied a clean HEAD export of typescript/ into the scratch dir and repeated the CI steps without building the provider. `tsc --noEmit` failed with TS2307 on the provider import in both files, and `npm test` failed to resolve the package. Then, as a control, I built the provider (`npm ci && npm run build`). After that, tsc passed and all 15 tests passed.

So the `Example (nextjs-memory-chat, Node 24)` CI leg fails, and so does `make ts-test-examples`. Makefile:835-848 builds only $(TS_DIR) and never builds packages/vercel-ai-provider.
