findings.title: 'Running an example' walkthrough for nextjs-memory-chat omits the provider build and fails
findings.detail: The index's run recipe uses nextjs-memory-chat as its worked example. It builds only the SDK (`cd typescript && npm ci && npm run build`), then runs `npm ci` and `npm run dev` in the example. The example now also needs typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider installed and built, and that package's dist/ is gitignored. A reader who follows the index gets a module-resolution failure for `@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider`. The example's own README (lines 118-138) has the extra steps, but the index does not mention them.
findings.evidence: typescript/examples/README.md:46-53: `cd typescript` / `npm ci` / `npm run build` / `cd examples/nextjs-memory-chat` / `npm ci` / `cp .env.example .env` / `npm run dev`. typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/README.md:130-138 also requires `cd packages/vercel-ai-provider`, `npm ci`, `npm run build`. The provider's package.json exports `./dist/index.js`, which is untracked (typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/.gitignore:5 `dist/`).
findings.fix: Add the vercel-ai-provider `npm ci && npm run build` step to the index snippet, or switch the worked example to one that depends only on the SDK and point to the nextjs README for its extra step.
findings.v1reason: Confirmed. The index snippet at README.md:46-53 builds only the SDK (`cd typescript; npm ci; npm run build`) and then runs `npm ci`/`npm run dev` in examples/nextjs-memory-chat. The example needs the provider's gitignored dist, which has no prepare script. Its own README (lines 130-138) adds the `cd packages/vercel-ai-provider; npm ci; npm run build` step and says 'npm does not build local file: dependencies on installation'. A reader following the index hits a module-resolution failure.
findings.v2reason:
The finding is real, and this branch caused it. At the merge-base (ec9fc65), typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/package.json depended only on "@neo4j-labs/agent-memory": "file:../..". At HEAD it also depends on "@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider": "file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider", and the branch rewrote the index's "Running an example" snippet (typescript/examples/README.md:46-53). The new snippet runs npm ci and npm run build only in typescript/. It never installs or builds packages/vercel-ai-provider.

Nothing else fills in that step:
- typescript/package.json has no "workspaces" field, so the root npm ci does not cover the provider.
- The provider's package.json has no prepare or postinstall script, only "prepublishOnly": "npm run build".
- The provider's exports point at ./dist/index.js, and dist/ is gitignored and not tracked (git ls-files packages/vercel-ai-provider/dist prints nothing).

npm installs a file: directory dependency as a symlink and does not build it. The example imports the provider at runtime in lib/handlers.ts:12 (`import { createNamsProvider } from "@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider"`), and handlers.ts is imported by every app/api/memory/* route. So in a fresh clone the example fails with module-not-found as soon as those routes compile.

The example's own README (nextjs-memory-chat/README.md:122-138) includes the provider `npm ci` and `npm run build` steps and says "npm does not build local `file:` dependencies on installation". CI does too (ci-typescript.yml:125-129, "Build vercel-ai-provider package ..."). Only the index omits them.

The index does say "Each example's own README has the full step-by-step", which gives an easy way out, but the snippet is presented as a complete recipe for this exact example. Major is the right severity; it could arguably be minor because of that pointer.
findings.reproduction:
1. Compared the old and new versions. git show ec9fc65:typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/package.json | grep nams gives no match, so the provider dependency was added on this branch. git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- typescript/examples/README.md shows the branch rewrote the run snippet: cd typescript, npm ci, npm run build, cd examples/nextjs-memory-chat, npm ci, npm run dev. There is no provider step.

2. Checked the provider package. packages/vercel-ai-provider/package.json has only these scripts: build, dev, typecheck, test, test:watch, prepublishOnly. There is no prepare script. Its exports point at ./dist/index.js, and .gitignore lists dist/.

3. Reproduced the install. Copied the provider's package.json, src, tsconfig.json and tsup.config.ts (no dist) to scratch/review/tsex2/prov. Created an app with the dependency "@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider": "file:../prov" and ran npm install --legacy-peer-deps. It printed "added 1 package", and node_modules/@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider is a symlink to ../../../prov that contains no dist. Running node -e "import('@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider')" failed with: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND Cannot find module '.../node_modules/@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider/dist/index.js'.

4. Checked where the example uses the provider. grep shows lib/handlers.ts:12 imports createNamsProvider from it, and app/api/memory/{context,trace,graph}/route.ts import from @/lib/handlers.

findings.title: README still says the model gets the rail's three tiers and the recent history, but the provider injects neither
findings.detail:
The chat route switched from `agentMemoryMiddleware` to `createNamsProvider`. The middleware called `shortTerm.getContext` and replayed reflections, observations and recent messages. The provider never calls getContext. It injects at most `maxMemories` (default 6) hits, interleaved from query-based `searchMessages`, `searchEntities`, graph expansion, `direct response` reasoning steps and cross-session search. Several unchanged or new README lines contradict this:
- Line 214-215 says the rail's `0 reflections · 1 observation · 6 recent messages` is 'exactly what the next model call will have prepended to it'. MemoryRail.tsx and the handleContext doc comment were updated to say the opposite.
- Lines 33-34 say 'the history the model sees comes back out of the graph'. In fact the model sees only search hits for the current question.
- Lines 28-32 present agentMemoryMiddleware as the choice 'if a conversation's own reflections, observations and recent messages were enough', which implies the provider supplies those and more.
- Line 25-26 lists 'reasoning history' as retrieved. The provider keeps only steps with `actionTaken === 'direct response'`, while this app records `generate_answer`, so its own trace is never retrieved.
The offline test cannot catch any of this. The msw `/conversations/:id/search` fake returns the conversation's last N messages whatever the query, so 'injects conversation history the request never sent' passes even though real retrieval depends on the query. The old observation-injection assertion ('avoids buses') was dropped.
findings.evidence: README.md:214-215: `the rail reads **0 reflections · 1 observation · 6 recent messages** — exactly what the next model call will have prepended to it;`. README.md:33-34: `the history the model sees comes back out of the graph.`. Provider retrieval, typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src/vercel-ai-provider-client.ts:369-412, uses searchMessages(query, {threshold: 0.4}), searchEntities, listSteps filtered by `s.actionTaken === 'direct response'` (:411) and searchPastConversations, with no getContext call. By contrast typescript/src/middleware/vercel-ai.ts:181-184 has `const ctx = await client.shortTerm.getContext(id); ... ctx.observations ... ctx.recentMessages`. lib/handlers.ts:155 records `actionTaken: "generate_answer"`. test/nams-server.ts `/conversations/:id/search` returns `conv.messages.slice(-(body.limit ?? 10))` regardless of query. The handleContext doc comment in lib/handlers.ts now says the route's retrieval 'draws on a wider set of sources than this endpoint shows'.
findings.fix: Rewrite README lines 25-36 and 214-215 to describe what the provider actually injects: search-ranked hits capped at maxMemories, with no replay of recent turns or observations. Either drop 'reasoning history' or record steps the provider retrieves. Consider making the fake search filter by query so the test reflects retrieval that depends on the query. If full conversational continuity is intended, keep agentMemoryMiddleware for history alongside the provider.
findings.v1reason: Confirmed. retrieveMemories (vercel-ai-provider-client.ts:352-412) uses searchMessages with a threshold, searchEntities, listSteps filtered to `actionTaken === 'direct response'`, and searchPastConversations (also 'direct response' only, :342). Nothing in the provider src calls getContext (grep finds none). The app records `actionTaken: "generate_answer"` (handlers.ts:155), so 'reasoning history' (README:26) is never retrieved for this app. README:214-215 ('exactly what the next model call will have prepended to it') was accurate under the old middleware and is now wrong; the branch's own MemoryRail.tsx:161-162 and the handlers.ts:177 comment now say retrieval is search-based over wider sources. The msw fake at test/nams-server.ts:202-205 returns `conv.messages.slice(-(limit))` whatever the query, and the 'avoids buses' observation assertion was removed in the diff.
findings.v2reason:
The finding holds. I traced the code path; I did not run the msw test. The branch moved the chat route from agentMemoryMiddleware to createNamsProvider (lib/handlers.ts:12 and :119). The provider's retrieveMemories (typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src/vercel-ai-provider-client.ts:352-412) never calls shortTerm.getContext. Grepping the provider src for getContext, recentMessages and observations finds nothing. What it retrieves:
- searchMessages(query, {threshold: RETRIEVAL.currentThreshold})
- searchEntities(query)
- listSteps, filtered to actionTaken === 'direct response' (:411)
- searchPastConversations
- expandEntityGraph

The results are interleaved and capped at min(maxMemories, RETRIEVAL.maxTotal). maxMemories defaults to 6 (vercel-ai-provider-middleware.ts:199).

Three README claims are wrong as a result:
- README.md:214-215, unchanged by the branch but now wrong, says the rail's '0 reflections · 1 observation · 6 recent messages' is 'exactly what the next model call will have prepended to it'. The branch's own MemoryRail.tsx:160-162 now says the provider 'searches messages, entities and graph relationships... to decide what to prepend'. The handleContext comment (handlers.ts:173-178) says the route's retrieval draws on a wider set of sources than the context endpoint.
- README.md:25-26 lists 'reasoning history' as retrieved. The app records actionTaken: "generate_answer" (handlers.ts:155) and the provider keeps only 'direct response' steps, so the app's own trace never reaches the prompt.
- README.md:28-32 contrasts the provider with the middleware that uses 'reflections, observations and recent messages'. This implies the provider is a superset, and it is not: it injects no observations and does not replay recent messages.

On the test: the msw fake at test/nams-server.ts:202-205 returns conv.messages.slice(-(limit)) whatever the query. The branch diff of routes.test.ts drops the 'avoids buses' observation assertion.

Major is the right severity: this is a wrong behaviour claim that a reader can act on, and it does not break a build.
findings.reproduction:
1. `sed -n 20,40p` and `sed -n 205,220p` on typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/README.md: lines 25-26, 28-32, 33-34 and 214-215 contain the quoted text. `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD` shows lines 22-32 are new on this branch. Lines 33-34 and 214-215 are unchanged but describe the old middleware.
2. `grep -rn "getContext\|recentMessages\|observations" typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src`: no matches.
3. `sed -n 330,420p vercel-ai-provider-client.ts`: retrieveMemories uses searchMessages with a threshold, searchEntities, listSteps filtered by `s.actionTaken === 'direct response'`, searchPastConversations and expandEntityGraph, then interleaves and caps the results.
4. `grep -n actionTaken lib/*.ts`: handlers.ts:155 has `actionTaken: "generate_answer"`.
5. `grep -rn maxMemories`: middleware.ts:199 has `config.maxMemories ?? 6`.
6. test/nams-server.ts:202-205: the search handler returns `conv.messages.slice(-(body.limit ?? 10))` whatever the query.
7. `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- test/routes.test.ts | grep buses`: `-    expect(prompt).toContain("avoids buses");` (removed).
8. MemoryRail.tsx:160-162 and handlers.ts:173-178 (the new comments) contradict README.md:214-215.

findings.title: README says the suite checks the abort and error settle paths, but no test covers either
findings.detail: The branch adds 'On abort it settles without storing a partial response; on error it settles and logs the failure. The suite checks this lifecycle.' It also rewrites the test-assertion bullet to say the waitUntil promise 'settles on completion, abort or error'. The handler does wire `onAbort: () => settle()` and `onError`. However, test/edge.test.ts has no test that aborts or cancels a stream or makes the model or NAMS error mid-stream; the only waitUntil tests drain the stream normally. A regression in either path would pass the suite.
findings.evidence: README.md:39-40: `On abort it settles without storing a partial response; on error it settles and logs the failure. The suite checks this lifecycle.` and README.md:268-269: `the single `waitUntil` promise owns the writes and settles on completion, abort or error;`. `grep -n -i "abort\|cancel" test/edge.test.ts` returns nothing. Test titles cover streaming/persist, deferring to waitUntil, reasoning step, replay, auth, Server-Timing, validation, context, graph, env and node-imports, but not abort or error.
findings.fix: Add tests that cancel the response body mid-stream and that make the mock model or NAMS fail, then assert that the deferred promise settles and nothing partial is stored. Otherwise remove 'The suite checks this lifecycle' and the 'abort or error' wording from the assertions list.
findings.v1reason: Confirmed. The branch-modified README.md:39-40 says 'The suite checks this lifecycle', and :268-269 says the promise 'settles on completion, abort or error'. test/edge.test.ts has no abort, cancel or mid-stream error test: the test titles are streams/persist, defers to waitUntil, reasoning step, replay, auth, Server-Timing, validation, context, graph, env, 404, missing secret and node imports. The handler does wire onAbort/onError (handlers.ts:160-161), but nothing tests them.

findings.title: The streaming-persistence section misdescribes both the Cloudflare pattern and `persistInteractions: false`
findings.detail: There are two problems in this section. First, it tells readers who want 'explicitly awaited writes with error handling the client can see' to follow the Cloudflare example. That example hands the write to `ctx.waitUntil` after the response is returned and only calls `console.error` on failure, so the client cannot see the error. Second, it says to pass `persistInteractions: false` 'so the response is not stored twice'. In the provider that flag turns off persistence of both the user turn and the assistant turn. The Cloudflare pattern it points to uses the SDK middleware's `persistResponses: false`, which turns off only the assistant write. A reader who follows this advice and writes only the response would silently stop storing user turns.
findings.evidence: nextjs-memory-chat/README.md:111-116: `For application-owned, explicitly awaited writes with error handling the client can see, follow the [Cloudflare lifecycle example]... pass `persistInteractions: false` to `createNamsProvider` when adding that explicit write, so the response is not stored twice.`. cloudflare-agents-edge/src/handlers.ts:165-168: `deps.waitUntil(persisted.catch((error: unknown) => { console.error("memory write failed", error); }))`, which runs after `return result.toTextStreamResponse(...)`. vercel-ai-provider-middleware.ts:116-125: `async function persistTurn(...) { if (!persist) return; ... addMessage(convId, 'user', userText) ... addMessage(convId, 'assistant', assistantText)`.
findings.fix: Drop 'the client can see' (say 'observable by the server/runtime'). State that `persistInteractions: false` disables both user-turn and assistant-turn writes, so the explicit write must store both.
findings.v1reason: Confirmed. The Cloudflare handler passes the promise to deps.waitUntil and only calls console.error on failure after returning the stream response (cloudflare handlers.ts:165-175), so the client cannot see a write error. In the provider, `persist = config.persistInteractions ?? true` (middleware.ts:200) gates persistTurn, which writes both the user and assistant messages (:116-125). The Cloudflare example instead uses the SDK middleware's `persistResponses: false` (:129), which only skips the assistant write. Following the README advice could silently drop user turns.

findings.title: 'Build the shared packages' section makes two wrong claims: a shared tsconfig and that everything runs on current source
findings.detail: The new section has two inaccuracies. It says the example's 'shared `../tsconfig.base.json`' requires the repository layout, but this example's tsconfig.json does not extend it; it is standalone. It also says the `file:` links make the example 'always run against current source'. The chat route's provider is a symlink to typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider, so at runtime and type-check time it resolves `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory` from that package's own node_modules. That is the npm-published 0.4.0 installed as its devDependency, not the in-tree 0.5.0 SDK. The provider's MemoryClient/RestTransport, which is the half the new tests exercise, is therefore not current source.
findings.evidence: README.md:120-127: `Its `file:../..` and `file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider` dependencies and shared `../tsconfig.base.json` require the repository layout ... this example pins both to the packages in this repository via `file:` links, so it always runs against current source.` typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/tsconfig.json has no `extends`. Resolving from the provider's realpath: `node -e ... createRequire(realpath(node_modules/@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider/package.json)).resolve(...)` gives `.../typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/node_modules/@neo4j-labs/agent-memory/...`, and that package.json has `"version": "0.4.0"`. The provider devDependencies include `"@neo4j-labs/agent-memory": "^0.4.0"`.
findings.fix: Remove the tsconfig.base.json clause for this example. Qualify the 'current source' claim by noting that the provider resolves its own devDependency copy of the SDK, or make the provider link resolve the in-tree SDK (for example, install the provider with install-links or dedupe).
findings.v1reason: Confirmed. nextjs-memory-chat/tsconfig.json has no `extends` (grep finds none), though examples/tsconfig.base.json exists. The provider's package.json devDependency is `"@neo4j-labs/agent-memory": "^0.4.0"` and the installed copy is version 0.4.0. Node resolution from the provider's realpath lands in typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/node_modules/@neo4j-labs/agent-memory. tsup keeps @neo4j-labs/agent-memory external, and the provider builds its own `new MemoryClient` (client.ts:68), so the provider path does not run against in-tree 0.5.0 source.

findings.title: make example-no-llm / example-eval-harness / examples now crash with KeyError on a clean checkout
findings.detail: Both scripts dropped their local defaults and now read NEO4J_URI and NEO4J_USERNAME with os.environ[...]. The Makefile was not updated. When NEO4J_URI is unset (no examples/.env), run_example starts the Docker Neo4j and passes only NEO4J_PASSWORD=test-password, so the script raises KeyError: 'NEO4J_URI' after Docker has started. Both targets are in RUNNABLE_EXAMPLES, so `make examples`, which CLAUDE.md calls key-free and auto-starting Docker, also fails. The same applies to examples/eval-harness/main.py:125-126.
findings.evidence: Makefile:573-576 `if [ -z "$$NEO4J_URI" ]; then ... $(MAKE) neo4j-start neo4j-wait-quiet; NEO4J_PASSWORD=test-password uv run python $(1) $(2);`. examples/no_llm/main.py:126-127 `uri=os.environ["NEO4J_URI"], username=os.environ["NEO4J_USERNAME"]`. examples/eval-harness/main.py:125-126 has the same lines. Makefile:694 and :699 list example-no-llm and example-eval-harness in RUNNABLE_EXAMPLES. Simulation: `env -u NEO4J_URI -u NEO4J_USERNAME NEO4J_PASSWORD=test-password uv run python -c '...load_env(); build_settings()'` prints `examples/no_llm/main.py KeyError 'NEO4J_URI'` and `examples/eval-harness/main.py KeyError 'NEO4J_URI'` (no examples/.env present).
findings.fix: In run_example's Docker branch, export NEO4J_URI=bolt://localhost:7687 and NEO4J_USERNAME=neo4j alongside NEO4J_PASSWORD. Alternatively, drop the Docker auto-start from these targets and fail early with a message pointing at examples/AURA_SETUP.md, then update CLAUDE.md to match.
findings.v1reason: The Makefile run_example Docker branch (Makefile ~574-576) exports only NEO4J_PASSWORD=test-password. The branch changed examples/no_llm/main.py:126-127 and examples/eval-harness/main.py:125-126 from os.getenv defaults to os.environ["NEO4J_URI"] / os.environ["NEO4J_USERNAME"]. I reproduced it: with `env -u NEO4J_URI -u NEO4J_USERNAME NEO4J_PASSWORD=test-password`, loading each module and calling load_env() and then build_settings() gives `KeyError 'NEO4J_URI'` for both, because examples/.env is absent. Both targets are in RUNNABLE_EXAMPLES, so `make examples` fails. No workflow runs these targets, so this is major, not blocker.
findings.v2reason: The defect is real, and this branch caused it. At ec9fc65, both examples fell back to local defaults: `os.getenv("NEO4J_URI", "bolt://localhost:7687")` and `os.getenv("NEO4J_USERNAME", "neo4j")`. At HEAD, examples/no_llm/main.py:126-127 and examples/eval-harness/main.py:125-126 read `os.environ["NEO4J_URI"]` and `os.environ["NEO4J_USERNAME"]` with no default. The branch did not change the Makefile's `run_example` Docker branch (Makefile:572-576). When NEO4J_URI is unset after it sources examples/.env, that branch starts Docker Neo4j and runs `NEO4J_PASSWORD=test-password uv run python $(1)`. It exports only the password, so both scripts raise KeyError: 'NEO4J_URI' after Docker has started. Both scripts' own `load_env()` only reads examples/.env, and that file is absent on a clean checkout (only examples/.env.example is tracked), so nothing supplies the URI. `example-no-llm` (Makefile:618-620) and `example-eval-harness` (Makefile:643-645) both call run_example and are listed in RUNNABLE_EXAMPLES (Makefile:694 and 699), so the `examples` target, described as key-free with Docker auto-start, also fails. No CI workflow runs these make targets, so major rather than blocker is the right severity. Suggested fix: export `NEO4J_URI=bolt://localhost:7687` and `NEO4J_USERNAME=neo4j` alongside `NEO4J_PASSWORD` in the Docker branch of run_example.
findings.reproduction:
From the repo root (`ls examples/.env` reports "No such file or directory"):

1) Run eval-harness end to end with the environment the Makefile's Docker branch provides:
   `env -u NEO4J_URI -u NEO4J_USERNAME -u NEO4J_DATABASE -u MEMORY_API_KEY NEO4J_PASSWORD=test-password uv run python examples/eval-harness/main.py`
   Output: a traceback ending `File ".../examples/eval-harness/main.py", line 125, in build_settings: uri=os.environ["NEO4J_URI"]` and `KeyError: 'NEO4J_URI'`.

2) Run no_llm/main.py the same way. It exits earlier in this venv because the local extraction stack is missing: "Local extraction stack is incomplete ... Missing: spaCy model, GLiNER". main() calls load_env() and then check_local_stack() before build_settings() (lines 148-151). So I ran the next step directly:
   `env -u NEO4J_URI -u NEO4J_USERNAME -u MEMORY_API_KEY NEO4J_PASSWORD=test-password uv run python -c 'import importlib.util; spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m","examples/no_llm/main.py"); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m); m.load_env(); m.build_settings()'`
   Output: `KeyError 'NEO4J_URI'`. A user who has the extraction stack installed reaches this KeyError.

3) `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- examples/no_llm/main.py examples/eval-harness/main.py` shows `-uri=os.getenv("NEO4J_URI", "bolt://localhost:7687")` and `-username=os.getenv("NEO4J_USERNAME", "neo4j")` replaced by `+uri=os.environ["NEO4J_URI"]` and `+username=os.environ["NEO4J_USERNAME"]` in both files. The same diff for the Makefile shows no change to the run_example macro (Makefile:561-576), which still passes only `NEO4J_PASSWORD=test-password` in the Docker branch.

I did not run `make example-no-llm` with Docker: the project memory notes that ports are occupied here and that make neo4j-start fails. The KeyError happens before any connection attempt, so Docker availability does not change the outcome.

findings.detail: The new Aura step says the backend and loading scripts read NEO4J_DATABASE. The loading scripts do (scripts/_common.py). The backend Settings class has no database field, and the memory client builds Neo4jConfig without one, so the backend always uses the driver default database.

findings.v1reason: examples/lennys-memory/README.md:130 says the backend reads NEO4J_DATABASE. backend/src/config.py:19-21 defines only neo4j_uri, neo4j_username and neo4j_password. backend/src/memory/client.py:96-100 builds Neo4jConfig without a database. findings.title: Keyboard users can't reach the new tutorial copy button: its container stays display:none unless hovered
findings.detail: tutorial-code.js swaps the upstream span for a native <button> inside `.code-inset`, and the CSS adds a :focus-visible outline to it. But the shared UI hides `.doc .listingblock .code-inset` with display:none and shows it only on `.listingblock:hover`. A display:none element is not focusable, so the button never gets keyboard focus and the focus-visible rule never applies. The claim in MAINTAINING.md ("make existing copy actions native buttons ... keyboard-focusable, with visible focus") is false for the button. Only the <pre> regions became reachable.
findings.evidence: Built site (antora --to-dir scratch), shared UI site.css: `.doc .listingblock .code-inset{display:none}` and `.doc .listingblock:hover .code-inset{display:block}`. Headless Chromium on tutorials/first-agent-memory.html: button computed display inline-block but parent `DIV.code-inset:none`, bounding rect 0x0. With the first <pre> focused, code-inset display is `none`. Pressing Tab moves focus to the next `PRE ... code block 2 source` and skips the button. Playwright click fails with 'Element is not visible' until the listing is hovered. docs/ui/css/tutorial-code.css:2 `body.code-nocollapse .doc .listingblock .code-inset button.btn-copy:focus-visible` has no effect. docs/MAINTAINING.md:107 claims the assets make copy actions keyboard-focusable.
findings.fix: In tutorial-code.css, add `body.code-nocollapse .doc .listingblock:focus-within .code-inset { display: block; }`. Then check with Tab that focus moves from each <pre> to its copy button.
findings.v1reason: The built shared UI CSS (docs/build/site/_/css/site.css) contains `.doc .listingblock .code-inset{display:none}` and `.doc .listingblock:hover .code-inset{display:block}`. Neither the shared CSS nor docs/ui has a focus-within or code-nocollapse override. docs/ui/css/tutorial-code.css:2 adds only a :focus-visible outline, and tutorial-code.js puts the new <button> inside the hidden .code-inset. A button whose ancestor is display:none cannot take focus, so keyboard users can't reach it. That makes MAINTAINING.md:107 ('make existing copy actions native buttons ... keyboard-focusable, with visible focus') false. I checked the CSS cascade but did not re-run a browser.
findings.v2reason:
I ran the built site in headless Chromium and the defect is real. The build is current: docs/build/site/_/css/tutorial-code.css and _/js/tutorial-code.js are byte-identical to docs/ui at HEAD.

On tutorials/first-agent-memory.html, tutorial-code.js does replace each span with a native <button class="btn btn-copy">; the page has 17 of them. Each one sits inside `.code-inset`, which the shared UI hides with `.doc .listingblock .code-inset{display:none}` and shows only on `.listingblock:hover`. The built site.css has no code-nocollapse or focus-within override.

Because of that, the button's parent computes to display:none and the button's bounding rect is 0x0. Even `btn.focus()` fails. Tabbing forward from the first <pre> goes pre, then the next pre, then summaries, and skips every copy button. In 300 Tab presses across the page, no copy button received focus. That makes docs/MAINTAINING.md:107 ("They make existing copy actions native buttons and source regions keyboard-focusable, with visible focus") false for the copy buttons. It also means the :focus-visible rule at docs/ui/css/tutorial-code.css:2 can never apply. Only the <pre> regions became reachable.

A correction to the suggested fix: `.listingblock:focus-within .code-inset{display:block}` is not enough. The button comes before the <pre> in the DOM (div.code-header > div.code-inset > button, then pre). With the fix injected, forward Tab still hit the button 0 times in 300 presses. Only Shift+Tab from a focused <pre> reaches it. A working fix has to keep `.code-inset` in the layout on code-nocollapse pages, for example display:block with opacity 0 until `.listingblock:hover` or `:focus-within`, or simply always visible. That way the button is in the tab order before its listing has focus. Major severity stands: this is a false accessibility claim, and keyboard users cannot reach the copy action at all.
findings.reproduction:
Scripts are under scratchpad/review/ (kb.cjs, kb2.cjs, kb3.cjs), run with the Playwright copy in docs/diagrams/node_modules, from docs/diagrams. 1. `diff docs/ui/css/tutorial-code.css docs/build/site/_/css/tutorial-code.css && diff docs/ui/js/tutorial-code.js docs/build/site/_/js/tutorial-code.js` gives `same`, so the built site matches HEAD. 2. `grep -o '[^}]*code-inset[^}]*}' docs/build/site/_/css/site.css` gives `.doc .listingblock .code-inset{display:none}` and `.doc .listingblock:hover .code-inset{display:block}`. The code-nocollapse and focus-within greps return nothing relevant. 3. kb.cjs on file://.../docs/build/site/agent-memory/tutorials/first-agent-memory.html gives `{"tag":"BUTTON","disp":"inline-block","parentDisp":"none","rect":[0,0],"nButtons":17}`. The Tab sequence from the first pre is `["PRE code block 2 source","CODE language-bash hljs","SUMMARY title","SUMMARY title","PRE core_memory_settings.py source","PRE first_agent_memory.py source"]`, and `programmatic focus succeeds: false`. 4. kb2.cjs gives `HEAD copy-button focus hits in 300 tabs: 0`. With the suggested `.listingblock:focus-within .code-inset{display:block}` injected, it also gives 0. 5. kb3.cjs shows the DOM order `
`. With the fix injected, Shift+Tab from the pre gives `BUTTON Copy code: code block 1`, which confirms the suggested fix covers only reverse tabbing.

findings.title: make docs-lint skips all rendered-layout checks after the documented setup; the skip hint names the wrong install
findings.detail: The docs-lint comment says the Playwright checks for inline TOC, undersized images, mobile overflow, heading case and scaffolding headings "fail this target". The defect is real, and this branch caused it: scripts/export_diagrams.mjs does not exist at ec9fc65 (`git show` exit 128). findings.title: Image alt-quoting check flags valid named attributes whose quoted value has a comma
findings.detail: The source check splits image attributes with csv.reader. The csv module honours a quote only at the start of a field, so a valid named attribute such as `title="One, two"` splits into `title="One` and ` two"`. The second fragment has no '=' and is not numeric, so the check reports 'quote comma-containing image alt text' even though the alt text is quoted. No current page trips this, but the error would send an author to the wrong fix.
findings.evidence: Fixture page `image::diagrams/a.svg["Alt text",title="One, two"]` → source_report errors: ['index.adoc: quote comma-containing image alt text: image::diagrams/a.svg["Alt text",title="One, two"]'].
findings.fix: Tokenize the attribute list the way AsciiDoc does: treat quotes after `name=` as quoting the value. Alternatively, check only that the first positional field is quoted when it contains a comma.
findings.v1reason: scripts/check_docs.py:56-63 splits image attributes with csv.reader. `csv.reader(['"Alt text",title="One, two"'])` returns ['Alt text', 'title="One', ' two"']. The fragment ' two"' has no '=' and is not numeric, so the check reports 'quote comma-containing image alt text' even though the alt text is quoted. No current page triggers this.

findings.title: MCPB manifest fails the official validator; Quick Start's extension env setup cannot work
findings.detail: This branch rewrote the `server` block and made four variables required (NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD, OPENAI_API_KEY). The README's Quick Start now tells readers to install the extension and configure those five variables "in the extension environment". The manifest is not a valid MCPB manifest, though. It has no `manifest_version`, `author` and `repository` are strings, and `server` uses invented keys (`command`/`args`/`env_required`/`env_optional`) in place of `type`/`entry_point`/`mcp_config`. There is no `user_config`, which is how an MCPB extension collects values from the user and maps them into `mcp_config.env` through `${user_config.*}`. So `mcpb pack`/`validate` rejects the file, and even a fixed one would give Claude Desktop no field for entering the Neo4j or OpenAI credentials. The stale `"version": "0.1.0"` (the package is 0.6.0) is a smaller symptom of the same drift.
findings.evidence:
deploy/mcpb/manifest.json:16-35 `"server": { "command": "uvx", "args": [...], "env_required": ["NEO4J_URI","NEO4J_USER","NEO4J_PASSWORD","OPENAI_API_KEY"], "env_optional": [...] }`; deploy/mcpb/README.md:22-23 `1. Install from Claude Desktop extension directory` / `2. Configure NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD, NEO4J_DATABASE and OPENAI_API_KEY in the extension environment.`
Command: `npx -y @anthropic-ai/mcpb@2.1.2 validate manifest.json` -> `Unrecognized or unsupported manifest version`. With `"manifest_version": "0.3"` added -> `author: Expected object, received string; repository: Expected object, received string; server.type: Required; server.entry_point: Required; server.mcp_config: Required; server: Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'command', 'args', 'env_required', 'env_optional'; Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'capabilities', 'tool_profiles'`.
findings.fix: Rewrite the manifest to the MCPB schema: add `manifest_version`, make `author` an object (`{"name": "Neo4j Labs"}`) and `repository` an object (`{"type":"git","url":...}`), and use `server: {type: "uv" or "binary", entry_point, mcp_config: {command: "uvx", args: [...], env: {NEO4J_URI: "${user_config.neo4j_uri}", ...}}}`. Declare `user_config` entries for uri/user/password (sensitive)/database/openai_api_key (sensitive), and set `version` to the package version. Check the result with `mcpb validate`. Otherwise, drop the "install from extension directory" step and keep only the claude_desktop_config.json path.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced: `npx -y @anthropic-ai/mcpb@2.1.2 validate` on deploy/mcpb/manifest.json prints 'Unrecognized or unsupported manifest version'. With manifest_version 0.3 added, it reports author/repository must be objects, server.type/entry_point/mcp_config are required, and 'command','args','env_required','env_optional','capabilities','tool_profiles' are unrecognized keys. There is no user_config, so Desktop has no field for entering credentials. The invalid shape is pre-existing: the ec9fc65 manifest fails the same way. The branch did edit the server block (lines 16-35) and rewrote README Quick Start step 2 (line 23) into an instruction that cannot work with this manifest, and version stays 0.1.0. Rated minor, not major: the root defect predates the branch, and the working claude_desktop_config.json developer path is documented right below.

findings.title: Documented endpoint `/mcp/` is a 307 redirect to an absolute http:// `/mcp` URL
findings.detail: The README (and Dockerfile comment) calls the endpoint `/mcp/`, and every verification command uses that URL. FastMCP 4 actually serves `/mcp` (`streamable_http_path = "/mcp"`). A POST to `/mcp/` gets a 307 whose Location is an absolute `http://<Host>/mcp`, even when `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` is sent, because uvicorn does not trust forwarded headers from non-local peers. It works locally because the client follows the redirect. On Cloud Run, TLS ends before the container, so a request to `https://<svc>.run.app/mcp/` is redirected to plain `http://<svc>.run.app/mcp`. Through `gcloud run services proxy`, the redirect can also point the client away from the authenticating proxy. I could not observe the cloud behaviour. The redirect itself is verified. Pointing clients at `/mcp` avoids the extra hop entirely.
findings.evidence: deploy/cloudrun/README.md:15 `The container uses Streamable HTTP at /mcp/`; :45 `fastmcp list http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp/`; :117 `fastmcp list http://127.0.0.1:8081/mcp/`; :145 `Streamable HTTP /mcp/`. Source: .venv/.../fastmcp/settings.py:201 `streamable_http_path: str = "/mcp"` (same default in the image's fastmcp 4.0.9). The built image logs `Starting MCP server ... on http://0.0.0.0:8080/mcp` and `"POST /mcp/ HTTP/1.1" 307 Temporary Redirect` then `"POST /mcp HTTP/1.1" 200 OK`. `curl -i -X POST -H 'Host: neo4j-memory-mcp-abc.a.run.app' -H 'X-Forwarded-Proto: https' http://127.0.0.1:18089/mcp/` -> `HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect` / `location: http://neo4j-memory-mcp-abc.a.run.app/mcp`.
findings.fix: Document the endpoint as `/mcp` (no trailing slash) in the README, the Dockerfile comment and the verification commands. Alternatively, start uvicorn with proxy headers trusted (forwarded_allow_ips) so redirects keep https. Either way, have the deployed-caller guidance use the exact path.
findings.v1reason: FastMCP's default is streamable_http_path='/mcp' (.venv fastmcp/settings.py:201), and src/neo4j_agent_memory/mcp/server.py:281/408 calls run_async(transport='http') without overriding the path. A Starlette TestClient POST to '/mcp/' on FastMCP().http_app() with X-Forwarded-Proto: https returns '307 http://svc.a.run.app/mcp', so the documented '/mcp/' is a redirect, not the endpoint. '/mcp/' was already in the ec9fc65 README, the Dockerfile comment and the CLI help (cli/main.py:757). The branch repeats it in new verification commands (README:45, :117, :145, :149). The downstream Cloud Run https->http consequence was not observed. Local and proxy use still works because clients follow the redirect.

findings.title: Test fakes vertexai availability but never asserts the Dockerfile installs an extra providing it
findings.detail: `test_cloudrun_command_builds_vertex_provider_without_implicit_llm` patches `factory._has` so `vertex_ai` always looks installed. The comment justifies this with "The Dockerfile installs [google]", but nothing checks that claim. If the `google` extra were dropped from `pip install -e ".[mcp,google]"`, `from_provider('vertex_ai/...')` inside the image would fall through to LiteLLM (not installed) and raise ImportError at server start. The test would still pass. It also never checks that secret names and the runtime service account agree between cloudbuild.yaml, service.yaml and the README.
findings.evidence: tests/docs/test_cloudrun_assets.py:91-96 `# The Dockerfile installs [google]. Emulate availability ... monkeypatch.setattr(factory, "_has", lambda package: package == "vertex_ai" or package_available(package))`; deploy/cloudrun/Dockerfile:32 `RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -e ".[mcp,google]"`; src/neo4j_agent_memory/llm/factory.py:244-255 (vertex_ai native path requires `_has("vertex_ai")`, else LiteLLM, else `raise ImportError`). In the built image: `vertexai True litellm False openai False`.
findings.fix: Parse the `RUN pip install` extras from the Dockerfile and assert they include `google` or `vertex-ai`, and that the pyproject extra lists google-cloud-aiplatform. Optionally, assert that the secret names in cloudbuild `--set-secrets` match the service.yaml `secretKeyRef` names and the README's secret loop.
findings.v1reason: tests/docs/test_cloudrun_assets.py:91-96 patches factory._has so 'vertex_ai' is always available. No test parses the Dockerfile's `RUN pip install -e ".[mcp,google]"` (Dockerfile:32) extras. The only Dockerfile parse before the install line checks COPY sources for the readme (lines 19-26). factory.py:244-255 routes vertex_ai to the native provider only when _has('vertex_ai') is true, otherwise LiteLLM, otherwise ImportError. So dropping 'google' from the image would break startup and the test would still pass. Secret-name agreement between cloudbuild.yaml:79 and service.yaml:52-64 is also untested, though the names currently match.

findings.title: 'stops before reasoning' assertion is vacuous: nams_quickstart.exercise never calls reasoning
findings.detail: test_hosted_extraction_timeout_stops_before_reasoning ends with `assert not client.reasoning.sessions`, and test_hosted_exercise_reuses_server_ids_and_checks_reads makes the same check (`set(short_term.ids + reasoning.sessions)` plus `assert not reasoning.sessions`, lines 196-197). The program under test, docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_quickstart.py, never uses `client.reasoning`. Its `exercise()` calls only short_term.create_conversation, short_term.bulk_add_messages, verify_messages, long_term.wait_for_extraction and long_term.search_entities. So the 'before reasoning' assertion and the reasoning part of the 'reuses server ids' check always pass. On timeout, the test does not check what should hold. It never asserts that `state.data['seed_verified']` stays unset, although exercise() sets it at line 50 after the wait. It also never asserts that the retained state still records the conversation and messages for cleanup. A regression that set seed_verified before the wait would still pass.
findings.evidence: tests/docs/test_hosted_tutorial_contracts.py:212-214: `with pytest.raises(TimeoutError):\n        asyncio.run(nams.exercise(client, make_state(tmp_path, "nams")))\n    assert not client.reasoning.sessions`; lines 196-197: `assert set(short_term.ids + reasoning.sessions) == {"server-conversation-id"}` / `assert not reasoning.sessions`. Source of truth: `grep -n reasoning docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_quickstart.py docs/modules/ROOT/examples/hosted_tutorial_state.py` prints nothing (exit 1). docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_quickstart.py:42-50 shows wait_for_extraction, then the TimeoutError raise, then `state.data["seed_verified"] = True`.
findings.fix: Drop the Reasoning stub and the reasoning assertions from the two nams tests. In the timeout test, keep the state object and assert `'seed_verified' not in state.data` (or that it is falsy). Also assert that the conversation and both messages are still recorded in `state.data['resources']` so cleanup can find them.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced. `grep -n reasoning` over docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_quickstart.py and hosted_tutorial_state.py prints nothing (exit 1). exercise() (nams_quickstart.py:16-53) calls only short_term.create_conversation, short_term.bulk_add_messages, verify_messages, long_term.wait_for_extraction and long_term.search_entities. So `assert not client.reasoning.sessions` (tests/docs/test_hosted_tutorial_contracts.py:214) and the reasoning parts of lines 196-197 always pass, and the test name 'stops_before_reasoning' describes a step the program does not have. The timeout test passes a fresh make_state(...) inline and throws it away, so it never checks that seed_verified (set at nams_quickstart.py:50, after the wait at :42-46) stays unset, or that the conversation and messages stay recorded for cleanup. pytest.raises(TimeoutError) is still a real check, so the test is only partly vacuous. Minor.

findings.title: Skills seed runs only against permissive fakes; its SDK calls are never checked against real NAMS signatures
findings.detail: The Bolt tutorials get their SDK calls checked against the real API: test_core_python_tutorials.py:79-84 binds every `client.<layer>.<method>(...)` call to the real signature, and client_double() uses create_autospec. The nams hosted lesson has a real-SDK wire test in test_hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py:303. The Skills seed has neither. test_skills_fixture_is_one_procedure_and_records_real_conversation and test_partial_seed_keeps_real_step_id_and_pending_tool_call replace client.short_term and client.reasoning with hand-written fakes that accept any keyword arguments. If NamsReasoningMemory.start_trace, add_step or record_tool_call renamed or dropped a parameter the seed passes, every in-scope test would still pass, and readers of the skills tutorial would get a TypeError at seed time. I bound the current calls against the real classes and they all bind, so this is a coverage gap and not a present bug.
findings.evidence: tests/docs/test_hosted_tutorial_contracts.py:158 `async def add_step(self, trace_id, **kwargs):` and :170 `async def complete_trace(self, trace_id, **kwargs):`; tests/docs/test_skills_tutorial.py:172-178 `async def trace(**_)`, `async def step(*_, **__)`, `async def call(*_, **__)`. By contrast, tests/docs/test_core_python_tutorials.py:82 does `inspect.signature(method).bind(...)`. Scratch check (scratchpad/review/bind_nams.py) binds each client.short_term/long_term/reasoning call in skills_quickstart.py to NamsShortTermMemory, NamsLongTermMemory and the NAMS reasoning class. Output: `ok skills_quickstart 75 reasoning start_trace`, `ok ... 92 reasoning add_step`, `ok ... 98 reasoning record_tool_call`, `ok ... 103 reasoning complete_trace`, `ok ... 107 reasoning get_session_traces`. No test in tests/ performs this binding.
findings.fix: Add a parametrized test like test_tutorial_calls_bind_to_current_python_api for the hosted programs (nams_quickstart, skills_quickstart, hosted_tutorial_state), binding against NamsShortTermMemory, NamsLongTermMemory and the NAMS reasoning class. Or build the fakes with create_autospec(..., instance=True) on those classes.
findings.v1reason: The gap is real. test_core_python_tutorials.py:52-84 (test_tutorial_calls_bind_to_current_python_api) walks only NAMES + RECIPE_NAMES (the Bolt programs first_agent_memory, conversation_memory, knowledge_graph, core_memory_recipes, extraction_recipes) and binds against the Bolt classes. skills_quickstart is not in that list. The skills seed tests use hand-written fakes: test_hosted_tutorial_contracts.py:149-175 has `add_step(self, trace_id, **kwargs)` and `complete_trace(self, trace_id, **kwargs)`, and test_skills_tutorial.py:172-178 has `trace(**_)`, `step(*_, **__)` and `call(*_, **__)`. test_hosted_tutorial_lifecycle.py and test_hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py do not bind the skills reasoning calls to NamsReasoningMemory either; the cleanup file's real-SDK wire test at :303 covers the nams program. I bound the current calls myself (start_trace(session_id=, task=), add_step(id, action=, observation=), record_tool_call(id, tool_name=, arguments=, result=), complete_trace(id, outcome=, success=), get_session_traces(id)) against src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/reasoning.py:158 NamsReasoningMemory, and all of them bind. Nothing is broken today, so this is hardening rather than a defect: nit.

findings.title: Three new docs test files fail the CI ruff format check, so the Python lint job goes red
findings.detail: The CI lint job runs `uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples`. Three test modules added on this branch are not ruff-formatted, so that step exits 1 on every PR that triggers Python CI. `make format-check` fails the same way, because it uses the same RUFF_PATHS. The formatter wants to wrap lines longer than 100 characters, for example test_nav_labels.py:130, 155 and 169, test_docs_checker.py:122, and the one-line set literals at test_rendered_site.py:24-43.
findings.evidence: Command: `uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples; echo exit=$?` printed `Would reformat: tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py`, `Would reformat: tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py`, `Would reformat: tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py`, `3 files would be reformatted, 562 files already formatted`, `exit=1` (ruff 0.14.14 from uv.lock). CI step: .github/workflows/ci-python.yml:80 `run: uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples`. All three files are new on the branch (`git show ec9fc65:tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py` fails).
findings.fix: Run `uv run ruff format tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py` and commit.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced. `uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples` printed 'Would reformat' for tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py, test_nav_labels.py and test_rendered_site.py ('3 files would be reformatted') and exited 1. CI runs this exact command at .github/workflows/ci-python.yml:80. All three files are new on the branch: `git show ec9fc65:` fails for each of them.
findings.v2reason:
I ran the same format check that CI runs, and it fails on three files this branch adds. At .github/workflows/ci-python.yml:80, the lint job runs `uv run ruff format --check src tests examples docs/modules/ROOT/examples`. With ruff 0.14.14 (the version uv resolves in this project), that command exits 1 and reports tests/docs/test_docs_checker.py, tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py and tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py as "Would reformat".

- **New on this branch:** `git show ec9fc65:<path>` fails for all three files, so none of them exists on main.

A failing CI job counts as blocker under the rubric, so the blocker severity stands. The fix is to run `uv run ruff format` on the three files and commit the result.

findings.title: Rendered-site checks skip silently: the 'make docs-install' named in the skip message never installs Playwright
findings.detail: All seven rendered checks depend on the render_report fixture. That fixture skips when docs/diagrams/node_modules/playwright is missing, and its message tells the reader to run `make docs-install`. MAINTAINING.md:45 says the same. But `make docs-install` only runs `cd docs && npm ci`. Playwright is declared in the separate package docs/diagrams/package.json, and docs/package.json does not depend on it. On a fresh checkout, `make docs-render-check` and `make docs-lint` (which depends on it) therefore collect seven tests, skip all of them, and exit 0. The Makefile comment says these defects 'fail this target, not just a separate one', yet the gate passes without checking anything, and the documented remedy does not fix it. CI never runs this module either: the docs-tests job builds into a temporary directory, so docs/build/site does not exist there.
findings.evidence: tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py:64-65: `if not (project_root / "docs/diagrams/node_modules/playwright").is_dir(): pytest.skip("Playwright not installed under docs/diagrams; run `make docs-install`")`. Makefile:451-454: `docs-install:` ... `cd docs && npm ci`. docs/diagrams/package.json: `"playwright": "1.62.1"` (a separate package). docs/package.json devDependencies contain only @antora/cli, @antora/site-generator and http-server. docs/MAINTAINING.md:44-45: 'when Playwright is not installed under `docs/diagrams` (`make docs-install`)'. Makefile:469-472 comment: '...Title Case headings and scaffolding headings fail this target'.
findings.fix: Choose one of two fixes. Either make docs-install also run `npm ci --prefix docs/diagrams && (cd docs/diagrams && npx playwright install chromium)`, or have docs-render-check fail instead of skip, for example by setting an env var that the fixture turns into `pytest.fail` rather than `pytest.skip`. Then correct the skip message and MAINTAINING.md:45.
findings.v1reason: tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py:64-65 skips with the message 'run `make docs-install`'. The docs-install target at Makefile:452-454 only runs `cd docs && npm ci`, and docs/package.json does not depend on Playwright. Playwright is declared only in docs/diagrams/package.json:9, and scripts/render_docs.mjs:17 imports it from docs/diagrams/node_modules. On a fresh checkout, docs-render-check (Makefile:480-481), and so docs-lint (Makefile:473), skips all seven checks and passes. The comment at Makefile:470-472 says these defects fail the target. MAINTAINING.md:44-46 gives the same wrong remedy. No workflow runs test_rendered_site.py.
findings.v2reason:
Confirmed by running it. `make docs-install` (Makefile:452-454) only runs `cd docs && npm ci`. docs/package.json has no Playwright dependency and no postinstall or prepare hook, and docs/package-lock.json has no `node_modules/playwright` entry. Playwright is declared only in the separate package docs/diagrams/package.json, which calls itself "Optional editable diagram export tooling; not required for the Antora build". scripts/render_docs.mjs:17 imports it from `../docs/diagrams/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs`.

The render_report fixture (tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py:64-65) skips when that directory is missing, and its skip message points to the wrong remedy (`make docs-install`). docs/MAINTAINING.md:44-45 points to the same wrong remedy.

I simulated a fresh checkout: a built site is present but docs/diagrams/node_modules is not. All seven tests were skipped and pytest exited 0. So `make docs-render-check`, and `make docs-lint` (Makefile:473) that depends on it, pass without checking anything. This contradicts the Makefile:469-472 comment that these defects "fail this target". I found no workflow that references test_rendered_site.py, docs-render-check or docs-lint.

One mitigation: the correct install steps do appear elsewhere, in the diagram-export section at docs/MAINTAINING.md:115-118 (`npm ci --prefix docs/diagrams`; `npx playwright install chromium`). They are not linked from the skip message or line 45, though. Major severity (a test gate that silently passes, plus a wrong remedy) is right.

On this machine the gate works only because docs/diagrams/node_modules/playwright was already installed by hand. All four files involved (the Makefile, MAINTAINING.md, docs/diagrams/package.json and the test module) are added or changed by this branch.
findings.reproduction:
1. `make -n docs-install` printed `cd docs && npm ci`, so the docs/diagrams package is never installed.
2. `grep -c '"node_modules/playwright"' docs/package-lock.json` printed 0. `grep -n "postinstall\|prepare" docs/package.json` found nothing.
3. Fresh-checkout simulation: I built a scratch root at .../scratchpad/review/fresh with docs/build/site/agent-memory symlinked to the real built site, scripts/render_docs.mjs symlinked, and docs/diagrams/package.json copied but no node_modules. I copied test_rendered_site.py next to a conftest.py whose project_root fixture points at that root, then ran `uv run pytest <scratch>/tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py -v -rs`. Output: 7 x `SKIPPED ... Playwright not installed under docs/diagrams; run \`make docs-install\``, then `7 skipped, 1 warning in 0.01s`. A re-run with -q gave `exit=0`.
4. `grep -rn "test_rendered_site\|docs-render-check\|docs-lint" .github/workflows/` returned no workflow matches.
5. `grep -rn playwright Makefile docs/MAINTAINING.md scripts/render_docs.mjs` found the only correct install instruction at MAINTAINING.md:118 (the diagram-export section) and the import at render_docs.mjs:17 from docs/diagrams/node_modules.

findings.detail: No CI step runs test_nav_labels.py. findings.title: Import checker counts names imported only under TYPE_CHECKING as declared, so it certifies imports that fail at runtime
findings.detail: local_import_errors builds each module's export set from its AST and descends into every `if` block, including `if TYPE_CHECKING:`. A name that a module imports only for type checking therefore counts as importable. The test that uses this checker says 'No missing-name allowlist hides nonexistent APIs', but a doc snippet that imports such a name passes and then raises ImportError for a reader. There is a real instance in the SDK: `from neo4j_agent_memory.llm.adapters.vertex_ai import VertexAIEmbedder` passes the checker but fails at runtime. No current doc snippet hits this; I ran all 93 distinct documented SDK imports at runtime and they resolve.
findings.evidence: extract_code.py:429-431: `elif isinstance(node, ast.If): visit(node.body); visit(node.orelse)`. Command: `local_import_errors('from neo4j_agent_memory.llm.adapters.vertex_ai import VertexAIEmbedder', Path('src'))` returned `[]`, while `exec(...)` raised `cannot import name 'VertexAIEmbedder' from 'neo4j_agent_memory.llm.adapters.vertex_ai'`. src/neo4j_agent_memory/llm/adapters/vertex_ai.py:28-31 has `if TYPE_CHECKING: ... from neo4j_agent_memory.embeddings.vertex_ai import VertexAIEmbedder`.
findings.fix: In visit(), skip the body of an `if` whose test is `TYPE_CHECKING` or `typing.TYPE_CHECKING`, and visit only its orelse.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced. `local_import_errors('from neo4j_agent_memory.llm.adapters.vertex_ai import VertexAIEmbedder', Path('src'))` returned [], but executing that import raised 'cannot import name VertexAIEmbedder'. extract_code.py:429-431 visits both branches of every `if`, including `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (vertex_ai.py:28-31). local_import_errors is new on this branch. No current doc snippet hits the gap, so it is latent.

findings.title: Obsolete is_signature_doc skip hides 141 blocks that all compile, including real programs, from syntax and drift checks
findings.detail: The branch switched the syntax test to compile with PyCF_ALLOW_TOP_LEVEL_AWAIT and rewrote the reference signatures as valid `def ...: ...` stubs. The skip heuristic stayed. It triggers on any first line with an annotated parameter, so it skips 141 of 341 snippets, and every one of them compiles. The same flag also exempts them from TestSettingsFieldDrift (line 390). Most are re-parsed by the `// contract:` checks in test_python_reference_contracts, and batch-processing.adoc is compiled by test_operational_howto_contracts. Two blocks have no syntax coverage at all: reference/api/factory.adoc:17 and reference/api/llm-provider.adoc:198. The 100-line program at how-to/batch-processing.adoc:348 is also skipped here and escapes the settings-drift check.
findings.evidence: Command: over `extract_python_snippets(Path('docs'))`, compiling every `is_signature_doc` snippet with `ast.PyCF_ALLOW_TOP_LEVEL_AWAIT` gave `sig ok 141 sig bad 0`. Run: `uv run pytest tests/docs/test_code_snippets.py -q -rs` reports `SKIPPED [141] tests/docs/test_code_snippets.py:58: Signature documentation snippet - not runnable Python`. Example of a skipped block: batch-processing.adoc:348 `async def import_product_catalog(products: list[dict]):` (100 lines).

The skip at test_code_snippets.py:57 and the exclusion at :390 still apply to them. reference/api/factory.adoc:17 and llm-provider.adoc:198 have no `// contract:` markers and no other test covers them. The batch-processing.adoc:348 block is skipped here. The skip predates the branch, but the branch's rewrite made it unnecessary. Every block is valid today, so the gap is latent.

findings.title: test_perturbed_label_is_caught tests Python's assert, not the alignment check
findings.detail: The test says it is a 'Sanity check that the alignment assertion actually fails on a real divergence'. What it actually does is build a perturbed string and check that `assert nav_labels == {perturbed}` raises. That is always true, and it never calls the comparison logic in test_nav_label_matches_target_h1 or test_index_label_matches_target_h1. If those tests stopped detecting mismatches, for example because of broken xref extraction or scope slicing, this test would still pass.
findings.evidence: tests/docs/test_nav_labels.py:180-183: `perturbed = h1 + " (perturbed)"` / `assert perturbed not in nav_labels` / `with pytest.raises(AssertionError):` / `    assert nav_labels == {perturbed}`.
findings.fix: Factor the mismatch computation into a helper that takes nav/index/H1 inputs. Feed it a perturbed nav text (for example with the memory-types label changed) and assert that it reports the mismatch.

findings.title: Trace-outcome assertions pass vacuously when a recipe records no trace
findings.detail: Several tests check trace outcomes with `all(...)` over `client.traces.values()` and never assert that a trace exists. If a recipe stopped calling `common.recorded_turn`, or stopped starting a trace at all, the success and failure outcome checks would still pass, because `all([])` is True. This affects the openai (both parametrizations), crewai success and failure, missing-readback, and pydantic tests.
findings.evidence: test_python_integration_contracts.py:174 `assert all(trace.success is not fail for trace in client.traces.values())`; also :110, :122, :131 and :141 `assert all(trace.success is True/False for trace in client.traces.values())`.
findings.fix: Assert `len(client.traces) == 1` (or `>= 1`) before each `all(...)` check.
findings.v1reason: The fake Client starts with `self.traces = {}` (test_python_integration_contracts.py:46) and adds entries only in start_trace. The assertions at :110, :122, :131, :141 and :174 use `all(...)` over client.traces.values(), and no length check exists anywhere in the module. If a recipe recorded no trace, `all([])` would be True and these tests would still pass.

findings.title: messages recipe asserts an order the SDK doesn't guarantee, and fails in about 40% of runs
findings.detail: add_messages_batch writes both messages in one Cypher statement. Neither message gets a timestamp, so CREATE_MESSAGES_BATCH gives both the same datetime(). get_conversation then sorts only by `ORDER BY m.timestamp ASC`, so which of the two tied messages comes first is not defined. Readback often comes back reversed, and the assertion `[m.id for m in conversation.messages] == [m.id for m in stored]` fails. how-to/messages.adoc:55 tells readers 'The ID assertion checks order and persistence'. So `python core_memory_recipes.py messages` crashes with AssertionError for readers following the page. The released python-v0.6.0 has the same batch-timestamp query, so the recipe fails against the PyPI package too. The mocked docs tests (tests/docs/test_core_python_tutorials.py) never run this against Neo4j, so they pass.
findings.evidence: core_memory_recipes.py:18-32 `stored = await client.short_term.add_messages_batch(session, [...])` ... `assert [m.id for m in conversation.messages] == [m.id for m in stored]`. Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:442 `timestamp = msg_dict.get("timestamp")` (None when omitted); graph/queries.py:109 `timestamp: CASE WHEN msg.timestamp IS NOT NULL THEN datetime(msg.timestamp) ELSE datetime() END`; graph/queries.py:169-173 GET_CONVERSATION_MESSAGES `ORDER BY m.timestamp ASC`. Ran against neo4j:5.26-community (testcontainer) with the recipe's own messages() function: probe readback `[('assistant','f5b92c05', 14:59:10.352000), ('user','5648aefd', 14:59:10.352000)]` vs stored `[('user','5648aefd'), ('assistant','f5b92c05')]`. With 10 fresh-client runs of core_memory_recipes.messages the result was `pass 6 fail 4`, and an earlier harness run failed 3/3.
findings.fix: Don't assert order the SDK doesn't guarantee. Either give each batch dict an explicit, increasing ISO `timestamp`, or add the two messages with sequential add_message calls, or compare ID sets and check the roles separately. Update the 'checks order' sentence in how-to/messages.adoc to match. A separate follow-up: fix add_messages_batch in the SDK so each message gets a distinct, increasing timestamp.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced. CREATE_MESSAGES_BATCH (graph/queries.py:109) gives each message without a timestamp `datetime()`, which uses the statement clock, so both messages get the same value. add_messages_batch passes timestamp=None when the dict has none (short_term.py:442). GET_CONVERSATION_MESSAGES (queries.py:169-173) orders only by `m.timestamp ASC`, so the two tied rows can come back in either order. I ran the recipe's own `messages()` function against a neo4j:5.26-community testcontainer with fresh clients. The first run gave `pass 1 fail 9`. A second run of 5 gave `pass 0 fail 5`, and every failure was AssertionError at core_memory_recipes.py:32 (the ID-order assert). how-to/messages.adoc:51 says 'The ID assertion checks order and persistence', so a reader running `python core_memory_recipes.py messages` usually crashes. The file is new on this branch.
findings.v2reason:
Confirmed by running it. The file docs/modules/ROOT/examples/core_memory_recipes.py is new on this branch: `git show ec9fc65:` says it is not in main, and the "checks order" sentence in how-to/messages.adoc:51 is new too.

The recipe calls `add_messages_batch` without timestamps. In short_term.py:442 `timestamp = msg_dict.get("timestamp")` is then None. CREATE_MESSAGES_BATCH (queries.py:109) then falls back to `ELSE datetime() END`, which uses the statement clock, so both messages get the same timestamp. GET_CONVERSATION_MESSAGES (queries.py:169-173) orders only by `ORDER BY m.timestamp ASC`, so the two tied rows can come back in either order. The assertion at core_memory_recipes.py:32, `assert [m.id for m in conversation.messages] == [m.id for m in stored]`, therefore fails nondeterministically, and in practice most of the time.

I ran the recipe's own `messages()` function against a neo4j:5.26-community testcontainer, using a fresh MemoryClient per run and a stub embedder. The first batch of 10 runs gave "pass 1 fail 9". The second batch of 4 runs gave "pass 0 fail 4", and every traceback pointed to core_memory_recipes.py, line 32, in messages. The released python-v0.6.0 tag has the same `ELSE datetime() END` batch query (queries.py:99 at that tag), so readers on the PyPI package hit the same failure.

The page tells readers "The ID assertion checks order and persistence" (how-to/messages.adoc:51). A reader running `python core_memory_recipes.py messages` usually gets an AssertionError. Blocker severity stands: a reader who follows the documented steps fails.

Fix: give each batch dict an explicit, increasing ISO timestamp, or use sequential add_message calls, or compare ID sets instead of order. Then update the sentence at messages.adoc:51 to match.

findings.title: Hosted first write uses a fixed display name as the conversation ID, contradicting the NAMS docs
findings.detail: The program sends add_message to a hard-coded conversation ID, 'docs-nams-first-write', without calling create_conversation first. On NAMS the SDK posts to /conversations/{id}/messages. Conversation IDs are assigned by the server (create_conversation sends only userId/metadata), and other pages on this branch tell readers to call create_conversation first and never use a display name as the session ID. Two outcomes are possible: (a) the write targets a conversation that doesn't exist, so the tutorial's first step fails; or (b) the service creates it on the fly, which gives every reader the same fixed-ID conversation in their workspace. In case (b), `conversation.messages[-1]` can come from an earlier run, and nothing checks the returned message ID. Either way the record is never put in the ledger. nams_quickstart's cleanup only deletes the ledgered conversation, so this write is never cleaned up. That contradicts the page's promise ('We will retain the IDs returned by NAMS and use them for scoped cleanup') and its later guidance to keep state until every created resource has a disposition.
findings.evidence: nams_first_write.py:11-14 `session_id = "docs-nams-first-write"` / `await client.short_term.add_message(session_id, "user", "Hello, NAMS!")` / `last = conversation.messages[-1]`. Contradicted by docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/short-term.adoc:24 'On NAMS, call `create_conversation` first and use its returned ID.'; how-to/migrate-to-nams.adoc:72 'Persist the ID returned by `create_conversation`; do not continue using its display name as the message session ID.'; how-to/use-nams.adoc:115 'A conversation's display name and a user ID are not substitutes for its returned ID.'; src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:465-476 (create_conversation body is only `{userId, metadata}`) and :292-298 (add_message posts to `/conversations/{conv}/messages` with no creation). `grep -rn docs-nams-first-write docs tests` finds no cleanup or test beyond the include at pages/tutorials/nams-quickstart.adoc:72.
findings.fix: Call `conversation = await client.short_term.create_conversation(name)` and use `str(conversation.id)` for add_message and get_conversation. Check the stored message by the returned ID rather than messages[-1]. Then either add the conversation to the ledger or give explicit instructions to delete it, so the lesson's cleanup covers every resource it creates.
findings.v1reason: nams_first_write.py:11-14 (new on this branch; included at tutorials/nams-quickstart.adoc:72) passes the fixed string 'docs-nams-first-write' to add_message/get_conversation and never calls create_conversation. That contradicts the SDK's own contract: the NamsShortTermMemory class docstring (nams/short_term.py:262-266) says 'session_id ... maps to the NAMS conversation UUID ... Pre-create your conversation, hold onto the UUID'. add_message (nams/short_term.py:274-299) only POSTs to /conversations/{conv}/messages and creates nothing. It also contradicts this branch's own pages: reference/api/short-term.adoc:24 'On NAMS, call `create_conversation` first and use its returned ID'; migrate-to-nams.adoc:72; use-nams.adoc:115. The use-nams check_nams.py (use-nams.adoc:48-68) does call create_conversation, uses str(conversation.id), and matches the message by its returned ID. I can't observe the service, so I can't tell whether it rejects the call or auto-creates the conversation. Either way the program breaks the documented contract, reads messages[-1] instead of the returned ID, and creates a conversation the lesson's ledger/cleanup never tracks (grep finds no other reference to docs-nams-first-write).
findings.v2reason:
The defect is real, and this branch added it: docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py does not exist at ec9fc65 and was added in d3db0ff. I ran the program with a recording fake transport. It sends POST /conversations/docs-nams-first-write/messages straight away and never calls create_conversation. The SDK creates nothing on that path: add_message (src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:274-299) only resolves the ID and POSTs to `/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages` (:76-80).

The repo's own live-NAMS test notes also settle the open question of (a) failure versus (b) auto-create. tests/integration/nams/test_smoke.py:11-15 says "Unlike bolt — which creates conversations implicitly on the first `add_message` — NAMS (Platinum tier) requires explicit conversation creation". tests/integration/nams/conftest.py:264-265 says "NAMS (unlike bolt) does **not** auto-create conversations on the first `add_message` — see `test_smoke.py` for the discovery." So case (a) is the documented outcome. At Step 3 of tutorials/nams-quickstart.adoc (line 72), the reader's first write targets a conversation that does not exist. The transport maps 404 to NotFoundError (nams/transport.py:358-359), so the tutorial's first hosted step fails.

The program also contradicts pages this branch edited: reference/api/short-term.adoc:24, how-to/migrate-to-nams.adoc:72 and how-to/use-nams.adoc:115. It contradicts the SDK class docstring (nams/short_term.py:262-266: "Pre-create your conversation, hold onto the UUID, and pass it as `session_id`"). Every other hosted example does it correctly: examples/nams-quickstart/main.py:103, examples/nams-langchain/main.py:118 and examples/nams-fastapi/main.py:326 all call create_conversation first.

Even if the service did auto-create, the finding's secondary points still hold. The program reads messages[-1] rather than the returned message ID, and the conversation is never ledgered or cleaned up: grep finds 'docs-nams-first-write' only in the example file itself. A reader who follows the docs fails at the first write, which is the blocker definition, so I raised the severity from major to blocker. One caveat: I could not observe the live service myself. The failure evidence is the repo's recorded live-test finding, not a live call.

findings.title: Comment says 'seed' runs without the openai package, but seed makes OpenAI embedding calls
findings.detail: The comment explains the deferred import by saying the seed branch doesn't need openai. But core_memory_settings selects `openai/text-embedding-3-small`, and seed calls add_message and add_preference with the default generate_embedding=True, which embeds through the OpenAI adapter. Without the openai package, seed fails. knowledge_graph.py:190-191 makes the same claim for `ingest` and `inspect`: ingest's add_message and add_entity also embed. The pages do install [openai], so the risk is limited to readers who trust the comment and trim dependencies.
findings.evidence: conversation_memory.py:124-125 '# Imported here: only this branch calls a model, so `seed` runs without the openai package installed.'; knowledge_graph.py:190-191 same claim for `ingest` and `inspect`. core_memory_settings.py:12 `embedding="openai/text-embedding-3-small"`; memory/short_term.py add_message `generate_embedding: bool = True`; llm/adapters/openai.py:85-91 lazily imports openai. Command: `sys.modules['openai']=None; from core_memory_settings import settings; asyncio.run(settings().embedding.embed_one('x'))` produced `ImportError: LiteLLM not installed. Install with: pip install 'neo4j-agent-memory[litellm]'`.
findings.fix: Reword both comments to say that only this branch calls the chat model; seed/ingest still need the openai extra for embeddings.
findings.v1reason: conversation_memory.py:124-125 and knowledge_graph.py:190-191 say seed/ingest run without the openai package. But core_memory_settings.py:12 sets embedding='openai/text-embedding-3-small', and seed's add_message/add_preference default to generate_embedding=True (short_term.py:677, long_term.py:649). I blocked the openai module (sys.modules['openai']=None), built MemoryClient(settings())._create_embedder() and called embed('x'). Result: `ImportError LiteLLM not installed. Install with: pip install 'neo4j-agent-memory[litellm]'`. So seed/ingest do need the model/embedding SDK. Minor, because the pages install the [openai] extra.

findings.title: aura_connection silently defaults the database to 'neo4j', but the pages say 'no database fallback'
findings.detail: Every Aura tutorial manifest describes this helper as 'Read explicit Aura credentials; no database fallback', and the setup partial says the examples 'do not supply a fallback database'. The helper actually falls back to database 'neo4j' when NEO4J_DATABASE is unset, so the readiness probe and every program run against a database the reader never named. This matters little on Aura (the default database is 'neo4j'), but the text and the code disagree.
findings.evidence: aura_connection.py:18 `database = os.environ.get("NEO4J_DATABASE", "neo4j")`. Pages: tutorials/first-agent-memory.adoc:47 (and conversation-memory.adoc:49, knowledge-graph.adoc:50, anthropic-and-local-embeddings.adoc:47, mcp-server.adoc:51, strands-agent-quickstart.adoc:49, microsoft-agent-memory.adoc:60) '|`aura_connection.py` |Read explicit Aura credentials; no database fallback.'; partials/aura-tutorial-setup.adoc:22 'They require Aura credentials and do not supply a fallback database.'
findings.fix: Either add NEO4J_DATABASE to the `required` tuple, or change the manifest and partial text to say the helper defaults to the 'neo4j' database and has no local-database fallback.
findings.v1reason: aura_connection.py:18 `database = os.environ.get("NEO4J_DATABASE", "neo4j")` does fall back to a database name. The manifests (e.g. first-agent-memory.adoc:47 'no database fallback') and partials/aura-tutorial-setup.adoc:22 'do not supply a fallback database' literally say it doesn't. The wording probably means 'no local-instance fallback', and the setup partial exports NEO4J_DATABASE='neo4j' (line 16) anyway, so the practical impact is nil. It is only a wording mismatch.

findings.title: Docs say the Aura helper has 'no fallback database', but aura_config() defaults to 'neo4j'

findings.title: Shared model-selection partial asks for Chat Completions support, but this lesson uses the Responses API
findings.detail: The included partial tells the reader to pick a model whose page lists 'Chat Completions' support. This lesson's program uses agent_framework.openai.OpenAIChatClient, which in the installed agent-framework-openai 1.14.4 is the Responses API client. The Chat Completions client is a separate class, OpenAIChatCompletionClient. A reader following the partial can pick a model that supports Chat Completions but not Responses, and the agent call then fails. They can also wrongly rule out models that only support Responses. The partial is correct for conversation-memory and knowledge-graph, which call `llm.chat.completions.create`.

The installed class docstring (.venv/.../agent_framework_openai/_chat_client.py) reads "OpenAI Responses client class with middleware, telemetry, and function invocation support." `dir(agent_framework.openai)` lists both 'OpenAIChatClient' and 'OpenAIChatCompletionClient'.
findings.fix: Make the API name a parameter of the partial (for example an attribute set to 'Responses' on this page), or add a sentence on this page saying the model must support the Responses API.
findings.v1reason: partials/python-openai-model-selection.adoc:1 says to check the model page for 'Chat Completions' support. The partial is included at microsoft-agent-memory.adoc:96. findings.title: Missing OPENAI_MODEL is only detected after the preference has been written
findings.detail: This lesson exports OPENAI_MODEL without the presence and placeholder check that conversation-memory and knowledge-graph run.
