findings.title: Step 3 writes to a client-chosen NAMS conversation ID without creating the conversation first
findings.detail: Step 3 of the NAMS tutorial runs nams_first_write.py, which calls add_message('docs-nams-first-write', ...) and then get_conversation on the same string. It never calls create_conversation. The Python NAMS client sends add_message to POST /conversations/{conversation_id}/messages. The repository's own NAMS contract says conversations must be created explicitly and addressed by the ID the server returns. So this first program most likely fails with a 404 before the reader reaches the ledgered part of the lesson. It also contradicts the sentence this branch removed from the page ('create the conversation first and use the id it returns everywhere else') and the backend-capabilities reference. One source comment points the other way: nams/short_term.py:156-157 says NAMS lets callers create conversations under arbitrary string IDs. But that comment is about creating a conversation, and this script creates none. No test runs nams_first_write.py: it has no 'Save as' listing, so test_build_pipeline and test_core_python_tutorials skip it.
findings.evidence:
Offending code, docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py:11-13: `session_id = "docs-nams-first-write"` / `await client.short_term.add_message(session_id, "user", "Hello, NAMS!")` / `conversation = await client.short_term.get_conversation(session_id)`. It is included at docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/nams-quickstart.adoc:72, and :80 promises `Stored and read back: user said 'Hello, NAMS!'`.

Sources of truth:
- tests/integration/nams/test_smoke.py:11-15: "Unlike bolt — which creates conversations implicitly on the first ``add_message`` — NAMS (Platinum tier) requires explicit conversation creation ... calls ``create_conversation()`` first and returns the canonical id".
- src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:465-468 (create_conversation): "NAMS accepts ``{userId?, metadata?}`` only — no ``session_id``".
- src/neo4j_agent_memory/integrations/strands/memory_store.py:203-204 and typescript/src/integrations/strands/memory-store.ts:426: "NAMS mints its own conversation ids".
- docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:15: "Python with NAMS:: Create a conversation and use its returned ID".
- The removed text, git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/nams-quickstart.adoc:106: "NAMS mints conversation ids server-side, so create the conversation first".
- grep for nams_first_write across tests/, .github/ and scripts/ finds no test.
findings.fix: Create the conversation first, e.g. `conversation = await client.short_term.create_conversation(); cid = str(conversation.id)`, then use `cid` for add_message and get_conversation, the same pattern as how-to/use-nams.adoc:54-62. Add an offline test for this file, as the other hosted programs have.
findings.v1reason: docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py:11-13 is new on this branch (commit d3db0ff). It calls add_message('docs-nams-first-write', ...) and get_conversation on that fixed string and never calls create_conversation. In nams/short_term.py:275-299, add_message POSTs to /conversations/{conversation_id}/messages and does not create the conversation if it is missing. The repository's own NAMS contract says conversations must be created first: tests/integration/nams/test_smoke.py:11-15 says NAMS requires explicit conversation creation, and the conftest nams_session fixture at :264-265 says NAMS does not auto-create conversations on the first add_message. reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:15 says 'Create a conversation and use its returned ID', examples/nams-quickstart/main.py:103 calls create_conversation first, and the old tutorial text this branch removed said the same. The comment at short_term.py:156 about arbitrary string IDs is about response normalisation, not an implicit create. grep finds no reference to nams_first_write in tests/, .github/ or scripts/, and the listing has no 'Save as' title, so nothing tests this program. The hosted service can't be observed from here, but every source in the repo agrees, so a reader's first hosted call most likely returns a 404.
findings.v2reason:
I ran the script and the defect is real. I couldn't call the live service, so the 404 itself comes from what the repository says NAMS does, not from a live call.

docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py is new on this branch (commit d3db0ff; `git show ec9fc65:` says it isn't in main). Lines 11-13 send `add_message("docs-nams-first-write", ...)` and then `get_conversation(...)`, and the script never calls `create_conversation`.

I ran the script unchanged with a mock httpx transport. The mock answers the connect probe, creates a conversation on `POST /conversations`, and returns 404 for any conversation that was never created, which is the rule the repository describes. The only calls the script made were `GET /v1/conversations` (the connect probe) and `POST /v1/conversations/docs-nams-first-write/messages`. So it never creates the conversation.

Nothing in the client would recover from that 404:
- `NamsShortTermMemory.add_message` (src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:275-299) POSTs straight to `/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages`.
- The transport turns a 404 into `NotFoundError` (src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/transport.py:358-359). It doesn't retry or create anything.
- The class docstring (short_term.py:262-267) says: "Pre-create your conversation, hold onto the UUID, and pass it as session_id."

Every repo source agrees that NAMS needs the conversation created first:
- tests/integration/nams/test_smoke.py:11-15.
- The `nams_session` fixture in tests/integration/nams/conftest.py: "NAMS (unlike bolt) does **not** auto-create conversations on the first add_message".
- test_tck_gold.py: "NAMS requires explicit create_conversation before add_message".
- test_adk_e2e.py calls `create_conversation` and then uses `str(conv.id)`.
- The tutorial text this branch removed (ec9fc65 nams-quickstart.adoc): "NAMS mints conversation ids server-side, so create the conversation first".

The comment at short_term.py:156-157 about "arbitrary string IDs" is about how the response is normalised after a conversation is *created*. It doesn't say an unknown ID gets created on the first message.

No test covers the file. `grep nams_first_write` finds nothing in tests/, .github/, scripts/ or docs/extensions/.

The result: a reader who follows Step 3 (nams-quickstart.adoc:65-80) most likely gets `NotFoundError` on their first hosted call instead of the promised `Stored and read back: user said 'Hello, NAMS!'`. I'm keeping it at blocker because the tutorial fails at step 3. If you give weight to the fact that the live service couldn't be checked, major would be defensible.
findings.reproduction:
1. `git log -1 -- docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py` shows d3db0ff (a docs commit on this branch). `git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py` fails with "exists on disk, but not in 'ec9fc65'".

2. The harness is scratchpad/review/run_first_write.py. It monkeypatches `httpx.AsyncClient` to use `httpx.MockTransport`, sets `MEMORY_API_KEY=nams_dummy`, and loads the unmodified script with runpy. The mock returns:
   - 200 for `GET /conversations` (the connect probe);
   - 201 with a UUID for `POST /conversations`;
   - 404 for anything else, meaning a conversation that was never created.

   Command:
   `uv run python .../scratchpad/review/run_first_write.py docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py`

   Output:
   ```
   EXC: NotFoundError NAMS POST https://memory.neo4jlabs.com/v1/conversations/docs-nams-first-write/messages → 404
   CALLS: [('GET', '/v1/conversations'), ('POST', '/v1/conversations/docs-nams-first-write/messages')]
   ```
   The script never sends `POST /conversations`.

3. `grep -rn nams_first_write tests .github scripts docs/extensions` finds nothing.

4. `git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/nams-quickstart.adoc` includes the removed line "NAMS mints conversation ids server-side, so create the conversation first and use the id it returns everywhere else", followed by `client.short_term.create_conversation(CONVERSATION_NAME)`.

Fix: create the conversation first, e.g. `conv = await client.short_term.create_conversation(); cid = str(conv.id)`, and pass `cid` to `add_message` and `get_conversation`. Add an offline test for this file.

findings.title: inspect-file handoff summary omits the ontology's previous active version needed to restore the binding
findings.detail: The shared lifecycle partial tells a reader whose key has expired or rotated to run `hosted_tutorial_state.py inspect-file` and give the owner "the workspace label, endpoint, run token, exact resource IDs and pending operation" so the owner can reconcile. In the ontology lesson, the interrupted state that matters most is a workspace still bound to the strict clone. Recovering from it needs the saved prior binding: its version_id and validation_mode, stored under state['ontology']['previous']. inspect_file() returns only resources, pending and operator_context, and resources hold only the clone ontology ID and the clone/strict version IDs. The original version to reactivate is therefore missing from the only output the page tells the reader to hand over. The authenticated `recover` command is blocked after a credential change, and the partial forbids editing the ledger.
findings.evidence:
docs/modules/ROOT/examples/hosted_tutorial_state.py:79-101: the returned dict has keys local_only, service_checked, lesson, run_token, started_at, identity, operator_context, pending, new_run_status, resources. There is no 'ontology'/'previous' key.

docs/modules/ROOT/partials/python-hosted-lifecycle.adoc:17-19: "Give the authorized owner the workspace label, endpoint, run token, exact resource IDs and pending operation ... The owner must establish the actual workspace and reconcile those resources". This partial is included at docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/ontology-quickstart.adoc:232.

Reproduction: I wrote an ontology ledger whose ontology.previous.version_id is 'ORIGINAL-VERSION' and ran inspect_file(). The output contains the clone and version IDs only; `'ORIGINAL-VERSION' in output` printed False.
findings.fix: Include a redacted restoration target in inspect_file(), e.g. `ontology: {previous: {version_id, ontology_id, revision, validation_mode}, clone_id, strict: {version_id}, status, restored, deleted}` without the document. Alternatively, say in the partial/ontology page that the owner also needs the previous active version ID and mode, and where to find them.
findings.v1reason: hosted_tutorial_state.py and partials/python-hosted-lifecycle.adoc are both new on this branch. The dict returned by inspect_file() at hosted_tutorial_state.py:79-101 has no 'ontology' key. Its resources entries keep only status/owned/disposition, so the prior binding that temporary_strict_ontology saves at hosted_tutorial_helpers.py:245 (state.data['ontology']['previous']) never appears in the summary. The partial at :17-19 tells the reader to hand over the 'exact resource IDs and pending operation' and 'reconcile those resources'. The original version to reactivate is therefore missing from that hand-off, unless the pending operation happens to be a restore. The reader can still read the private ledger or the 'Previous active version:' line printed in Step 3, so there is a workaround. That makes this minor rather than major.

findings.title: Step 3's first-write record is never recorded in the ledger or cleaned up
findings.detail: Assuming Step 3 writes successfully, it creates a conversation and message that the lesson's ledger and cleanup never see. nams_first_write.py does not use TutorialState. The cleanup in Step 7 deletes only state.data['conversation_id'] and the entities linked to it. This contradicts the page's promise that NAMS-returned IDs are retained for scoped cleanup, and the Step 7 rule to keep state until every returned ID has a disposition. The fixed ID 'docs-nams-first-write' also means repeated runs keep appending to one untracked conversation.
findings.evidence:
docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/nams-quickstart.adoc:10-11: "We will retain the IDs returned by NAMS and use them for scoped cleanup."

nams-quickstart.adoc:242-243: "Keep the private state until every returned ID has a verified deletion or retention disposition."

docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py:5-15: no ledger import and no deletion.

findings.v1reason: nams-quickstart.adoc:10-11 promises: 'We will retain the IDs returned by NAMS and use them for scoped cleanup'. But nams_first_write.py does not import TutorialState or record anything, and the page never mentions deleting the Step 3 record. The cleanup section at :242-243 says to keep state until every returned ID has a disposition, yet the Step 3 conversation and message stay outside the ledger. Because the ID is fixed, reruns keep adding to the same untracked conversation. If finding 0 holds and Step 3 fails, this becomes moot, but any fix to Step 3 has to deal with it.

findings.title: attestationConfigured is presented as part of the attestation file, but it comes from /skills/capabilities
findings.detail: Step 5 prints skills-attestation.json, which holds the GET /skills/{id}/verify response. It then tells the reader to interpret `attestationConfigured: false`. The only documented source of that field is the capabilities response. The program saves that response in the ledger under state.data['capabilities'] (visible via the `state` command), not in skills-attestation.json. A reader looking for the flag in the file just printed may not find it and may misjudge whether the package is signed.
findings.evidence:
docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/skills-quickstart.adoc:271 runs `python -m json.tool .tutorial-state/skills-attestation.json`, then :279-281 say "Inspect attestation separately ... `attestationConfigured: false` means signing is not configured".

The field is documented only in docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/skills-api.adoc:28: "`/v1/skills/capabilities` ... Gate state: `{distillation, composition, attestationConfigured}`".

docs/modules/ROOT/examples/skills_quickstart.py:325 stores the capabilities as `state.data["capabilities"] = await preflight(http)`; :263-264 writes only the /verify response to skills-attestation.json.
findings.fix: Say that `attestationConfigured` is in the capabilities saved in the ledger (shown by `python skills_quickstart.py state`), and describe what to check in skills-attestation.json (the /verify result) separately.
findings.v1reason: skills-api.adoc:28 documents attestationConfigured only on /v1/skills/capabilities, and the program saves that response in state.data['capabilities'] (skills_quickstart.py:325). skills-attestation.json holds the /verify response (skills_quickstart.py:263-264). The page at :279-281 mentions attestationConfigured right after printing that file. However, the /verify response shape isn't documented or modelled anywhere in the SDKs (grep of src and typescript/src finds nothing), and the hosted service can't be observed. So I can't rule out that /verify also returns the field. The wording is ambiguous, but I can't confirm it is wrong.

findings.title: After publish detects changed provenance, the page doesn't say to rerun inspect
findings.detail: If the skill or its provenance changed, `publish` sets provenance_verified to False and stops. Rerunning `publish` then fails with "Inspect provenance first; do not repeat publication". The only way forward is to run `inspect` again, which re-polls the run and sets provenance_verified to True. The page says only that publish "saves the new report and stops for another review" and gives no next command.
findings.evidence:
docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/skills-quickstart.adoc:255-257: "If they changed since inspection, it saves the new report and stops for another review."

docs/modules/ROOT/examples/skills_quickstart.py:239-248: `if not data.get("provenance_verified") ...: raise RuntimeError("Inspect provenance first; do not repeat publication")`, and after a hash change `data["provenance_verified"] = False`.

findings.title: MCP lesson's documented install makes `npm run build` fail with a type error (two zod copies)
findings.detail: The lesson installs the SDK with `npm install ../typescript`, which creates a symlink. The SDK's `mcp/register` then resolves `zod` from `typescript/node_modules` (4.6.1 from the lockfile), while the reader's `McpServer` resolves the newer `zod@^4` that npm installs in `my-memory-mcp/node_modules` (4.6.5 today). tsc rejects `registerMemoryTools(server, …)` with TS2345, so `npm run build` exits 2. Step 4 tells the reader to run that build before pointing Desktop at `dist/server.js`. tsc still emits `dist/`, and the server does start: tools/list and zod validation work. But a reader following the page sees the build fail and stops. The build passes only when both zod versions match exactly (confirmed by installing zod@4.6.1). It also conflicts with the checkout partial's line 3-4 statement that 'application code instead installs the published `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0` package from npm'. `my-memory-mcp` is exactly that kind of standalone application project.
findings.evidence:
Offending text at mcp-server-typescript.adoc:62: `npm install ../typescript @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4`. mcp-server-typescript.adoc:258 then says: "Run `npm run build` first so `dist/server.js` exists."

Reproduction in the scratchpad: npm init, the documented installs, the three copied helpers, the page's server.ts / tsconfig.json / package fields, then `npm run build`. Output:
`src/server.ts(21,41): error TS2345: Argument of type 'McpServer' is not assignable to parameter of type 'RegisterToolCapable'. ... Type 'MemoryToolShape' is missing the following properties from type 'ZodType<any, any, any>': _type, _output, _input, _def, and 34 more.` exit=2.

`npm ls zod` shows `zod@4.6.5` (the reader's) and `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory -> ../typescript` using `zod@4.6.1`. After `npm install zod@4.6.1`, `npm run build` exits 0.

Source of truth: typescript/src/mcp/register.ts:53 `import { z } from "zod";` and typescript/node_modules/zod/package.json `"version": "4.6.1"`.
findings.fix: In the standalone `my-memory-mcp` project, install the published release: `npm install @neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0 @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4`. npm then dedupes zod and the MCP SDK. The copied helpers only need the public API. If the source build is kept on purpose, pin `zod` to the exact version in typescript/package-lock.json, or compile with `--noEmitOnError false` and state that TS2345 is expected. Either way, make the checkout partial's npm sentence agree with whichever path is chosen.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced it in the scratchpad (review/v0), with `typescript` symlinked to the real SDK so the layout matches the page. I ran npm init, then the page's `npm install ../typescript @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4` and the dev-deps install (mcp-server-typescript.adoc:62-63), copied the three helpers, and wrote server.ts, tsconfig.json and the package fields from the page's blocks. `npm run build` exits 2 with `src/server.ts(21,41): error TS2345: Argument of type 'McpServer' is not assignable to parameter of type 'RegisterToolCapable'`. `npm ls zod` shows two copies: the reader's zod@4.6.5 (npm latest; MCP SDK 1.30.1 dedupes to it) and zod@4.6.1 under the linked SDK (typescript/node_modules/zod/package.json:3). typescript/src/mcp/register.ts:52 imports its own `z`, and :58 types `MemoryToolShape` against it. tsc still emits dist/server.js because noEmitOnError is off, but Step 4 (adoc:258) tells the reader to run the build, and they see it fail. The checkout partial is new on this branch, and its lines 3-4 say application code installs the published package, which contradicts this project's `../typescript` install.
findings.v2reason:
I ran the lesson in a fresh scratch project and it fails the way the finding says. The project was built from the page's own blocks: package fields (adoc:80-89), tsconfig (adoc:94-106), `src/server.ts` (adoc:144-196) and the three copied helpers. The dependencies were installed with the command at mcp-server-typescript.adoc:62, `npm install ../typescript @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4`. `npm run build` then exits 2 with `src/server.ts(21,41): error TS2345: Argument of type 'McpServer' is not assignable to parameter of type 'RegisterToolCapable' ... 'MemoryToolShape' is missing the following properties from type 'ZodType<any, any, any>'`.

The cause is two copies of zod. `npm ls zod` shows the reader's zod@4.6.5, which MCP SDK 1.30.1 also uses. The linked SDK resolves its own zod@4.6.1 from typescript/node_modules (typescript/node_modules/zod/package.json:3). typescript/src/mcp/register.ts:52 imports `z` from "zod", and :58 types `MemoryToolShape` against that second copy.

As a control, I swapped only the dependency install for the published package: `npm install @neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0 @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4`. npm view confirms 0.5.0 is on the registry. With that install, zod dedupes to a single 4.6.5 and `npm run build` exits 0.

The branch caused this. On main the line was `npm install @neo4j-labs/agent-memory @modelcontextprotocol/sdk zod` (`git show ec9fc65:...mcp-server-typescript.adoc` line 44). `git log -S` shows commit 8fc3ead changed it to `../typescript`.

The change also contradicts the new partial typescript-tutorial-checkout.adoc:3-4, which says "application code instead installs the published `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0` package from npm".

tsc still writes dist/server.js, because noEmitOnError is not set, so the server itself could run. But adoc:258 tells the reader to run `npm run build` before pointing Claude Desktop at `dist/server.js`, and that build step fails. Blocker severity stands: a reader who follows the docs hits a failed build. You could argue for major only because the compiled output is still usable.
findings.reproduction:
Scratch dir: review/v1. The `typescript` symlink points to the repo's typescript/ folder, and typescript/dist/index.js already exists.

Commands, in my-memory-mcp:
1. `npm init -y`
2. `npm install ../typescript @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4`
3. `npm install --save-dev typescript@^5.9 tsx@^4 @types/node@^22`
4. Copy tutorial-{state,cleanup,mcp}.ts into src/.
5. Take server.ts from adoc lines 145-195 and tsconfig.json from adoc lines 95-106. Merge the package fields (type module, engines, start/build scripts) into package.json.

`npm run build` prints `src/server.ts(21,41): error TS2345: Argument of type 'McpServer' is not assignable to parameter of type 'RegisterToolCapable'.` It exits 2 (v1exit=2), and dist/ is still emitted.

`npm ls zod` output:
- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.1` → `zod@4.6.5 deduped`
- `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0 -> .../typescript` → `zod@4.6.1`
- top level: `zod@4.6.5`

Control run (review/v2): the same project with the dependencies replaced by `npm install @neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0 @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4`. `npm run build` exits 0 (v2exit=0), and zod resolves to a single 4.6.5.

Origin of the change: `git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/mcp-server-typescript.adoc` line 44 is `npm install @neo4j-labs/agent-memory @modelcontextprotocol/sdk zod`. `git log -S'npm install ../typescript @modelcontextprotocol' ec9fc65..HEAD` returns 8fc3ead "docs: align guides and examples with current SDK behavior".

findings.title: Extraction wait treats only status "done" as finished; the Python client and fixtures use "completed"
findings.detail: `waitForTerminalExtraction` returns only when every message's status is exactly `"done"`. It fails fast only on `"error"` or `"failed"`. Any other finished status, such as `"completed"` or `"skipped"`, makes it poll until the 60-second deadline and then throw 'Extraction deadline expired'. The Python SDK's client for the same endpoint documents and tests `completed` as the per-message status. The Python tutorial's cleanup helper accepts `{done, completed, skipped}` as finished. Every TypeScript lesson's cleanup, and the knowledge-graph lesson's `seed`/`observe`, go through this wait. If the service reports `completed`, all of them time out, and the pages tell the reader to keep the state and not claim cleanup. The helper also requires `messages[]` to list exactly the recorded IDs. The Python fixtures often return `messages: []` and rely on `summary`. The hosted service can't be observed from here, but the two clients in this repo contradict each other.
findings.evidence:
tutorial-cleanup.ts:37-38:
`if (value.messages.some(m => ["error", "failed"].includes(m.status!))) throw ...; if (value.messages.every(m => m.status === "done")) return;`

src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:240-241: "``summary`` maps each per-message extraction status (``pending`` / ``completed`` / ``failed`` / …)".

tests/unit/nams/test_short_term.py:361: `"messages": [{"id": "m1", "status": "completed"}]`.

tests/examples/test_nams_quickstart_example.py:130: `{"completed": 3}`.

docs/modules/ROOT/examples/hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py:57: `terminal = {"done", "completed", "skipped"}`.

The TS stub typescript/examples/vercel-ai/test/docs-hosted-stub.ts:14 hard-codes `extraction: "done"`, so the TS tests never exercise `completed`.
findings.fix: Match the Python helper: treat `done`, `completed` and `skipped` as finished, `pending`/`processing`/`running`/`in_progress`/`queued` as still running, and fail on `failed`/`error`/`cancelled` or any unknown status. Use `summary` when `messages` is missing or empty. Add a `completed` case to the docs stub tests.
findings.v1reason: typescript/examples/shared/tutorial-cleanup.ts:37-38 fails fast only on 'error'/'failed' and returns only when every per-message status is exactly 'done'. It also throws if `messages` does not list exactly the recorded IDs (:35-36). Everything else in the repo treats 'completed' as a finished status. src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:240 documents per-message statuses as `pending` / `completed` / `failed`, and :126-127 counts only pending/processing/running/in_progress/queued as not finished. Python fixtures return `{"completed": N}` with `messages: []` (tests/unit/nams/test_long_term.py:78; tests/examples/test_nams_quickstart_example.py:130; test_claude_code_team_memory_example.py:165). This branch's own Python helper accepts both `{done, completed, skipped}` (docs/modules/ROOT/examples/hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py:58), and tests/docs/test_hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py:173 parametrizes both 'completed' and 'done'. The only TS fixture hard-codes 'done' (docs-hosted-stub.ts:14). So if the service reports 'completed', or returns an empty `messages` list, every TS lesson's cleanup times out or throws. The live service can't be observed from here, but the branch's two helpers contradict each other.
findings.v2reason:
I ran the helper and the defect is real. `typescript/examples/shared/tutorial-cleanup.ts` is new on this branch (`git show ec9fc65:` finds no such file). Its `waitForTerminalExtraction` (lines 27-43) returns only when every per-message status is exactly "done" (line 38). It fails fast only on "error" or "failed" (line 37). Any other finished status loops until the deadline and then throws "Extraction deadline expired". It also throws "does not cover exactly the recorded messages" (line 36) when the response has an empty `messages` array and only a `summary`.

The rest of the repo contradicts it:
- The released Python client is unchanged on this branch. `src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:240-241` documents the per-message statuses as `pending` / `completed` / `failed`.
- `short_term.py:126-127` treats only pending, processing, running, in_progress and queued as unfinished.
- The Python unit test uses `"status": "completed"` (`tests/unit/nams/test_short_term.py:361`).
- This branch's own Python helper reads `summary`, not `messages`, and treats `{"done", "completed", "skipped"}` as finished (`docs/modules/ROOT/examples/hosted_tutorial_cleanup.py:51-58`).

Two helpers written for the same tutorial therefore disagree. Every TS lesson's cleanup goes through this function (`tutorial-cleanup.ts:118`), and so does the knowledge-graph lesson (`typescript/examples/vercel-ai/src/tutorials/knowledge-graph.ts:18`). If the service returns "completed", or returns an empty `messages` list, all of them fail.

Caveats:
- The failure is safe: nothing is deleted, so the reader loses no data. The reader just can't finish the lesson or its cleanup.
- The stub calls itself a fixture for "captured hosted routes" (`docs-hosted-stub.ts:1`). It returns `{id, status: "done", attempts: 1}`, which hints that the live service may really send "done". I can't observe the live service, so the real-world impact is unproven. The contradiction with the released Python SDK is concrete, and so is the lack of a TS test for "completed", "skipped" or summary-only responses.

I kept the severity at major. It drops to minor if the live service is confirmed to send only "done" with a full `messages` list.
findings.reproduction:
Scratch script: /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-lyonwj-github-neo4j-labs-agent-memory/66a2977c-9670-4b56-8270-fc84ea0f1100/scratchpad/review/repro-extraction.mts. It uses the branch's own stub (`typescript/examples/vercel-ai/test/docs-hosted-stub.ts`), seeds one message, sets `stub.behavior.extraction`, then calls `waitForTerminalExtraction(run, 3000, 200)` and `cleanupTutorial(run, {timeoutMs: 3000})`. A final case replaces `run.request` so it returns `{messages: [], summary: {completed: 1}}`.

Command (from typescript/examples/vercel-ai): `./node_modules/.bin/tsx <scratch>/repro-extraction.mts`

Output:
```
done -> returned OK in 1 ms
done cleanup complete= true
completed -> threw: Extraction deadline expired; no records were deleted. after 3000 ms
completed cleanup threw: Extraction deadline expired; no records were deleted. ; deletes= 0
skipped -> threw: Extraction deadline expired; no records were deleted. after 3001 ms
skipped cleanup threw: Extraction deadline expired; no records were deleted. ; deletes= 0
summary-only -> threw: Extraction status does not cover exactly the recorded messages.
```

Other checks:
- `git show ec9fc65:typescript/examples/shared/tutorial-cleanup.ts` fails, so the file is new on this branch.
- `git show ec9fc65:src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py | grep completed` finds line 241 (`pending` / `completed` / `failed`), so the Python client already documented "completed" before this branch.
- The existing TS test `tutorial-state-cleanup.test.ts:116` covers only pending, failed, error and unknown, each with `timeoutMs: 0`. No test covers "completed", "skipped" or a summary-only response.
- Neither the repo nor the audit evidence contains a captured live extraction-status payload that shows which value the service sends.

findings.title: MCP docs-assembly test builds from the SDK's own node_modules, not the lesson's install
findings.detail: The test claims to compile the tutorial's server as assembled from the page. It skips the page's `npm install ../typescript @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4` and instead symlinks `@modelcontextprotocol`, `@types` and `zod` from the SDK's own `typescript/node_modules`. That gives it a single zod copy, so it passes while the reader's install fails to typecheck (see the blocker finding). It also writes a bare `{ type: "module" }` package.json instead of the page's package fields. The test cannot fail on the dependency layout it is meant to guard.

docs-assembly.test.ts:47-49:
`await symlink(sdkRoot, join(directory, "node_modules", "@neo4j-labs", "agent-memory"));`
`for (const name of ["@modelcontextprotocol", "@types", "zod"]) await symlink(join(sdkRoot, "node_modules", name), join(directory, "node_modules", name));`

Compare mcp-server-typescript.adoc:62: `npm install ../typescript @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4`. The reader-path reproduction fails with TS2345, as shown in the blocker finding.
findings.fix: Have the test (or a separate opt-in check) install `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `zod` into the temp project as the page does, or pin them to versions different from the SDK's lockfile, so a duplicate zod copy is exercised. Alternatively, assert that the page's install command matches the layout the test builds.
findings.v1reason: typescript/examples/mcp/test/docs-assembly.test.ts:48-49 symlinks the SDK itself, plus `@modelcontextprotocol`, `@types` and `zod` from the SDK's own node_modules. It never runs the page's `npm install ... zod@^4`, and :51 writes a bare `{ type: "module" }` package.json. That layout always has a single zod copy, so the test passes while the reader's install fails typecheck (reproduced for finding 0). The test cannot catch the dependency failure a reader actually hits.
findings.v2reason:
The finding holds up when run. This branch adds typescript/examples/mcp/test/docs-assembly.test.ts; before it, typescript/examples/mcp only had a .env example and a README. Lines 48-52 of the test build a layout the reader never gets. They symlink the SDK as @neo4j-labs/agent-memory. They symlink @modelcontextprotocol, @types and zod from typescript/node_modules. They write a bare {type:"module"} package.json. They never run the page's `npm install ../typescript @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30 zod@^4` (mcp-server-typescript.adoc:62).

findings.detail: All TypeScript lesson commands and the MCP `start` script pass `--env-file-if-exists=.env`. Node added that flag in v22.9.0; on 22.0 to 22.8 node refuses to start with 'bad option'. The new partial typescript-tutorial-checkout.adoc:1 says 'Node.js 22 or later'. mcp-server-typescript.adoc:37 says the same, and its package.json snippet sets `engines: >=22.0.0` with `tsx --env-file-if-exists=.env`. The reference's `client.reasoning` section lists methods and bridge/hosted availability only. It says nothing about cleanup, deletion or retention of reasoning records. findings.fix: Add a short note to the `client.reasoning` section of reference/typescript-api.adoc: the hosted service has no verified delete route for steps or tool calls, so they persist until the workspace owner removes them. findings.title: Reasoning page newly labeled bolt-only ("raises NotSupportedError"), but NAMS implements these calls
findings.detail: This branch added the bolt-only banner to the reasoning-traces page. The banner says the APIs on the page raise NotSupportedError against NAMS. The Python NAMS backend does implement start_trace, add_step, record_tool_call, complete_trace, get_trace_with_steps and get_session_traces. It adapts them to conversation-level steps and tool calls, with the trace lifecycle built client-side. Only search_steps, get_similar_traces and list_traces raise. The banner therefore contradicts the source, the backend capabilities reference and the reasoning API reference. The actual limits on NAMS are different: complete_trace is kept only in memory, and TraceOutcome and error are not sent. A NAMS reader is told the whole feature is unavailable, and the real limits go unmentioned.
findings.evidence:
Offending: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/reasoning-traces.adoc:7 `include::partial$backend-bolt-only.adoc[]` -> docs/modules/ROOT/partials/backend-bolt-only.adoc:3 "*Available on NAMS: No.* The APIs on this page are *bolt-only* — calling them against the hosted NAMS backend raises `NotSupportedError`." (At ec9fc65 the page had no backend partial: `git show ec9fc65:.../reasoning-traces.adoc | grep partial$backend` -> empty.)
Source of truth: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/reasoning.py:165 `async def start_trace(...)`, :190 `add_step` (POST /v1/reasoning/steps), :206 `record_tool_call` (POST /v1/reasoning/tool-calls), :236 `complete_trace`, :281 `get_trace_with_steps`, :307 `get_session_traces`; none of these raise. Only :245 search_steps, :253 get_similar_traces and :331 list_traces raise NotSupportedError.
Other pages: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:50-52 "Python with NAMS:: Python accessors adapt supported service records; check each accessor's contract"; docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/reasoning.adoc:6 "NAMS stores conversation-level steps and tool calls and synthesizes the trace lifecycle locally."
findings.fix: Replace the bolt-only banner with backend-both, or with a page-specific note: the recipe is Bolt-only because it relies on persisted TraceOutcome/success, while NAMS supports the step and tool-call calls with a synthetic trace lifecycle. Point to reference/api/reasoning-search-stats.adoc for the NAMS lifecycle table.
findings.v1reason: reasoning-traces.adoc:7 includes partial$backend-bolt-only.adoc, which says (partials/backend-bolt-only.adoc:3) that the page's APIs raise NotSupportedError on NAMS. The page at ec9fc65 had no backend partial; its old NOTE said the core trace operations port to NAMS. In src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/reasoning.py, start_trace (:165), add_step (:190), record_tool_call (:206), complete_trace (:236) and get_trace_with_steps (:281) do not raise. Only search_steps (:245), get_similar_traces (:253), list_traces (:331) and get_tool_stats (:342) raise. The banner contradicts reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:50 and reference/api/reasoning.adoc:6. The recipe still would not pass on NAMS, but not because of NotSupportedError. complete_trace stores only kwargs 'outcome' and 'success', and the recipe passes no success kwarg, so `saved.success is False` fails. That real limit goes unmentioned.
findings.v2reason:
The finding is real. docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/reasoning-traces.adoc:7 includes partial$backend-bolt-only.adoc. That partial (docs/modules/ROOT/partials/backend-bolt-only.adoc:3) says "*Available on NAMS: No.* The APIs on this page are *bolt-only* — calling them against the hosted NAMS backend raises `NotSupportedError`." At ec9fc65 the page had no backend partial, and its old NOTE said the core trace operations port to NAMS, so this branch introduced the claim.

I ran every call the page's recipe makes (docs/modules/ROOT/examples/core_memory_recipes.py, tag=reasoning) against NamsReasoningMemory, which is what the NAMS client returns for `.reasoning` (src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/client.py:50,110). start_trace, add_step, record_tool_call, complete_trace and get_trace_with_steps all run without NotSupportedError. Only search_steps, get_similar_traces, list_traces and get_tool_stats raise it (nams/reasoning.py:245, 253, 331, 342). So the banner contradicts the source, and it also contradicts reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:50 ("Python accessors adapt supported service records") and reference/api/reasoning.adoc:6 ("NAMS stores conversation-level steps and tool calls and synthesizes the trace lifecycle locally"). docs/MAINTAINING.md records no deliberate exception for this banner.

Running the code turned up a different failure than the one reported. The recipe does fail on NAMS, but not with NotSupportedError. complete_trace(outcome=TraceOutcome(...)) stores the TraceOutcome object as-is (nams/reasoning.py:241). get_trace_with_steps then passes it to ReasoningTrace, whose outcome field only accepts a string, and pydantic raises ValidationError. Also, record_tool_call drops the `error` kwarg, because it is not in the request body (nams/reasoning.py:213-223). The page's own line 60 says "`complete_trace` accepts an outcome string or `TraceOutcome`". That is true on Bolt only, and the page never mentions these NAMS limits.

So "not suitable on NAMS" is roughly right for this particular recipe, but the stated mechanism (NotSupportedError) and scope ("the APIs on this page") are wrong. A NAMS reader is told the whole reasoning API is unavailable, and the real limits (in-memory trace lifecycle, TraceOutcome breaking readback, `error` dropped) go unmentioned. Major is the right severity: this is a wrong behaviour claim that contradicts two reference pages.

The suggested fix should also add one point: warn that on NAMS you must pass a string outcome plus `success=`, because passing a TraceOutcome breaks get_trace_with_steps.

findings.title: Merge claim that every copied edge carries the source id and migrated_from is wrong for most types
findings.detail: The page says each copied edge carries the source edge's `id` and a `migrated_from` property, and that this keeps the merge reversible and auditable. In MERGE_ENTITIES only the RELATED_TO copies get `id`. The MENTIONS and SAME_AS copies get neither `id` nor `migrated_from`; SAME_AS copies get match_type 'merged' instead. The EXTRACTED_FROM, EXTRACTED_BY, APPLIES_TO and TOUCHED copies get `migrated_from` but no `id`. A reader who plans to undo or audit a merge through `migrated_from` or `id` cannot tell copied MENTIONS or SAME_AS edges from original ones. The source docstring (long_term.py:1579-1582) makes the same overbroad claim, so it needs fixing too.
findings.evidence:
Offending: deduplication.adoc:63 "It copies rather than deletes: the source keeps its own edges so the merge stays reversible and auditable, and each copied edge carries the source edge's `id` plus a `migrated_from` property."
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:1023-1028 `MERGE (m)-[:MENTIONS]->(target)` (no properties set); :1033-1037 `MERGE (target)-[:SAME_AS {confidence: r.confidence, match_type: 'merged', created_at: datetime()}]-(other)` (no id/migrated_from); :1046-1053 and :1061-1068 RELATED_TO `nr.id = r.id ... nr.migrated_from = source.id`; :1075-1082 EXTRACTED_FROM, :1089-1094 EXTRACTED_BY, :1101-1102 APPLIES_TO, :1109-1112 TOUCHED set `migrated_from` but no `id`.
findings.fix: State the actual per-type behaviour: RELATED_TO copies keep the source `id` and gain `migrated_from`; provenance, APPLIES_TO and TOUCHED copies gain `migrated_from` only; MENTIONS and SAME_AS copies carry no marker. Alternatively, fix MERGE_ENTITIES so every copy is marked, and correct the docstring.
findings.v1reason: deduplication.adoc:63 is new on this branch (the old page has no migrated_from). It says each copied edge carries the source edge's id and migrated_from. In MERGE_ENTITIES (queries.py:1019+), the MENTIONS copy is a bare `MERGE (m)-[:MENTIONS]->(target)`. The SAME_AS copy sets only confidence, match_type 'merged' and created_at. The EXTRACTED_FROM, EXTRACTED_BY, APPLIES_TO and TOUCHED copies set migrated_from but no id. Only the RELATED_TO copies set both nr.id = r.id and nr.migrated_from. The docstring at long_term.py:1579-1582 repeats the overbroad claim. Rated minor rather than major: the list of copied types is correct, and only the marker detail is wrong.

findings.title: find_potential_duplicates confidence is always 0.0 on Bolt, and each pair is returned twice
findings.detail: The rewritten review section says find_potential_duplicates returns (entity1, entity2, confidence) tuples for pending pairs. On Bolt the query returns the relationship `r` through Result.data(), which turns a Relationship into a (start_props, type, end_props) tuple. A tuple has neither `_properties` nor `items`, so confidence falls back to 0.0 for every pair. The pattern is also undirected, so each SAME_AS edge comes back twice with the endpoints swapped. A reader who ranks or filters review candidates by that confidence gets zeros and duplicates. This is a source defect, but the new page states the contract without caveat.
findings.evidence:
Offending: deduplication.adoc:57 "`find_potential_duplicates(limit=...)` returns `(entity1, entity2, confidence)` tuples for pending pairs."
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:1001-1006 `MATCH (e1:Entity)-[r:SAME_AS]-(e2:Entity) WHERE r.status = 'pending' RETURN e1, e2, r`; src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/client.py:134 `data = await result.data()`; src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/long_term.py:1547-1555 `if hasattr(rel, "_properties") ... elif hasattr(rel, "items") ... else: rel_data = {}` then `confidence = rel_data.get("confidence", 0.0)`. Driver: `uv run python -c "import neo4j._data as d, inspect; print(inspect.getsource(d.RecordExporter))"` shows `elif isinstance(x, Relationship): return (self.transform(dict(x.start_node)), x.__class__.__name__, self.transform(dict(x.end_node)))`. The source comment at queries.py:364-366 notes the same flattening.
findings.fix: Fix the query to project `r.confidence AS confidence` and use a directed match (or `elementId(e1) < elementId(e2)`), then keep the doc. Until then, document that confidence is not populated and pairs appear twice in 0.6.0.
findings.v1reason: GET_POTENTIAL_DUPLICATES (queries.py:1001-1006) is an undirected match that returns `e1, e2, r`. Neo4jClient.execute_read runs `await result.data()` (client.py:134). The driver's RecordExporter.transform turns a Relationship into a (start_props, type, end_props) tuple; I printed the source with uv run to check. A tuple has neither `_properties` nor `items`, so long_term.py:1547-1554 yields confidence 0.0 for every row. Because the match is undirected, each SAME_AS edge is returned twice with the endpoints swapped. queries.py:364-366 documents the same flattening. The source defect predates the branch, and the old page also printed confidence. The branch's rewritten line (deduplication.adoc:57) restates the contract without a caveat, so this stays minor.

findings.title: Extraction pages say standalone extractors raise NotSupportedError on NAMS, but they never contact a backend
findings.detail: This branch added the bolt-only banner to entity-extraction.adoc, entity-extraction-batch.adoc and entity-extraction-schemas.adoc. The banner says calling the page's APIs against NAMS raises NotSupportedError. The same pages say the recipes do not connect to a database, and GLiNEREntityExtractor, ExtractionPipeline and StreamingExtractor run locally with no client. What actually differs is that Bolt pipeline configuration does not configure NAMS extraction. That is how backend-capabilities.adoc words it.
findings.evidence:
Offending: entity-extraction.adoc:7, entity-extraction-batch.adoc:7 and entity-extraction-schemas.adoc:7 `include::partial$backend-bolt-only.adoc[]` -> partials/backend-bolt-only.adoc:3 "calling them against the hosted NAMS backend raises `NotSupportedError`". The same page, entity-extraction.adoc:29: "These commands do not connect to a database or require an LLM API key."
Source: docs/modules/ROOT/examples/extraction_recipes.py:6-8 imports only local extractor classes and creates no MemoryClient. reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:59-60 "Python with NAMS::: Server-managed; Bolt pipeline options do not configure the service".
findings.fix: On the three extraction pages, replace the bolt-only partial with a short note: local extractors run without a backend, and the client pipeline configuration applies only to Bolt, because NAMS extraction is server-managed.
findings.v1reason: entity-extraction.adoc, entity-extraction-batch.adoc and entity-extraction-schemas.adoc each include partial$backend-bolt-only.adoc at line 7. The ec9fc65 versions had no backend partial. The partial says calling the page's APIs against NAMS raises NotSupportedError. entity-extraction.adoc:29 says the commands do not connect to a database, and examples/extraction_recipes.py imports only the local GLiNEREntityExtractor, ExtractionPipeline and StreamingExtractor classes, with no client. backend-capabilities.adoc:59 words the difference correctly: extraction is server-managed on NAMS, and Bolt pipeline options do not configure it.

findings.title: Catalog example's "Avoid duplicates" filter never matches GLiNER output types
findings.detail: The catalog example stores products as entity_type="PRODUCT". It then skips extracted entities whose type is "PRODUCT" or "BRAND" to avoid duplicates. This branch switched the extractor to the `business` schema. That schema's `product` label maps to (OBJECT, PRODUCT) and it has no brand label, so extracted entities never have type PRODUCT or BRAND. The filter excludes nothing. Every product name found in a description is stored again as a separate OBJECT entity and linked RELATED_TO the PRODUCT node.
findings.evidence:
Offending: batch-processing.adoc:420 `if entity.type not in ["PRODUCT", "BRAND"]:  # Avoid duplicates` with batch-processing.adoc:366 `GLiNEREntityExtractor.for_schema("business")`.
Source: `uv run python -c "from neo4j_agent_memory.extraction.gliner_extractor import get_schema; print(get_schema('business').entity_types.keys())"` -> dict_keys(['company', 'person', 'product', 'industry', 'financial_metric', 'location']); GLiNEREntityExtractor.DEFAULT_LABEL_MAPPING has 'product': ('OBJECT', 'PRODUCT'), and src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/gliner_extractor.py:444 returns `self.label_mapping[label_lower]`.
findings.fix: Filter on the mapped type and subtype, e.g. `if (entity.type, entity.subtype) == ("OBJECT", "PRODUCT") or entity.name in {product["name"], product.get("brand")}: continue`, or compare by name.
findings.v1reason: This branch changed the catalog example to use GLiNEREntityExtractor.for_schema('business'); the old 'ecommerce' schema is not among the eight listed. Running the extractor's label_mapping for that schema gives product -> ('OBJECT','PRODUCT') and company -> ('ORGANIZATION','COMPANY'), with no brand label. The mapping is applied at gliner_extractor.py:443-444. entity.type can therefore never be 'PRODUCT' or 'BRAND', and the filter `if entity.type not in ["PRODUCT", "BRAND"]` at batch-processing.adoc:420 excludes nothing. Extracted product and brand names are re-stored as OBJECT and ORGANIZATION entities.

findings.title: How-to index says the dedup page reviews a flagged SAME_AS pair; the recipe merges a manual pair
findings.detail: The index entry for the rewritten deduplication page says it reviews a flagged SAME_AS pair and confirms or rejects the merge. The page's runnable recipe creates two entities with deduplicate=False, so no SAME_AS flag is created. It then calls merge_duplicate_entities directly, and review_duplicate appears only in prose. Readers who pick the page from the index expect a confirm/reject workflow the recipe doesn't show.
findings.evidence:
Offending: how-to/index.adoc:32 "xref:how-to/deduplication.adoc[Merge a reviewed entity pair] -- Review a flagged `SAME_AS` duplicate pair and confirm or reject the merge."
Page: deduplication.adoc:7 "To combine two known duplicate entities, choose the source and target explicitly, merge that pair…"; examples/core_memory_recipes.py:163-170 `add_entity(..., deduplicate=False)` x2 then `store.merge_duplicate_entities(source.id, target.id)`.
findings.fix: Reword the index entry, e.g. "Merge a known duplicate pair and verify aliases; review flagged SAME_AS candidates with review_duplicate".
findings.v1reason: how-to/index.adoc:32 (added by this branch) says the page will 'Review a flagged `SAME_AS` duplicate pair and confirm or reject the merge.' findings.title: Redundant legacy anchors duplicate section auto-ids, so the sections render as _prerequisites_2 and _see_also_2
findings.detail: `anchor:_prerequisites[]` sits right before `== Prerequisites`, and `anchor:_see_also[]` right before `== See also`. findings.title: Newly published eval-harness docstring tells NAMS users to run the preference dimension, which is unsupported
findings.detail: This branch starts including examples/eval-harness/main.py in full on how-to/evaluation.adoc (include::example$eval-harness/main.py[] at line 219; the include and docs/extensions/example-files.json are both new since ec9fc65). The module docstring shown there tells readers: 'On NAMS, seed through the memory APIs and run --dimensions retrieval,preference'. On NAMS, the preference dimension calls long_term.get_preferences_for, which always raises NotSupportedError. The same page's Prerequisites say the opposite ('its preference calls are unsupported'). On top of that, build_settings() hard-codes backend="bolt", so the script cannot run against NAMS at all. examples/eval-harness/README.md:128 repeats the claim.
findings.evidence: examples/eval-harness/main.py:47-48: "On NAMS, seed through the memory APIs and run ``--dimensions retrieval,preference``." | src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/long_term.py:549-554: "async def get_preferences_for(...): raise NotSupportedError(backend=\"nams\", ... message=\"NAMS does not expose a preferences endpoint.\")" | src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/eval.py:214 calls self._client.long_term.get_preferences_for | docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/evaluation.adoc:19-21: "The hosted client exposes `eval`, but its preference calls are unsupported" | examples/eval-harness/main.py:123: backend="bolt"
findings.fix: Change the docstring (and README.md:128) to say that on NAMS only the retrieval dimension can run, through the reader's own client, and that this script is Bolt-only.
findings.v1reason: examples/eval-harness/main.py:47-48 says 'On NAMS, seed through the memory APIs and run --dimensions retrieval,preference'. The docstring was already there, but this branch publishes the file in full on evaluation.adoc:219 through the new example-files.json mapping. The branch also added backend="bolt" at main.py:123, so the script is Bolt-only. EvalMemory._eval_preference (src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/eval.py:214) calls long_term.get_preferences_for with no error handling, and the NAMS version (nams/long_term.py:549-554) always raises NotSupportedError. evaluation.adoc:19-21 says the hosted preference calls are unsupported, so the published script contradicts its own page. README.md:128 repeats the claim.
findings.v2reason:
The defect is real. examples/eval-harness/main.py:47-48 (and README.md:128) tell NAMS users to run `--dimensions retrieval,preference`. When I ran it, EvalMemory.run with a preference case on the NAMS LongTermMemory raises NotSupportedError, and nothing catches it: _eval_preference at src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/eval.py:214 calls get_preferences_for directly, and src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/long_term.py:549-554 always raises. So the whole run fails, including the retrieval dimension.

The branch did not write the sentence itself; it was already in the docstring at ec9fc65 (old line 40). The branch does make it wrong where readers see it, in three ways:
(1) It publishes the file in full on how-to/evaluation.adoc:219 through the new include and the new docs/extensions/example-files.json. That file does not exist at ec9fc65, and the old page had no example include.
(2) It adds the Prerequisites text at evaluation.adoc:19-21 ("its preference calls are unsupported"), so the page now contradicts the script it embeds.
(3) It adds backend="bolt" at main.py:123. The old file had no backend= line. With that line, the script cannot be pointed at NAMS at all.

Major fits: a wrong behaviour claim on a published page. The failure is loud (an exception), not silent, and it loses no data, so it is not a blocker.
findings.reproduction:
1) git show ec9fc65:examples/eval-harness/main.py | grep -n "On NAMS" -> 40 (the sentence predates the branch); | grep backend= -> no match (backend="bolt" is new, HEAD main.py:123).
2) git show ec9fc65:docs/extensions/example-files.json -> "fatal: path ... exists on disk, but not in 'ec9fc65'". git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/evaluation.adoc shows +include::example$eval-harness/main.py[] and +"client exposes `eval`, but its preference calls are unsupported".
3) Scratch script (scratchpad/eval_nams.py): built EvalMemory with _client.long_term set to the NAMS LongTermMemory class from neo4j_agent_memory.nams.long_term, then ran ev.run(EvalSuite(preference=[PreferenceCase(user_identifier="u", expected_active_pref_ids={"x"})]), dimensions=["retrieval","preference"]).
Output: "NotSupportedError LongTermMemory.get_preferences_for is not supported on the 'nams' backend. NAMS does not expose a preferences endpoint." The exception propagates out of run(), so no report is produced.
4) examples/eval-harness/main.py:120-123: build_settings() returns MemorySettings(backend="bolt", ...), and main.py:391 uses it by default, so the script cannot target NAMS.

findings.title: README says the runner ignores NEO4J_DATABASE, but main.py now reads it

findings.title: Claude Code .mcp.json snippet puts literal Aura password and OpenAI key in the committed project file
findings.detail: The Claude Code step tells readers to paste the Aura URI, username, password and an OpenAI key as literal values into the project-root `.mcp.json`, and says these fields need no interpolation. Two things on the same page contradict this. The `.mcp.json.example` template included on the page uses `${NEO4J_URI}`, `${NEO4J_USERNAME}`, `${NEO4J_PASSWORD}` and `${OPENAI_API_KEY}` expansion. The example README tells readers to copy that template to the project root and commit it because it holds no secret. So a reader who follows the page and then the README's copy/commit guidance ends up with a project-scoped file that contains database and model credentials. The page also dropped the old sentence explaining that Claude Code expands `${VAR}`.
findings.evidence: Page line 181: "For the stdio entry ... copy its URI, username and password into the literal JSON values. Also supply an OpenAI key ... these JSON fields do not require shell interpolation. Keep the populated credential file private." Page lines 198-202: "NEO4J_PASSWORD": "replace-with-your-Aura-password", "OPENAI_API_KEY": "replace-with-your-OpenAI-key". The template included at page line 90 (examples/claude-code-team-memory/.mcp.json.example:27-28): "NEO4J_USER": "${NEO4J_USERNAME}", "NEO4J_PASSWORD": "${NEO4J_PASSWORD}". examples/claude-code-team-memory/README.md:102: "# Claude Code (project scope — commit it, it holds no secret)".
findings.fix: Make the inline Claude Code snippet match the included template: use `${NEO4J_URI}`, `${NEO4J_USERNAME}`, `${NEO4J_PASSWORD}`, `${OPENAI_API_KEY}` and `${USER}`. Restore the sentence saying Claude Code expands `${VAR}`/`${VAR:-default}`, so no secret lands in the committed file. Keep literal values only for the Desktop and Cursor configs, which must stay untracked.
findings.v1reason: team-memory-in-your-editor.adoc:181 tells the reader to paste the Aura URI, username and password, plus an OpenAI key, as literal JSON values into the project-root .mcp.json, and the inline snippet at lines 186-208 has literal NEO4J_PASSWORD and OPENAI_API_KEY values. The template the same page includes at line 90 (examples/claude-code-team-memory/.mcp.json.example) uses ${NEO4J_URI}, ${NEO4J_USERNAME}, ${NEO4J_PASSWORD} and ${OPENAI_API_KEY}. README.md:102 says to copy that template to ../../.mcp.json and 'commit it, it holds no secret'. The branch introduced the problem: at ec9fc65 lines 136-137 said 'Project scope, so it is committed ... ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} are expanded from the environment, so no secret lands in git', and the old snippet used ${VAR}. 'Keep the populated credential file private' only partly helps, because a project-scope .mcp.json is meant to be committed.
findings.v2reason:
The defect is real, and the branch introduced it. At HEAD, docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/team-memory-in-your-editor.adoc:181 tells the reader to "copy its URI, username and password into the literal JSON values" of the project-root `.mcp.json`, adds that "these JSON fields do not require shell interpolation", and ends with "Keep the populated credential file private". The inline snippet (lines 186-208) sets literal values for NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD and OPENAI_API_KEY.

Three things contradict it:
- The template the same page includes at line 90 (examples/claude-code-team-memory/.mcp.json.example) uses `${NEO4J_URI}`, `${NEO4J_USERNAME}`, `${NEO4J_PASSWORD}`, `${USER}`, `${NEO4J_DATABASE:-neo4j}` and `${OPENAI_API_KEY}`.
- The linked maintained README (examples/claude-code-team-memory/README.md:102) says "Claude Code (project scope — commit it, it holds no secret)".
- The README's own prose tells Claude Code users to export OPENAI_API_KEY because "its template expands `${OPENAI_API_KEY}`".

At the merge base (ec9fc65), the page said at lines 136-137: "Project scope, so it is committed and every teammate gets it. `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` are expanded from the environment, so no secret lands in git". Its snippet used `${NEO4J_PASSWORD}` (line 155). The branch removed that guidance and switched to literal credentials in the file that is conventionally committed.

Two things soften the risk:
- The page itself says "Keep the populated credential file private" (line 181), and line 47 says "Configure private editor copies separately in step 3".
- This repo's own .gitignore:92 ignores `.mcp.json`, so within this repo the README's "commit it" would silently not stage it.

The page, however, targets the reader's own `agent-memory-tutorials/` folder. That folder has no such ignore rule, and the page never says to add one. So a normal `git add -A` there stages the credential-bearing `.mcp.json`. Because of the "keep private" caveat I don't rate this a blocker. Major is about right: it reverses correct security guidance, contradicts the template and README shown on the same page, and a reader who follows the page and the linked README can plausibly commit an Aura password and an OpenAI key.
findings.reproduction:
1. Page text at HEAD:
   sed -n 80,230p docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/team-memory-in-your-editor.adoc
   Line 181 contains "copy its URI, username and password into the literal JSON values ... these JSON fields do not require shell interpolation. Keep the populated credential file private." The snippet has "NEO4J_PASSWORD": "replace-with-your-Aura-password" and "OPENAI_API_KEY": "replace-with-your-OpenAI-key".

2. The included template:
   cat examples/claude-code-team-memory/.mcp.json.example
   Its env block is "NEO4J_URI": "${NEO4J_URI}", "NEO4J_USER": "${NEO4J_USERNAME}", "NEO4J_PASSWORD": "${NEO4J_PASSWORD}", "OPENAI_API_KEY": "${OPENAI_API_KEY}". docs/extensions/example-files.json:8 maps team-memory/.mcp.json.example to this file.

3. The README:
   sed -n 90,115p examples/claude-code-team-memory/README.md
   Line 102 reads "# Claude Code (project scope — commit it, it holds no secret)", followed by "cp .mcp.json.example ../../.mcp.json".

4. The old page:
   git show ec9fc65:docs/.../team-memory-in-your-editor.adoc | grep -n VAR
   Lines 136-137: "Project scope, so it is committed and every teammate gets it. `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` are expanded from the environment, so no secret lands in git." Line 155: "NEO4J_PASSWORD": "${NEO4J_PASSWORD}".

5. Simulating a reader, in a scratch dir (scratchpad/review/mcpjson/agent-memory-tutorials):
   - Ran git init.
   - Saved the template to team-memory/ as the page says.
   - Extracted the page's inline Claude Code snippet to .mcp.json and parsed it. Output: {'NEO4J_URI': 'neo4j+s://<instance-id>.databases.neo4j.io', 'NEO4J_USER': 'neo4j', 'NEO4J_DATABASE': 'neo4j', 'NEO4J_PASSWORD': 'replace-with-your-Aura-password', 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'replace-with-your-OpenAI-key', ...}
   - `git add -A; git status --short` gave "A  .mcp.json" and "A  team-memory/.mcp.json.example".
   - `git check-ignore .mcp.json` gave "not ignored".
   - `grep -c '${'` found 6 matches in the template and 0 in the inline snippet.

6. Mitigations:
   - The page says "Keep the populated credential file private" (line 181).
   - The repo's .gitignore:92 lists `.mcp.json` (git check-ignore -v confirms), but that covers only this repo, not the reader's tutorial folder.
   - doctor.py only flags literal `nams_` keys (lines 184-189), not Neo4j or OpenAI secrets, so it would not catch this.

findings.title: Index says multi-tenancy scopes entities to users; the target page and scope reference say it does not
findings.detail: The how-to index says the multi-tenancy guide scopes conversations, entities and preferences to individual users. The rewritten guide and the scope reference say `user_identifier` is accepted only on some writes, is not accepted by Bolt `add_entity`, and does not filter entity searches. Entity knowledge is shared within a database or workspace. The index therefore overstates the isolation guarantee, which is a security-relevant behaviour claim.
findings.evidence: index.adoc:47: "Scope conversations, entities, and preferences to individual users in a multi-tenant deployment." how-to/multi-tenancy.adoc:46: "It is not accepted by every API; for example, Bolt `add_entity` does not take this argument." reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:132: "It is not a universal parameter and does not automatically filter entity, preference or trace searches." reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:148: "Entity knowledge can be shared within the selected database/workspace."
findings.fix: Reword the blurb, for example: "Associate supported conversation, message and preference writes with a user and use explicitly scoped reads; this is not access control."
findings.v1reason: index.adoc:47 (a new blurb; the old one also overclaimed) says the guide scopes 'conversations, entities, and preferences to individual users'. The target page contradicts this at multi-tenancy.adoc:7 ('does not establish user authentication or database access control') and :46 ('Bolt `add_entity` does not take this argument'). So does reference/backend-capabilities.adoc: the scope table says user_identifier 'does not automatically filter entity, preference or trace searches', and the paragraph before the [#mcp] block says 'Entity knowledge can be shared within the selected database/workspace'. Overstating tenant isolation is security-relevant, so this stays major.
findings.v2reason:
The finding holds. Branch commit c90d191 wrote the new blurb at docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/index.adoc:47: "Scope conversations, entities, and preferences to individual users in a multi-tenant deployment." That claim is contradicted by the page it links to and by the source code.

- The linked guide says at multi-tenancy.adoc:7 that it "does not establish user authentication or database access control". At multi-tenancy.adoc:46 it says "Bolt `add_entity` does not take this argument".
- reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:132 says `user_identifier` "does not automatically filter entity, preference or trace searches". Line 148 of the same page says "Entity knowledge can be shared within the selected database/workspace."
- The source code agrees with the guide and the reference, not with the blurb. At HEAD, `LongTermMemory.add_entity`, `search_entities` and `search_preferences` have no `user_identifier` parameter. Only `add_preference`, `get_preferences_for` and `ShortTermMemory.add_message` accept it.

The index therefore promises per-user scoping of entities, and of preferences in general, that the SDK does not provide. Readers could wrongly believe tenants are isolated from each other, which is a security concern.

The old index at ec9fc65 also overclaimed ("keeps tenants isolated", "scope writes and reads per end-user"). This branch rewrote the blurb and kept the overclaim, and it now contradicts the rewritten target page on the same branch. That makes it a defect introduced by this branch's change. findings.title: Several index blurbs overclaim relative to the rewritten pages (offline, ontology effect, migration effort, audit)
findings.detail: Four new index descriptions promise more than the pages deliver. Run without an LLM: the index says fully offline, but the page says an Aura network connection is still required. Ontology: the index says the page confirms the ontology applies to new entities, but the page only verifies the active binding and says extraction is verified separately. Migrate: the index says minimal code changes, but the page requires an inventory and the replacement of unsupported paths. Privacy: the index says encrypt at rest and audit who accessed what, but the page records explicit audit nodes and says no client setting installs an encrypter.
findings.evidence: index.adoc:53 "so the client runs fully offline, with no API keys" vs running-without-an-llm.adoc: "This example stores its memory in AuraDB, so a network connection to Aura is still required." index.adoc:24 "confirm it applies to new entities" vs use-ontologies.adoc:103 "That lesson does not test rejection of an unknown entity label" and :109 "Ontology activation, direct entity writes and asynchronous message extraction have different success criteria." index.adoc:23 "with minimal code changes" vs use-nams.adoc:114 "Configuration alone does not migrate stored data or make all Bolt operations available." index.adoc:51 "Encrypt sensitive memory fields at rest and audit who accessed what" vs privacy-and-audit.adoc:17-18 "there is no client setting that installs an encrypter."
findings.fix: Align each blurb with its page: "...without constructing an LLM provider (Aura still required)"; "...activate a version and verify the active binding"; "...inventory unsupported operations and verify against a sandbox"; "Record explicit audit events and mark conversations for archival".
findings.v1reason: All four mismatches checked out. running-without-an-llm.adoc:11 says 'a network connection to Aura is still required', but index.adoc:53 says 'fully offline'. use-ontologies.adoc:103 and :109 say activation is verified separately from extraction, while index.adoc:24 says the page will 'confirm it applies to new entities'. migrate-to-nams.adoc:6 calls for inventorying and replacing unsupported paths, and use-nams.adoc:114 says 'Configuration alone does not migrate stored data', versus 'minimal code changes' at index.adoc:23. privacy-and-audit.adoc:17-18 says 'there is no client setting that installs an encrypter', versus 'Encrypt sensitive memory fields at rest' at index.adoc:51. All four blurbs are new on this branch.

findings.title: Cursor prose refers to ${VAR} expansion that the included cursor template does not use
findings.detail: The Cursor subsection says to paste the key into the Authorization header "if your build does not expand ${VAR}". That implies the template uses `${VAR}`. The cursor_mcp.json.example included on the same page already has a literal placeholder and no variable. README.md: "If your Cursor build does expand `${VAR}`, use that instead of pasting."
findings.fix: Say: "Replace REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_NAMS_KEY (or use ${MEMORY_API_KEY} if your Cursor build expands variables) and keep the file untracked."
findings.v1reason: The sentence at page lines 233-234 is unchanged from main. However, the branch now includes cursor_mcp.json.example on the page (line 110), and that file has a literal 'Bearer REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_NAMS_KEY' with no ${VAR}. findings.title: Cloud embeddings recipe raises TypeError for both Bedrock and Vertex before any database write
findings.detail: `main()` calls `settings(embedding=embedder)` with a legacy `BedrockEmbedder` or `VertexAIEmbedder`. `MemorySettings._resolve_providers` only accepts an EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an `EmbeddingProvider` protocol instance. The old embedders expose `embed(text)`, `embed_batch` and a `_model` attribute but have no `model` or `embed_one`, so construction raises TypeError. As a result, both `python integrations/cloud_embeddings_recipe.py bedrock` (aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:83) and `... vertex` (google-cloud.adoc:94) print the vector check and then crash. Neither page's 'Expected ... then stored-message verification' step can succeed. aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:107 also says 'The recipe's shared setup accepts the explicit embedder object', which is false. The offline contract test (tests/docs/test_python_integration_contracts.py:257-283) only exercises `build_embedder` and `verify_vectors`. It never passes the embedder through `common.settings` or `main()`, so it passes (32 passed) while the program cannot run.
findings.evidence: Command: NEO4J_URI=… NEO4J_USERNAME=n NEO4J_PASSWORD=p AWS_REGION=us-east-1 GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=p GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-central1 uv run python -c "...common.settings(embedding=cloud.build_embedder(p))" -> 'bedrock ERR TypeError MemorySettings.embedding must be EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an EmbeddingProvider instance; got BedrockEmbedder.' and 'vertex ERR TypeError ... got VertexAIEmbedder.' Source of truth: src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:720-730 (isinstance check against llm.protocol.EmbeddingProvider, which requires model/dimensions/embed/embed_one per src/neo4j_agent_memory/llm/protocol.py:157-197). Other docs show the correct pattern: reference/api/adapters.adoc:226 ('construct VertexAIEmbedder(...) directly and pass it as embedder= to MemoryClient') and configure-embedding-provider.adoc:110-121 (BedrockEmbeddingProvider).
findings.fix: Pass an `EmbeddingProvider` instead. For example, `settings(embedding=from_provider('bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0', kind='embedding', aws_region=os.environ['AWS_REGION']))` and `settings(embedding='vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001')` both construct (Bedrock gives 1024 dims, Vertex 768). Alternatively, pass the legacy embedder with `MemoryClient(settings(embedding=<matching provider>), embedder=embedder)`. Fix the Bedrock page:107 sentence to match, and add a contract test that calls `common.settings(embedding=cloud.build_embedder(p))` or `cloud.main` with a stubbed client.
findings.v1reason: I reproduced it. cloud_embeddings_recipe.py:41 passes the legacy embedder into common.settings(embedding=embedder), and common.py:17 forwards it to BoltSettings(embedding=...). I imported common and cloud_embeddings_recipe from docs/modules/ROOT/examples/integrations with dummy env vars and ran common.settings(embedding=cloud.build_embedder(p)). Output: 'bedrock ERR TypeError MemorySettings.embedding must be EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an EmbeddingProvider instance; got BedrockEmbedder.' and the same for VertexAIEmbedder. The check is at src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:726-735. Both documented run commands (aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:83 and google-cloud.adoc:94) crash after the vector check. aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:107 ('The recipe's shared setup accepts the explicit embedder object') is false. tests/docs/test_python_integration_contracts.py:259-283 only exercises build_embedder and verify_vectors, never settings() or main().
findings.v2reason: The finding holds. docs/modules/ROOT/examples/integrations/cloud_embeddings_recipe.py is new on this branch: `git show ec9fc65:<path>` says it does not exist at the merge-base. At line 41, `main()` passes the legacy embedder from `build_embedder()` (BedrockEmbedder at lines 15-17, VertexAIEmbedder at lines 18-23) to `settings(embedding=embedder)`. common.py:10-19 forwards it to `BoltSettings(embedding=...)`. src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py (lines ~728-736 at HEAD) accepts only an EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an instance of `llm.protocol.EmbeddingProvider`. That protocol needs `embed_one`, which neither legacy class has, so both raise TypeError. BedrockEmbedder also lacks `model`. The error comes before `MemoryClient` connects, and only after `verify_vectors` has already printed its success line. So both documented commands crash, and neither page's stored-message verification step can succeed: `python integrations/cloud_embeddings_recipe.py bedrock` (aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:83) and `... vertex` (google-cloud.adoc:94). aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:107 ("The recipe's shared setup accepts the explicit embedder object, so OpenAI credentials are not required here.") is false. Blocker severity is right: a reader who follows either page exactly gets a crash. No data is lost.
findings.reproduction:
From docs/modules/ROOT/examples/integrations, with dummy env vars (NEO4J_URI=bolt://localhost:1 NEO4J_USERNAME=n NEO4J_PASSWORD=p AWS_REGION=us-east-1 GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=p GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-central1):
uv run --project <repo> python -c "import common, cloud_embeddings_recipe as cloud; for each p in bedrock/vertex: e=cloud.build_embedder(p); print(type(e).__name__, hasattr(e,'model'), hasattr(e,'embed_one')); common.settings(embedding=e)"
Output:
bedrock BedrockEmbedder False False
bedrock ERR TypeError MemorySettings.embedding must be EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an EmbeddingProvider instance; got BedrockEmbedder.
vertex VertexAIEmbedder True False
vertex ERR TypeError MemorySettings.embedding must be EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an EmbeddingProvider instance; got VertexAIEmbedder.
The raising branch is in src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py: `if not isinstance(self.embedding, _EP): raise TypeError(...)`. `git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/examples/integrations/cloud_embeddings_recipe.py` gives "exists on disk, but not in 'ec9fc65'", so this branch added the file. grep shows the pages that include it and give the run commands: aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:62/83/107 and google-cloud.adoc:65/94.

findings.title: Hybrid 'explicit route' verification cannot fail; search errors are swallowed
findings.detail: The recipe treats `result.filters_applied['memory_types_searched'] == ['message']` as evidence that the route was selected. HybridMemoryProvider fills that field from the caller's own `memory_types` argument under the EXPLICIT strategy, whether or not any search ran. The parent search also catches every exception from `short_term.search_messages` and only logs it at debug level. A missing vector index or a dimension mismatch therefore still prints 'Verified stored message and explicit route'. aws-hybrid-memory.adoc:86 presents this as a confirmation step.
findings.evidence: hybrid_recipe.py:34 `if result.filters_applied.get("memory_types_searched") != ["message"]`. src/neo4j_agent_memory/integrations/agentcore/hybrid.py:287-289 (EXPLICIT keeps supplied memory_types) and :348 `result.filters_applied["memory_types_searched"] = memory_types`. memory_provider.py:291 `logger.debug(f"Message search failed: {e}")`. aws-hybrid-memory.adoc:86 "then confirms `memory_types_searched == [\"message\"]`".
findings.fix: Describe the check as reporting the configured route, not verifying it. Alternatively, assert that message search returned the stored id (for example with threshold 0.0 and a session filter), or call `client.short_term.search_messages` directly so that errors surface.
findings.v1reason: hybrid.py:287-289 keeps the caller's memory_types under EXPLICIT, and :350 sets filters_applied['memory_types_searched'] = memory_types unconditionally. memory_provider.py:277-291 wraps search_messages in try/except and only logs `logger.debug(f"Message search failed: {e}")`. The check at hybrid_recipe.py:34 therefore cannot fail. aws-hybrid-memory.adoc:86 presents it as a confirmation. The separate persistence check (get_session_memories readback, lines 22-24) is real, so the impact is limited.
