findings.title: ADK recipe iterates event.content.parts without guarding for None
findings.detail: `google.genai.types.Content.parts` is Optional and defaults to None. A final-response event whose content has no parts (for example an empty or blocked model reply) makes the join raise TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable. The run then fails with a confusing error instead of reaching persistence and readback.
findings.evidence: google_adk_recipe.py:39-40 `if event.is_final_response() and event.content:` / `print("".join(part.text or "" for part in event.content.parts))`. Installed google-genai 2.22.0: `types.Content.model_fields['parts']` -> 'annotation=Union[list[Part], NoneType] required=False default=None'.
findings.fix: Guard with `and event.content.parts`, or iterate `event.content.parts or []`.
findings.v1reason: google_adk_recipe.py:39-40 guards only `event.content` and then iterates `event.content.parts`. Installed google-genai reports Content.parts as `annotation=Union[list[Part], NoneType] required=False default=None`. A final event with content but parts=None raises TypeError before persistence. The project's own notes call out this ADK case ('ADK events can have content set but content.parts as None').

microsoft-agent.adoc:113 at HEAD says: "`create_memory_tools(...)` returns tool definitions that require the corresponding execution path; inspect the installed adapter before translating them into framework tool objects."

The source disagrees. src/neo4j_agent_memory/integrations/microsoft_agent/tools.py:27-35 declares `-> list[FunctionTool]`, and its docstring says: "Returns FunctionTool instances that the agent framework auto-invokes during streaming. No manual ``execute_memory_tool()`` dispatch needed." The docstring's own example passes them straight in with `chat_client.as_agent(tools=tools)`.

Running the function confirms it. With include_gds_tools=False it returned 6 objects of type agent_framework._tools.FunctionTool (search_memory, remember_preference, recall_preferences, search_knowledge, remember_fact, find_similar_tasks), and isinstance(..., agent_framework.FunctionTool) is True. Nothing needs translating, and no separate execution path is needed.

The branch caused this. At ec9fc65 the page described the behaviour correctly: line 250 said "tools are callable `FunctionTool` instances that the agent framework auto-invokes during `agent.run()`", and line 705 was an API row saying the same thing. The branch removed both and put the wrong sentence in their place. Line 113 is now the only place on the page, or in reference/api/adapters.adoc, that mentions create_memory_tools, so nothing else on the page corrects it.

A reader following the page would write needless wrapping or dispatch code, or would decide the tools can't be passed straight to the agent. That makes this a wrong API/behaviour claim, so major is the right severity.

   Output: 6 ['agent_framework._tools.FunctionTool', ...] ['search_memory','remember_preference','recall_preferences','search_knowledge','remember_fact','find_similar_tasks'] / True
3) git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/integrations/microsoft-agent.adoc | grep -n FunctionTool
   Output: line 250 "tools are callable `FunctionTool` instances that the agent framework auto-invokes during `agent.run()`", plus lines 410, 545 and 705. None of these survive at HEAD.

findings.title: Overstates what the OpenAI Agents recipe does, and nothing tests the Agents SDK path
findings.detail: The page says main() passes make_recall_tool(memory) and that the recipe exercises the wrapper on every run. In the code, the tool is built from memory_holder[0] inside a nested run() and only registered with the Agent. Whether the model calls it is the model's choice. Also, openai-agents is not in uv.lock and not installed in the venv. The contract test calls exercise() with a fake run that has no bind_memory, so make_recall_tool, the tagged function_tool snippet the page includes, and main()'s Agent/Runner code are never imported or run. MAINTAINING.md says missing framework dependencies fail the contract suite, but this path is simply never checked.
findings.evidence: openai-agents.adoc:119: "`main()` passes `tools=[make_recall_tool(memory)]` into `Agent(...)`, so the shipped recipe exercises the wrapper on every run". openai_agents_recipe.py:69-78: `async def run(prompt, context): agent = Agent(..., tools=[make_recall_tool(memory_holder[0])]) ...; run.bind_memory = memory_holder.append`. `uv run --no-sync python -c "import agents"` gives ModuleNotFoundError. `grep '^name = "openai-agents"' uv.lock` gives no output. tests/docs/test_python_integration_contracts.py:160-175 passes its own `run` without bind_memory.
findings.fix: Say the recipe registers the tool and the model may call it. Add a contract test that installs openai-agents, or mocks `agents.function_tool`/`Runner.run`, so make_recall_tool and main() are at least imported and built.
findings.v1reason: openai_agents_recipe.py:69-78 only registers make_recall_tool on the Agent, so 'exercises the wrapper on every run' (openai-agents.adoc:119) overstates it: the model decides whether to call the tool. The contract test (test_python_integration_contracts.py:160-175) passes a plain `run` without bind_memory, so make_recall_tool and main() are never run. Signature (inspect): `async` ShortTermMemory.get_conversation(self, session_id, *, conversation_id=None, limit=None, since=None) -> Conversation. common.py:23 correctly uses `conversation = await client.short_term.get_conversation(session_id)`.

findings.title: Next.js guide pairs persistInteractions:false with an assistant-only write pattern, so user turns are lost
findings.detail: The guide sends readers who need a guaranteed write to the edge-runtime 'application-owned write pattern' and tells them to pass `persistInteractions: false` to `createNamsProvider` 'so the response is not stored twice'. That pattern writes only the assembled assistant answer, because it relies on the SDK middleware's `persistResponses: false`, which still persists the user's input. In the NAMS provider, `persistInteractions: false` turns off the whole `persistTurn`, including the user-message write. A reader who combines the two instructions stores the assistant answers and never stores the user turns, so the transcript and the provider's later retrieval are missing half of each exchange.
findings.evidence:
nextjs-memory-chat.adoc:165-169: "use the xref:how-to/typescript/edge-runtime.adoc[application-owned write pattern] and pass `persistInteractions: false` to `createNamsProvider` so the response is not stored twice."
edge-runtime.adoc:72-73: ". Disable automatic assistant persistence (`persistResponses: false`). . On a successful stream end, call `addMessage` once with the assembled answer."
Source: typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src/vercel-ai-provider-middleware.ts:115-121: `async function persistTurn(params, assistantText) { if (!persist) return; ... if (userText) await client.shortTerm.addMessage(convId, 'user', userText)` (the user write is skipped when persist is false). typescript/src/middleware/vercel-ai.ts:244-254: the SDK middleware's persistInput is separate from persistResponses.
findings.fix: State that `persistInteractions: false` disables both user and assistant writes in the provider. Tell the reader to write both turns in the application-owned lifecycle (the user message, then the assembled answer, then `waitUntil`). Alternatively, point to the SDK middleware with `persistResponses: false`, which keeps input persistence.
findings.v1reason: The branch added nextjs-memory-chat.adoc:165-169 (diff +175/+176), which pairs the edge-runtime 'application-owned write pattern' with `persistInteractions: false`. The pattern at edge-runtime.adoc:72-73 writes only the assembled assistant answer. It depends on the SDK middleware's `persistResponses: false` and leaves user input persistence (`persistInput`) on (typescript/src/middleware/vercel-ai.ts:243-254). The Cloudflare example handlers.ts:129/197 follows the same shape and only calls addMessage for 'assistant'. In the provider, `persistTurn` returns early when `!persist` (vercel-ai-provider-middleware.ts:116-117), and `persist = config.persistInteractions ?? true` (line 200). That early return also skips the user addMessage at lines 119-122. A reader who follows both instructions never stores user turns.
findings.v2reason:
The finding holds. This branch added nextjs-memory-chat.adoc:165-169 (diff lines +175/+176). Those lines tell readers who need a guaranteed write to use the edge-runtime "application-owned write pattern" and to pass `persistInteractions: false` to `createNamsProvider` "so the response is not stored twice". That pattern, also rewritten on this branch (edge-runtime.adoc:72-73), writes only the assistant answer. It keeps user-input persistence because it depends on the SDK middleware's `persistResponses: false` (typescript/src/middleware/vercel-ai.ts:243-254, where `persistInput` is separate). The Cloudflare example follows it and calls addMessage only for "assistant" (handlers.ts:129, :197).

In the provider, `persist = config.persistInteractions ?? true` (vercel-ai-provider-middleware.ts:200), and `persistTurn` returns immediately when `!persist` (lines 116-117). That early return skips both the user write (lines 119-122) and the assistant write. The provider has no option that turns off only the assistant write. `persistUserPrompt` in vercel-ai-provider-hooks.ts belongs to the separate hooks API, not `createNamsProvider`.

The package's own test says the same. vercel-ai-provider-middleware.test.ts:335-342 wraps with `persistInteractions: false` and asserts that `fake.shortTerm.addMessage` is never called, which rules out the user write too. So a reader who follows both pages stores assistant answers and never stores user turns. The transcript and the provider's later retrieval then miss half of each exchange. That is a wrong behaviour claim that loses data silently, so major is the right severity; you could argue for blocker, but it only affects the advanced, opt-in path.
findings.reproduction:
1) sed -n 115,125p typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src/vercel-ai-provider-middleware.ts shows `async function persistTurn(params, assistantText) { if (!persist) return; ... if (userText) await client.shortTerm.addMessage(convId, 'user', userText) ... if (assistantText) await client.shortTerm.addMessage(convId, 'assistant', assistantText)`. Line 200: `const persist = config.persistInteractions ?? true;`.
2) grep -rn "persistInteractions|persistInput|persistUser" typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src: persistInteractions is the only persistence switch on the provider/middleware path. persistUserPrompt appears only in vercel-ai-provider-hooks.ts, a different API.
3) The test at vercel-ai-provider-middleware.test.ts:335-342 calls createNamsMemory({ apiKey:'k', persistInteractions:false }).wrap(...), then doGenerate(...), then `expect(fake.shortTerm.addMessage).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`.
4) cd typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider && npx vitest run test/vercel-ai-provider-middleware.test.ts -t persist: "Tests 10 passed | 8 skipped (18)". The persistInteractions=false test passes, so no addMessage call is made, the user write included.
5) grep for addMessage in typescript/examples/cloudflare-agents-edge/src finds handlers.ts:129 `persistResponses: false` and handlers.ts:197 `addMessage(turn.conversationId, "assistant", turn.answer)`. The application code writes only the assistant turn.
6) git diff ec9fc65..HEAD on nextjs-memory-chat.adoc shows the application-owned-pattern/persistInteractions sentence as added lines (+175/+176). The edge-runtime.adoc steps "Disable automatic assistant persistence (`persistResponses: false`)" and "call `addMessage` once with the assembled answer" are also added by this branch.

findings.title: Mastra follow-up snippet stores only the assistant reply in the new thread and drops the user turn
findings.detail: The rewritten cross-thread snippet sends a new user question to the agent in the second thread, then saves only the assistant reply to `second.id`. The user question is never persisted, so the second thread opens with an assistant message that answers nothing. This contradicts the page's own procedure step 3 ('Save the new user and assistant messages under that thread id') and the runnable example, which saves both.

findings.title: Docs imply omitting conversationId starts a new conversation; it silently reuses the user's latest
findings.detail: The landing page tells readers to create one instance per user session and to pass a conversationId only when they have one to resume. That implies leaving it out starts a new conversation. In the source, a scope without conversationId resolves to the user's most recent conversation (listConversations limit 1), and a new one is created only when the user has none. So every 'fresh session' in the provider, middleware and tools demos writes into the same NAMS conversation, and the offline test asserts exactly that. None of the seven pages says so. A reader who wants a separate conversation per session will not pass an id and will get every session merged into one. Their 'current conversation' search then returns old sessions, and crossSessionLimit has no other conversations to search.
findings.evidence: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/typescript/nams-ai-provider.adoc:104-106: "construct one provider/middleware/tools/hooks instance per user session, and pass a `conversationId` once you have one to resume."  Source: typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src/vercel-ai-provider-client.ts:83 "/** The conversation id: the given one, else the cached one, else the user's latest, else a new one. */" and :100-105 `const convs = await client.shortTerm.listConversations({ userId: scope.userId, limit: 1 }); if (convs.length > 0) { ... return convs[0].id; }`. Test: typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/test/docs-pages.test.ts:136 `expect(stub.conversations.size).toBe(1);` after the provider demo's 'Session 2 -- fresh session, same user'. grep for 'latest|most recent|new conversation' across the 7 pages finds no statement of this rule.
findings.fix: Say it outright on the landing page (and in the reference's NamsScope section): without conversationId, the package resumes the user's most recent conversation and creates one only if none exists. To start a new conversation, create one and pass its id. Note on the provider and middleware pages that 'fresh session' means a fresh JS object, not a new NAMS conversation.
findings.v1reason: how-to/typescript/nams-ai-provider.adoc:104-106 says to 'construct one ... instance per user session, and pass a conversationId once you have one to resume', which implies that leaving it out starts a new conversation. The source says otherwise. vercel-ai-provider-client.ts:83-105 (resolveConversation) uses the given id, then the cached one, then the user's latest via listConversations({limit:1}), and creates a new conversation only when the user has none. None of the 7 pages says this. grep for 'latest', 'most recent' and 'new conversation' finds only unrelated hits. provider-mode.adoc:167 describes 'fresh session, same user' as a new provider object, and never says it is the same NAMS conversation. The offline test asserts stub.conversations.size === 1 (docs-pages.test.ts:136). My own run of tools mode also left a single conversation.
findings.v2reason:
The defect is real, and this branch introduced it. All seven NAMS AI provider pages are new on this branch (git diff --stat ec9fc65..HEAD shows nams-ai-provider.adoc +148, provider-mode +232, reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc +432, and so on).

What the docs say:
- docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/typescript/nams-ai-provider.adoc:104-106: "`NamsScope` is `{ userId: string; conversationId?: string }` — construct one provider/middleware/tools/hooks instance per user session, and pass a `conversationId` once you have one to resume." A reader will take this to mean that leaving the id out gives a new conversation.
- docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc:285-287: the NamsScope section gives only the type and no resolution rule.
- docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/typescript/nams-ai-provider-provider-mode.adoc:167-170: "Session 2 ("fresh session, same user") constructs a **new** `createNamsProvider` — no JavaScript object is shared with session 1". It never says the second session writes into the same NAMS conversation.

What the code does:
- typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src/vercel-ai-provider-client.ts:83-114 (resolveConversation) uses the given conversationId, then the cached one, then `client.shortTerm.listConversations({ userId, limit: 1 })[0].id`. It calls createConversation only when the user has no conversations, or when listConversations fails.
- findExistingConversation (lines 116+) applies the same latest-conversation fallback.

I grepped the provider pages for "latest", "most recent", "new conversation", "resum" and "reuse". None of the hits states this rule: the hooks page's "created | resumed" reason names are the only nearby text.

Effect on a reader: a "fresh session" without an id writes into the user's latest conversation. The "current conversation" source in explanation/nams-ai-provider-retrieval.adoc:18 therefore returns earlier sessions' messages. crossSessionLimit also has fewer other conversations to search than a reader would expect. The provider-mode demo's recall works partly because both sessions share one conversation, which the page does not say.

Major is the right severity: this is missing behavioural content a reader needs, and it leads them to merge separate sessions into one conversation without noticing. No data is lost, so it is not a blocker.
findings.reproduction:
1. `sed -n 83,114p typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src/vercel-ai-provider-client.ts` shows resolveConversation. The doc comment reads "the given one, else the cached one, else the user's latest, else a new one", and the code runs listConversations({userId, limit:1}) and returns convs[0].id when one exists.
2. `sed -n 44,56p typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/src/provider-mode.ts` shows that each session() builds a new createNamsProvider with `scope: { userId }` and no conversationId. The per-client convCache is therefore empty, and the listConversations path is the one that runs.
3. `cd typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider && npx vitest run test/docs-pages.test.ts -t "provider mode"` passes (1 passed, 7 skipped). That test asserts `expect(stub.conversations.size).toBe(1)` and `messages toHaveLength(4)` (test/docs-pages.test.ts:136-137): both sessions ran through different provider objects and ended up in a single NAMS conversation.
4. `grep -rniE "latest|most recent|new conversation|resum|conversationId|reuse"` over how-to/typescript/nams-ai-provider*.adoc and reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc found no statement that omitting conversationId resumes the user's latest conversation. The only hits are the "pass a conversationId once you have one to resume" line, type signatures, and the hooks 'created'/'resumed' reason names.
5. `git diff --stat ec9fc65..HEAD -- docs` shows every one of these pages as newly added on this branch.

findings.title: Hooks/tools offline tests can't fail if deny, retry or recall breaks: they assert the mock's canned text
findings.detail: The hooks test is named 'runs all eight lifecycle events', but it never checks that any hook ran. The comments on the retry and deny assertions say they prove the retry and the denial. In fact they check strings the mock model returns no matter what the tools did. I disabled both hooks in a scratch copy (PreToolUse matcher changed to one that matches nothing, retry only on attempt 99) and ran it against the same stub and mock. The answers came out unchanged, so these assertions would still pass. The same holds for tools mode: the turn-2 answer is hard-coded in the mock regardless of what query_memory returns, and '>= 2 POST /entities/search' is already met by turn 1 (the query_memory search plus the findEntity search in store). Nothing checks that turn 2 got the stored memory back.
findings.evidence: test/docs-pages.test.ts:232-233 `expect(answers[1]).toContain("documented"); // survived the flaky_lookup retry` / `expect(answers[2]).toContain("disabled"); // delete_account was denied, never executed` while the mock at :218 and :221 returns those texts unconditionally once any tool message exists. Mutation run (scratch copy of src/hooks-mode.ts with `matcher: 'nothing_matches'` and `attempt === 99`): output still 'assistant: Graph databases are well documented.' for turn 2, and turn 3 went on to the answer step, with delete_account now executing because nothing denies it. Tools: :186-188 turn 2 returns the fixed text after any tool result, and :194 asserts that fixed text. :198 `filter(c => c === "POST /entities/search").length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2)` is met in turn 1 alone (vercel-ai-provider-client.ts:371 query search + :445 findEntity search).
findings.fix: Assert on the stored transcript and the tool outputs, not on the canned answers. Check that the persisted delete_account tool-result contains `"blocked":true`, that flaky_lookup's tool-result has `fact` (so the retry happened), and that the SessionStart context reached turn 1's instructions (calls[0] system prompt contains 'free plan'). For tools mode, check that turn 2's query_memory tool result contains 'Neovim'.
findings.v1reason: I reproduced this. In a scratch copy of hooks-mode.ts I changed the PreToolUse matcher to 'nothing_matches' and the retry condition to attempt === 99, then ran it with the test's mock model against the hosted stub. All four answers were identical to the original run, so the assertions at docs-pages.test.ts:231-234 would still pass. The stored transcript did change: 'delete_account: {"deleted":true}' and 'flaky_lookup: Error: transient lookup error'. No assertion inspects it. The mock at :218/:221 returns its canned text once toolResultCount > 0, and a tool error also counts as a tool message. Tools mode has the same gap. Turn 2's text is hard-coded (:186-188), and the recall result is never checked. My run counted 11 POST /entities/search calls, so '>= 2' (:198) cannot fail.
findings.v2reason:
I confirmed this by running the tests against mutants. I copied the example into a scratch tree with the real node_modules, the hosted stub and tsconfig.base.json. The unmodified offline suite passes (4 passed). I then broke all three behaviours the tests claim to prove:
- Hooks mode (src/hooks-mode.ts): the PreToolUse matcher `delete_account` became `nothing_matches`, the PostToolUseFailure retry became `attempt === 99`, and SessionStart became `[]`.
- Tools mode (src/tools-mode.ts): turn 2's `query_memory.execute` now returns `{memories: []}`.

The whole offline suite still passed. I instrumented the test to print what actually happened, and all three behaviours were really broken:
- delete_account ran, and its stored tool-result is `{"deleted":true}`.
- The stored flaky_lookup tool-result is `Error: transient lookup error`, so the retry never happened.
- Turn 2's query_memory output was `{"memories":[],"note":"MUTANT: recall broken"}`.

Yet the answers were unchanged ("Graph databases are well documented.", "...account deletion is disabled in this demo.", "You use Neovim, and you like short answers."). The mock returns those strings whenever any tool message exists (typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/test/docs-pages.test.ts:186-188, :218, :221). So the assertions at :194, :232 and :233 cannot fail when deny, retry or recall breaks. The check at :198 (`POST /entities/search` >= 2) saw 6 searches with recall broken, so it cannot fail either. The file header (:14-16) says 'The assertions are the ones that fail if memory stops working', and for tools mode that is false.

Scope: the hooks test's redaction assertions (:241-242) and the recall prompt checks in provider and middleware mode (:120, :143) are real. The gap is limited to deny, retry and SessionStart in hooks mode and to recall in tools mode. The branch added this file, so the gap is new. Major severity is right: these are tests that pass silently.
findings.reproduction:
Scratch dir: /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-lyonwj-github-neo4j-labs-agent-memory/66a2977c-9670-4b56-8270-fc84ea0f1100/scratchpad/review/mut2/examples/. It holds copies of nams-ai-provider/{src,test,package.json,tsconfig.json}, with node_modules symlinked to the repo's, plus vercel-ai/test/docs-hosted-stub.ts, shared/*, and tsconfig.base.json.

1. Baseline: `npx vitest run -t "offline"` gave Tests 4 passed | 4 skipped.
2. Mutations:
   - hooks-mode.ts: `sed "s/matcher: 'delete_account'/matcher: 'nothing_matches'/; s/attempt === 1 ?/attempt === 99 ?/"`, and SessionStart set to `[]`.
   - tools-mode.ts: inserted `if (label.startsWith('Turn 2')) (tools as any).query_memory.execute = async () => ({ memories: [], note: 'MUTANT: recall broken' });`
   - Result: `npx vitest run -t "offline"` gave Tests 4 passed | 4 skipped. The mutants survived.
3. I instrumented the test to log the stored transcript, turn 2's tool results and the search count, then ran `npx vitest run -t "tools mode|hooks mode" --reporter=verbose`:

   - Tests 2 passed.

findings.title: Tools-mode expected output: wrong line order, missing final-step lines and turn-2 fallback line
findings.detail: The program logs the ensureMemoryStored outcome inside onFinish, which runs during agent.generate(), so that line prints before the '--- Turn N' header, not after the step list. result.steps also includes the final text-only step, so the program prints an extra 'step N [unconstrained]' line with no tool call in each turn. And in turn 2 the model never calls store_memory, so ensureMemoryStored prints 'persisted the turn'. The expected output omits that line. The same wrong transcript is in the example's header comment (tools-mode.ts:15-26), which the page embeds.
findings.evidence:
Page :207-218 shows '--- Turn 1 ...', step 0, step 1, 'ensureMemoryStored: already-stored', 'assistant: ...', then Turn 2 with only step 0. Actual output from src/tools-mode.ts with the test's mock model and hosted stub (scratch runner): "ensureMemoryStored: already-stored

--- Turn 1 -- teach it something
step 0 [enforced: some tool required]
  tool call: query_memory(...)
step 1 [unconstrained]
  tool call: store_memory(...)
step 2 [unconstrained]
assistant: Got it.
ensureMemoryStored: persisted the turn

--- Turn 2 -- fresh tool set, same user
step 0 [enforced: some tool required]
  tool call: query_memory(...)
step 1 [unconstrained]
assistant: You use Neovim." Source: tools-mode.ts:66-70 (log inside onFinish) and :74-84 (header printed after generate).
findings.fix: Regenerate the expected output from a real or mocked run, in both the page and the example's header comment, or move the header print before agent.generate() and skip steps that have no tool calls.
findings.v1reason: I ran src/tools-mode.ts with the test mock and the stub. The output was: 'ensureMemoryStored: already-stored' printed before the '--- Turn 1' header (onFinish logs during agent.generate(), tools-mode.ts:66-70 vs :74-76), a 'step 2 [unconstrained]' line with no tool call, and 'ensureMemoryStored: persisted the turn' printed before Turn 2, with turn 2 also ending in a text-only 'step 1'. The page (tools-mode.adoc:207-218) and the header comment (tools-mode.ts:15-26) show a different order and leave out those lines. One detail in the finding is slightly off: each ensureMemoryStored line prints before its own turn's header, not after the previous turn. The conclusion stands.

findings.title: Hooks-mode expected output shows 3/3/2/2 saved turns; one tool call per turn saves 4
findings.detail: onFinish saves the user prompt, one audit turn for the tool call, one for the tool result, and the final answer. A turn with one tool call therefore saves 4 turns. The expected output says 3 for turns 1 and 2 and 2 for turn 3. A count of 2 in turn 3 would mean delete_account was never called, which contradicts the page's own claim that PreToolUse denied it. The listing also leaves out the logged hook systemMessages ('[nams] PreToolUse denied delete_account ...', '[nams] PostToolUseFailure hook: ...', '[nams] UserPromptSubmit hook: Redacted a card number.').

Running src/hooks-mode.ts with the test's mock (one tool call per turn) against the hosted stub printed 'saved 4 turns' for turns 1, 2 and 3 and 'saved 2 turns' for turn 4. Stored transcript: user, '[tool-call] delete_account: {"confirm":true}', '[tool-result] delete_account: {"blocked":true,...}', answer. Source: vercel-ai-provider-hooks.ts:424-433 and turnsFromResponse :148-184.

The output also printed '[nams] PostToolUseFailure hook: ...', '[nams] PreToolUse denied delete_account ...' and '[nams] UserPromptSubmit hook: ...' lines, which the listing leaves out. findings.title: 'Each event fires once across the four turns' is false: UserPromptSubmit, PreMemoryWrite and Stop fire every turn
findings.detail: UserPromptSubmit runs on every prepare() call, and PreMemoryWrite and Stop run on every onFinish(). So across the four turns each of these fires four times. The page's own expected output prints the Stop hook's '[hook] saved N turns' line four times. The header is embedded verbatim on the hooks-mode page (lines 39-40).

findings.title: How-to prerequisites omit OPENAI_API_KEY, which all four programs need by default
findings.detail: All four programs default to the @ai-sdk/openai `openai` provider, which needs OPENAI_API_KEY. Each page's Prerequisites list only Node, MEMORY_API_KEY and the npm install. A reader who follows the page as written gets an OpenAI 'API key is missing' error on the first model call. The key appears only inside the embedded code comment and the example README. The same omission is in the middleware (:19-28), tools (:20-29) and hooks (:20-29) pages.
findings.evidence: provider-mode.adoc:20-29 Prerequisites: Node.js 22, 'A `MEMORY_API_KEY` from ...', npm install. The program defaults `baseProvider ... = openai` (provider-mode.ts:34) and its comment runs `MEMORY_API_KEY=nams_... OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... npx tsx ...` (:9). The example's .env.example also requires OPENAI_API_KEY.
findings.fix: Add 'An `OPENAI_API_KEY` (or pass a different model factory)' to the Prerequisites on all four how-to pages.
findings.v1reason: The Prerequisites on all four how-to pages (e.g. provider-mode.adoc:20-29) list Node, MEMORY_API_KEY and npm install. None mentions OPENAI_API_KEY. The programs default to buildModel = openai (e.g. hooks-mode.ts:32, tools-mode.ts:41). The key appears only in the embedded code comment (e.g. provider-mode.adoc:44). The landing page's prerequisites (nams-ai-provider.adoc:20) do not mention it either.

findings.title: 'Save as provider-mode.ts' has no matching run step; run instructions assume the repo checkout and src/
findings.detail: Each how-to installs the published npm packages and tells the reader to 'Save as `<mode>-mode.ts`'. The 'Run and verify' section then switches to running `src/<mode>-mode.ts` from `typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/` 'after the workspace build'. The embedded comment likewise says `npx tsx src/provider-mode.ts`. A reader who saved the file in their own project gets no command that runs it, and tsx is not in the install line. The same pattern is on the middleware (:159-167), tools (:193-201) and hooks (:232-240) pages.
findings.evidence: provider-mode.adoc:33 '.Save as `provider-mode.ts`'; :28 npm install (no tsx); :178-184 'From `typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/`, after the workspace build ... npx tsx --env-file-if-exists=.env src/provider-mode.ts'.
findings.fix: Add a standalone run command for the saved file (for example `MEMORY_API_KEY=... OPENAI_API_KEY=... npx tsx provider-mode.ts`), and present the repo-checkout command as the alternative.
findings.v1reason: Each how-to installs the published packages (e.g. provider-mode.adoc:28, no tsx) and says '.Save as `provider-mode.ts`' (:33). The only run command is 'From typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/, after the workspace build ... npx tsx --env-file-if-exists=.env src/provider-mode.ts' (:178-184). middleware (:32/:166), tools (:33/:200) and hooks (:33/:239) are the same. A reader who saved the file in their own project gets no run command for it.

findings.title: Run-guard `import.meta.url === file://${argv[1]}` silently skips the demo when the path has a space
findings.detail: import.meta.url is percent-encoded but process.argv[1] is not. In any directory whose path contains a space or another escaped character (and on Windows), the guard is false and the program exits 0 without printing anything. The same guard is in middleware-mode.ts:76, tools-mode.ts:106 and hooks-mode.ts:121, and all four are embedded on the how-to pages.
findings.evidence: A copy of the guard run with the example's tsx from '<scratch>/my proj/guard.ts' printed: "GUARD FALSE file:///.../my%20proj/guard.ts /.../my proj/guard.ts". The same file run from a path without a space printed "RAN".
findings.fix: Compare with `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` (from node:url), then re-embed the files on the pages.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced: a file containing the same guard, placed in a 'my proj' directory and run with node, printed 'GUARD FALSE file:///.../my%20proj/g.mjs'. import.meta.url is percent-encoded and process.argv[1] is not. The same guard is in all four programs (e.g. hooks-mode.ts:121, tools-mode.ts:106), which are embedded on the pages. The result is a silent exit 0.

findings.title: query_memory limit documented as 1–20 without noting that results are capped at 12
findings.detail: The tool schema accepts limit up to 20, but retrieveMemories caps the merged result at Math.min(limit, 12). So a model asking for 20 gets at most 12. The reference documents a 12 cap for maxMemories but not for the tool's limit. The tools-mode page repeats '1–20'.
findings.evidence: reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc:163-164 "`{ query: string; limit?: number (1–20, default 5) }`"; tools-mode.adoc:230 "Input `{ query: string, limit: number (1–20, default 5) }`". Source: vercel-ai-provider-tools.ts:32 `limit: z.number().int().min(1).max(20).default(5)` → :146-147 retrieveMemories(..., limit, ...) → vercel-ai-provider-client.ts:417-419 `interleave([...], Math.min(limit, RETRIEVAL.maxTotal))` with maxTotal 12 (:145).
findings.fix: Add 'at most 12 hits are returned regardless of `limit`' in both places.
findings.v1reason: vercel-ai-provider-tools.ts:32 accepts limit up to 20. The execute handler passes it to retrieveMemories (:146-148), which returns interleave(..., Math.min(limit, RETRIEVAL.maxTotal)) with maxTotal 12 (vercel-ai-provider-client.ts:145, :417-419). The reference (:163-164) and tools-mode.adoc (:230) document 1-20 and do not mention the 12 cap on this path.

findings.title: baseProvider typed as `(modelId) => LanguageModel`; a string model id is not accepted
findings.detail: In ai 7, `LanguageModel` includes `GlobalProviderModelId` (a string). baseProvider's real type is WrappableModel, the model parameter of wrapLanguageModel, which accepts only LanguageModelV2, V3 or V4 objects. A baseProvider that returns a gateway id string matches the documented type but fails to type-check against the real one.
findings.evidence: reference :43 "| `(modelId: string) => LanguageModel`". Source: vercel-ai-provider.ts:15 `baseProvider: (modelId: string) => WrappableModel;` and vercel-ai-provider-middleware.ts:14 `WrappableModel = Parameters<typeof wrapLanguageModel>[0]['model']`. node_modules/ai/dist/index.d.ts:9024 `model: LanguageModelV2 | LanguageModelV3 | LanguageModelV4;` vs :112 `type LanguageModel = GlobalProviderModelId | LanguageModelV4 | LanguageModelV3 | LanguageModelV2;`.
findings.fix: Document it as `(modelId: string) => LanguageModelV4 | LanguageModelV3 | LanguageModelV2` (a model object, not a string id).
findings.v1reason: The reference (:43) types baseProvider as `(modelId: string) => LanguageModel`. The source is vercel-ai-provider.ts:15 `baseProvider: (modelId: string) => WrappableModel`, and WrappableModel = Parameters<typeof wrapLanguageModel>[0]['model'] (middleware.ts:14). In ai 7.0.112 that parameter is `LanguageModelV2 | LanguageModelV3 | LanguageModelV4` (index.d.ts:9024), while LanguageModel also includes GlobalProviderModelId (:112). The practical impact is small because the Notes column says 'Any @ai-sdk/* provider function'.

findings.title: loadSession documented as 'Never throws', but it throws when no userId is available
findings.detail: loadSession calls resolveScope outside its try block. resolveScope throws when neither the call nor createNamsHooks supplied a userId, so loadSession rejects in that case instead of returning [].
findings.evidence: reference :217 "Never throws — returns `[]` for a new user or on a backend error." Source: vercel-ai-provider-hooks.ts:261-262 `const loadSession = async (...) => { const scope = resolveScope(opts, 'loadSession');` (before `try {` at :264). :226-230 `throw new Error(`${hookName} needs a userId ...`)`.
findings.fix: Say 'Never throws on a backend error (returns `[]`); throws if no userId is set on the call or on createNamsHooks().'
findings.v1reason: vercel-ai-provider-hooks.ts:261-262 calls resolveScope(opts, 'loadSession') before the try block, and resolveScope throws when no userId is set on the call or on createNamsHooks (:224-230). The reference's 'Never throws' (:217) is therefore wrong in that case. The source's own JSDoc (:260) makes the same claim.

findings.title: Reference claims 'every export' but omits exported types, including tool result shapes
findings.detail: The package has no TypeDoc, so this page is the only reference. Several public exports from index.ts are missing: the query_memory/store_memory result shapes (QueryOutput, StoreOutput) that a UI renders in tools mode; McpConnectionStatus, the shape of NamsToolsResult.mcp whose `.error` the tools page tells readers to check; NamsMode; and several hook types (NamsHookEvent, NamsHookGroup, NamsHookHandler, NamsHookResult, NamsHookInputs/Outputs, NamsHookBase, NamsOnFinishEvent, FinishedTurn, QueryInput, ToolStoreInput).
findings.evidence: reference :6-7 "every export, grouped by the mode that uses it". A grep of each name exported from typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/src/index.ts:7-54 against the reference page finds no match for: McpConnectionStatus, QueryInput, ToolStoreInput, QueryOutput, StoreOutput, FinishedTurn, NamsOnFinishEvent, NamsHookEvent, NamsHookGroup, NamsHookHandler, NamsHookInputs, NamsHookOutputs, NamsHookResult, NamsHookBase, NamsMode. Shapes: vercel-ai-provider-tools.ts:49-50 (QueryOutput `{ found; count?; message?; memories }`, StoreOutput `{ stored; type; preview; message }`), :76-82 (McpConnectionStatus `{ connected; toolNames; error? }`).
findings.fix: Add the QueryOutput, StoreOutput and McpConnectionStatus shapes and a short list of the remaining exported type names, or soften 'every export' to 'the public API'.
findings.v1reason: The reference (:6-7) says 'every export'. grep finds zero mentions of McpConnectionStatus, QueryInput, ToolStoreInput, QueryOutput, StoreOutput, FinishedTurn, NamsOnFinishEvent, NamsHookEvent, NamsHookGroup, NamsHookHandler, NamsHookInputs, NamsHookOutputs, NamsHookResult, NamsHookBase or NamsMode, all of which index.ts exports. The reference gives NamsToolsResult as `{ tools, close, mcp? }` (:90) without the shape of mcp, yet tools-mode.adoc:277 tells readers to check `mcp.error`.

findings.title: Explanation says assistant text is skipped only for tool-call-only steps; any step with an app tool call is skipped
findings.detail: The middleware drops the assistant text for any step whose output contains an app tool call, even when the model also produced text. The middleware-mode page states this correctly, so the two pages disagree.
findings.evidence: explanation :88-89 "is skipped when a step only produced tool calls with no answer text". Source: vercel-ai-provider-middleware.ts:59-61 `const answerFromResult = ... if (content.some(callsAppTool)) return '';` and :182-187 (stream: `handsOffToTools ? '' : text`). middleware-mode.adoc:206-208 "A step whose output includes a call to an app tool persists **no assistant text** for that step, even if the model also produced text alongside the call".
findings.fix: Reword it as 'is skipped for any step that calls an app tool, even if that step also produced text'.
findings.v1reason: The explanation (:88-89) says the answer 'is skipped when a step only produced tool calls with no answer text'. middleware.ts:59-61 returns '' whenever the content contains an app tool call, even alongside text, and the streaming path uses `handsOffToTools ? '' : text` (:186). middleware-mode.adoc:206-208 states the correct rule, so the two pages disagree.

findings.title: Turn-4 card redaction is credited to PreMemoryWrite; UserPromptSubmit already redacted the saved prompt
findings.detail: The prompt saved by onFinish is prepared.prompt, passed in through runtimeContext. The UserPromptSubmit hook has already rewritten it to '[redacted card]'. So in this demo the stored user turn is clean because of UserPromptSubmit. PreMemoryWrite would matter only if the model echoed the number back in its answer.
findings.evidence: hooks-mode.adoc:271-272 "the card number typed in turn 4 never reaches NAMS unredacted, because `PreMemoryWrite` rewrites it before `onFinish` saves the turn." hooks-mode.ts:107 `options: { userId, prompt: prepared.prompt, ... }` and :42 UserPromptSubmit returns `{ updatedPrompt: clean }`. Source: vercel-ai-provider-hooks.ts:312 `prompt = submitted.input.prompt` and :419,426 (onFinish persists context.prompt).
findings.fix: Say that UserPromptSubmit redacts what the model sees and saves, and that PreMemoryWrite is a second line of defence for anything the model's reply or tool records echo back.
findings.v1reason: hooks-mode.ts:107 passes prepared.prompt, which UserPromptSubmit has already redacted (hooks.ts:312, hooks-mode.ts:40-42), through runtimeContext. onFinish then persists context.prompt (hooks.ts:416-426). In my run, the stored user turn was already '[redacted card]'. PreMemoryWrite redacts again, but that is not why the saved prompt is clean, so the page's causal claim at :271-272 is inaccurate.

findings.title: Test header and README still say the doc pages 'don't exist yet' and mention 'another worker'
findings.detail: The four pages exist on this branch and the fidelity tests pass (8/8). The leftover work-in-progress wording, including 'another worker', ships in the example's test and README.

Until then this half of the suite fails", and README.md:127-129 says the pages are written separately 'until they exist'. The four pages exist on this branch. findings.title: get_facts_about described as matching subject or object; it matches subject only
findings.detail: The new preferences/facts subpage says get_facts_about returns facts where the entity name is the subject or the object. The bolt implementation runs GET_FACTS_BY_SUBJECT, which filters only on f.subject. A reader who relies on the documented behaviour will miss every fact where the entity is the object. The parameter table on the same page (line 180, '`subject` | The fact subject') also disagrees with the prose.
findings.evidence: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/long-term-preferences.adoc:169 "Return facts where the entity name occurs as the subject or object." vs src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/long_term.py:2133-2153 (get_facts_about runs queries.GET_FACTS_BY_SUBJECT with {"subject": subject}) and src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:374-376 "MATCH (f:Fact) WHERE f.subject = $subject"
findings.fix: Change the sentence to: "Return facts whose subject exactly equals `subject`. Facts where the name appears as the object are not returned. There is no `get_facts` wrapper."
findings.v1reason: long-term-preferences.adoc:169 (a page this branch adds) says 'Return facts where the entity name occurs as the subject or object.' The code does not do that. LongTermMemory.get_facts_about (src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/long_term.py:2133-2153) runs queries.GET_FACTS_BY_SUBJECT with {subject}, and that query is 'MATCH (f:Fact) WHERE f.subject = $subject' (graph/queries.py:374-376). It matches the subject only. The page's own parameter table (line 180, '`subject` | The fact subject') disagrees with the prose.
findings.v2reason:
The finding holds. docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/long-term-preferences.adoc:169 says "Return facts where the entity name occurs as the subject or object." This branch adds the page: it is not in ec9fc65, and commits c90d191 and 4052e1b created and edited it. I ran the bolt implementation against a mocked Neo4jClient. It sends GET_FACTS_BY_SUBJECT, which is `MATCH (f:Fact) WHERE f.subject = $subject` (src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:374-379). The only parameters it passes are {'subject': 'Alice', 'limit': 100}, and nothing matches on the object.

Two more sources agree with the code, not the page:
- The protocol docstring at src/neo4j_agent_memory/core/protocols.py:404-411 says "Return facts where the given entity is the subject."
- The page's own parameter table (line 180, "`subject` | The fact subject") says the same.

No other backend matches on the object. The NAMS backend (src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/long_term.py:563-567) raises NotSupportedError. The "subject or object" wording appears nowhere else in the source or the docs. A reader who follows the page will miss every fact where the entity is the object. That is a wrong behaviour claim, so major is the right severity.
findings.reproduction:
1) sed -n 160,190p docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/long-term-preferences.adoc
   -> line 169: "Return facts where the entity name occurs as the subject or object. There is no `get_facts` wrapper."
   -> table: "| `subject` | The fact subject"

2) git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/long-term-preferences.adoc
   -> "fatal: path ... exists on disk, but not in 'ec9fc65'" (the page is new on this branch)

3) Scratch script scratchpad/review/facts.py:
   - It builds LongTermMemory(client=MagicMock with execute_read=AsyncMock([]), embedder=None).
   - It awaits get_facts_about("Alice").
   - It prints the query and parameters from execute_read.call_args.
   Command: uv run python scratchpad/review/facts.py
   Output:
     MATCH (f:Fact)
     WHERE f.subject = $subject
     RETURN f
     ORDER BY f.confidence DESC, f.created_at DESC
     LIMIT $limit
     {'subject': 'Alice', 'limit': 100}

4) core/protocols.py:404-411 docstring: "Return facts where the given entity is the subject."
   nams/long_term.py:563-567: get_facts_about raises NotSupportedError("NAMS does not expose a facts endpoint.")

5) grep -rn "subject or object" docs/modules/ROOT/pages src/
   -> only long-term-preferences.adoc:169

findings.title: search_entities prose claims a subtype control that does not exist (also NAMS table 'Bolt subtypes')
findings.detail: The prose says bolt search_entities has type, subtype and similarity controls, and the NAMS-differences table lists `subtypes` as a Bolt parameter that NAMS does not send. Bolt search_entities has no subtype parameter: it takes query, entity_types, limit and threshold, and it filters on entity type only. The signature block directly below line 79 is correct, so the prose contradicts it.
findings.evidence: long-term-entities.adoc:79 "Semantic search with type, subtype, and similarity controls."; long-term-geospatial.adoc:133 "Bolt `entity_types`, `subtypes`, and `threshold` are not sent." vs `uv run python -c 'inspect.signature(LongTermMemory.search_entities)'` -> (self, query, *, entity_types=None, limit=10, threshold=0.7) -> list[Entity]; src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/long_term.py:1127-1180 filters only on entity_data["type"]
findings.fix: Change line 79 to "Semantic search with entity-type and similarity-threshold controls." and change long-term-geospatial.adoc:133 to "Bolt `entity_types` (list) and `threshold` are not sent."
findings.v1reason: long-term-entities.adoc:79 says 'Semantic search with type, subtype, and similarity controls.', but inspect.signature(LongTermMemory.search_entities) gives (query, *, entity_types=None, limit=10, threshold=0.7). There is no subtype parameter, and the body filters only on entity_data['type'] against the normalized entity_types. long-term-geospatial.adoc:133 also names a Bolt `subtypes` parameter that does not exist. Both pages are new on this branch. The signature block right below line 79 is correct, which limits the harm.

findings.title: NAMS table omits that get_entity_relationships takes an id and returns a different shape
findings.detail: On bolt, get_entity_relationships takes an entity *name* and returns list[tuple[Entity, Relationship]], as long-term-entities.adoc:170-175 documents. The NAMS wrapper takes an entity *id* (it calls GET /entities/{id}) and returns a plain list[Relationship]. The NAMS-behavior row covers only the synthesized ids and timestamps. Code ported from bolt that passes a name, or unpacks tuples, fails on NAMS.
findings.evidence: long-term-geospatial.adoc:136 "| `get_entity_relationships` | Adapts inline relationships into Relationship models. IDs and creation times are synthesized locally..." vs src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/long_term.py:2195-2198 "get_entity_relationships(self, entity_name: str) -> list[tuple[Entity, Relationship]]" and src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/long_term.py:570 "async def get_entity_relationships(self, entity_id: UUID | str) -> list[Relationship]"
findings.fix: Add to the row: "Takes an entity id (not a name) and returns `list[Relationship]`, not `(Entity, Relationship)` tuples."
findings.v1reason: On bolt, get_entity_relationships takes a name and returns tuples: LongTermMemory.get_entity_relationships(self, entity_name: str) -> list[tuple[Entity, Relationship]]. On NAMS it takes an id and returns plain models: NamsLongTermMemory.get_entity_relationships(self, entity_id: UUID | str) -> list[Relationship] (nams/long_term.py:570), and it calls GET entity by id. The NAMS-behavior row at long-term-geospatial.adoc:136 covers only the synthesized ids and timestamps, not the different argument or return shape. Code ported from bolt would pass a name and unpack tuples, and both would fail.

findings.title: Says unsupported calls raise NotSupportedError; bolt-only long_term methods raise AttributeError on NAMS
findings.detail: memory-client.adoc says unsupported accessors or calls raise NotSupportedError. The geospatial table row for preferences says the same about preference methods. NamsLongTermMemory does not define several bolt-only methods and has no __getattr__ fallback, so calling them on NAMS raises AttributeError. Examples are get_preferences_by_category (listed on the preferences page), review_duplicate, search_locations_in_bounding_box and get_location_coordinates. A reader who catches NotSupportedError to detect backend support will not catch these. Line 139 of the geospatial page describes this correctly as 'not exposed', which contradicts line 92.
findings.evidence: memory-client.adoc:92 "Unsupported accessors or calls raise `NotSupportedError`"; long-term-geospatial.adoc:138 "| Preferences, facts, `add_relationship` | Raise `NotSupportedError`" vs command `uv run python -c "from neo4j_agent_memory.nams.long_term import NamsLongTermMemory as N; print([m for m in ['get_preferences_by_category','search_locations_in_bounding_box','get_location_coordinates','review_duplicate'] if not hasattr(N,m)])"` -> ['get_preferences_by_category', 'search_locations_in_bounding_box', 'get_location_coordinates', 'review_duplicate']; `grep -n __getattr__ src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/*.py` -> no matches
findings.fix: memory-client.adoc:92: "Unsupported accessors and Protocol methods raise `NotSupportedError`; bolt-only methods that NAMS does not define (for example `get_preferences_by_category`) raise `AttributeError`." In geospatial:138, name the methods that raise, or add `get_preferences_by_category` to the 'not exposed' row.
findings.v1reason: memory-client.adoc:92 (new text) says 'Unsupported accessors or calls raise `NotSupportedError`'. A hasattr check on NamsLongTermMemory shows that get_preferences_by_category, search_locations_in_bounding_box, get_location_coordinates and review_duplicate are not defined, and grep finds no __getattr__ under src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams, so calling them raises AttributeError. The preferences row at geospatial:138 says preferences raise NotSupportedError, but get_preferences_by_category, which the preferences page documents at line 48, does not.

findings.title: Escaped `\{...}` renders with a literal backslash in the built page
findings.detail: The branch changed `{...}` to `\{...}`. `{...}` is not a valid attribute reference, so Asciidoctor does not treat the backslash as an escape and prints it. The published page now reads 'largest balanced \{…}' block.
findings.evidence: llm-provider.adoc:215 "finds the largest balanced `\{...}` block"; `grep -o 'largest balanced [^<]*' docs/build/site/agent-memory/reference/api/llm-provider.html` -> largest balanced \{…​}; asciidoctor on a one-line test renders `\{...}` as \{…} and `{...}` as {…}
findings.fix: Revert to `{...}`, or use a passthrough such as `+{...}+` inside the backticks.
findings.v1reason: llm-provider.adoc:215 now contains `\{...}`, and the branch diff adds the backslash. The built site (docs/build/site/agent-memory/reference/api/llm-provider.html, built today) contains 'largest balanced \{…​}', so the published page shows a literal backslash.

findings.title: query.cypher shown with a 'parameters' argument; the real parameter is 'params'
findings.detail: The properties table shows `await client.query.cypher(query, parameters)`. The parameter on both backends is named `params`, so a reader who passes `parameters=` as a keyword gets a TypeError. Positional use works.
findings.evidence: memory-client.adoc:80 "Read-only `await client.query.cypher(query, parameters)`" vs src/neo4j_agent_memory/core/query.py:66-70 and src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/query.py:47-51 "async def cypher(self, query: str, params: dict[str, Any] | None = None)"
findings.fix: Write `await client.query.cypher(query, params)`.
findings.v1reason: memory-client.adoc:80 shows `client.query.cypher(query, parameters)`, but on both backends the parameter is named `params` (core/query.py:66-70, nams/query.py:47-51). The old page wrote `cypher(...)`, so the branch introduced the wrong name. Passing it positionally works; only `parameters=` as a keyword raises a TypeError.

findings.title: clear_session is documented as deleting a session's traces, but the SDK never creates the link it follows
findings.detail: Two pages say clearing a bolt session deletes the session's reasoning traces, steps and tool calls through `(Conversation)-[:HAS_TRACE]->(ReasoningTrace)`. No SDK code path writes that relationship. `start_trace` only CREATEs the trace node, plus an optional INITIATED_BY link to a message and a `(:User)-[:HAS_TRACE]` link. `LINK_CONVERSATION_TO_TRACE` is defined in queries.py but nothing uses it. So `DELETE_SESSION_DATA` never matches a trace, and `clear_session` leaves every trace, step and tool call for the session in the database. A reader who relies on `clear_session` to erase a session's data (for example, for privacy) keeps all of its reasoning data. how-to/messages.adoc:78 sends readers to this page as the contract to check before deleting.
findings.evidence: short-term-sessions.adoc:44: "Delete the matching conversation, its linked messages, and any traces, steps, and tool calls connected through its `:HAS_TRACE` relationships." reasoning-traces.adoc:152: "Clearing a bolt session deletes traces connected through its conversation's `:HAS_TRACE` relationship." Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:482-495 CREATE_REASONING_TRACE creates only the node. queries.py:727-733 DELETE_SESSION_DATA uses `OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[:HAS_TRACE]->(rt:ReasoningTrace)`. `grep -rn "LINK_CONVERSATION_TO_TRACE" src/` finds only its definition (queries.py:660). `grep -rn HAS_TRACE src/` finds only the User link (reasoning.py:507) and these two queries.
findings.fix: State that `clear_session` deletes the conversation and its messages but does not delete traces that `start_trace` created, because the SDK does not link conversations to traces. Say how to remove them instead, for example a Cypher delete on `ReasoningTrace {session_id: ...}` and its steps and tool calls. Alternatively, fix the SDK to link conversations to traces and document the fixed behaviour. Update reasoning-traces.adoc:152 to match.
findings.v1reason: short-term-sessions.adoc:44 and reasoning-traces.adoc:152 (both new on this branch) say clear_session deletes traces through (Conversation)-[:HAS_TRACE]. DELETE_SESSION_DATA (queries.py:727-733) does follow that link, but CREATE_REASONING_TRACE (queries.py:482-495) only creates the node. The only HAS_TRACE writer is the User link at reasoning.py:507. LINK_CONVERSATION_TO_TRACE (queries.py:660) is never used in src/. The repo already knows about this: examples/full-stack-chat-agent/backend/src/api/routes/threads.py:55-58 says "clear_session() only reaches traces linked with (:Conversation)-[:HAS_TRACE]->, which start_trace(session_id=...) does not create" and adds its own DELETE_SESSION_TRACES. So traces, steps and tool calls survive clear_session, which is misleading for anyone deleting data for privacy.
findings.v2reason:
I traced the code path and the finding holds. `ShortTermMemory.clear_session` (src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:1007-1009) runs only `queries.DELETE_SESSION_DATA`. That query (queries.py:727-733) reaches traces only through `OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[:HAS_TRACE]->(rt:ReasoningTrace)`. No code in src/ ever writes `(:Conversation)-[:HAS_TRACE]`:
- `CREATE_REASONING_TRACE` (queries.py:482-495) creates just the trace node, with `session_id` stored as a property.
- The only `HAS_TRACE` MERGE in the SDK is the User link at reasoning.py:507.
- `LINK_CONVERSATION_TO_TRACE` (queries.py:660) is defined but nothing in src/ uses it, and no public method exposes it.

So for any session built through the SDK, the trace match comes back null and every ReasoningTrace, ReasoningStep and ToolCall for that session survives `clear_session`. The repo already works around this in examples/full-stack-chat-agent/backend/src/api/routes/threads.py:55-58: "`clear_session()` only reaches traces linked with (:Conversation)-[:HAS_TRACE]->, which `start_trace(session_id=...)` does not create — so a deleted thread would leave its ReasoningTrace/ReasoningStep/ToolCall nodes behind". That file also adds its own DELETE_SESSION_TRACES query.

Read literally, the new docs are true: "any traces ... connected through its `:HAS_TRACE` relationships" (short-term-sessions.adoc:44) and "Clearing a bolt session deletes traces connected through its conversation's `:HAS_TRACE` relationship" (reasoning-traces.adoc:152). In practice that set is always empty, and the pages never say so. A reader will conclude that `clear_session` removes a session's reasoning data. how-to/messages.adoc:78 sends readers to this contract before they delete anything. Both reference pages are new on this branch (`git diff --stat` shows 198 and 159 lines added), so the branch introduced the misleading claim.

Major fits: this is a wrong behaviour claim, and someone relying on it to delete data for privacy reasons would leave reasoning data behind. It is not a blocker, because nothing breaks and a reader loses no data.
findings.reproduction:
I didn't run a live Neo4j test. The checks were a grep and a line-by-line trace of the code path.
1. `grep -rn "HAS_TRACE\|LINK_CONVERSATION_TO_TRACE\|DELETE_SESSION_DATA" src/` found:
   - users.py:13 and reasoning.py:448 (docstrings)
   - reasoning.py:507 `MERGE (u)-[:HAS_TRACE]->(rt)` (User link only)
   - queries.py:660/663 (the `LINK_CONVERSATION_TO_TRACE` definition only, with no callers)
   - queries.py:727/730 (`DELETE_SESSION_DATA`)
   - short_term.py:1009 (its only caller, `clear_session`)
2. `sed -n 480,500p queries.py`: `CREATE_REASONING_TRACE` is `CREATE (rt:ReasoningTrace {id, session_id, ...}) RETURN rt`, with no Conversation link.
3. `sed -n 720,740p queries.py`: `DELETE_SESSION_DATA` does `MATCH (c:Conversation {session_id})`, then `OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[:HAS_TRACE]->(rt)`, then `DETACH DELETE c, m, rt, rs, tc`. Traces are reached only through the missing link.
4. `sed -n 50,62p examples/full-stack-chat-agent/backend/src/api/routes/threads.py`: the comment confirms the gap, and the example adds its own `DELETE_SESSION_TRACES` that matches `ReasoningTrace {session_id}`.
5. `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD --stat` on the two reference pages shows both are new files on this branch (+198 and +159 lines). The claims are at short-term-sessions.adoc:44 and reasoning-traces.adoc:152.

findings.title: NAMS create_conversation looks like session_id is optional, but calling it without one raises TypeError
findings.detail: The signature shown, `session_id: str | None=None`, and the prose ("a supplied `session_id` is not sent as the identity") suggest a NAMS caller can omit `session_id`. `NamsShortTermMemory.create_conversation` calls `_resolve_conversation_id`, which raises TypeError when neither `session_id` nor `conversation_id` is given. So `create_conversation(user_identifier=...)` fails. The name is only used locally, to fill `Conversation.session_id`.
findings.evidence: short-term-messages.adoc:147: "NAMS sends `user_identifier` and `metadata` from kwargs; it returns a server-issued ID, and a supplied `session_id` is not sent as the identity." Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:470 `conv = _resolve_conversation_id(session_id, conversation_id, method="create_conversation")`, and :227-232 raises when both are None. Running it with a stub transport: `create_conversation(user_identifier='u')` gives `TypeError create_conversation requires session_id (alias: conversation_id) on NAMS`, and `create_conversation('mine')` returns `id=<server id> session_id='mine'`.
findings.fix: State that NAMS also requires a `session_id` (or the `conversation_id` alias). It is used only as the local `Conversation.session_id` label, and the server-issued `Conversation.id` is the value to pass to later calls.
findings.v1reason: I reproduced it with a stub transport. NamsShortTermMemory.create_conversation(user_identifier='u') raises "TypeError create_conversation requires session_id (alias: conversation_id) on NAMS", because of _resolve_conversation_id (nams/short_term.py:470 and :227-232). create_conversation('mine') returns the server UUID as id and 'mine' as session_id. short-term-messages.adoc:147 implies the session_id is optional and ignored on NAMS, and it is not optional.

findings.title: delete_message raises a Neo4j error for stored messages; it does not return False
findings.detail: The page says the method returns whether deletion succeeded and that deletion "can fail" when relationships remain. `CREATE_MESSAGE` always creates HAS_MESSAGE and sequence links, and `DELETE_MESSAGE` uses a plain `DELETE` (not DETACH). So for any message stored through `add_message`, the write transaction raises a Neo4j ConstraintError, which propagates because `Neo4jClient.execute_write` does not catch it. The method returns False only for an ID that is not a UUID or does not exist. A reader who writes `if not await delete_message(id)` gets an exception instead.
findings.evidence: short-term-messages.adoc:124: "Returns whether deletion succeeded. ... deletion can fail when those relationships remain". Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:184-195 (`DELETE r, m` / `DELETE m`, no DETACH). graph/client.py:155-164 has no exception handling. tests/integration/test_queries_neo4j.py:130-133 says "The DELETE_MESSAGE query handles MENTIONS but not conversation relationships, so we use a direct DETACH DELETE for this test".
findings.fix: Say that on bolt, for messages stored through `add_message`, the call currently raises a Neo4j constraint error because the conversation and sequence relationships remain, and that False is returned only for unknown or invalid IDs.
findings.v1reason: DELETE_MESSAGE and DELETE_MESSAGE_NO_CASCADE (queries.py:184-195) use plain DELETE. CREATE_MESSAGE always creates HAS_MESSAGE plus NEXT_MESSAGE or FIRST_MESSAGE links (queries.py:91-96), and Neo4j rejects deleting a node that still has relationships at commit. Neo4jClient.execute_write (client.py:155-164) does not catch the error, so it propagates. delete_message returns False only for a non-UUID or unknown ID (short_term.py:1105-1116). tests/integration/test_queries_neo4j.py:130-133 works around this with DETACH DELETE. The page does warn that deletion 'can fail', but 'Returns whether deletion succeeded' suggests False rather than an exception. I did not run it against a live Neo4j, but this is standard Neo4j semantics.

findings.title: On NAMS, only get_tool_stats raises NotSupportedError; the other tool-stat methods raise AttributeError
findings.detail: The NAMS table says "tool statistics" raise NotSupportedError. On NAMS, `client.reasoning` is a `NamsReasoningMemory`. It defines `get_tool_stats`, which raises NotSupportedError, but it has no `migrate_tool_stats` or `get_tool_usage_stats`. Calling either raises AttributeError, and code that catches NotSupportedError does not catch it.
findings.evidence: reasoning-search-stats.adoc:141: "| `search_steps`, `get_similar_traces`, `list_traces`, tool statistics | Raise `NotSupportedError`." This page documents all three stat methods (lines 82-116). Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/reasoning.py:342-348 defines only get_tool_stats. `inspect.getmembers(NamsReasoningMemory)` lists no migrate_tool_stats or get_tool_usage_stats. src/neo4j_agent_memory/__init__.py:660 `self._reasoning = cast(_RT, self._nams_backend.reasoning)`.
findings.fix: Change the row to `get_tool_stats` and say that `migrate_tool_stats` and `get_tool_usage_stats` do not exist on NAMS and raise AttributeError.
findings.v1reason: hasattr(NamsReasoningMemory, x) gives [True, False, False] for get_tool_stats, migrate_tool_stats and get_tool_usage_stats, and the class has no __getattr__. __init__.py:660 binds client.reasoning to the NAMS object. So on NAMS only get_tool_stats raises NotSupportedError (nams/reasoning.py:342-348); the other two raise AttributeError. That contradicts reasoning-search-stats.adoc:141, which says 'tool statistics | Raise NotSupportedError'. The section headings do say 'bolt only', which limits the harm.

findings.title: search_steps note implies steps have no embeddings unless complete_trace generates them
findings.detail: `add_step` generates a step embedding by default (`generate_embedding=True`) whenever an embedder is configured. `complete_trace(generate_step_embeddings=True)` is needed only for steps recorded with `generate_embedding=False`, which is the default for `StreamingTraceRecorder`. As written, the page presents it as a general prerequisite for step search.
findings.evidence: reasoning-search-stats.adoc:43: "Generate step embeddings with `complete_trace(..., generate_step_embeddings=True)` before relying on step search." Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/reasoning.py:524 `generate_embedding: bool = True` and :551-561 embeds thought, action and observation. StreamingTraceRecorder.__init__ has `generate_step_embeddings: bool = False` (reasoning.py:160).
findings.fix: Say that steps recorded with `generate_embedding=False` (including the StreamingTraceRecorder default) need `complete_trace(..., generate_step_embeddings=True)` before step search can find them, and that an embedder is required in all cases.
findings.v1reason: add_step defaults to generate_embedding=True and embeds thought, action and observation whenever an embedder is configured (memory/reasoning.py:524, 551-561). Only StreamingTraceRecorder defaults generate_step_embeddings=False (reasoning.py:161, 242). reasoning-search-stats.adoc:43 presents complete_trace(generate_step_embeddings=True) as a general prerequisite for step search, which is inaccurate. The text is new on this branch; the old reasoning.adoc has no such sentence.

findings.title: conversation_ttl_days row names a nonexistent `older_than_days` argument (actual: `ttl_days`)
findings.detail: The MemoryConfig table tells readers to pass the TTL to `archive_expired_conversations()` via `older_than_days`. The method has no such parameter; its keyword-only argument is `ttl_days`. A reader who follows the row gets a TypeError. The page also contradicts how-to/consolidation.adoc and how-to/privacy-and-audit.adoc, which both use `ttl_days=`.
findings.evidence:
configuration-operations.adoc:33: "pass it explicitly to `archive_expired_conversations()` via `older_than_days`. †"
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/consolidation.py:319-324 `async def archive_expired_conversations(self, *, ttl_days: int | None = None, dry_run: bool = True)`; line 332-336 raises ValueError asking for `ttl_days`.
`uv run python -c "...inspect.signature(ConsolidationMemory.archive_expired_conversations)"` -> `(self, *, ttl_days: 'int | None' = None, dry_run: 'bool' = True)`
how-to/privacy-and-audit.adoc:59 `ttl_days=settings.memory.conversation_ttl_days,`
findings.fix: Replace `via `older_than_days`` with `as `ttl_days=`` (for example `archive_expired_conversations(ttl_days=settings.memory.conversation_ttl_days)`).
findings.v1reason: configuration-operations.adoc:33 (a new file on this branch) says to pass the TTL 'via `older_than_days`'. The signature at src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/consolidation.py:319-324 is archive_expired_conversations(self, *, ttl_days=None, dry_run=True), and lines 332-335 raise if ttl_days is missing. A grep of src/ and docs pages finds `older_than_days` only on this row and on environment-variables.adoc:226. A reader who follows the row gets a TypeError.
findings.v2reason: The defect is real, and this branch introduced it. docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/configuration-operations.adoc is a new file on the branch (it does not exist at ec9fc65). Line 33 tells readers to pass the TTL to `archive_expired_conversations()` "via `older_than_days`". The only parameters of the method at src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/consolidation.py:319-324 are `ttl_days` and `dry_run`, both keyword-only. Calling it with `older_than_days=` raises a TypeError. how-to/consolidation.adoc:57 and how-to/privacy-and-audit.adoc:59 both use `ttl_days=`, so this page also contradicts them. The same wrong name appears in docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/environment-variables.adoc:226 ("TTL value for `archive_expired_conversations(older_than_days=...)`"), and the branch added that line too: the ec9fc65 version of that file has no `older_than_days`. Both lines should be fixed together. Major is the right severity: it is a wrong API claim, and a reader who follows it gets an immediate TypeError, which is easy to diagnose, so it does not reach blocker.

Now they sit on the Neo4j/NAMS connections bullet (line 10). `_python_configuration_6` and `_environment_variables_6` were the LLM subsections. findings.title: DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL documented as jackboyla/glirel_base; the source default is jackboyla/glirel-large-v0
findings.detail: The page gives the wrong default model for GLiRELExtractor, GLiNERWithRelationsExtractor.for_schema and GLiNERWithRelationsExtractor.for_poleo. A reader who sizes downloads or hardware, or who pins the model on the strength of this line, gets a different (large) model from the one they expect. No other docs page states the default, so this one is the only source and it is wrong.
findings.evidence: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/extractor-relations.adoc:175: "`DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL` is `jackboyla/glirel_base`."  Source of truth: src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/gliner_extractor.py:827: `DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL = "jackboyla/glirel-large-v0"` (the same value at ec9fc65; the source is unchanged on this branch).
findings.fix: Change the sentence to: `DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL` is `jackboyla/glirel-large-v0`.
findings.v1reason: extractor-relations.adoc:175 says "`DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL` is `jackboyla/glirel_base`". The source says `DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL = "jackboyla/glirel-large-v0"` (src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/gliner_extractor.py:827). The same wrong value was already on main (old extractors.adoc:362). The branch still repeats it on a page it newly added and states it as a fact. It is a wrong default-value claim.
findings.v2reason: The finding is real. The branch adds docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/extractor-relations.adoc as a new file (182 insertions, 0 deletions against ec9fc65). Line 175 of that page says "`DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL` is `jackboyla/glirel_base`." The installed package gives a different value: `jackboyla/glirel-large-v0`, defined at src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/gliner_extractor.py:827. The same page uses DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL as the default in three signatures (lines 18, 119 and 149). Those signatures match the source at lines 903, 1191 and 1232, so the one value readers are told for that default is wrong. The old main page (reference/extractors.adoc:362) showed the same wrong string as a signature default. This branch carries it over and states it as a fact on a page it wrote, so the branch is responsible for it. Severity stays major: it is a wrong default-value (API) claim, and it names a smaller "base" model when the real default is the "large" one. The fix is to change the string to `jackboyla/glirel-large-v0`.

findings.title: Says the 4000/200 chunk defaults change when token chunking is selected; the constructor keeps them
findings.detail: "unless token-based chunking is selected" suggests that StreamingExtractor(..., chunk_by_tokens=True) switches to token-sized defaults. It does not. The constructor always defaults to DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE=4000 and DEFAULT_OVERLAP=200, so a reader who turns on token chunking without passing chunk_size gets 4000-token chunks (about 16k characters). Only create_streaming_extractor() switches to 1000/50.
findings.evidence: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/extractor-streaming.adoc:10: "`DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE` is 4000 characters and `DEFAULT_OVERLAP` is 200, unless token-based chunking is selected."  Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/streaming.py:353-355 (`chunk_size: int = DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE`, `overlap: int = DEFAULT_OVERLAP`, `chunk_by_tokens: bool = False`), and 603-605 (only create_streaming_extractor picks DEFAULT_TOKEN_CHUNK_SIZE). Command: `uv run python -c "...StreamingExtractor(NoOpExtractor(), chunk_by_tokens=True)...; create_streaming_extractor(NoOpExtractor(), chunk_by_tokens=True)"` printed `ctor 4000 200` / `factory 1000 50`.
findings.fix: State that the constructor defaults are 4000/200 whatever the chunking mode, so pass chunk_size/overlap explicitly with chunk_by_tokens=True, or use create_streaming_extractor(chunk_by_tokens=True), which defaults to 1000 tokens and 50 overlap.
findings.v1reason: extractor-streaming.adoc:10 says the defaults are 4000 and 200 "unless token-based chunking is selected". The StreamingExtractor.__init__ signature (streaming.py:353-355) always defaults to DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE and DEFAULT_OVERLAP, whatever chunk_by_tokens is. Only create_streaming_extractor switches to the token defaults (streaming.py:603-606). So the page implies the class defaults change with the chunking mode, and they don't.

Download with: python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm"). findings.title: with_llm_fallback is called a fallback, but build() runs the LLM on every extraction
findings.detail: build() appends the LLM as an ordinary stage and returns ExtractionPipeline(stages, merge_strategy) without stop_on_success. Every stage therefore runs on every call and the results are merged. The LLM is never skipped when spaCy or GLiNER succeed. A reader who picks this method to limit LLM cost gets an LLM call on every text.
findings.evidence: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/extractor-builder.adoc:103: "Add LLM extractor as fallback." (the example at line 24 uses `.with_llm_fallback("gpt-4o-mini")` together with `.merge_by_confidence()`). Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/factory.py:569-584 (`stages.append(LLMEntityExtractor(...))` ... `return ExtractionPipeline(stages=stages, merge_strategy=self._merge_strategy)`); src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/pipeline.py:480 (early stop happens only `if self.stop_on_success or self.merge_strategy == MergeStrategy.FIRST_SUCCESS`).
findings.fix: Describe the method as adding an LLM stage that runs alongside the other stages and whose results are merged. To get real fallback behaviour, build ExtractionPipeline directly with stop_on_success=True or MergeStrategy.FIRST_SUCCESS.
findings.v1reason: with_llm_fallback only sets _enable_llm (factory.py:451-455). build() appends the LLM as an ordinary stage and returns ExtractionPipeline(stages, merge_strategy) (factory.py:569-584). The builder's strategies are CONFIDENCE, UNION, INTERSECTION and CASCADE, never FIRST_SUCCESS, and it never sets stop_on_success, so the early stop at pipeline.py:480 never fires and the LLM runs on every call. The wording carries over from main ("Add LLM as fallback stage") and from the docstring, but it is on a page this branch added and it misleads the reader.

findings.title: SchemaManager(client.graph) goes through the deprecated graph proxy; load_schema emits a DeprecationWarning
findings.detail: This branch changed the example from `client._client` to `client.graph`. On bolt, client.graph returns _DeprecatedGraphProxy, and SchemaManager.load_schema, list_schemas and the other read methods call execute_read on it. That call raises a DeprecationWarning saying the accessor "will be removed in v0.6.0", although the released package is 0.6.0. The docs therefore recommend a path that the SDK itself says is deprecated. Other pages (reference/api/memory-client.adoc:122, how-to/migrate-to-nams.adoc:103) tell readers not to use client.graph for reads.
findings.evidence: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/schemas-custom.adoc:55: `manager = SchemaManager(client.graph)`. Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/__init__.py:1047 `return _DeprecatedGraphProxy(self._client)`; __init__.py:346-357 execute_read warns "MemoryClient.graph.execute_read is deprecated and will be removed in v0.6.0"; src/neo4j_agent_memory/schema/persistence.py:179,200 (load paths use `self._client.execute_read`).
findings.fix: Say what the SchemaManager constructor actually needs (a connected Neo4jClient). Show a Neo4jClient built from settings, or note that passing client.graph triggers the execute_read deprecation warning. Maintainers may prefer a non-deprecated public accessor in the SDK.
findings.v1reason: schemas-custom.adoc:55 shows `SchemaManager(client.graph)`, which was `client._client` on main. On bolt, client.graph returns _DeprecatedGraphProxy (__init__.py:1047), whose execute_read emits a one-time DeprecationWarning saying it "will be removed in v0.6.0" (__init__.py:346-357). SchemaManager's read methods call self._client.execute_read (persistence.py:179, 200 and others). The code still works and the default warning filters will likely hide the warning, so this is a minor inconsistency, not a failure. Whether the SDK should offer a non-deprecated public accessor is a maintainer decision.
