findings.title: Embedded Python SDK credentials named as NEO4J_URI/NEO4J_USERNAME/NEO4J_PASSWORD; MemorySettings ignores them
findings.detail: The embedded-SDK option lists `NEO4J_URI` / `NEO4J_USERNAME` / `NEO4J_PASSWORD` as its credentials. `MemorySettings` uses `env_prefix="NAM_"` with `__` nesting, so it reads `NAM_NEO4J__URI` / `NAM_NEO4J__USERNAME` / `NAM_NEO4J__PASSWORD`. A reader who sets the documented variables in a deployment and constructs `MemorySettings()` connects to bolt://localhost:7687 with an empty password. The deployment page this branch replaced had a correct 'Application environment variables' table (`NAM_NEO4J__URI` etc.), so the branch introduced the regression. It also contradicts the environment-variables reference.
findings.evidence: Offending text, deploy-an-application.adoc:26: "Credentials:: `NEO4J_URI` / `NEO4J_USERNAME` / `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, plus embedding/LLM provider credentials...". Source of truth: src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:629 `env_prefix="NAM_"`, env_nested_delimiter="__". The command `env -i ... NEO4J_URI=bolt://example:7687 NEO4J_USERNAME=bob NEO4J_PASSWORD=pw .venv/bin/python -c "from neo4j_agent_memory import MemorySettings; s=MemorySettings(); print(s.neo4j.uri, s.neo4j.username, repr(s.neo4j.password.get_secret_value()))"` prints `bolt://localhost:7687 neo4j ''`. With `NAM_NEO4J__URI=bolt://example:7687 NAM_NEO4J__PASSWORD=pw` it prints `bolt://example:7687 neo4j 'pw'`. environment-variables.adoc:310: "The Python settings family instead uses NAM_NEO4J__... and USERNAME." The old page (git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/deployment.adoc) listed `NAM_NEO4J__URI`, `NAM_NEO4J__USERNAME`, `NAM_NEO4J__PASSWORD` under 'Application Environment Variables'.
findings.fix: State `NAM_NEO4J__URI` / `NAM_NEO4J__USERNAME` / `NAM_NEO4J__PASSWORD`, which `MemorySettings` reads. Alternatively, say the application must read `NEO4J_*` itself and pass the values into `MemorySettings(neo4j=...)`, and link reference/environment-variables.adoc.
findings.v1reason: deploy-an-application.adoc:26 (a new page) lists `NEO4J_URI` / `NEO4J_USERNAME` / `NEO4J_PASSWORD` as the credentials for the embedded SDK. settings.py:629-630 sets env_prefix="NAM_" and env_nested_delimiter="__". I ran MemorySettings() in a clean env with NEO4J_URI=bolt://example:7687, NEO4J_USERNAME=bob and NEO4J_PASSWORD=pw; it printed `bolt://localhost:7687 neo4j ''`. environment-variables.adoc:310 says the Python settings use NAM_NEO4J__..., and the old deployment.adoc:173-181 listed NAM_NEO4J__URI/USERNAME/PASSWORD. The branch introduced this regression.

findings.title: Active-binding caveat covers Python 0.6.0 only; released TS 0.5.0 has the same latest-revision bug
findings.detail: The new 'Python 0.6.0 active binding' section warns that Python's `get_active()` can report the latest revision when an older one is active. It then says 'Current TypeScript source exposes versionId, revision and validationMode from the authoritative response'. The released npm package `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0`, which MAINTAINING.md tells application instructions to pin, still uses the old composed lookup: `list()` then `currentVersion(...)`, which picks the latest revision. The authoritative-version code exists only in this branch's unreleased typescript/src change. A TS 0.5.0 user reading this page would trust `getActive().versionId` / `validationMode` for a rollback target, which is exactly the hazard the page warns Python users about. The disclaimer 'this is not a statement that a corresponding npm release is available' does not say that 0.5.0 is affected.
findings.evidence: ontology-api.adoc:91-96: "Current TypeScript source exposes `versionId`, `revision` and `validationMode` from the authoritative response... this is not a statement that a corresponding npm release is available." The command `git show typescript-v0.5.0:typescript/src/ontology/index.ts` shows, at lines 410-424: "// Compose version metadata via a second lookup ... const summaries = await this.list(); ... const current = currentVersion(detail, match.currentRevision)". `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- typescript/src/ontology/index.ts` shows this branch replacing that code with `raw.version` parsing. The typescript/CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] section is empty. docs/MAINTAINING.md: "Application instructions install the verified npm releases (`@neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0`...)" and "Python 0.6.0 still has the older active-ontology metadata inference" (TS 0.5.0 is not mentioned).
findings.fix: Extend the caveat to cover `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory` 0.5.0 (`getActive()` metadata can report the latest revision) and point TS readers to the same direct `GET /ontologies/active` read until a release ships the fix. Also add an [Unreleased] CHANGELOG entry for the source change.
findings.v1reason: `git show typescript-v0.5.0:typescript/src/ontology/index.ts` shows getActive() getting its metadata from list(), then get(), then currentVersion(detail, match.currentRevision). That returns the latest revision, not the bound one. This branch replaces that code with raw.version parsing. typescript/CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] is empty. ontology-api.adoc:91-96 describes only 'current TypeScript source' and gives no warning that the released 0.5.0, which MAINTAINING.md:85 tells applications to pin, has the same hazard the page warns Python 0.6.0 users about.
findings.v2reason:
I ran both versions of the code and the finding holds. The released TS 0.5.0 `getActive()` in typescript/src/ontology/index.ts (tag typescript-v0.5.0, lines 400-425) and the released Python 0.6.0 `get_active()` in src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py (tag python-v0.6.0, lines 370-405) build the version metadata the same way: `list()`, then the `is_active` match, then `get()`, then `currentVersion`/`_current_version`. That last step picks the summary's `current_revision`, or the highest revision if `current_revision` is missing, and it ignores the authoritative `version` in the `/ontologies/active` response. So whatever ontology-api.adoc:76-81 says about Python 0.6.0 also applies to TS 0.5.0.

I ran the 0.5.0 source against a mock transport where revision 1 is the bound version and revision 2 is the latest. `getActive()` returned `versionId` ver-2, `revision` 2 and `validationMode` permissive. HEAD source returned ver-1, 1 and strict. So the correct behaviour exists only in this branch's unreleased typescript/src change (commit d41e4bd). The `[Unreleased]` section of typescript/CHANGELOG.md is empty.

The docs point TS readers at the unfixed release:
- ontology-api.adoc:91-96 describes only 'Current TypeScript source' and says 'this is not a statement that a corresponding npm release is available'. It never says that 0.5.0 is affected.
- docs/MAINTAINING.md:85 tells application instructions to pin `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0`, and it flags only Python 0.6.0 as having the old inference.
- reference/typescript-api.adoc:440-441 still describes `getActive()` as returning 'composed `validationMode` / `revision` / `versionId`' with no caveat.

A TS 0.5.0 user who follows these pages would trust `getActive().versionId` or `.validationMode` to capture a rollback target. That is exactly the hazard the page warns Python users about. The page's own warning covers only Python, so this is a real omission, not a guess about the hosted service. Major severity is right: the docs misdescribe how the released API behaves, and no build breaks.
findings.reproduction:

findings.title: multi_tenant=True claim is backwards: scoping works without it and unscoped writes then raise
findings.detail: The page says multi-tenant scoping needs `multi_tenant=True` plus `user_identifier=`, and that unscoped calls then keep working exactly as before. The source does the opposite on both counts. `user_identifier` links the conversation or preference to a `:User` whether or not the flag is set. The flag only makes the enforced write paths (add_message, add_messages_batch, add_preference, start_trace) raise ValueError when `user_identifier` is left out. A reader who turns the flag on expecting unscoped code to keep running will see existing writes fail. The how-to has it right: 'memory.multi_tenant=True requires it on specific write paths'.
findings.evidence:
operational-primitives.adoc:21-23: "Multi-tenant scoping requires `MemorySettings.memory.multi_tenant=True` plus a `user_identifier=` kwarg on the specific call; unscoped calls keep working exactly as before."
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:340-346, multi_tenant description: "When True, APIs that accept ``user_identifier=`` raise a ValueError if the kwarg is omitted."; src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:350-357 _enforce_multi_tenant raises ValueError.
Command: `ShortTermMemory(client=None, multi_tenant=True).add_message('s','user','hi',extract_entities=False,generate_embedding=False)` gives `ValueError MemorySettings.memory.multi_tenant=True but no user_identifier was supplied.`
how-to/multi-tenancy.adoc:46: "`memory.multi_tenant=True` requires it on specific write paths but does not make all reads user-scoped."
findings.fix: Rewrite the bullet: `user_identifier=` on the supported write methods associates records with a `:User` whether or not the flag is set. Setting `MemorySettings.memory.multi_tenant=True` makes those write paths raise ValueError when `user_identifier` is omitted, so it is a guard against accidental unscoped writes. It is not what turns scoping on.
findings.v1reason: operational-primitives.adoc (new on this branch) lines 21-23 say scoping 'requires `MemorySettings.memory.multi_tenant=True` plus a `user_identifier=` kwarg ... unscoped calls keep working exactly as before'. The source says otherwise. settings.py:340-346 describes multi_tenant as 'When True, APIs that accept user_identifier= raise a ValueError if the kwarg is omitted'. short_term.py:350-357 _enforce_multi_tenant raises when the flag is on and user_identifier is None, and it is called at 413 and 712. _ensure_conversation (1263-1278) links the user whenever user_identifier is given, whether or not the flag is set. So the flag is a guard that makes unscoped writes fail. It is not what turns scoping on.
findings.v2reason:
The page is new on this branch (commit d3db0ff; `git show ec9fc65:` reports the path does not exist on main). At docs/modules/ROOT/pages/explanation/operational-primitives.adoc:21-23 it says: "Multi-tenant scoping requires `MemorySettings.memory.multi_tenant=True` plus a `user_identifier=` kwarg on the specific call; unscoped calls keep working exactly as before."

Running add_message shows that turning scoping on does not need the flag:
- With multi_tenant=False, passing user_identifier='alice' still links the conversation to the :User. The code is _ensure_conversation, src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:1263 and 1277-1278, which runs `if user_identifier is not None: await self._link_user_to_conversation(...)` with no check on the flag.
- The flag's only effect is the guard in _enforce_multi_tenant (short_term.py:350-357). It raises ValueError when user_identifier is omitted. The field description at src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:340-346 says the same thing.

So the claim that scoping "requires multi_tenant=True" is wrong. It also contradicts how-to/multi-tenancy.adoc:46: "`memory.multi_tenant=True` requires it on specific write paths but does not make all reads user-scoped."

One softening point. The bullet sits under "Opt-in by default", so "unscoped calls keep working exactly as before" can be read as describing the default (flag off), and that reading is true. Even so, the sentence ties the flag to scoping in the wrong direction. A reader who sets the flag believing it is what turns scoping on will find that every unscoped write on the guarded paths raises. That is a loud failure with no data loss. It is still a wrong behaviour claim, so major stands.

I wrote scratchpad/mt.py. Command: `uv run python .../scratchpad/mt.py`

Output:
- flag=False uid=None: ok, user links=[]
- flag=False uid=alice: ok, user links=['alice']   (user scoping works with no flag)
- flag=True uid=None: ValueError MemorySettings.memory.multi_tenant=True but no user_identifier was supplied. Pass user_identifier= to scope this write.
- flag=True uid=alice: ok, user links=['alice']

Supporting checks:
- `git log ec9fc65..HEAD -- docs/.../operational-primitives.adoc` returns d3db0ff, and `git show ec9fc65:<path>` returns "exists on disk, but not in 'ec9fc65'", so this branch introduced the text.

findings.title: POLE+O subtype catalog removed; the page it defers to has no subtype list
findings.detail: The branch cut the per-type subtype lists (PERSON: INDIVIDUAL, ALIAS, ...) from this page and now says the schema reference owns them. reference/schemas.adoc is an index of GLiNER domain schemas. No docs page now lists the valid POLE+O subtypes. This matters on Bolt: for a POLE+O type, a subtype outside the known list is silently left off the node's labels. A reader can no longer find out which subtypes produce labels such as `:Vehicle`.
findings.evidence:
poleo-model.adoc:36: "The xref:reference/schemas.adoc[schema reference] owns the complete supported type and subtype lists." (also line 99: "Domain schemas and subtype catalog").
`grep -rn "SUSPECT\|WITNESS\|COORDINATES\|LANDMARK\|PHONE\|NONPROFIT\|EDUCATIONAL" docs/modules/ROOT/pages` returns no matches. The old page (git show ec9fc65:.../poleo-model.adoc lines 32-226) had `=== PERSON` ... `=== ORGANIZATION` subtype sections.
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/schema/models.py:372-430 defines the subtype lists. src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/query_builder.py:194-201: "For POLE+O types, only allow known subtypes" (invalid subtype gets no label).
findings.fix: Add the POLE+O subtype table, taken from schema/models.py, to a reference page (for example reference/schema-objects.adoc or reference/schemas-custom.adoc). Point this page and its See-also entry at that section, and say that an unknown subtype on a POLE+O type gets no label.
findings.v1reason: poleo-model.adoc:36 says 'The xref:reference/schemas.adoc[schema reference] owns the complete supported type and subtype lists', and line 99 links to 'Domain schemas and subtype catalog'. reference/schemas.adoc is an index of GLiNER domain schemas. schemas-domains.adoc's poleo section lists only extraction labels (person, organization, ...), and schemas-custom.adoc:68-92 lists only GLiNER-to-type mappings. `git grep SUSPECT|WITNESS` at ec9fc65 finds them only in the old poleo-model.adoc, and at HEAD no page lists them. query_builder.py:194-201 returns None, so no label, for a subtype that is not in the known list for a POLE+O type. The catalog readers need is therefore gone.
findings.v2reason:
The finding holds. At HEAD, poleo-model.adoc:36 says "The xref:reference/schemas.adoc[schema reference] owns the complete supported type and subtype lists", and its See-also entry (line ~99) links to "Domain schemas and subtype catalog". No page under docs/modules/ROOT/pages or partials lists the POLE+O subtypes:
- reference/schemas.adoc and schema-objects.adoc contain no subtype list.
- schemas-custom.adoc:68-92 lists only GLiNER-to-POLE+O mappings.
- extractors.adoc, mcp-tools.adoc, long-term-entities.adoc and long-term.adoc give only one-off examples (VEHICLE, ADDRESS, COMPANY, INDIVIDUAL).

At ec9fc65, the old poleo-model.adoc had "=== PERSON" through "=== ORGANIZATION" subtype sections (lines 34-194). That page was the only one in docs/modules that contained SUSPECT. The branch removed the catalog.

I ran the code path, and the lost information does change behaviour. For a POLE+O type, validate_subtype returns None for any subtype outside VALID_SUBTYPES, so the node gets no subtype label: validate_subtype('ORGANIZATION','RESTAURANT') returned None, while ('OBJECT','VEHICLE') returned 'Vehicle'. A reader can no longer find out which subtypes produce labels.

One addition for the fix: VALID_SUBTYPES in graph/query_builder.py, which decides the labels, is a superset of the lists in schema/models.py. It also includes OBJECT PRODUCT, LOCATION FACILITY/GEOGRAPHIC/GEOPOLITICAL, EVENT DATE/TIME and ORGANIZATION GROUP. Any restored catalog should be generated from VALID_SUBTYPES, not from models.py alone, or it will under-report the subtypes that get labels. Major is the right severity: the page links to missing reference content, and the missing content governs label behaviour. No build or test breaks.

The new answer sends readers to 'database prerequisites' in Getting started and 'vector-index requirements' in the Configuration reference. Neither page, nor any other docs page, states a Neo4j server version. findings.v2reason: The defect is real. The FAQ answer at docs/modules/ROOT/pages/faq.adoc:51 sends Bolt users to "the database prerequisites in Getting started" and "the vector-index requirements in Configuration", but neither exists. In getting-started.adoc, "_prerequisites" is only an empty legacy anchor, `anchor:_2_install_the_sdk[]anchor:_prerequisites[]` at line 68, sitting above a "See also" list, and the page's Aura section (lines 26-38) names no Neo4j server version. reference/configuration.adoc has no match for "version", "vector" or "Neo4j 5". tutorials/first-agent-memory.adoc and sdks/python.adoc have no vector-index or server-version text either. findings.title: Says Strands and Mastra merge tiers into one block and replay recent messages; they do not
findings.detail: The page says the Vercel middleware, the Strands ConversationManager and the Mastra recipe all fold reflections and observations into a single prepended block and then replay recent messages as ordinary turns. Only the Vercel middleware does that. Strands adds each reflection and each observation as its own system message and never replays `recentMessages`; the inner manager's messages are kept. The Mastra recipe only calls `getContext()` and does no prompt assembly. Strands also does not fall back to flat conversation history (line 66-68): on failure it leaves the inner manager's output unchanged.
findings.evidence:
context-tiers.adoc:57-64: "the Vercel AI SDK middleware ..., the Strands `ConversationManager` ..., and the Mastra recipe ... all call `getContext()` ... and fold reflections and observations into a single prepended context block, then replay recent messages as ordinary turns."
typescript/src/integrations/strands/conversation-manager.ts:111-125: one `contextInjectionMessage(...)` per reflection and per observation, `agentLike.messages = [...prepend, ...agentLike.messages]` (recentMessages unused); lines 131-134: on failure "fall back to whatever the inner manager produces".
typescript/src/middleware/vercel-ai.ts:181-217: the single "Relevant memory" block plus the recentMessages history.
how-to/typescript/mastra.adoc:97: `const context = await client.shortTerm.getContext(thread.id);` with no prompt assembly.
findings.fix: Describe each integration separately. Vercel middleware: one prepended block plus recent messages, falling back to flat history. Strands: one system message per reflection or observation, layered over the inner manager, left unchanged on failure. Mastra: the application reads `getContext()` itself.
findings.v1reason: context-tiers.adoc:57-64 says the Vercel middleware, Strands and Mastra all 'fold reflections and observations into a single prepended context block, then replay recent messages'. In strands/conversation-manager.ts:111-129 Strands pushes one contextInjectionMessage per reflection and per observation, prepends them to agent.messages, and never uses recentMessages. On failure (131-134) it falls back to the inner manager. The Mastra how-to (mastra.adoc:97) only calls getContext() and does no prompt assembly. The finding's point about the line 66-68 fallback is weaker, because that sentence says 'that middleware' (singular). The main claim is still wrong for two of the three integrations.

findings.title: Observations/reflections called hosted-TS-only, but the Python MCP server has its own three-tier view
findings.detail: The glossary, context-tiers.adoc:5-17 and memory-types.adoc:37 present observations and reflections as a hosted-service concept of the TypeScript client, and name exactly two senses of 'observation'. The Python MCP reference documents `memory_get_observations` as returning 'the three-tier context hierarchy: reflections ..., observations ...'. That tool comes from the local MemoryObserver in src/neo4j_agent_memory/mcp/_observer.py and works on Bolt, so it is a third, Bolt-available sense. The Python NAMS client also exposes `get_context` (three-tier), `get_observations` and `get_reflections`, so the concept is not limited to TypeScript.
findings.evidence:
glossary.adoc:30: "Observation (context tier) |A hosted-service, auto-generated summary ... returned by `getObservations()`"; glossary.adoc:31: "Reflection |A hosted-service, higher-level synthesis"; memory-types.adoc:37: "The hosted TypeScript client also uses 'observation' and 'reflection' in an unrelated sense".
reference/mcp-tools.adoc:371: "Returns the three-tier context hierarchy: reflections (session summaries), observations (facts, decisions), and session statistics."
src/neo4j_agent_memory/mcp/_observer.py:1-4: "Observational Memory - context compression and observation extraction".
src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:400-401 `get_context` "Return three-tier context (reflections + observations + recent messages)"; lines 542, 559: `get_observations`, `get_reflections`.
findings.fix: Say that the hosted three-tier context is available from both SDKs on NAMS (TypeScript `getContext`/`getObservations`/`getReflections`, Python `short_term.get_context`/`get_observations`/`get_reflections`). Separately note the Python MCP server's local observational memory (`memory_get_observations`) and its own observations and reflections.
findings.v1reason: memory-types.adoc:37 says 'The hosted TypeScript client also uses observation and reflection', and context-tiers.adoc:5-17 frames the three tiers as a concept of the TypeScript client. The Python NAMS client has get_context ('three-tier context', nams/short_term.py:400-401), get_observations (542) and get_reflections (559). The branch's own rest-api.adoc:68-69 maps these endpoints to both `short_term.get_observations` and `getObservations`. mcp-tools.adoc:371 documents a third, MCP-local sense ('three-tier context hierarchy: reflections ..., observations ...'). The glossary names only two senses and cites only the TS methods, which contradicts those pages.

findings.title: llm=None check attributed to _resolve_providers; it lives in _validate_llm_consistency
findings.detail: The list says `_resolve_providers` does step 5: keep explicit `llm=None` only when extraction needs no LLM, otherwise raise, and auto-fill when omitted. `_resolve_providers` just lets `None` through. A separate validator, `_validate_llm_consistency`, raises or fills in `LLMConfig()`.
findings.evidence:
why-provider-protocol.adoc:81,87: "implemented by a `@model_validator(mode=\"after\")` on `MemorySettings` (named `_resolve_providers`). It: ... Keeps explicit `llm=None` only when extraction does not require an LLM; otherwise construction raises."
src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:740-742 (_resolve_providers): `elif self.llm is None: # Legitimate "no LLM" — handled by _validate_llm_consistency below. pass`; lines 769-790: `_validate_llm_consistency` raises ValueError or sets `self.llm = LLMConfig()`.

findings.v1reason: why-provider-protocol.adoc:81-87 (new text) credits the llm=None keep-or-raise and auto-fill behaviour to `_resolve_providers`. findings.title: Reasoning 'observation' described as a tool call's result; it is a ReasoningStep field
findings.detail: The glossary (lines 15 and 30) calls a reasoning observation 'a tool call's recorded result'. context-tiers.adoc:74-75 calls it part of 'a tool call's thought/action/observation triple'. In the source, thought, action and observation are ReasoningStep fields, and a ToolCall carries `result`. `record_tool_call(auto_observation=True)` can copy a result into the step's observation, but the two fields are separate.
findings.evidence:
glossary.adoc:15: "\"observation\" here is a tool call's recorded result"; context-tiers.adoc:74-75: "as part of a tool call's thought/action/observation triple".
src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/reasoning.py:78-86: `class ReasoningStep` with `thought`, `action`, `observation`; lines 70-71: `ToolCall` has `result`; line 269: "auto_observation: If True, set the step's observation from the result".
findings.fix: Describe it as a reasoning step's recorded observation (often derived from a tool result), part of the step's thought/action/observation.
findings.v1reason: glossary.adoc:15 says '"observation" here is a tool call's recorded result', and line 30 repeats it. context-tiers.adoc:74-75 says 'a tool call's thought/action/observation triple'. In reasoning.py:77-86 thought, action and observation are ReasoningStep fields, and ToolCall (65-74) carries `result`. auto_observation (269) only optionally copies a result into the step's observation. The distinction is small but the wording misstates the model.

findings.title: MAINTAINING says `make docs-install` installs Playwright; it doesn't, so render checks silently skip
findings.detail: The page says the rendered-site pytest module skips when Playwright is not installed under docs/diagrams, and points to `make docs-install` as the fix. That target only runs `npm ci` in docs/, whose package.json has no Playwright. A maintainer who follows the documented workflow (`make docs-install`, `make docs`, `make docs-lint`) gets the render test skipped, and `make docs-lint` still passes. The Makefile comment says these checks 'fail this target'. Line 15 is also inaccurate: `make docs-lint` does not 'build once into a fresh temporary directory'. findings.title: Edited README MCP command still uses deprecated `--transport sse` for 'network deployment'
findings.detail: The branch rewrote this command (adding `--backend bolt --user`) but kept `--transport sse` with the comment 'SSE transport (network deployment)'. In the released CLI, sse is deprecated: it prints a warning and serves Streamable HTTP. The bind host defaults to 127.0.0.1, so the command as shown is not reachable from the network. The project's own guidance is to use `--transport http` in docs.

findings.v1reason: README.md:274-275 was edited on this branch (the diff line '+... --transport sse --port 8080 --backend bolt ...') and still says 'SSE transport (network deployment)'. As written, the command is not reachable from the network.

findings.v2reason:
The finding holds. HEAD docs/modules/ROOT/pages/explanation/poleo-model.adoc:36 says "The xref:reference/schemas.adoc[schema reference] owns the complete supported type and subtype lists." No page under docs/modules/ROOT/pages or partials lists the POLE+O subtypes. A whole-word grep for SUSPECT, PHONE, LANDMARK, EVIDENCE, ALIAS, PERSONA, WITNESS, VICTIM, WEAPON or FACILITY returns nothing. reference/schemas.adoc only links to other pages. Its only POLE+O references are an xref back to the poleo-model page (line 22) and a pointer to the partial GLiNER mapping in schemas-custom.adoc. The old page at ec9fc65 did have a subtype table for each type (for example SUSPECT at line 51, VEHICLE at line 78, LANDMARK/FACILITY at lines 139/142, with === PERSON/OBJECT/LOCATION/EVENT/ORGANIZATION sections at lines 34-194). Running the code confirms that the list matters. src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/query_builder.py:20-45 defines VALID_SUBTYPES, and validate_subtype (around lines 194-203) returns None for any POLE+O subtype outside that set. build_label_set_clause('OBJECT','CAR') produces only 'SET e:Object', with no subtype label. So a reader cannot find out which subtypes become the `:Entity:Object:Vehicle`-style labels that poleo-model.adoc:43 describes. Major is the right severity: needed content is missing and the pointer is wrong. Nothing fails at build time, and the workaround (read the source) is not documented.

findings.title: Exporter's sibling PNGs make the orphan check fail after the documented export steps
findings.detail: The exporter always writes a PNG next to every SVG. The new check_manifest() orphan rule (manage_diagrams.py:117) fails on any file under images/diagrams that is not in the manifest, and the manifest has no PNG record for 24 of the SVG diagrams. So exporting any diagram as MAINTAINING.md:120 describes (except the-three-layer one, whose PNG happens to be tracked) leaves an orphan PNG. After that, `manage_diagrams.py status`, `make docs-lint` (check_docs.py:269) and tests/docs/test_diagram_manifest.py::test_published_diagrams_are_mapped_and_fresh all fail. The `--all` mode that the Makefile tells maintainers to run ('4. Export: node scripts/export_diagrams.mjs --all') is worse. Mapping every record's output to .svg creates 25 untracked files. It also overwrites 37 tracked outputs, including the legacy unresolved-provenance architecture-overview.png: the committed 1460x1157 image gets replaced by a 758x548 re-render.
findings.evidence: scripts/export_diagrams.mjs:78 `await writeFile(output.replace(/\.svg$/, '.png'), ...)`; lines 21-23 map each record with a source to `.replace(/\.(png|svg)$/, '.svg')`. Simulation over docs/diagrams/manifest.json: 'would create untracked: 25' (architecture-overview.svg, bolt-vs-nams-data-flow.png, buffered-write-flow.png, ... typescript-mcp-architecture.png), 'would overwrite tracked: 37'. Re-exporting architecture-overview to scratch: committed PNG pixelWidth 1460 / pixelHeight 1157, fresh export 758 / 548. Makefile:525 `@echo "4. Export: node scripts/export_diagrams.mjs --all"`.
findings.fix: Add a flag (or make it the default) so the exporter writes only the SVG, or writes the PNG only when the manifest tracks that PNG. Limit `--all` to records whose output is .svg and whose status is not unresolved-provenance. Or document that the sibling PNG must be deleted or recorded before running status.
findings.v1reason: export_diagrams.mjs:78 always writes a sibling PNG. check_manifest() (manage_diagrams.py:109-117) flags any file under images/diagrams that is in neither the manifest nor a page reference. Of the 30 SVG records that have a source, 24 have no PNG record. My simulation of --all (Makefile:525) gives 25 new untracked files and 37 overwritten tracked outputs. I exported architecture-overview to scratch: the committed PNG is 1460x1157, the fresh one is 758x548, and they differ. The documented single example (the-three-layer, MAINTAINING.md) happens to have a tracked PNG. It is only a maintainer-tooling trap with an easy workaround (delete the PNG or record it), and current CI passes, so minor rather than major.

findings.v2reason:
The defect is real, and this branch introduced it. At HEAD, docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/team-memory-in-your-editor.adoc:181 calls the Claude Code `.mcp.json` "a project-scoped template". It tells readers to "copy its URI, username and password into the literal JSON values" and to "Also supply an OpenAI key", and says "these JSON fields do not require shell interpolation". The sample at :201-202 has literal `"NEO4J_PASSWORD": "replace-with-your-Aura-password"` and `"OPENAI_API_KEY": "replace-with-your-OpenAI-key"` values.

At the merge-base (ec9fc65, old lines 136-137) the same section said: "Project scope, so it is committed and every teammate gets it. `${VAR}` ... are expanded from the environment, so no secret lands in git."

Other files contradict the new text:
- The template the page includes at :90, examples/claude-code-team-memory/.mcp.json.example, still uses `${NEO4J_PASSWORD}`, `${NEO4J_USERNAME}` and `${OPENAI_API_KEY}`.
- examples/claude-code-team-memory/README.md says "For Claude Code, export OPENAI_API_KEY ... its template expands ${OPENAI_API_KEY}".
- The same README still says "# Claude Code (project scope — commit it, it holds no secret)".

Step 4 (:238-240) says doctor.py checks that configs "contain no pasted key". I ran doctor.py on a populated file and confirmed it does not catch these secrets: its only credential check is `KEY_SHAPE = re.compile(r"nams_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{12,}")` (doctor.py:69, 182-189). A `.mcp.json` holding a literal Aura password and an `sk-` OpenAI key passes with "no pasted key".

Mitigations exist but don't fix the page:
- The page says "Keep the populated credential file private".
- This repo's .gitignore:92 ignores `.mcp.json`. But the tutorial targets the reader's own project (agent-memory-tutorials/), where no such ignore rule is guaranteed.

Result: the page contradicts its own included template and the README. A reader who follows it and then the README's "commit it" advice commits an Aura password and an OpenAI key. The branch caused this. Major is the right severity. It is not a blocker because the page does say to keep the file private.
findings.reproduction:
1. `sed -n 80,260p docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/team-memory-in-your-editor.adoc` shows, at HEAD line 181: "This is a project-scoped template. ... copy its URI, username and password into the literal JSON values. Also supply an OpenAI key ... these JSON fields do not require shell interpolation. Keep the populated credential file private." Lines 201-202 hold the literal NEO4J_PASSWORD and OPENAI_API_KEY placeholders.
2. `git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/team-memory-in-your-editor.adoc` shows the old lines 136-137: "Project scope, so it is committed and every teammate gets it. `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` are expanded from the environment, so no secret lands in git."
3. `cat examples/claude-code-team-memory/.mcp.json.example` shows the env block uses "${NEO4J_PASSWORD}", "${NEO4J_USERNAME}" and "${OPENAI_API_KEY}". This is the file the page includes.
4. The README Claude Code copy step says "# Claude Code (project scope — commit it, it holds no secret)". The README's prose says the Claude Code template expands ${OPENAI_API_KEY}.
5. I wrote scratchpad/review/populated.mcp.json with NEO4J_PASSWORD="Sup3rS3cretAuraPassw0rdXYZ" and OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-AAAA...". Then from examples/claude-code-team-memory I ran: `uv run python -c "import doctor; doctor.check_config_file(Path(...), show_servers=False, committed=True)"`. Output: `[PASS] populated.mcp.json: valid JSON, 2 server(s), no pasted key`. So doctor.py's "no pasted key" check misses Aura and OpenAI secrets even in committed mode.
6. `grep -n mcp.json .gitignore` returns `92:.mcp.json`. This mitigates the risk only inside this repo, not in a reader's project.

findings.title: CI skips the provider build that the nextjs-memory-chat example now needs, so its type-check leg fails
findings.detail: This branch made nextjs-memory-chat depend on @neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider through file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider, and its code imports that package. That package's dist/ is gitignored and has no prepare script. The type-check-examples job builds typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider only for the nams-ai-provider example. On a fresh checkout, the nextjs-memory-chat leg therefore installs a link to a package with no dist/index.d.ts, and `npx tsc --noEmit` cannot resolve the module. findings.title: Index 'Running an example' commands for nextjs-memory-chat omit the provider build and fail
findings.detail: The index README runs nextjs-memory-chat as its worked example but builds only the SDK before `npm ci` in the example. That example also links @neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider from typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider, whose dist/ is not committed. The example's own README says both packages must be built first. The Notes section (line 60) repeats the gap: it says to build 'the SDK' and names only `file:../..`.
findings.evidence: typescript/examples/README.md:44-53: `cd typescript` / `npm ci` / `npm run build` / `cd examples/nextjs-memory-chat` / `npm ci` / ... `npm run dev`. The source of truth is typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/README.md:134-143: `cd packages/vercel-ai-provider` / `npm ci` / `npm run build` ... 'Build **both packages before** installing this example; their exports point at `typescript/dist/` and `typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider/dist/`, and npm does not build local `file:` dependencies on installation.'
findings.fix: Add `(cd packages/vercel-ai-provider && npm ci && npm run build)` before `cd examples/nextjs-memory-chat`. In Notes, state that nextjs-memory-chat and nams-ai-provider also need the provider package built.
findings.v1reason: typescript/examples/README.md:44-53 runs `cd typescript && npm ci && npm run build`, then `cd examples/nextjs-memory-chat && npm ci ... npm run dev`, and never builds packages/vercel-ai-provider. The example's own README (lines 128-143) says: 'Build **both packages before** installing this example ... npm does not build local `file:` dependencies'. The Notes section (lines 58-61) mentions only `file:../..`. A reader who follows the index gets an unresolved @neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider import.
findings.v2reason:
I ran it and the finding holds. The steps at typescript/examples/README.md:44-53 are `cd typescript && npm ci && npm run build`, then `cd examples/nextjs-memory-chat && npm ci ... npm run dev`. Those steps never build typescript/packages/vercel-ai-provider.

This branch's commit e2bcb93 added `"@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider": "file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider"` to typescript/examples/nextjs-memory-chat/package.json:24. At ec9fc65 the example had only the `file:../..` SDK link.

The example imports the provider at lib/handlers.ts:12 (`import { createNamsProvider } from "@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider"`) and lib/memory.ts:15.

The provider package cannot supply those imports until someone builds it:
- Its exports point only at ./dist/index.js and ./dist/index.d.ts (packages/vercel-ai-provider/package.json).
- dist/ is gitignored (packages/vercel-ai-provider/.gitignore:5).
- It has no `prepare` script, only `prepublishOnly`, so `npm ci` in the example will not build it.

The index's Notes (lines 58-61) name only `file:../..` and 'Build the SDK'. That contradicts the example's own README (lines 134-146), which says to build both packages before installing.

I simulated the linked, unbuilt provider and the import fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The fix is easy for a reader who also reads the example's README, so major (not blocker) is right.

Related, not verified, needs a human check: ci-typescript.yml:127-129 builds the provider only when `matrix.example == 'nams-ai-provider'`, but nextjs-memory-chat is in the matrix (line 95). On a clean runner, its `tsc --noEmit` and build may fail with TS2307. That could be a separate CI blocker; I did not run CI.

findings.v1reason: typescript/examples/README.md:41 `(../../../examples/)` and :82 `(../../../.github/workflows/ci-typescript.yml)`. The diff shows both were changed from `../../`. From typescript/examples/, `../../` is the repo root: `ls -d typescript/examples/../../examples typescript/examples/../../.github/workflows/ci-typescript.yml` both resolve. `../../../` points above the repository, so both links break on GitHub.

findings.title: 'Current source and artifact evidence' links to a DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md that does not exist

Each points readers to DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md at the repository root 'before selecting an SDK artifact'. findings.evidence: examples/README.md:234 `See the [current source and artifact evidence](../DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md) before selecting an SDK artifact.` `ls DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md` prints 'No such file or directory'. `git log --all --oneline -- DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md` returns nothing. `git grep -n DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS HEAD` lists 28 READMEs, including examples/audit-trail/README.md:103, examples/nams-quickstart/README.md:156, examples/lennys-memory/README.md:1321, examples/microsoft_agent_retail_assistant/README.md:369 and :412, and examples/full-stack-chat-agent/frontend/README.md:166.

findings.v1reason: examples/README.md:234 links `../DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md`. `ls DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md` gives 'No such file or directory'. `git log --all -- DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md` is empty, and `find` finds no such file anywhere. `git grep -l DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS HEAD` returns 30 files, so every one of these added 'current source and artifact evidence' links is broken.
findings.v2reason: The finding holds. The branch adds links to DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md in 30 files at HEAD. There are none at the merge-base ec9fc65. In every file the target resolves to that name at the repository root. That file does not exist in the working tree, in the untracked files or anywhere in the git history. So each "current source and artifact evidence" link sends the reader to a page that does not exist, and the reader is told to read it "before selecting an SDK artifact". A broken link that misleads readers is major under the given rubric. It breaks no build or test, so it is not a blocker.
findings.reproduction:
From the repo root:
- `ls DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md` printed "No such file or directory".
- `git log --all --oneline -- DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md` returned nothing.
- `find . -name 'DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION*'` returned nothing, untracked files included.
- `git grep -l DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS HEAD | wc -l` gave 30. The same command against ec9fc65 gave 0, so this branch added every one.
- examples/README.md:234 reads: "See the [current source and artifact evidence](../DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md) before selecting an SDK artifact."
- A script then extracted every markdown link target that contains the name, resolved each one relative to its README's directory (os.path.normpath), and tested it with `-e`. Every target resolved to DOCUMENTATION_REMEDIATION_STATUS.md at the repo root, and every one was marked MISSING.

findings.title: Aura quickstarts hardcode anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-latest, unlike the tutorial's reader-supplied model
findings.detail: The branch turned the bolt quickstart in README.md and README-pypi.md into a runnable recipe: it exports ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, installs [anthropic,openai]==0.6.0 and runs the program. The program still hardcodes `claude-3-5-sonnet-latest`. The maintained Anthropic tutorial on this branch avoids a fixed id and asks for an accessible model. To my knowledge Anthropic has retired the Claude 3.5 Sonnet models, so a reader who runs the README program may get a model-not-found error.
findings.evidence: README.md:195 and README-pypi.md (quickstart) `llm="anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-latest",`, preceded by `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...`. By contrast, docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/anthropic-and-local-embeddings.adoc:86 has `export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="replace-with-your-accessible-Anthropic-model-id"`, and docs/modules/ROOT/examples/anthropic_local_memory.py:14 has `from_provider(f"anthropic/{os.environ['ANTHROPIC_MODEL']}", kind="llm")`.
findings.fix: Read the model id from ANTHROPIC_MODEL, as the tutorial does, or use a current model id in both READMEs.
findings.v1reason: README.md:195 and README-pypi.md:107 do hardcode `anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-latest`, and the tutorial reads ANTHROPIC_MODEL instead. But the line already existed on main (ec9fc65:README.md:149), and the branch only changed the surrounding recipe. Two things I could not settle from the repository: whether this model id is currently rejected by the Anthropic API (retirement is external knowledge), and whether the quickstart's operations (add_message, add_entity, add_preference, get_conversation) invoke the configured LLM at all under the default extraction settings.

The only mention is inside the program comment at provider-mode.adoc:44: ` *   MEMORY_API_KEY=nams_... findings.v1reason: All four mode pages (provider:20-29, middleware:19-28, tools:20-29, hooks:20-29) list Node 22, MEMORY_API_KEY and the npm install as prerequisites. None lists OPENAI_API_KEY. findings.title: Mode how-tos have the reader save a file in their own project, then run a different file in the repo checkout
findings.detail: Each mode page tells the reader to install the pinned npm releases and 'Save as `provider-mode.ts`'. 'Run and verify' then says to run from `typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/` after 'the workspace build', using `src/provider-mode.ts`. The file the reader saved is never run. The checkout example links the SDK and provider with `file:` paths, so it doesn't exercise the pinned 0.3.0/0.5.0 packages the reader just installed. The prerequisites also never mention a repository checkout or the workspace build. The same mismatch appears in middleware-mode.adoc:161, tools-mode.adoc:195 and hooks-mode.adoc:234.
findings.evidence: provider-mode.adoc:28 `npm install @neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider@0.3.0 @neo4j-labs/agent-memory@0.5.0 ...`; :33 `.Save as `provider-mode.ts``; :178-184 'From `typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/`, after the workspace build and `.env` setup described in the example's README: ... npx tsx --env-file-if-exists=.env src/provider-mode.ts'. typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/package.json dependencies: '@neo4j-labs/agent-memory': 'file:../..', '@neo4j-labs/nams-ai-provider': 'file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider'. MAINTAINING.md: 'Application instructions install the verified npm releases ... pinned to an exact version'.
findings.fix: Choose one path. Either run the saved file from the reader's project (`npx tsx --env-file-if-exists=.env provider-mode.ts`, with `tsx` added to the install line), or drop 'Save as' and the npm install and make the checkout plus workspace build an explicit prerequisite.
findings.v1reason: provider-mode.adoc:28 installs the pinned npm releases (no tsx), and :33 says 'Save as `provider-mode.ts`'. But :178-184 says to run `npx tsx --env-file-if-exists=.env src/provider-mode.ts` from typescript/examples/nams-ai-provider/ 'after the workspace build'. That example's package.json uses `file:../..` and `file:../../packages/vercel-ai-provider`, so it doesn't run the file the reader saved or the pinned packages they installed. The prerequisites never mention a checkout or a workspace build. The other mode pages follow the same pattern (middleware:161-166, tools:195-200, hooks:234-239).

findings.title: Mode how-tos don't end with verification: long reference sections follow 'Run and verify'
findings.detail: All four mode pages put 'Run and verify' in the middle and follow it with a '<Mode> mode specifics' section. In hooks-mode that section is about 100 lines: an event table, matcher rules, and timeout/failure semantics. This largely duplicates reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc 'Hook events' (lines 302-362). The 'Procedure' sections also narrate what the code does line by line ('Read the demo userId...', 'Require MEMORY_API_KEY...') rather than giving steps for the reader to perform. Similar trailing sections: provider-mode.adoc:205, middleware-mode.adoc:188, tools-mode.adoc:225-314.
findings.evidence: hooks-mode.adoc:232 `== Run and verify`, then :274 `== Hooks mode specifics`, :285 `=== The eight events` (8-row event table), :343 `=== Matchers`, :356 `=== Rewrites, denial, and failure isolation`, :373 `== See also`. The same content is at reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc:302 `== Hook events` and :353-362 'Rules: a `matcher`...'. Rules: .claude/skills/docs-diataxis/SKILL.md How-To: 'No teaching, just doing', 'Numbered steps for the solution', 'End with verification/testing'; 'Don't put reference in tutorials: Link to reference for complete option lists'; 'Don't mix quadrants: A how-to guide shouldn't teach concepts (link to explanation instead)'.
findings.fix: End each mode page's body with 'Run and verify'. Move the 'specifics' material into reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc, or the retrieval explanation where it's conceptual, and link to it. Rewrite 'Procedure' as reader actions or rename it (for example 'How the program works').
findings.v1reason: Structure confirmed. hooks-mode.adoc:232 'Run and verify' is followed by :274 'Hooks mode specifics' (event table :285, Matchers :343, Rewrites :356), which overlaps reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc:302 'Hook events'. Provider (:205), middleware (:188) and tools (:225) have trailing 'specifics' sections too. The 'Procedure' steps (for example hooks:166 '`redact(text)` replaces...') narrate the code instead of giving reader actions. This goes against the how-to shape in MAINTAINING.md:58 ('ordered solution and final verification') and SKILL.md ('End with verification'). It's a structure/style rule, not a factual error, so nit.

findings.title: write_mode is placed on MemorySettings; it's MemorySettings.memory.write_mode
findings.detail: The explanation says buffered writes need `write_mode="buffered"` in `MemorySettings`. The next bullet correctly writes `MemorySettings.memory.multi_tenant`. The field lives on MemoryConfig, and MemorySettings forbids extra fields, so a reader who passes it at the top level gets a ValidationError.
findings.evidence: operational-primitives.adoc:19: '* Buffered writes require `write_mode="buffered"` in `MemorySettings`'. src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:349 `write_mode: Literal["sync", "buffered"]` is in MemoryConfig (beside multi_tenant at :340). `uv run python -c "from neo4j_agent_memory import MemorySettings; MemorySettings(write_mode='buffered')"` gives `write_mode  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden ...]`.
findings.fix: Write '`MemorySettings.memory.write_mode="buffered"`' (or `MemorySettings(memory={"write_mode": "buffered"})`).
findings.v1reason: operational-primitives.adoc:19 (a new file on this branch) says '`write_mode="buffered"` in `MemorySettings`', while the next bullet correctly writes `MemorySettings.memory.multi_tenant`. write_mode is a field of MemoryConfig (settings.py:349). `MemorySettings(write_mode='buffered')` fails with 'Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden]'.

findings.title: Embedded-SDK deployment lists NEO4J_URI/NEO4J_USERNAME/NEO4J_PASSWORD, which the SDK doesn't read
findings.detail: The 'Python SDK embedded in your own application' option gives its credentials as the plain NEO4J_* variables. MemorySettings reads only the NAM_-prefixed variables (NAM_NEO4J__URI and so on) and deliberately filters plain NEO4J_URI out of .env. A reader who deploys with only NEO4J_URI set silently connects to the bolt://localhost:7687 default with an empty password. The page doesn't say the application must pass these values itself.
findings.evidence: deploy-an-application.adoc:26: 'Credentials:: `NEO4J_URI` / `NEO4J_USERNAME` / `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, plus embedding/LLM provider credentials'. src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:629 `env_prefix="NAM_"`, and :636 comment 'Unrelated keys in a user's .env (e.g. plain NEO4J_URI=...) are filtered out'. `NEO4J_URI=bolt://example:7687 uv run python -c "from neo4j_agent_memory import MemorySettings; print(MemorySettings().neo4j.uri)"` prints `bolt://localhost:7687`. configuration-connections.adoc:23 documents `NAM_NEO4J__URI` as the env var.
findings.fix: List `NAM_NEO4J__URI` / `NAM_NEO4J__USERNAME` / `NAM_NEO4J__PASSWORD`, or state that the application reads NEO4J_* itself and passes them to `MemorySettings(neo4j=...)`.
findings.v1reason: deploy-an-application.adoc (new on this branch) :26 lists 'Credentials:: `NEO4J_URI` / `NEO4J_USERNAME` / `NEO4J_PASSWORD`' for the embedded Python SDK. MemorySettings uses env_prefix='NAM_' (settings.py:629) and filters out plain NEO4J_URI (comment at :636-638). With `NEO4J_URI=bolt://example:7687`, `MemorySettings().neo4j.uri` prints `bolt://localhost:7687`. The page doesn't say the application must read and pass these values itself.

findings.title: Numbered config ids are shifted by one section and forward to the wrong config block
findings.detail: When the configuration reference was split, the auto-numbered ids `_python_configuration_N`, `_environment_variables_N` and `_parameters_N` were assigned as if the old page had a NAMS section after Neo4j. The old page had no NAMS section, so each id was moved one section too early. Old links to the Embedding, Extraction, LLM and Memory settings now open unrelated settings (NAMS connection, Embedding, Memory, Search). The hub bullets at reference/configuration.adoc:10-12 send the ids to the wrong sub-page. configuration.adoc forwards every old id to this hub, so links to the old top-level page break the same way.
findings.evidence:
At ec9fc65, git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/configuration.adoc (the same ids exist in the old configuration.adoc) has: 151 '== Embedding Configuration', 155 '=== Python Configuration' (_python_configuration_2), 172 Environment Variables (_environment_variables_2), 187 Parameters (_parameters_2); 277 '== Extraction Configuration', 281/325 (_python_configuration_3/_environment_variables_3); 509 '== LLM Configuration', 513/534 (_6); 548 '== Memory Configuration', 552/568 (_7).
At HEAD: reference/configuration-connections.adoc:37-41 'anchor:_python_configuration_2[] anchor:_environment_variables_2[] anchor:_parameters_2[]' then '== NAMS connection'; reference/configuration-providers.adoc:11-14 'anchor:_python_configuration_3[] anchor:_environment_variables_3[]' then '== Embedding configuration'; reference/configuration-operations.adoc:10-14 'anchor:_python_configuration_6[] anchor:_environment_variables_6[]' then '== Memory behavior'; reference/configuration-operations.adoc:41-44 'anchor:_python_configuration_7[] anchor:_environment_variables_7[]' then '== Search configuration'. The hub bullet at reference/configuration.adoc:10 lists '_python_configuration_2 ... _environment_variables_2' next to the connections xref.
findings.fix: Move _python_configuration_2, _environment_variables_2 and _parameters_2 to configuration-providers.adoc before '== Embedding configuration'. Move _python_configuration_3 and _environment_variables_3 to before '== Extraction configuration'. Move _python_configuration_6 and _environment_variables_6 to before '== LLM configuration' in configuration-providers.adoc. Move _python_configuration_7 and _environment_variables_7 to before '== Memory behavior'. Update the hub bullets at reference/configuration.adoc:10-12 to match.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced. In the old reference/configuration.adoc (ec9fc65), the auto-numbered ids run Neo4j=_python_configuration/_parameters, Embedding=_2 (with _parameters_2), Extraction=_3, Schema=_4, Resolution=_5, LLM=_6, Memory=_7, Search=_8. At HEAD, configuration-connections.adoc:37-39 puts _python_configuration_2, _environment_variables_2 and _parameters_2 before '== NAMS connection'. configuration-providers.adoc:11-12 puts _3 before '== Embedding configuration' and :81-82 puts _4 before '== Extraction configuration'. configuration-operations.adoc:10-11 puts _6 before '== Memory behavior', :41-42 puts _7 before 'Search configuration', and :62-63 puts _8 before 'Geocoding configuration'. The hub bullets at reference/configuration.adoc:10-12 repeat the error. They send _2 (Embedding) to the connections page and _6 (LLM) to the operations page, which are the wrong pages. Only _5 (Resolution) and the geocoding/enrichment ids from _9 onward land correctly. One detail in the finding is off: the top-level configuration.adoc puts all ids in one anchor line that links to the hub, rather than forwarding each id. The core defect is real.
findings.v2reason:
The defect is real. The mapping of old ids is off by one section, so a few legacy links point to the wrong place. I'm lowering the severity to minor because the impact is small. Every old id still resolves, so no link is broken. An old deep link like reference/configuration.adoc#_python_configuration_2 lands on the hub page's four-bullet list, where all four labelled sub-page links are on screen. Only 5 ids end up at the wrong bullet.

How the old ids were numbered: I rendered the ec9fc65 page with asciidoctor. The Neo4j section got the unnumbered ids _python_configuration, _environment_variables and _parameters. Then Embedding got _2 (including _parameters_2), Extraction _3, Schema _4, Resolution _5, LLM _6, Memory _7, Search _8, Geocoding (_environment_variables_9, _parameters_3), Enrichment (_python_configuration_9, _environment_variables_10, _parameters_4), Deduplication _10, CLI (_environment_variables_13) and Complete example (_python_configuration_11).

What happens at HEAD, in two layers:

(1) The hub, reference/configuration.adoc:10-12. This is the layer that old links actually reach, because the hub keeps the old URL. I rendered it and found:
- _python_configuration_2, _environment_variables_2 and _parameters_2 (old Embedding) sit in the bullet that links to configuration-connections. Embedding is documented in configuration-providers.
- _python_configuration_6 and _environment_variables_6 (old LLM) sit in the bullet that links to configuration-operations. LLM is also documented in configuration-providers (configuration-providers.adoc:40).
- The ids for Extraction, Schema, Resolution, Memory, Search, Geocoding, Enrichment, Deduplication, Observability, CLI and Complete example are all in the correct bullet.

(2) The sub-pages have the same off-by-one placement:
- configuration-connections.adoc:37-39 puts _2 before '== NAMS connection'.
- configuration-providers.adoc:11-12 puts _3 before Embedding, and :81-82 puts _4 before Extraction.
- configuration-operations.adoc:10-11 puts _6 before 'Memory behavior', :41-42 puts _7 before Search, and :62-63 puts _8 before Geocoding.

The sub-pages are new URLs, so no old link carries a fragment to them. These wrong placements only matter to someone who adds one of these ids to a new URL by hand. So this layer has little effect, but it is still wrong.

One claim in the finding is overstated. The top-level configuration.adoc:10 does not route each old id to a section: it holds every legacy id on a single forwarding paragraph that links to the hub page with no fragment. So old top-level links do not "break the same way". They land on generic forwarding text.

The ids 9 through 13 and the Neo4j ids are correct. No test in tests/docs checks where these configuration anchors land.

Suggested fix, as the finding proposes: move the _2 ids to before '== Embedding configuration', _3 to before Extraction, _4 to before '== Graph schema configuration', _6 to before '== LLM configuration', _7 to before '== Memory behavior' and _8 to before Search. On the hub, move the _2 and _6 anchors into the providers bullet.
findings.reproduction:
1) git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/configuration.adoc > oldconf.adoc; asciidoctor -S safe oldconf.adoc; then listed the h2/h3 ids. The order in the output was: _python_configuration, _environment_variables, _parameters, _embedding_configuration, _python_configuration_2, _environment_variables_2, _parameters_2, _extraction_configuration, _python_configuration_3, ..., _schema_configuration, _python_configuration_4, ..., _resolution_configuration, _python_configuration_5, ..., _llm_configuration, _python_configuration_6, _environment_variables_6, _memory_configuration, _python_configuration_7, ..., _search_configuration, _python_configuration_8, ..., _geocoding_configuration, ..., _environment_variables_9, _parameters_3, _enrichment_configuration, _python_configuration_9, _environment_variables_10, _parameters_4, _deduplication_configuration, _python_configuration_10, ...
2) grep -n 'anchor:' docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/configuration-*.adoc and grep -nE '^==+ ' on the same files. Output: connections.adoc:37-39 has _python_configuration_2/_environment_variables_2/_parameters_2, then :41 '== NAMS connection'. providers.adoc:11-12 has _3, then :14 '== Embedding configuration'. providers.adoc:81-82 has _4, then :85 '== Extraction configuration'. operations.adoc:10-11 has _6, then :14 '== Memory behavior'. operations.adoc:41-42 has _7, then :44 '== Search configuration'. operations.adoc:62-63 has _8, then :72 '== Geocoding configuration'.
3) Rendered the HEAD hub (reference/configuration.adoc) with asciidoctor and mapped each <li>'s anchor ids to its href:
- configuration-connections.html has [_python_configuration, _environment_variables, _parameters, _python_configuration_2, _environment_variables_2, _parameters_2]
- configuration-providers.html has [_3, _4, _5]
- configuration-operations.html has [_python_configuration_6, _environment_variables_6, _7, _8, geocoding/enrichment ids]
So the old Embedding id (_2) sends readers to connections, and the old LLM id (_6) sends them to operations. Both sections are in providers.
4) grep of tests/ and scripts/ for these ids found no test covering configuration anchor placement. docs/build/site had no built copy of the reference/configuration page to grep.

createNamsProvider’s stream wrapper awaits the assistant-turn write as part of closing the response stream, so a fully drained client stream implies the write was attempted — not skipped, unlike a plain fire-and-forget write. It is still best-e..."

The rendered schema ends in "default `[]" inside the code, followed by ") }`." as plain text with a literal backtick. The tools-mode how-to writes the same schema without the inner backticks and renders correctly.
findings.evidence: Source reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc:164-167 "`{ content: ... tags?: string[] (max 10 entries, each ≤40 chars, default `[]`) }`." (added in e2bcb93). Built reference/nams-ai-provider.html: "{ content: string (1–2000 chars); ... tags?: string[] (max 10 entries, each ≤40 chars, default `[]) }`."
findings.fix: Drop the inner backticks ("default []") or wrap the whole schema in a passthrough: `+{ content: ... default [] }+`.
findings.v1reason: Lines 164-167 are from e2bcb93. The built nams-ai-provider.html has "default `[]) }`.", so the span closes early at the inner backtick. A fresh render of "`{ content: string; tags?: string[] (default `[]`) }`." gives "{ ... (default `[]) }`.".

findings.title: `=>`/`->` inside inline code render as ⇒/→, corrupting TS signatures and Cypher patterns
findings.detail: Asciidoctor's replacements step also runs inside backtick code, turning => into ⇒ and -> into →. Readers see, and copy, invalid TypeScript arrow types and invalid Cypher relationship patterns. New occurrences on this branch: reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc:43, 122 and 137 (TS `=>`); reference/typescript-api.adoc:312; how-to/privacy-and-audit.adoc:96 (Python `-> str`); how-to/preferences.adoc:14; how-to/audit-reasoning.adoc:18; reference/api/short-term-messages.adoc:50 and 87; reference/api/reasoning-traces.adoc:40; reference/api/reasoning-steps.adoc:78; reference/api/long-term-preferences.adoc:42-43; explanation/nams-ai-provider-retrieval.adoc:36; how-to/typescript/nams-ai-provider-tools-mode.adoc:233; how-to/typescript/nams-ai-provider-middleware-mode.adoc:198. Some of the reference/api lines were moved here from the old split pages. The docs already use the `+...+` passthrough elsewhere, for example the NAM_* variables.
findings.evidence: Source reference/nams-ai-provider.adoc:43 "| `(modelId: string) => LanguageModel`"; how-to/preferences.adoc:14 "`(User)-[:HAS_PREFERENCE]->(Preference)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Entity)`". Built HTML: reference/nams-ai-provider.html "(modelId: string) ⇒ LanguageModel"; how-to/preferences.html "(User)-[:HAS_PREFERENCE]→(Preference)-[:APPLIES_TO]→(Entity)"; how-to/privacy-and-audit.html "encrypt(plaintext: str) → str"; reference/api/long-term-preferences.html "(:User)-[:HAS_PREFERENCE]→(:Preference)".
findings.fix: Wrap each span in a passthrough, e.g. `+(modelId: string) => LanguageModel+` and `+(:User)-[:HAS_PREFERENCE]->(:Preference)+`, or escape the arrow as `-\>`/`=\>`.
findings.v1reason: A fresh render turns "`(modelId: string) => LanguageModel`" into "(modelId: string) ⇒ LanguageModel" and "`(User)-[:HAS_PREFERENCE]->(Preference)`" into "→" inside . The built pages show the same, for example "encrypt(plaintext: str) →" in privacy-and-audit.html. Blame shows every listed line is a branch commit (e2bcb93, 8fc3ead or c90d191). The same pattern already existed on main (for example ec9fc65 how-to/multi-tenancy.adoc:162), so the defect class is not new, but this branch adds many new instances.

findings.detail: The row warns that a spread copy of the tool set throws. The replacements step turns the three dots into a single U+2026 ellipsis plus a zero-width space, so the example the reader is warned about shows as non-JavaScript.

findings.title: `<<graph>>` points at a bare anchor with no title and renders as the link text "[graph]"
findings.detail: The cross-reference points at `anchor:graph[]` (line 118), which has no reftext. Asciidoctor therefore falls back to the bracketed id as the link text.
findings.evidence: Source reference/api/memory-client.adoc:81 "| `graph` | `Neo4jClient`, bolt only | Deprecated direct graph access; see <>." and :118 "anchor:graph[]" (both new in 8fc3ead; the merge-base page has neither). Built reference/api/memory-client.html: "see [graph]".

findings.v1reason: Lines 81 and 118 are both from 8fc3ead (branch). The built memory-client.html has "see [graph].". A fresh render of "see <>.\n\nanchor:graph[]" also produces the link text "[graph]".

findings.title: `Thought: ` / `Action: ` / `Observation: ` show literal backticks (trailing space inside code)
findings.detail: A constrained code span can't end with a space before the closing backtick, so none of these three prefixes is recognised. The table cell shows raw backticks, and the exact prefix strings the reader needs in order to rebuild step embeddings are not visibly delimited.
findings.evidence: Source how-to/migrate-embedding-model.adoc:142 "prefixed with `Thought: `, `Action: `, and `Observation: `, joined with a space" (added in 8fc3ead). Built how-to/migrate-embedding-model.html: "prefixed with `Thought: `, `Action: `, and `Observation: `, joined" (no <code> elements).
findings.fix: Use `+Thought: +`, `+Action: +` and `+Observation: +` (passthrough inside backticks), or describe it as `Thought:` followed by a space.
findings.v1reason: Line 142 is from 8fc3ead. The built migrate-embedding-model.html has "prefixed with `Thought: `, `Action: `, and `Observation: `, joined" with no <code> elements, and a fresh render is identical.

findings.title: Bolt-only label says every API raises NotSupportedError on NAMS; many labelled calls do not
findings.detail: The partial tells readers that the page's APIs raise `NotSupportedError` on NAMS. This branch adds the label to 14 more pages (reasoning-traces, entity-extraction, entity-extraction-batch, entity-extraction-schemas, configure-llm-provider, configure-embedding-provider, bring-your-own-model, migrate-to-providers, running-without-an-llm, migrate-embedding-model, batch-processing, preferences, privacy-and-audit, create-context-graph-mcp). For many of the calls on those pages the claim is false. Standalone extractors (`extraction_recipes.py`) never touch a backend. On NAMS, `MemorySettings.embedding`/`extraction` are accepted with a UserWarning and then ignored. Methods missing from the NAMS classes raise `AttributeError`, for example `add_messages_batch`, `link_entity_to_message`, `find_potential_duplicates`, `get_preferences_by_category` and `reasoning.on_tool_call_recorded`. The documented positional calls `get_preferences_for(user)` and `supersede_preference(old, new)` raise `TypeError`. `record_tool_call(touched_entities=...)` succeeds and drops the argument. A reader who catches `NotSupportedError` to detect a missing feature will get `AttributeError`, `TypeError` or silent success instead.
findings.evidence:
Offending: docs/modules/ROOT/partials/backend-bolt-only.adoc:3 "The APIs on this page are *bolt-only* — calling them against the hosted NAMS backend raises `NotSupportedError`."
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/__init__.py:678-712 `_warn_inactive_layers_on_nams` only warns ("NAMS backend ignores client-side memory layers"); src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/reasoning.py:206-234 record_tool_call builds the body without touched_entities. Probe on a NAMS MemoryClient with a fake transport (scratchpad review/nams_probe.py):
"ERR c.short_term.add_messages_batch('s', []): AttributeError: 'NamsShortTermMemory' object has no attribute 'add_messages_batch'"
"ERR c.reasoning.on_tool_call_recorded: AttributeError: 'NamsReasoningMemory' object has no attribute 'on_tool_call_recorded'"
"ERR c.long_term.get_preferences_for('sara-demo'): TypeError: NamsLongTermMemory.get_preferences_for() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given"
"ERR c.long_term.supersede_preference('a','b'): TypeError: ... takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given"
"OK c.reasoning.record_tool_call(..., touched_entities=[]): ToolCall"
Settings probe (review/nams_settings.py): "connected OK; warnings: ['NAMS backend ignores client-side memory layers: embedding (server-managed), extraction (server-managed)...']"
findings.fix: Reword the partial to say the procedure needs Bolt and is not available on NAMS, without promising one exception type. For example: "On NAMS these operations are unavailable: depending on the call they raise NotSupportedError or AttributeError, or are ignored." Alternatively, add a separate 'client-side only' partial for the extraction and provider-configuration pages, which never call a backend.
findings.v1reason: The partial is unchanged: backend-bolt-only.adoc:3 still says calling these APIs on NAMS "raises `NotSupportedError`". This branch adds it to 14 pages that had no label or had backend-both at ec9fc65; the list matches the finding, taken from comm of grep -l at HEAD vs ec9fc65. I re-ran the probe (real NAMS store classes, fake transport) and reproduced every result. add_messages_batch, on_tool_call_recorded, get_preferences_by_category, link_entity_to_message and find_potential_duplicates raise AttributeError. Positional get_preferences_for('sara-demo') and supersede_preference('a','b') raise TypeError. start_trace and get_session_traces succeed. c.users returns a _NamsUnsupported sentinel without raising. The provider and extraction pages (e.g. configure-embedding-provider.adoc:9) carry the label although NAMS only warns and ignores client-side embedding/extraction settings. So the label makes a wrong behaviour claim across many pages. What a reader should conclude ("use Bolt") is broadly right, but the exception promise is wrong.
findings.v2reason:
The partial is unchanged on this branch, but the branch adds it to 14 pages that did not carry it at ec9fc65. I confirmed that list by checking each page that includes backend-bolt-only against `git show ec9fc65:<page>`. The partial, docs/modules/ROOT/partials/backend-bolt-only.adoc:3, says "Available on NAMS: No. ... calling them against the hosted NAMS backend raises `NotSupportedError`." Running the code shows that claim is false for many calls on those pages.

- **AttributeError.** On NAMS, `MemoryClient` returns the plain `Nams*` store classes (for example `NamsShortTermMemory`), with no proxy that raises `NotSupportedError`. So methods those classes lack raise `AttributeError`. Examples: `add_messages_batch`, `find_potential_duplicates`, `reasoning.on_tool_call_recorded`.
- **TypeError.** The NAMS signatures are keyword-only: `get_preferences_for(self, **kwargs)` and `supersede_preference(self, preference_id, **kwargs)`. The documented positional call raises `TypeError`.
- **Calls that work on NAMS.** Some APIs on the newly labelled pages exist on NAMS, so the label calls usable features unavailable. preferences.adoc documents `add_preference` and `search_preferences`, which `NamsLongTermMemory` has. reasoning-traces.adoc covers `start_trace`, `add_step`, `complete_trace` and `get_session_traces`, which `NamsReasoningMemory` has.
- **Pages that never call the backend.** configure-embedding-provider.adoc:19 itself says embedding runs server-side on NAMS. The extraction pages configure client-side extractors that never call a backend.

`NotSupportedError` is raised only from a few places: the `_NamsUnsupported` sentinels (`c.users`, `c.consolidation`), a few `MemoryClient` methods (src/neo4j_agent_memory/__init__.py:1037, 1119, 1178, 1457) and a few NAMS reasoning methods (src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/reasoning.py:246-343).

This is a wrong behaviour claim spread across 14 pages, and it newly marks usable NAMS features as unavailable, so major is the right severity. One correction to the original evidence: with a non-UUID step_id, `record_tool_call(..., touched_entities=[])` failed with a pydantic `ValidationError`. I did not re-check the claim that it "silently succeeds"; the other claims reproduce.
findings.reproduction:
1) Which pages newly include the partial: for each page under docs/modules/ROOT/pages that includes backend-bolt-only, test `git show ec9fc65:<page> | grep -q backend-bolt-only`. It prints 14 NEW pages: configure-llm-provider, privacy-and-audit, create-context-graph-mcp, migrate-to-providers, reasoning-traces, migrate-embedding-model, entity-extraction-batch, entity-extraction, running-without-an-llm, batch-processing, configure-embedding-provider, bring-your-own-model, preferences, entity-extraction-schemas.
2) Class introspection with `uv run python` (inspect on the NAMS classes):
- NamsShortTermMemory: add_messages_batch MISSING
- NamsLongTermMemory: find_potential_duplicates MISSING, link_entity_to_message MISSING, get_preferences_by_category MISSING
- `get_preferences_for (self, **kwargs)`; `supersede_preference (self, preference_id, **kwargs)`
- NamsReasoningMemory: on_tool_call_recorded MISSING
- No class defines __getattr__.
- NAMS classes do have add_preference, search_preferences, start_trace, add_step, complete_trace and get_session_traces.
3) Probe on a NAMS MemoryClient with a fake transport (scratchpad review/nams_probe.py):

- `c.reasoning.on_tool_call_recorded` raises AttributeError
- `c.users` and `c.consolidation` return `_NamsUnsupported` sentinels (these do raise NotSupportedError when used)
4) `grep -rn NotSupportedError src/neo4j_agent_memory`: raised only in core/_unsupported.py:48, __init__.py:1037/1119/1178/1457, nams/reasoning.py:246/254/332/343, and the bolt-side stubs in memory/long_term.py:1922/1935 and memory/short_term.py:589/602.
