findings.title: Reasoning-traces page newly labelled Bolt-only/NotSupportedError though NAMS implements its calls
findings.detail: The branch adds `backend-bolt-only` to this page. Every call in its recipe exists on `NamsReasoningMemory` and does not raise: `start_trace`, `add_step`, `record_tool_call`, `complete_trace`, `get_trace_with_steps` and `get_session_traces`. Only `list_traces`, `get_similar_traces`, `search_steps` and `get_tool_stats` raise `NotSupportedError`. The label also contradicts two other pages on this branch: backend-capabilities says Python with NAMS reasoning adapts supported service records, and the MemoryClient reference says NAMS assembles steps into compatibility traces. A Python NAMS user is told reasoning is unavailable. (On NAMS, `complete_trace` stores `success` only from a `success=` kwarg, so the recipe's `saved.success is False` assertion would not hold as written. That is a real difference to document, not a NotSupportedError.)
findings.evidence:
Offending: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/reasoning-traces.adoc:7 "include::partial$backend-bolt-only.adoc[]" (the page had no label at ec9fc65; the partial says calls raise NotSupportedError).
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/reasoning.py:165-243 (start_trace/add_step/record_tool_call/complete_trace implemented), :281-305 get_trace_with_steps, :307-329 get_session_traces; NotSupportedError only at :245,:253,:331,:342.
Contradicting pages: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:52 "Python with NAMS:: Python accessors adapt supported service records"; docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/memory-client.adoc:76 "NAMS assembles conversation-level steps into compatibility traces."
Probe: "OK c.reasoning.start_trace('conv-1', 'task'): ReasoningTrace", "OK c.reasoning.get_session_traces('conv-1'): list", "ERR c.reasoning.list_traces(): NotSupportedError".
findings.fix: Use `backend-both`, or a page-specific NOTE saying the recipe targets Bolt. On NAMS the trace lifecycle is synthesized client-side from conversation-scoped steps; `list_traces`, similarity search and tool stats raise `NotSupportedError`; and `complete_trace(outcome=TraceOutcome(...))` does not set `success`.
findings.v1reason: backend-bolt-only is new at reasoning-traces.adoc:7; the page had no label at ec9fc65. The probe shows start_trace, add_step, record_tool_call, complete_trace, get_trace_with_steps and get_session_traces do not raise on NAMS (nams/reasoning.py:164-329). Only list_traces, get_similar_traces, search_steps and get_tool_stats raise NotSupportedError. That contradicts memory-client.adoc:76 ("NAMS assembles conversation-level steps into compatibility traces") and backend-capabilities.adoc:52. Severity is minor, not major: the page's recipe really does not pass on NAMS. complete_trace stores kwargs.get('success') (nams/reasoning.py:241), so `saved.success is False` fails. The page also recommends list_traces, similarity, touched_entities and hooks, which are not on NAMS. So "not available" is defensible for this procedure. What is wrong is the NotSupportedError claim, which largely overlaps [0].

findings.title: Messages page newly labelled 'Available on NAMS: Yes' but its procedure and table fail on NAMS
findings.detail: This branch adds `backend-both` to the page. The page's only procedure is a Bolt recipe, and on NAMS it fails at the first call: `add_messages_batch` does not exist on `NamsShortTermMemory` (`AttributeError`). Its next call, `get_conversation_summary`, raises `NotSupportedError`, and `search_messages` without a `session_id` raises `ValueError` on NAMS. The operation table also recommends `list_sessions`, `get_conversation_summary` and `get_preferences_for` with no backend note, and all three raise on NAMS. The shared intro partial names only preferences, facts, relationship writes and dedup config as non-portable, so a reader has no signal that these message operations are unavailable. The backend-capabilities row for Python/NAMS conversations lists none of these gaps either.
findings.evidence:
Offending: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/messages.adoc:7 "include::partial$backend-both.adoc[]" (new on this branch) → partial says "Available on NAMS: Yes"; messages.adoc:73-78 table rows for `add_messages_batch`, `list_sessions`, `get_conversation_summary`, `get_preferences_for`; docs/modules/ROOT/partials/python-core-recipe-intro.adoc:3 lists only "preferences, facts, direct relationship writes, and this deduplication configuration" as non-portable; docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:15 "Python with NAMS:: Create a conversation and use its returned ID".
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:367-376 list_sessions and :441-457 get_conversation_summary raise NotSupportedError; no add_messages_batch in NamsShortTermMemory (dir listing: add_message, bulk_add_messages, clear_session, ...).
Probe: "ERR c.short_term.add_messages_batch('s', []): AttributeError", "ERR c.short_term.get_conversation_summary('s'): NotSupportedError", "ERR c.short_term.list_sessions(): NotSupportedError", "ERR c.short_term.search_messages('x', threshold=0.0, limit=5): ValueError: search_messages requires session_id ... on NAMS".
findings.fix: Either label the page Bolt-only with a pointer to the NAMS conversation flow, or keep `backend-both` and add a NAMS column/NOTE. That note should cover: create_conversation → server ID, `bulk_add_messages` instead of `add_messages_batch`, required conversation ID for `search_messages`, and no summary/list_sessions/preferences on NAMS. Extend the backend-capabilities conversations row to match.
findings.v1reason: backend-both is new at messages.adoc:7; the ec9fc65 version has no backend partial. The probe reproduces the failures: add_messages_batch raises AttributeError; get_conversation_summary and list_sessions raise NotSupportedError; search_messages without session_id raises ValueError. The operation table (messages.adoc:73-77) recommends these calls plus get_preferences_for with no NAMS note. The Python/NAMS conversations row in backend-capabilities.adoc:15 lists none of these gaps. Downgraded to minor: messages really are available on NAMS, step 1 says "Prepare the Bolt client", and python-core-recipe-intro.adoc:3 says to consult backend capabilities before adapting to NAMS.

On NAMS, long-term `get_context` returns an empty string.
findings.evidence:
Offending: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/memory-client.adoc:164 "| `include_long_term` | Whether to include facts and preferences" (old: "Include entities and preferences").
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/long_term.py:1327-1345 (include_entities / include_preferences only). Contradiction: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/long-term-geospatial.adoc:114 "facts are not included by this formatter"; nams/long_term.py:612-620 returns "".

findings.title: 'Unsupported accessors or calls raise NotSupportedError' is inaccurate for sentinels and missing methods
findings.detail: Accessing `client.users`, `client.buffered`, `client.consolidation` or `client.schema` on NAMS does not raise. It returns a truthy `_NamsUnsupported` sentinel, and only attribute or method use on it raises. Only `client.graph` raises on property access. Calls to methods missing from the NAMS stores raise `AttributeError`, not `NotSupportedError`. Separately, `client.flush()`/`wait_for_pending()` raise `NotSupportedError` on NAMS, while `write_errors` returns `[]`. The page says those methods are "Bolt only" but not that NAMS raises.
findings.evidence:
Offending: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/api/memory-client.adoc:92 "Unsupported accessors or calls raise `NotSupportedError`".
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/core/_unsupported.py:24-29 "Property access on the shim itself ... does NOT raise — only attempts to call methods on it do" and :60-63 `__bool__` returns True; src/neo4j_agent_memory/__init__.py:760-763 flush awaits self._buffered.flush(). Probe: "ERR c.flush(): NotSupportedError: buffered.flush is not supported on the 'nams' backend", "ERR c.reasoning.on_tool_call_recorded: AttributeError".
findings.fix: Reword: "Bolt-only accessors return a sentinel whose method calls raise NotSupportedError, and `client.graph` raises on access. Store methods absent from the NAMS classes raise AttributeError. On NAMS, `flush()`/`wait_for_pending()` raise NotSupportedError."
findings.v1reason: The sentence at memory-client.adoc:92 is new; ec9fc65 only had the per-row ontology/auth notes. findings.title: Preferences row says NAMS methods raise NotSupportedError; documented call forms raise TypeError
findings.detail: The NAMS stubs `get_preferences_for(self, **kwargs)` and `supersede_preference(self, preference_id, **kwargs)` do not accept the positional forms the docs use: `get_preferences_for(user)` in multi-tenancy.adoc/preferences recipe, and `supersede_preference(old.id, new.id)`. Those calls raise `TypeError` before reaching the NotSupportedError body. `get_preferences_by_category` is missing on NAMS and raises `AttributeError`. Code that catches `NotSupportedError` to fall back will crash instead.
findings.evidence:
Offending: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:45 "Python with NAMS:: Unsupported; methods raise `NotSupportedError`".
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/long_term.py:549 `async def get_preferences_for(self, **kwargs: Any)`, :556 `async def supersede_preference(self, preference_id: UUID | str, **kwargs: Any)`. Probe: "TypeError: NamsLongTermMemory.get_preferences_for() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given"; "TypeError: NamsLongTermMemory.supersede_preference() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given"; "AttributeError: 'NamsLongTermMemory' object has no attribute 'get_preferences_by_category'".
findings.fix: Either make the NAMS stub signatures mirror Bolt (`get_preferences_for(self, user_identifier, **kwargs)`, `supersede_preference(self, old, new)`) so they reach `NotSupportedError`, or qualify the row, for example: "unsupported; keyword calls raise NotSupportedError, other call forms may raise TypeError/AttributeError".
findings.v1reason: backend-capabilities.adoc is a new page on this branch. Line 45 says the NAMS preference methods raise NotSupportedError. nams/long_term.py:549 `get_preferences_for(self, **kwargs)` and :556 `supersede_preference(self, preference_id, **kwargs)` reject the positional forms the docs use (multi-tenancy.adoc:55,93, evaluation.adoc:120, privacy-and-audit.adoc:27), and the probe reproduces TypeError for both. get_preferences_by_category is absent on NAMS (hasattr check), so calling it raises AttributeError.

findings.title: NOTE blames 'the hosted Python bridge' for dropping touched_entities; REST client drops it too
findings.detail: The old text said "NAMS drops `touched_entities` today", which was accurate. The branch changes this to "The hosted Python bridge does not forward `touched_entities`". Elsewhere these docs use "bridge" for the TCK bridge transport, which is separate from the hosted REST API. `NamsReasoningMemory.record_tool_call` builds the same body for both transports and never includes `touched_entities`. The call succeeds silently rather than raising, which also contradicts the bolt-only partial directly above.
findings.evidence:
Offending: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/audit-reasoning.adoc:7 "The hosted Python bridge does not forward `touched_entities`."
Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/reasoning.py:213-224 body has toolName/input/stepId/status/output/durationMs only; docs/modules/ROOT/pages/explanation/backends.adoc:50 "A TCK bridge exists for development and conformance testing; it is not an alternative hosted feature surface." Probe: "OK c.reasoning.record_tool_call(..., touched_entities=[]): ToolCall".
findings.fix: Write: "The Python NAMS client accepts `touched_entities` but silently drops it (no error is raised), so no `:TOUCHED` edges are written on NAMS."
findings.v1reason: audit-reasoning.adoc:7 now says "The hosted Python bridge does not forward `touched_entities`"; ec9fc65 said NAMS drops it. What actually drops it is the Python NAMS client: nams/reasoning.py:213-224 builds the body without touched_entities, and the probe shows the call succeeds silently. Elsewhere the docs use "bridge" for the TCK bridge (backends.adoc:50: "A TCK bridge exists for development and conformance testing; it is not an alternative hosted feature surface"). findings.title: get_active() behavior fixed in source with no CHANGELOG entry; references still call it a limitation
findings.detail: The branch rewrites `NamsOntology.get_active()`. It now reads the response's `version` record instead of inferring the latest revision, raises `ValueError` on malformed or conflicting metadata, and adds `ActiveOntology.schema_hash`. `pyproject.toml` and `__version__` still say 0.6.0, and `CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]` is empty. The reference pages say they describe "the SDK implementations in this source tree", yet they still present the old behavior as current Python behavior. ontology-api contrasts Python with "Current TypeScript source reads the authoritative response `version`". The use-ontologies note is correct for the PyPI 0.6.0 artifact, but the checked-out source and the reference framing now disagree, and the new ValueError paths and field are undocumented.
findings.evidence:
Source change: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py:391-422 (new `_parse_active_version`, `raise ValueError("Active ontology version schema conflicts with the active document.")`, `schema_hash=version.schema_hash`); `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD --stat -- CHANGELOG.md` → no change; CHANGELOG.md:8 "## [Unreleased]" empty.
Docs: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:5 "This reference describes the SDK implementations in this source tree."; docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/ontology-api.adoc:22 "Python 0.6.0 has a binding-metadata limitation ... Current TypeScript source reads the authoritative response `version`."; docs/modules/ROOT/pages/how-to/use-ontologies.adoc:26.
findings.fix: Add an [Unreleased] CHANGELOG entry: get_active uses the authoritative version, raises ValueError on malformed/conflicting metadata, and adds schema_hash. Reword ontology-api.adoc:22/75-87 to say the limitation applies to the published 0.6.0 artifact and the fix is unreleased.
findings.v1reason: `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py` shows get_active() rewritten. It now reads payload['version'] via the new _parse_active_version, raises ValueError on malformed or conflicting metadata, and adds ActiveOntology.schema_hash. CHANGELOG.md is untouched and [Unreleased] is empty, while __version__ and pyproject still say 0.6.0. ontology-api.adoc:22 and :75-87 describe the old behaviour as the Python limitation and contrast it with "Current TypeScript source". backend-capabilities.adoc:5 says the references describe "the SDK implementations in this source tree". The docs are correct for the published 0.6.0 artifact, which is the stated target. The concrete defects are the missing CHANGELOG entry and the undocumented new ValueError paths and field.

findings.title: messages recipe's order assertion fails in 8 of 9 live runs: batch messages share one timestamp
findings.detail: The recipe asserts that `get_conversation(session).messages` comes back in the same order as `add_messages_batch` returned it. CREATE_MESSAGES_BATCH stamps every row with `datetime()`, which Cypher evaluates once per statement. Both messages therefore get the same timestamp, and GET_CONVERSATION_MESSAGES orders only by `m.timestamp`, so the database is free to return the tie in either order. A reader who runs `python core_memory_recipes.py messages` as how-to/messages.adoc step 3 says gets an AssertionError most of the time instead of the documented `Verified: ordered message IDs and summary count`. The mocked suite (tests/docs/test_core_python_tutorials.py) never calls `messages()`, so nothing catches this.
findings.evidence: Offending: core_memory_recipes.py:32 `assert [m.id for m in conversation.messages] == [m.id for m in stored]`; messages.adoc:51 `Expected: ... Verified: ordered message IDs and summary count; session=...`. Source of truth: src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:109 `timestamp: CASE WHEN msg.timestamp IS NOT NULL THEN datetime(msg.timestamp) ELSE datetime() END` inside one UNWIND statement; queries.py:170-172 `MATCH (c:Conversation {id: $conversation_id})-[:HAS_MESSAGE]->(m:Message) RETURN m ORDER BY m.timestamp ASC`. Live runs against a neo4j:5.26-community testcontainer (harness redirects aura_config to bolt and uses a local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedder): `for i in 1..8: python harness.py core_memory_recipes.py messages` gave exit 1,1,1,1,1,1,0,1 (plus 1 failure on the first run), each failing with `File ".../core_memory_recipes.py", line 32, in messages  assert [m.id for m in conversation.messages] == [m.id for m in stored]  AssertionError`. A probe on the stored rows returned `{'s': 'docs-messages-0f05ecd9', 'n': 2, 'distinct_ts': 1}` for all 9 sessions.
findings.fix: Don't assert readback order after a batch without explicit timestamps. Either pass explicit, increasing ISO `timestamp` values in each batch dict (supported: queries.py:109), or compare the IDs as sets and check order through the NEXT_MESSAGE chain. Update the messages.adoc:51 wording to match, and add a live test for this recipe.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced this myself. CREATE_MESSAGES_BATCH (queries.py:109) stamps every row with datetime() when no timestamp is given, and GET_CONVERSATION_MESSAGES (queries.py:170-173) orders only by m.timestamp. I ran core_memory_recipes.messages 10 times against a fresh neo4j:5.26-community container with a local MiniLM embedder: 1 passed and 9 failed with an AssertionError at line 32. A probe of the stored rows showed n=2 messages but only 1 distinct timestamp in every session. The branch added this recipe and the messages.adoc step that runs it.
findings.v2reason:
I confirmed the finding by running the recipe and by tracing the code. The branch adds docs/modules/ROOT/examples/core_memory_recipes.py; `git show ec9fc65:<path>` says the file does not exist on main. Its `messages()` recipe calls `add_messages_batch` without any timestamps.

The storage code writes every message with the same time. In src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:442-450, `timestamp = msg_dict.get("timestamp")` is None, and one `execute_write(queries.CREATE_MESSAGES_BATCH, ...)` inserts the whole batch (short_term.py:474-480). In graph/queries.py:109, that UNWIND statement sets each row to `ELSE datetime() END`. Cypher evaluates `datetime()` once per statement, so every message in the batch gets the same timestamp.

The readback cannot break that tie. `get_conversation` runs GET_CONVERSATION_MESSAGES (short_term.py:858-861), and that query sorts only on `ORDER BY m.timestamp ASC` (queries.py:170-172). It has no tiebreaker and does not follow NEXT_MESSAGE. As a result, the assertion at core_memory_recipes.py:32, `assert [m.id for m in conversation.messages] == [m.id for m in stored]`, depends on whatever order the database returns.

When I ran the unmodified recipe function 10 times against a real neo4j:5.26-community container, it passed once and failed 9 times with an AssertionError at that line. Every session had 2 messages and only 1 distinct timestamp.

A reader who follows how-to/messages.adoc step 3 (`python core_memory_recipes.py messages`, expecting `Verified: ordered message IDs and summary count`) will usually get an AssertionError. That fits blocker: someone following the docs fails.

The suggested fix is sound: pass explicit, increasing ISO `timestamp` values in the batch dicts (supported at queries.py:109), or compare the IDs without relying on order. Either way, the messages.adoc:51 wording needs to change to match.

findings.title: Anthropic tutorial always stops at 'No entity candidates': extracted entities are stored without embeddings
findings.detail: The program stores a message with `extract_entities=True`, then calls `client.long_term.search_entities("Maya Chen", limit=5)` and raises if nothing comes back. search_entities is a pure vector search. The auto-extraction path in short_term writes every extracted entity with `embedding: None`, so the search can never match them. The tutorial therefore fails at step 5 however well the Anthropic model extracts. Step 6's check also fails: it expects `the returned entity vectors have 384 dimensions`, but the query returns no rows.
findings.evidence: Offending: anthropic_local_memory.py:37-41 `entities = await client.long_term.search_entities("Maya Chen", limit=5)` / `if not entities: raise RuntimeError("No entity candidates returned; ...")`; tutorials/anthropic-and-local-embeddings.adoc:127 `One or more Entity candidate: lines, then Verified: context assembly returned text` and :146 `Expected: the returned entity vectors have 384 dimensions`. Source of truth: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:1376 `"embedding": None,` in _extract_and_link_entities; long_term.py:1150-1153 search_entities embeds the query and runs SEARCH_ENTITIES_BY_EMBEDDING. Live run, 5 times, against a neo4j:5.26 testcontainer: the real BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 embedder, with AnthropicProvider.complete_structured patched to return Maya Chen/Northstar Robotics/Denver. Output: `Verified message readback; session=anthropic-tutorial-3591e6c3` then `RuntimeError: No entity candidates returned; inspect extraction before continuing` (FAKE structured calls: 1). The DB then held `{'n': 'Maya Chen', 't': 'PERSON', 'noemb': True, 'dim': 0}` for all three entities, and `MATCH (entity:Entity) WHERE entity.embedding IS NOT NULL RETURN count(*)` returned `0`.
findings.fix: Verify extraction with an exact lookup instead of vector search. For example, query `MATCH (m:Message {id:$id})-[:MENTIONS]->(e:Entity) RETURN e.name, e.type` through client.query.cypher, or call get_entity_by_name. Rewrite the step-6 Cypher and its expectation to check message and index dimensions rather than entity embeddings. Alternatively, fix the SDK so it embeds extracted entities, and pin the docs to the release that includes that fix.
findings.v1reason: short_term._extract_and_link_entities (short_term.py:1376) writes extracted entities with embedding None. The MERGE query in build_create_entity_query sets e.embedding=$embedding on create. search_entities (long_term.py:1150-1159) is a pure vector-index search. I ran it live with a fake extractor returning Maya Chen and Northstar Robotics: both entities were stored and MENTIONS-linked with no embedding, and search_entities('Maya Chen') returned []. So anthropic_local_memory.py:37-41 always raises 'No entity candidates' on the fresh database the tutorial assumes. The step-6 query (entity.embedding IS NOT NULL) also returns no rows.
findings.v2reason: I ran it and the defect is real. `short_term._extract_and_link_entities` (src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:1376) writes every auto-extracted entity with `"embedding": None`. Nothing in the SDK adds an embedding later: `UPDATE_ENTITY_EMBEDDING` in graph/queries.py:287 is defined but never used anywhere under src/. `long_term.search_entities` (long_term.py:1127-1159) only runs a vector search, `db.index.vector.queryNodes('entity_embedding_idx', ...)` (queries.py:272-278), so nodes without an embedding can never match. Because of that, docs/modules/ROOT/examples/anthropic_local_memory.py:37-41 always gets back an empty list and raises `RuntimeError("No entity candidates returned; ...")` on a fresh database, no matter how well the model extracts. The page's promised milestone at tutorials/anthropic-and-local-embeddings.adoc:127 ("One or more `Entity candidate:` lines") never appears. The step-6 query at :139-146 (`WHERE entity.embedding IS NOT NULL` ... "Expected: the returned entity vectors have 384 dimensions") returns no rows. This branch caused the break. On main (ec9fc65) the tutorial snippet only printed `Found {len(entities)} entities:`, so a run showed 0 and carried on. The branch added the hard raise and the explicit expectation, which turns a quiet empty result into a stopped tutorial. Blocker is the right severity: a reader who follows the tutorial hits an exception at step 5.
findings.reproduction:
1) Code trace: `grep -rn UPDATE_ENTITY_EMBEDDING src/neo4j_agent_memory` returns only its definition at queries.py:287, never a use. At short_term.py:757-759, add_message's 'auto' mode calls `_extract_and_link_entities`, which runs build_create_entity_query with `embedding: None`.
2) Live run: scratchpad/review/verify_anthropic.py ran against a neo4j:5.26 testcontainer. It used MemoryClient(settings, embedder=tests.conftest.MockEmbedder(), extractor=FakeExtractor) where the extractor returns Maya Chen/PERSON, Northstar Robotics/ORGANIZATION and Denver/LOCATION. It then called add_message(..., extract_entities=True) followed by search_entities("Maya Chen", limit=5). Output:
readback ok: True
search_entities -> []
search_entities threshold=0 -> []
entities: [{'n': 'Maya Chen', 'noemb': True}, {'n': 'Northstar Robotics', 'noemb': True}, {'n': 'Denver', 'noemb': True}]
mentions: [{'c': 3}]
The entities are stored and MENTIONS-linked but have no embedding, so even threshold=0 finds nothing. The tutorial program would raise at line 39.
3) Regression check: `git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/pages/tutorials/anthropic-and-local-embeddings.adoc` lines 108-114 show the old snippet only printing `Found {len(entities)} entities`, with no raise. The file anthropic_local_memory.py does not exist at ec9fc65; commits 8fc3ead and 881c337 on this branch added it.

findings.title: Knowledge-graph tutorial ingest fails: documented install cannot load GLiREL, and working GLiREL finds no relations
findings.detail: The documented install pulls huggingface-hub 1.33.0 and transformers 5.16.1. With those, glirel 1.2.1 cannot load its model, so `python knowledge_graph.py ingest` fails on the first document. With huggingface-hub<1 plus protobuf, the model loads. Even then, GLiRELExtractor returns zero relations at the program's threshold of 0.5, so ingest stops with `No resolved relationships were stored` after both documents have been written. The cause is that `_entities_to_glirel_format` passes character offsets where GLiREL expects token indices. At threshold 0.1 the SDK instead crashes with a pydantic ValidationError, because head_text comes back as a token list. A reader following the page cannot reach `Verified: extraction produced storable relationships` or the later inspect/answer steps. The storage, inspect and answer code itself is correct: with a deterministic extractor supplying the same entities and relations, 5/5 runs printed `Verified: 2 source documents and 4 relationships read back`.
findings.evidence: Offending: knowledge-graph.adoc:33 `python -m pip install 'neo4j-agent-memory[openai,gliner,spacy]==0.6.0' glirel 'loguru>=0.7,<1'`; :131 `Expected: ... followed by Verified: extraction produced storable relationships`; knowledge_graph.py:55 `GLiRELExtractor(relation_types=SCHEMA.relation_types, threshold=0.5)`. Command: `uv pip install --dry-run 'neo4j-agent-memory[openai,gliner,spacy]==0.6.0' glirel 'loguru>=0.7,<1'` resolves `huggingface-hub==1.33.0, transformers==5.16.1, glirel==1.2.1, gliner==0.2.29`. In a venv installed exactly that way from PyPI, plus `python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm`, `python knowledge_graph.py ingest` fails with `RuntimeError: Could not load GLiREL model 'jackboyla/glirel-large-v0': GLiREL._from_pretrained() missing 2 required keyword-only arguments: 'proxies' and 'resume_download'`. With huggingface-hub 0.36.2 + protobuf the log shows `leadership.txt: stored 4 mentions, 0 relationships; skipped 0`, `partnership.txt: stored 4 mentions, 0 relationships; skipped 0`, `RuntimeError: No resolved relationships were stored; inspect extraction output`. The GLiRELExtractor probe at threshold 0.5 and 0.3 returned `[]`; at 0.1 it raised `ValidationError: 2 validation errors for ExtractedRelation source Input should be a valid string [input_value=['Maya', 'Chen', 'is', 'C...'Northstar', 'Robotics']`. SDK source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/gliner_extractor.py:989-993 (character positions used as GLiREL spans) and :1030-1041.
findings.fix: Don't publish this lesson on GLiREL until the SDK's GLiREL span conversion is fixed and released. For now, use a relation source that works (for example the LLM extractor, which the page already requires an OpenAI key for), or build relations from the GLiNER entities explicitly. If GLiREL stays, pin 'huggingface-hub<1' and protobuf and verify that a real run stores at least one relationship before publishing.
findings.v1reason: I resolved the documented install with `uv pip compile`: huggingface-hub==1.33.0, transformers==5.16.1, glirel==1.2.1. In a venv at those versions, loading GLiRELExtractor().model raised `RuntimeError Could not load GLiREL model 'jackboyla/glirel-large-v0': GLiREL._from_pretrained() missing 2 required keyword-only arguments: 'proxies' and 'resume_download'`. In a venv with huggingface-hub 0.36.2 plus protobuf, the probe returned [] relations at thresholds 0.5 and 0.3. At a lower threshold it crashed with a pydantic ValidationError because head_text was a token list. The cause is gliner_extractor.py:989-993, which passes character offsets as GLiREL spans. knowledge_graph.py:55 uses threshold 0.5, so ingest cannot store any relationship. The SDK bug predates this branch, but the branch's new tutorial depends on it.
findings.v2reason: I ran both failure modes in clean venvs, and both reproduce. This branch added the install command (knowledge-graph.adoc:33) and the new program docs/modules/ROOT/examples/knowledge_graph.py, which does not exist at ec9fc65. The old page used `pip install neo4j-agent-memory[all]`. (1) The documented install resolves huggingface-hub 1.33.0 and transformers 5.16.1. With those versions glirel 1.2.1 cannot load its model, so GLiRELExtractor.model raises `GLiRELExtractor.model` raises `RuntimeError: Could not load GLiREL model 'jackboyla/glirel-large-v0': GLiREL._from_pretrained() missing 2 required keyword-only arguments: 'proxies' and 'resume_download'`. That means `python knowledge_graph.py ingest` (adoc:128) fails. (2) With huggingface-hub 0.36.2 and protobuf the model loads, but `extractor()` as built in knowledge_graph.py:44-56 returns `relations: []` for both DOCUMENTS. The cause is in src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/gliner_extractor.py:989-993. `_entities_to_glirel_format` passes character offsets (for example [20, 38], [40, 58] and [65, 71]) as GLiREL spans. GLiREL reads spans as token indices, and the text has only 14 tokens. At threshold 0.3 the result is also []. At 0.1 the SDK crashes with a pydantic ValidationError, because head_text comes back as a token list (gliner_extractor.py:1030-1041). So ingest() in knowledge_graph.py:118-128 has total == 0 and raises `No resolved relationships were stored`. The reader never sees `Verified: extraction produced storable relationships` (adoc:131), and the later inspect and answer steps fail too. The SDK span bug existed before this branch. This branch made it a blocker: the new tutorial depends on GLiREL, uses an install command that cannot load GLiREL, and stops the lesson at a hard gate. A reader following the page cannot finish it, so blocker severity is right.

findings.title: No test or CI job runs the Bolt docs programs against Neo4j; mocked suite passes while live runs fail
findings.detail: test_core_python_tutorials.py is fully mocked by design: create_autospec clients, canned query rows, a fake extractor. It never calls core_memory_recipes.messages, anthropic_local_memory, mcp_local_tutorial, integrations/hybrid_recipe, or a real GLiNER/GLiREL pipeline. It also enshrines the install that fails: the knowledge-graph parameter asserts extras {openai,gliner,spacy} plus glirel and loguru, and that exact install cannot load GLiREL (see the knowledge-graph finding). test_document_relations_use_exact_endpoints_and_record_provenance feeds hand-built relations that the real GLiREL path never produces. On the CI side, docs-tests has no services block, integration-test runs only tests/integration, and example-tests runs only tests/examples. None of them executes docs/modules/ROOT/examples/* against Neo4j, so the three live failures above ship with every job green.
findings.evidence: `uv run pytest tests/docs/test_core_python_tutorials.py -q` gives `105 passed in 0.54s` (also 105 passed in a dev-only venv without openai/gliner/spacy). Live runs of the same programs: messages 8/9 AssertionError, anthropic 5/5 RuntimeError, knowledge_graph ingest 5/5 failure. test_core_python_tutorials.py:379 `("knowledge-graph", {"openai", "gliner", "spacy"}, "knowledge_graph.py")` and :428-431 `assert "glirel" in requirements` / loguru specifier. .github/workflows/ci-python.yml:647-705 docs-tests job has no `services:`; :242 `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/integration`; :442 `uv run pytest tests/examples`. The only Neo4j-backed docs tests are behind `make test-docs-integration` (Makefile:365-367), which runs the stale test_tutorial_examples.py/test_howto_examples.py and is not wired into CI.
findings.fix: Add a Neo4j-backed docs job, for example in example-tests, which already has a neo4j:5.26 service. It should import each maintained program with aura_connection pointed at the service and run every recipe command and tutorial phase with a local embedder and a stub chat client. Run it several times, or add explicit ordering checks, so the flake is caught.
findings.v1reason: Nothing in tests/ calls core_memory_recipes.messages, and nothing runs anthropic_local_memory against a database. test_python_integration_contracts.py runs in the integration-test job, which has a Neo4j service (ci-python.yml:170, 221), but it uses create_autospec mocks, labels itself 'Offline', and its mock search filters by session_id, which the real SDK does not do. test_core_python_tutorials.py:428-431 asserts the glirel/loguru install that cannot load GLiREL. test_tutorial_examples/test_howto_examples are ignored in `make test-docs` (Makefile:345-346), and nothing under .github runs them. No CI job runs the Bolt docs programs against Neo4j, so the live failures in findings 0-2 pass CI.
findings.v2reason:
The finding holds up when run. The mocked suite passes (105 passed in 0.55s). Running the same maintained program, docs/modules/ROOT/examples/core_memory_recipes.py:16 `messages()`, against a real Neo4j 5.26 fails 9 times out of 10 with an AssertionError. So CI stays green while a documented Bolt program fails for readers.

No CI job runs docs/modules/ROOT/examples/* against Neo4j:
- The docs-tests job (.github/workflows/ci-python.yml:647-705) has no `services:` block. It runs test_core_python_tutorials.py, test_aura_tutorial_setup.py and test_aura_tutorial_persona.py. The persona file calls itself "Offline" in its docstring (test_aura_tutorial_persona.py:1) and uses a synthetic `neo4j+s://` URI.
- The integration-test job has a Neo4j service. Its only docs step is test_python_integration_contracts.py (ci-python.yml:221), which calls itself "Offline" (line 1) and uses create_autospec memory layers (lines 47-49).
- The example-tests job runs only tests/examples (ci-python.yml:442). The one tests/examples file that mentions docs/modules only reads audit-reasoning.adoc (test_audit_trail_example.py:15).
- `make test-docs` ignores test_tutorial_examples.py and test_howto_examples.py (Makefile:345-346). `test-docs-integration` (Makefile:365-367) is not called from any workflow.

A grep of tests/ and .github/ turns up no caller that runs core_memory_recipes.messages against a database.

This branch adds the programs and the mocked tests, so the gap is new with the branch. docs/MAINTAINING.md:62 lists "local integration" as its own category of check, but nothing implements it for these programs.

Not checked: I did not re-run the anthropic_local_memory, knowledge_graph/GLiREL or mcp_local_tutorial live failures. They belong to the other findings; the messages repro alone shows the gap lets a real failure through. Major is the right severity: the tests pass without checking the behaviour the docs promise, and it is not a blocker because no build or CI job breaks.

`uv run pytest tests/docs/test_core_python_tutorials.py -q`
Output: `105 passed in 0.55s`

findings.title: test_tutorial_examples.py still tests the old tutorial code, which the rewritten pages no longer show
findings.detail: Each class says `Test code from tutorials/<page>.adoc`, but the branch replaced those pages with included programs about different data and APIs. `make test-docs-integration` now passes (24 of 27; the 3 failures are the known pre-existing ones) while testing code no reader sees, and it never runs first_agent_memory.py, conversation_memory.py or knowledge_graph.py. Stale classes: TestFirstAgentMemoryTutorial (line 18), which tests Nike/running-shoe messages and `search_messages(session_id=...)`, while the page now shows seed/verify/search with Maya Chen and search_entities. TestConversationMemoryTutorial (line 106), which tests `search_preferences` and cross-session search_messages, while the page now shows get_preferences_for plus a chat completion and trace. TestKnowledgeGraphTutorial (line 176), which tests Apple/Tim Cook add_entity, search_entities and add_fact(Satya Nadella), while the page now shows a GLiNER/GLiREL DomainSchema pipeline with provenance. TestTutorialPatterns is generic and is not tied to a page.
findings.evidence: Comparing ec9fc65 with HEAD pages: `Nike`, `running shoes` and `search_preferences` appeared in the old first-agent-memory.adoc and conversation-memory.adoc and appear in no HEAD tutorial page; `Apple Inc`, `Tim Cook` and `Satya` appeared in the old knowledge-graph.adoc only; `search_messages` appeared in the old first-agent-memory.adoc only. test_tutorial_examples.py:19 `"""Test code from tutorials/first-agent-memory.adoc.`, :44 `content="Hello! I'm looking for running shoes. I really like Nike products."`, :135 `search_preferences(`, :190 `name="Apple Inc."`. Running the file against the testcontainer (NEO4J_URI set, RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1) gives `FAILED ...TestConversationMemoryTutorial::test_store_user_preferences` (known) and the rest passing.
findings.fix: Delete these classes, or replace them with tests that import and run the maintained programs' seed/verify/resume/ingest/inspect functions against the Neo4j fixture. Update the docstrings so they no longer claim to test page code.
findings.v1reason: These tests are unchanged, but the branch rewrote the tutorial pages so they now only include first_agent_memory.py, conversation_memory.py and knowledge_graph.py (first-agent-memory.adoc:64 and the matching lines in the other two pages). A grep for Nike|running shoes|search_preferences|Apple Inc|Tim Cook|Satya|search_messages finds 0 matches in each HEAD page, against 16, 18 and 5 matches at ec9fc65. The class docstrings at test_tutorial_examples.py:19, 107 and 177 still claim to test 'code from tutorials/<page>.adoc'. They now test code that no reader sees, and no Neo4j-backed test runs the maintained programs.
findings.v2reason:
The defect is real, but it is smaller than major. At HEAD, tests/docs/test_tutorial_examples.py (unchanged by the branch) still has class docstrings that say it tests page code: :19 "Test code from tutorials/first-agent-memory.adoc.", :107 conversation-memory.adoc, :177 knowledge-graph.adoc. The branch rewrote those three pages so each one includes a maintained program: first-agent-memory.adoc:64 include::example$first_agent_memory.py[], conversation-memory.adoc:66 conversation_memory.py, knowledge-graph.adoc:67 knowledge_graph.py. None of the old content (Nike, running shoes, search_preferences, Apple Inc, Tim Cook, Satya, search_messages) is left in any of the HEAD pages: 0 matches each, against 16, 18 and 5 at ec9fc65. `make test-docs-integration` (Makefile:365-367) runs only test_tutorial_examples.py and test_howto_examples.py. So the Neo4j-backed docs job tests code that no reader sees, and it never runs the maintained tutorial programs against a database. That part of the finding holds.

The finding overstates the coverage gap, though. The branch adds tests/docs/test_core_python_tutorials.py, which imports first_agent_memory, conversation_memory and knowledge_graph from docs/modules/ROOT/examples. It checks every client.<layer>.<method>( call against the real SDK signatures with inspect.signature().bind. It also exercises the programs' restart-chat, trace-on-failure, provenance, relation-inspection and empty-extraction paths with mocks, and checks that the pages include the complete programs. tests/docs/test_aura_tutorial_persona.py adds more offline checks on assembling the files. That suite passes: 105 tests. So the maintained programs are tested, just not against a live Neo4j. The stale classes are still valid SDK smoke tests, so their passing is not false. What is wrong is the docstrings, which claim a link to the pages that is no longer true. What is missing is a live-database run of the maintained programs. Readers are not misled and nothing breaks, so this is minor, not major.

Suggested fix: re-label the old classes as generic SDK checks or delete them, and optionally add a Neo4j-backed test that runs the seed/verify/resume/inspect functions of the three programs.
findings.reproduction:
1) git diff --stat ec9fc65..HEAD -- tests/docs/test_tutorial_examples.py shows no change. The tutorial pages first-agent-memory.adoc, conversation-memory.adoc and knowledge-graph.adoc were rewritten (-571/-696/-789 lines of churn).
2) For each page, counted matches of `grep -cE "Nike|running shoes|search_preferences|Apple Inc|Tim Cook|Satya|search_messages"`: HEAD gives 0, 0, 0. ec9fc65 gives 16, 18, 5.
3) grep -n include:: shows the pages now include example$first_agent_memory.py (first-agent-memory.adoc:64), example$conversation_memory.py (conversation-memory.adoc:66) and example$knowledge_graph.py (knowledge-graph.adoc:67).
4) Makefile:365-367 `test-docs-integration: uv run pytest tests/docs/test_tutorial_examples.py tests/docs/test_howto_examples.py`. It runs no test that imports the maintained programs.
5) Counter-evidence: `uv run pytest tests/docs/test_core_python_tutorials.py -q` gives `105 passed in 0.52s`. The file's docstring says "Offline public-API and failure-path contracts for the core tutorial programs. No provider requests, model downloads, or database connections are made here". Its NAMES list is ["first_agent_memory", "conversation_memory", "knowledge_graph"] (line 31). It includes test_tutorial_calls_bind_to_current_python_api (line 80) and test_pages_include_the_complete_maintained_programs (line 362). So the programs are tested offline, but not against Neo4j.

findings.title: test_howto_examples.py tests the old how-to code, not the core_memory_recipes.py/extraction_recipes.py tags now shown

The test classes still say `Test examples from how-to/<page>.adoc` and exercise the old code. TestMessagesHowTo (line 18) uses `search_messages(session_id=..., metadata_filters=...)` and portfolio metadata; the page now shows add_messages_batch, get_conversation, get_conversation_summary and a database-wide search, and warns that the session_id filter is not applied. TestEntitiesHowTo (line 109) uses iPhone/AAPL `SECURITY` add_entity and search_entities; the page now shows add_relationship, add_fact, query.cypher and get_facts_about. TestPreferencesHowTo (line 176) uses search_preferences; the page now shows get_preferences_for and supersede_preference and calls search_preferences a broader, non-user-scoped query. TestReasoningTracesHowTo (line 220) covers a success-path lifecycle and list_traces; the page now shows the failure path with TraceOutcome and get_trace_with_steps. TestEntityExtractionHowTo (line 310) covers add_message auto-extraction; the page now shows a DB-free GLiNER extract. TestDeduplicationHowTo (line 354) adds Apple Inc twice and searches; the page now shows LongTermMemory.merge_duplicate_entities. findings.evidence: `grep -o 'client\.[a-z_]*\.[a-z_]*('` finds no inline calls in HEAD messages/entities/preferences/reasoning-traces/deduplication.adoc. The old pages had, for example, 8x search_messages, 13x add_entity, 14x search_preferences and 5x review_duplicate. HEAD messages.adoc:41 `include::example$core_memory_recipes.py[tag=messages]`, entities.adoc:41, preferences.adoc:43, reasoning-traces.adoc:43, deduplication.adoc:39, entity-extraction.adoc:41 `include::example$extraction_recipes.py[tags=extract]`. Old-page strings such as `portfolio` (3x in the old messages.adoc) and `AAPL`/`SECURITY` (3x/5x in the old entities.adoc) are absent at HEAD. test_howto_examples.py:19 `"""Test examples from how-to/messages.adoc."""`, :97-101 `search_messages(... session_id=session_id, metadata_filters={"topic": "trading"} ...)`. Live run of both files: `3 failed, 24 passed` (the 3 known pre-existing failures).
findings.fix: Replace these classes with fixture-backed tests that call core_memory_recipes.messages/entities/preferences/reasoning/deduplication/audit and extraction_recipes functions directly, repeating the ordering-sensitive ones. Or delete them and update the `make test-docs-integration` description.
findings.v1reason: At ec9fc65, messages, entities, preferences, reasoning-traces, deduplication and entity-extraction.adoc had 30, 40, 31, 45, 16 and 6 lines with client.x.y( calls. At HEAD each has 0 and instead includes a core_memory_recipes.py or extraction_recipes.py tag. test_howto_examples.py is unchanged and still says 'Test examples from how-to/<page>.adoc' (lines 19, 110, 177, 221, 311, 355). It exercises the old APIs, so the tagged recipes, including the flaky messages recipe, have no Neo4j-backed test. The docs rules in MAINTAINING.md record no exception for these tests.
findings.v2reason:
The finding holds. This branch rewrote six how-to pages. None of them has an inline client.x.y( call any more (grep count is 0 for each). Each now includes a tag from docs/modules/ROOT/examples/core_memory_recipes.py or extraction_recipes.py, for example messages.adoc:41 `include::example$core_memory_recipes.py[tag=messages]`. tests/docs/test_howto_examples.py did not change between ec9fc65 and HEAD. It still says it tests those pages ("Test examples from how-to/messages.adoc." at :19, and likewise at :110, :177, :221, :311 and :355) and still runs the old code. For example, :97-101 calls `search_messages(query="financial query", session_id=session_id, metadata_filters={"topic": "trading"})`. That is the exact pattern messages.adoc:61 now warns against, because the session_id filter is not applied. The recipe's messages() at core_memory_recipes.py:16-47 instead uses add_messages_batch, get_conversation, get_conversation_summary and a database-wide search_messages. So `make test-docs-integration` (Makefile:365-367) keeps passing without exercising any code the pages show.

Nothing runs the recipes against Neo4j. A git grep for core_memory_recipes/extraction_recipes, excluding the audit-evidence and TypeDoc output, finds only the docs pages, partials and tests/docs/test_core_python_tutorials.py. That file is offline, with fake env vars (:34-49) and mocks. It gives partial coverage:
- an AST check that each client.<layer>.<method>( call binds to the real signature
- a tag-existence check (test_howto_tag_includes_resolve_to_actual_functions)
- a mocked run of reasoning() (:549-564)
- a regex comparison of the RELATED_TO Cypher (:134-172)
- mocked batch, streaming and schema checks for extraction_recipes

That mock coverage softens the gap a little, and neither test_howto_examples.py nor test_tutorial_examples.py ran in CI before or after this branch; only a local make target runs them. But no test runs messages, entities, preferences, deduplication or audit, or checks their in-script asserts (message ID ordering, summary count, dedup merge) against a real database. The stale tests also imply that coverage exists. The rubric counts a test that silently passes as major, so I kept major.

findings.title: hybrid recipe passes session_id to search_memory, but results include other sessions relabelled as this one
findings.detail: The recipe calls `provider.search_memory(..., session_id=session_id, memory_types=["message"])` and prints the candidate count. The call reports `filters_applied['session_id']` and wraps every hit with `Memory.from_message(msg, session_id=session_id)`. Underneath it calls short_term.search_messages, which does not filter by session; messages.adoc already warns about this. Messages from earlier runs and other sessions therefore come back labelled with the new session ID. aws-hybrid-memory.adoc gives no warning, so a reader will take the search as session-scoped.
findings.evidence: hybrid_recipe.py:25-33 `result = await provider.search_memory("project code", session_id=session_id, memory_types=["message"], ... threshold=0.0)`. Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/integrations/agentcore/memory_provider.py:273-286 `filters["session_id"] = session_id` ... `search_messages(query=query, session_id=session_id, ...)` ... `Memory.from_message(msg, session_id=session_id)`; messages.adoc WARNING: `the underlying Cypher (SEARCH_MESSAGES_BY_EMBEDDING) never filters on it`. Live second run: `FILTERS {'threshold': 0.0, 'session_id': 'docs-hybrid-00d089d2', ...}` with memories `[('What is the project code?', 'docs-hybrid-00d089d2'), ('The fictional project code is ', 'docs-hybrid-00d089d2'), ('The fictional project code is ', 'docs-hybrid-00d089d2'), ('Stored reply', 'docs-hybrid-00d089d2')]`. Only one of these was stored in that session; the others came from the previous run and from a docs-common-turn-* session.
findings.fix: Add the same warning messages.adoc uses to aws-hybrid-memory.adoc: search_memory's session_id does not scope message search on Bolt. Either drop session_id from the recipe's search call or filter the results by stored IDs from get_session_memories.
findings.v1reason: hybrid_recipe.py:25-33 passes session_id to search_memory. memory_provider.py:273-286 records it in filters_applied and passes it to short_term.search_messages. short_term.search_messages (short_term.py:920-949) never uses session_id: it runs SEARCH_MESSAGES_BY_EMBEDDING (queries.py:176-182), which has no session filter. Every hit is then wrapped with Memory.from_message(msg, session_id=session_id), so messages from other sessions come back labelled with this one. aws-hybrid-memory.adoc does not warn about this, and it even keeps a legacy `_session_scoped_search` anchor. The recipe only prints a count and verifies persistence through get_session_memories, so this is minor.

findings.title: Reference page gives the wrong DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL value
findings.detail: This line was added by the branch. The model id named here is not the SDK default, so a reader pre-downloading models for the knowledge-graph tutorial fetches the wrong model.
findings.evidence: extractor-relations.adoc:175 `DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL is jackboyla/glirel_base.` vs src/neo4j_agent_memory/extraction/gliner_extractor.py:827 `DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL = "jackboyla/glirel-large-v0"`. The live run loaded `jackboyla/glirel-large-v0` (error text: `Could not load GLiREL model 'jackboyla/glirel-large-v0'`).

findings.v1reason: This line was added on the branch (commit c90d191). extractor-relations.adoc:175 says '`DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL` is `jackboyla/glirel_base`'. The source, gliner_extractor.py:827, has DEFAULT_GLIREL_MODEL = "jackboyla/glirel-large-v0", and lines 863, 903 and 1096 use it as the default. 'glirel_base' appears nowhere in src/.

findings.title: Manual-wiring Strands block fails strict tsc: Neo4jConversationManager is not a ConversationManager
findings.detail: The 'wire each surface yourself' block passes `new Neo4jConversationManager(...)` straight into `new Agent({ sessionManager, conversationManager, model, tools })`. Neo4jConversationManager copies the shape of Strands' abstract `ConversationManager` but does not extend it. It also declares its own `protected _compressionThreshold`, so TypeScript rejects the assignment under `strict`. A reader who copies this block into a strict TS project gets a compile error. The SDK's own `connectMemoryToAgent` avoids the error with a cast. The type-compatibility test only checks `Pick<ConversationManager, "name"|"reduce"|"initAgent">`, so it cannot catch this. The code lines predate this branch. It is reported because the branch rewrote this page's 'Version compatibility' paragraph and added a 'Verify the integration' section, and both still say the tests show each class satisfies the interface it implements.
findings.evidence:
Scratch project with typescript/dist, @strands-agents/sdk 1.17.0 (from typescript/node_modules), tsc 5.9.3 --strict (also under --module nodenext --verbatimModuleSyntax --noUncheckedIndexedAccess). Block at strands.adoc:228-253 plus `declare const memory: MemoryClient; declare const conv: {id:string}; declare const model: any; declare const tools: any[]` gives:
`error TS2322: Type 'Neo4jConversationManager' is not assignable to type 'ConversationManager'. Property '_compressionThreshold' is protected but type 'Neo4jConversationManager' is not a class derived from 'ConversationManager'.` (maps to strands.adoc:250 `const agent = new Agent({ sessionManager, conversationManager, model, tools });`).
Source: typescript/src/integrations/strands/conversation-manager.ts:48 `export class Neo4jConversationManager {` (no extends) and :55 `protected readonly _compressionThreshold: number | undefined = undefined;`. The SDK's own wiring casts: typescript/src/integrations/strands/connect.ts:78 `conversationManager: publicSurface as unknown as StrandsConversationManager`. The test checks only a Pick: typescript/test/unit/strands/type-compatibility.test.ts:41 `const ducktyped: Pick<ConversationManager, "name" | "reduce" | "initAgent"> = cm;`.
findings.fix: In the block, import `type ConversationManager` from @strands-agents/sdk and pass `conversationManager: conversationManager as unknown as ConversationManager`, as connect.ts does. Alternatively, have Neo4jConversationManager's public typing satisfy ConversationManager. Change the compatibility sentence to say the test checks the name/reduce/initAgent shape, not full assignability.
findings.v1reason: I reproduced the error. I type-checked the block at strands.adoc:228-253 in a scratch project with tsc --strict, module nodenext and @strands-agents/sdk 1.17.0 from typescript/node_modules, with the package paths mapped to typescript/src. The compiler output was: `a.ts(7,43): error TS2322: Type 'Neo4jConversationManager' is not assignable to type 'ConversationManager'. Property '_compressionThreshold' is protected but type 'Neo4jConversationManager' is not a class derived from 'ConversationManager'.` That line is strands.adoc:250 `new Agent({ sessionManager, conversationManager, model, tools })`. The source bears this out. conversation-manager.ts:48 declares the class without `extends`, and :55 declares `protected readonly _compressionThreshold`. connect.ts:78 casts with `as unknown as StrandsConversationManager`. type-compatibility.test.ts:41 checks only a `Pick<ConversationManager, "name"|"reduce"|"initAgent">`. Scope caveat: the code block and the sentence 'asserts each of our classes still satisfies the interface it implements' are both on main (ec9fc65 lines 246 and 325), so the branch did not introduce the defect. The branch did rewrite this Version-compatibility paragraph, adding 'The tests check installed typings', and kept the overstated claim, so I count it as minor. A human may prefer to treat it as out of scope.

findings.title: New streaming block defaults to gpt-4o-mini; the quick-start block it extends defaults to gpt-5-mini
findings.detail: The branch added a streaming block that the page says continues the quick start ('Add `streamText` to the existing `ai` import, then use:'). Its fallback model id differs from the quick start's, so the same script falls back to two different models depending on the path. The other TS pages also default to gpt-5-mini: nextjs-memory-chat, strands and langchain.

findings.title: Docs call Python get_active() unreliable, but this branch's SDK source fixes it
findings.detail: This branch rewrites NamsOntology.get_active() (commit d41e4bd). It now reads the response's authoritative `version` record, validates it, and never falls back to the latest revision. It also adds a new ActiveOntology.schema_hash field. The same branch's docs say the Python SDK's get_active() 'can report the latest revision when an older revision is active' and tell readers to avoid its version_id/validation_mode. The docs set this against 'Current TypeScript source reads the authoritative response version', which implies the Python source does not. The HEAD source still reports __version__ = "0.6.0" and has no CHANGELOG entry, so a reader of HEAD docs plus HEAD source gets contradictory guidance. The new schema_hash field is not listed anywhere in the ontology reference. The same caveat appears at use-ontologies.adoc:26 and :120 and at tutorials/ontology-quickstart.adoc:87.
findings.evidence: docs/modules/ROOT/pages/reference/ontology-api.adoc:77-81: "Python `neo4j-agent-memory==0.6.0` does not use that field consistently: its `get_active()` metadata can report the latest revision when an older revision is active." and :22 "Python 0.6.0 has a binding-metadata limitation ... Current TypeScript source reads the authoritative response `version`." Source of truth: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py:409-422 at HEAD: `raw_version = payload.get("version")` ... `version = _parse_active_version(raw_version)` ... `return ActiveOntology(..., version_id=version.id, schema_hash=version.schema_hash)`. `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py` removes the old `summaries = await self.list()` / `_current_version(...)` latest-revision fallback and adds `schema_hash: str | None = None` at ontology.py:176. src/neo4j_agent_memory/__init__.py:234 `__version__ = "0.6.0"`. `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- CHANGELOG.md` is empty.
findings.fix: Decide which version these pages describe (needs a human decision). If the fix ships in the next Python release, keep the 0.6.0 caveat but say the source/next release reads the authoritative `version`. Add a CHANGELOG entry and list the ActiveOntology fields, including schema_hash, under Return types. Otherwise, if the docs must describe only published 0.6.0, flag the unreleased source change in the PR description.
findings.v1reason: This branch rewrote NamsOntology.get_active() in commit d41e4bd. The `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/ontology.py` output removes the list()/_current_version latest-revision fallback. At HEAD, ontology.py:409-422 reads payload['version'], validates it with _parse_active_version and returns version_id/validation_mode/schema_hash taken from that record. ontology.py:176 adds `schema_hash: str | None = None` to ActiveOntology. The docs pin PyPI 0.6.0 (use-ontologies.adoc:21, ontology-quickstart.adoc:38-42), so the caveat is literally true for the published wheel. At HEAD, though, the source and __version__ both say 0.6.0. CHANGELOG.md has an empty `## [Unreleased]` section and `git diff ec9fc65..HEAD -- CHANGELOG.md` is empty. ontology-api.adoc:22 says only 'Current TypeScript source reads the authoritative response `version`', which implies the Python source does not, and the Python source now does. ActiveOntology's fields, including the new schema_hash, are not listed: ontology-api.adoc:64 names only the type, and :129-130 lists schema_hash for OntologyVersion only. A human must decide whether this is a release-note gap or a docs-wording gap. The inconsistency and the missing changelog entry are real, and the harm is small because the docs route readers to a workaround helper.

findings.title: Capabilities page implies add_relationship stores attributes; the Bolt write drops them
findings.detail: The new capabilities page says Bolt relationship writes are supported by 'passing source, target, relationship_type, and attributes', which suggests attributes are stored. The Bolt Cypher write never receives `attributes`, and two other pages on this branch say so explicitly. A reader porting provenance attributes from this page would lose data without any error.
findings.evidence: backend-capabilities.adoc:30: "Python with Bolt::: Supported with `add_relationship()`, passing source, target, relationship_type, and attributes". Source: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/long_term.py:1045-1056 passes only id, source_id, target_id, relation_type, description, confidence, valid_from, valid_until to queries.CREATE_ENTITY_RELATIONSHIP (src/neo4j_agent_memory/graph/queries.py:353-372, which sets no attributes). Contradicting pages: how-to/entities.adoc:67 "Its write does not persist the `attributes` argument" and reference/api/long-term-entities.adoc:141 "includes `attributes` on the returned model but does not pass them to the graph write".
findings.fix: Change the Bolt cell to e.g. "Supported with `add_relationship(source, target, relationship_type, ...)`; `attributes` are returned on the model but not persisted in 0.6.0", or drop 'and attributes'.
findings.v1reason: This branch adds backend-capabilities.adoc:30 (line 36 of the file's diff): 'Supported with `add_relationship()`, passing source, target, relationship_type, and attributes'. At HEAD, long_term.py:1045-1056 passes execute_write only id, source_id, target_id, relation_type, description, confidence, valid_from and valid_until. `attributes` goes only onto the returned Relationship model (long_term.py:1042). queries.py:353-372 CREATE_ENTITY_RELATIONSHIP sets no attributes. Two pages in this same branch say the attributes are not persisted: how-to/entities.adoc:67 ('Its write does not persist the `attributes` argument') and reference/api/long-term-entities.adoc:141 ('does not pass them to the graph write'). So the new capabilities cell contradicts them and implies the attributes are stored.

findings.title: Cloud embeddings recipe crashes after the vector check; the stored-message step never runs
findings.detail: `main()` hands the `BedrockEmbedder`/`VertexAIEmbedder` instance to `common.settings(embedding=embedder)`, which passes it on as `BoltSettings(embedding=...)`. `MemorySettings.embedding` rejects legacy `BaseEmbedder` instances with a TypeError. A reader following aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc or google-cloud.adoc sees `Verified 2 vectors of ... dimensions` and then a traceback. The promised 'then stored-message verification' (`Verified stored messages; session=...`) can never print, and nothing is written to Aura. The contract tests only call `build_embedder()` and `verify_vectors()`. None of them builds settings from a cloud embedder, so the suite passes.
findings.evidence: Offending: cloud_embeddings_recipe.py:41 `async with MemoryClient(settings(embedding=embedder)) as client:`; google-cloud.adoc:97 "Expected: `Verified 2 vectors of 768 dimensions`, then stored-message verification."; aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:86 "Expected: `Verified 2 vectors of 1024 dimensions`, then stored-message verification." Command: `uv run python -c "...import common, cloud_embeddings_recipe as c; common.settings(embedding=c.build_embedder(p))"` for p in vertex/bedrock -> `TypeError MemorySettings.embedding must be EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an EmbeddingProvider instance; got VertexAIEmbedder.` (same for BedrockEmbedder). Source of truth: `MemoryClient.__init__(self, settings=None, *, embedder: Embedder | None = None, ...)` accepts a legacy embedder separately; VertexAIEmbedder MRO is (VertexAIEmbedder, BaseEmbedder, ABC, object), not an EmbeddingProvider.
findings.fix: Pass the checked embedder to the client instead of the settings, e.g. `MemoryClient(settings(embedding=<provider string such as 'vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001' / 'bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0'>), embedder=embedder)`, or add a `settings()` variant that does not build the OpenAI provider. Add a test that builds the client configuration with each cloud embedder.
findings.v1reason: Reproduced this. cloud_embeddings_recipe.py:41 is new on this branch, and it passes the legacy embedder to common.settings(embedding=embedder), which calls BoltSettings(embedding=...). Running build_embedder + common.settings for each provider raised `TypeError MemorySettings.embedding must be EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an EmbeddingProvider instance; got VertexAIEmbedder.`, and the same error for BedrockEmbedder. So the stored-message step that google-cloud.adoc:97 and aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:86 promise can never run: a reader following those pages gets a traceback.
findings.v2reason: I ran the code, and the finding holds. docs/modules/ROOT/examples/integrations/cloud_embeddings_recipe.py:41 calls `MemoryClient(settings(embedding=embedder))`. The embedder there is the legacy `VertexAIEmbedder` or `BedrockEmbedder` that `build_embedder()` returns. Both classes have the MRO (X, BaseEmbedder, ABC, object). `common.settings()` (docs/modules/ROOT/examples/integrations/common.py:10-19) passes that object on as `BoltSettings(embedding=...)`. The validator at src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:728-736 raises a TypeError for any object that is not an EmbeddingProvider. So the script prints the "Verified 2 vectors..." line from verify_vectors, then fails with a traceback before it writes anything to Neo4j. It never reaches the "stored-message verification" that google-cloud.adoc:97 and aws-bedrock-embeddings.adoc:86 promise. The file is new on this branch: it does not exist at ec9fc65, and it was added in commit 8fc3ead. tests/docs/test_python_integration_contracts.py only loads the module as `cloud` and never builds settings from a cloud embedder, so no test catches this. A reader who follows either page cannot complete the documented procedure, so blocker is the right severity. The fix is to keep the embedding provider string in the settings and pass the checked embedder separately. For Vertex: `MemoryClient(settings(embedding="vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001"), embedder=embedder)`. For Bedrock, use the Bedrock provider string with `embedder=embedder` in the same way.
findings.reproduction:
From docs/modules/ROOT/examples/integrations, with dummy env values (GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=p GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-central1 AWS_REGION=us-east-1 NEO4J_URI=bolt://localhost:7687 NEO4J_USERNAME=neo4j NEO4J_PASSWORD=x):
uv run --project <repo> python -c "import common, cloud_embeddings_recipe as c; from neo4j_agent_memory import MemoryClient; [MemoryClient(common.settings(embedding=c.build_embedder(p))) for p in ['vertex','bedrock']]" (the actual run wrapped each provider in its own try/except)
Output:
vertex TypeError MemorySettings.embedding must be EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an EmbeddingProvider instance; got VertexAIEmbedder.
bedrock TypeError MemorySettings.embedding must be EmbeddingConfig, a provider string, or an EmbeddingProvider instance; got BedrockEmbedder.
Printed MROs: (VertexAIEmbedder, BaseEmbedder, ABC, object) and (BedrockEmbedder, BaseEmbedder, ABC, object).
The error is raised by src/neo4j_agent_memory/config/settings.py:731-736.
`git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/examples/integrations/cloud_embeddings_recipe.py` returns "exists on disk, but not in 'ec9fc65'", so the file is new on this branch (added in commit 8fc3ead).

findings.title: NAMS first-write step posts to a made-up conversation id and 404s instead of printing its success line
findings.detail: Step 3 of nams-quickstart says 'You should see `Stored and read back: user said 'Hello, NAMS!'`'. The program calls `add_message("docs-nams-first-write", ...)` without first calling `create_conversation`. On NAMS, add_message posts to `/conversations/{session_id}/messages`. The SDK docstring says session_id is the server-minted conversation UUID from `create_conversation`. The repo's own hosted fixture returns 404 for an unknown conversation, so the program raises NotFoundError before printing. The same page later says the conversation ID 'identifies the actual server-created conversation', and hello-memory/main.py creates the conversation first on NAMS for this reason. Even with that fixed, this step creates a hosted record outside the ledger, and the page's careful cleanup never removes or reports it. No test covers this file.
findings.evidence: Offending: nams_first_write.py:11-12 `session_id = "docs-nams-first-write"` / `await client.short_term.add_message(session_id, "user", "Hello, NAMS!")`; nams-quickstart.adoc:80 "You should see `Stored and read back: user said 'Hello, NAMS!'`." Source of truth: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:264-266 "The Protocol's session_id parameter on every method maps to the NAMS conversation UUID — usually the one returned from create_conversation. Pre-create your conversation"; examples/hello-memory/main.py "NAMS mints conversation ids server-side" + `create_conversation(SESSION)` before add_message. Command: ran nams_first_write.py with MEMORY_ENDPOINT pointed at typescript/examples/vercel-ai/test/docs-hosted-stub.ts -> exit 1, `NotFoundError: NAMS POST .../v1/conversations/docs-nams-first-write/messages → 404: Not found`; stub calls ['GET /conversations', 'POST /conversations/docs-nams-first-write/messages'].
findings.fix: Create the conversation first (`conversation = await client.short_term.create_conversation(...)`), then use `str(conversation.id)` for add_message and get_conversation. Also delete that conversation at the end of the step, or tell the reader it is kept, so the page's cleanup claims stay true. Add a test for this file against the hosted stub.
findings.v1reason: nams_first_write.py is new on this branch. It calls add_message with a made-up id 'docs-nams-first-write' and never calls create_conversation. NamsShortTermMemory's docstring (src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:264-267) says session_id is the conversation UUID from create_conversation and tells the reader to pre-create the conversation. add_message posts to the conversation_id path. The branch's own reference page (backend-capabilities.adoc:15, 'Python with NAMS:: Create a conversation and use its returned ID') and examples/hello-memory/main.py:77-79 ('NAMS mints conversation ids server-side') say the same. The repo's hosted stub (typescript/examples/vercel-ai/test/docs-hosted-stub.ts:67) returns 404 for an unknown /conversations/ path. I could not observe the live service, but the SDK and the docs agree that the step as written cannot produce the 'You should see' line at nams-quickstart.adoc:80.
findings.v2reason:
I ran it, and the defect is real. docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py is new on this branch; it does not exist at ec9fc65. Line 12 passes a made-up id, "docs-nams-first-write", to add_message on NAMS and never calls create_conversation first.

The SDK uses that value as the conversation id in the request path: src/neo4j_agent_memory/nams/short_term.py:291-295 posts to /conversations/{conversation_id}/messages. The class docstring at lines 264-267 says to pre-create the conversation and pass its UUID. This branch's own docs say the same:
- reference/api/short-term.adoc:24: "On NAMS, call `create_conversation` first and use its returned ID."
- reference/backend-capabilities.adoc:15 says the same.
- reference/api/short-term-messages.adoc:147: create_conversation "returns a server-issued ID".
- examples/hello-memory/main.py:77-79: "NAMS mints conversation ids server-side".

Run against the repo's hosted stub, the documented program exits 1 with a NotFoundError (404) on the add_message POST, so the "You should see `Stored and read back: ...`" line at nams-quickstart.adoc:80 is never printed.

The failure does not depend on how strict the stub is. The Python Conversation model has `id: UUID` (src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:268). Suppose the live service did auto-create a conversation under that string and echoed it back. get_conversation would still fail: I passed `{'id': 'docs-nams-first-write'}` through _normalize_conversation and payload_to_model, and it raised a pydantic ValidationError. The step cannot succeed on any NAMS that returns the id it was given.

I am keeping severity at major, not blocker. It is a sanity-check step, and later steps in the tutorial do not depend on it. The side point in the finding also stands: the step would leave a hosted record that the ledger and cleanup never track. That part is secondary.

Coverage: I did not run against the live memory.neo4jlabs.com. I checked the fix only up to the create_conversation call, because the stub returns non-UUID ids such as 'conversation-1'. That also means the stub cannot, as written, back the test the finding suggests for this file. One housekeeping note: my first command accidentally created an empty file, typescript/examples/vercel-ai/test/.zz-scratch-not-created.txt. I deleted it, and git status now matches the starting snapshot.
findings.reproduction:
1) Started the stub (typescript/examples/vercel-ai/test/docs-hosted-stub.ts) with tsx and ran `uv run python docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py` with MEMORY_API_KEY=nams_test, MEMORY_ENDPOINT=<stub>/v1 and MEMORY_WORKSPACE_ID="". Runner: scratchpad/review/run_first_write.mts.
   Output: exit 1, `neo4j_agent_memory.core.exceptions.NotFoundError: NAMS POST http://127.0.0.1:61820/v1/conversations/docs-nams-first-write/messages → 404: Not found`
   Stub calls: ["GET /conversations","POST /conversations/docs-nams-first-write/messages"]. The success line is never printed.

2) Checked whether a non-UUID id can survive readback even if the service auto-created it:
   `uv run python -c "from neo4j_agent_memory.nams.short_term import _normalize_conversation; from neo4j_agent_memory.nams._serialization import payload_to_model; from neo4j_agent_memory.memory.short_term import Conversation; payload_to_model(_normalize_conversation({'id':'docs-nams-first-write'}, session_id='docs-nams-first-write', messages=[...]), Conversation)"`
   Output: `ValidationError 1 validation error for Conversation id Input should be a valid UUID`. Cause: Conversation.id is typed `UUID` at src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/short_term.py:268.

3) Ran a fixed variant against the stub that calls create_conversation first. The request sequence is correct (["GET /conversations","POST /conversations"]). It then failed only because the stub's ids are not UUIDs ('conversation-1'), which is a stub limitation.

4) `git show ec9fc65:docs/modules/ROOT/examples/nams_first_write.py` fails with "exists on disk, but not in 'ec9fc65'", and git log shows the file was added in d3db0ff on this branch. `grep -rn nams_first_write tests` finds no matches, so no test covers the file.

findings.title: LangChain example: first turn shows injected memory the program no longer produces
findings.detail: This branch removed the seeded preference that used to fill the first turn's memory block. Before the first turn, `getContext` has no messages yet, because persistence happens in `afterAgent`. In a fresh workspace the entity search is empty too, so `buildMemoryBlock` returns '' and the middleware logs `memory: nothing recalled yet (first turn)`. It logs this on each model call of the turn: twice when the tool is called. The README still shows `memory: injected 4 lines of graph context` on turn one. That line is left over from the removed preference, which gave exactly 4 lines: header, blank line, 'Known user preferences:' and one entry.
findings.evidence: Offending: README.md:84-86 `user> I'm evaluating graph databases ... Neo4j is top of my list.` / `memory: injected 4 lines of graph context`. Source: src/nams-memory.ts:172-173 `if (block === "") { log("memory: nothing recalled yet (first turn)");`. Command: ran `main()` under test/fake-nams.ts + fakeModel via tsx -> output: `user> I'm evaluating graph databases...` / `memory: nothing recalled yet (first turn)` / `tool search_memory_entities("graph database") -> 0 entities` / `memory: nothing recalled yet (first turn)` / `memory: persisted human message (84 chars)`; the second turn shows `memory: injected 8 lines of graph context`.
findings.fix: Replace the first-turn line with `memory: nothing recalled yet (first turn)`, shown once per model call (before and after the tool call). Or add a note that it only reads 'injected N lines' when the workspace already holds matching entities.
findings.v1reason: This branch removed the seeded addPreference from src/index.ts and changed buildMemoryBlock to search entities instead of preferences (nams-memory.ts:115-150). On the first turn the program has no recent messages, and a fresh workspace has no entities, so the block is empty. In that case nams-memory.ts:172-173 logs 'memory: nothing recalled yet (first turn)'. README.md:86 still shows 'memory: injected 4 lines of graph context', which is exactly the old header, blank line, 'Known user preferences:' and one entry. The branch edited this README's expected-output block (it removed the Preferences lines) but left this stale line in place.

findings.title: MCP 'Verify the integration' runs `npm run lint`, but the mcp example has no lint script
findings.detail: The new verification section tells readers to run `npm run lint` in typescript/examples/mcp. That package defines `start`, `typecheck`, `build`, `serve` and `test`, with no `lint`. npm fails with 'Missing script: "lint"' before `npm test`, so the verification step fails as written. The langchain, mastra, strands and vercel-ai examples do define `lint`.
findings.evidence: Offending: mcp.adoc:317 "In `typescript/examples/mcp/`, run `npm run lint` and `npm test`." Source: typescript/examples/mcp/package.json scripts: start, typecheck ("tsc --noEmit"), build, serve, test. Command: `cd typescript/examples/mcp && npm run lint` -> `npm error Missing script: "lint"`.
findings.fix: Use `npm run typecheck` on this page, or add `"lint": "tsc --noEmit"` to typescript/examples/mcp/package.json to match the other examples.
findings.v1reason: mcp.adoc:317 is new on this branch: 'In `typescript/examples/mcp/`, run `npm run lint` and `npm test`.' The scripts in typescript/examples/mcp/package.json are only start, typecheck, build, serve and test, with no lint, so `npm run lint` fails with 'Missing script'. The workaround is easy: run npm run typecheck instead.

README.md:100 says 'This runner uses the `neo4j` database; it does not read a `NEO4J_DATABASE` override.' main.py:128 reads `database=os.getenv("NEO4J_DATABASE", "neo4j")`, and main.py:29 says 'NEO4J_DATABASE defaults to neo4j'.
